CIPCon User Manual 
Section 1 Terms 
Abbreviation/ Terms 
Description 
EtherNet/IP 
EtherNet/IP is an industrial application layer protocol for automation. Built on 
standard UDP/IP and TCP/IP protocols, it defines an application layer protocol for 
configuring, accessing , and controlling industrial automation devices using fixed 
Ethernet hardware and software. 
ENIP 
Abbreviation for EtherNet/IP. 
Scanner 
Scanner. EtherNet/IP master. 
Adapter 
Adapter. EtherNet/IP slave station. 
EDS 
Open device description file. 
DBM 
DBM file is the final file of ETHERNET/IP configuration software which provides 
to hardware. 
PBC 
PBC file is the engineering configuration file generated by CIPCon.
--- pag 5 ---
CIPCon User Manual IM41S93-E 
Section 2 System Application Overview 
The network device can be compartmentalized to Scanner (master) and Adapter (slave) on the 
basis of EtherNet/IP specifications. Scanner can manage and initiate communication with client 
devices. The communication module connects standard EtherNet/IP Scanner and Adapter 
devices to the system. Through E-BUS and controller communication, in-system control station 
and operation station can realize message both-way communication with other control system 
and intelligent device, and make heterogeneity device as subsystem of SUPCON DCS. 
CIPCon software is the software to configure EtherNet/IP communication module. And the 
CIPCon software is mainly used to configure hardware of EtherNet/IP module in ECS-700 system. 
System Index 
 
Communication Interface: 1 channel EtherNet/IP interface. 
 
Supported communicate rate of EtherNet/IP: 10/100Mbps. 
 
Input total data of all ENIP devices connected to a communication module is no longer 
than 3.5k bytes. 
 
Input data of single ENIP devices connected to a communication module is no longer 
than 512 bytes. 
 
Output total data of all ENIP devices connected to a communication module is no longer 
than 3.5k bytes. 
 
Output data of single ENIP devices connected to a communication module is no longer 
than 256 bytes. 
 
The maximum number of ENIP devices supported by the ECS-700 system is 64, and 
there can be at most one Scanner device. 
2

CIPCon User Manual IM41S93-E 
Section 3 EtherNet/IP 
Configuration 
Management 
Software (CIPCon) Usage 
User can configure the EtherNet/IP site, view and set the basic properties of station, add 
submodules to the slave station and set the parameter information of module with the EtherNet/IP 
configuration management software (CIPCon). 
The station types of EtherNet/IP include Scanner and Adapter. When the system is configured, 
the EtherNet/IP communication module acts as Scanner and Adapter. But only one Scanner can 
be connected at the same time.

Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
1 
Config Explorer 
Section 1 Overview 
As the work platform of system configuration, VFExplorer is associated with VFIOBuilder, 
VFTAGBuilder, VFFBDBuilder and VFHMICfg, and supports functions of offline download, online 
download, online configuration, offline configuration, parallel configuration, configuration publish, 
single control station configuration backup and load, simulation, etc. 
VFExplorer is applied in engineer station, connecting both configuration server and each control 
station. After building the system structure in VFSysBuilder, configuration of hardware, tag, control 
scheme, custom function block and HMI can be done in VFExplorer, and online download and 
online publish of configuration are available too. 
1.1 Function Features 
The main functions of the software include: 
1. Parallel Configuration: the control configuration takes a single control station as a unit, 
and each engineer is responsible for the configuration of one or more control stations. 
When the control part is connected with configuration server, several engineers can 
configure the same project in different engineer stations simultaneously. For monitoring 
configuration, parallel configuration can be done in unit of single operation domain (or 
single file when the objects are resources files such as graphics or schedule). 
2. Online Download: check the control configuration in unit of single control station to 
make sure it can pass compilation and find out the part which should be downloaded by 
comparing with the configuration in control station, then download online. The memory of 
each configuration in control station is fixed and independent from each other, thus can 
be edited and compiled separately while configuring, and the minimum unit to download 
is a hardware module, a tag or a custom program. 
3. Offline Download: when the version of configuration in control station is different from 
that in engineer station, online download will not be allowed, and offline download can be 
used, which will skip over the configuration comparison if the field devices are safe, to 
completely download the correct configuration of engineer station directly. 
4. Online Configuration: the real-time value (including parameters of function block and 
tag, hardware configuration data) in controller can be modified directly when it is 
connected with controller. 
5. Control Configuration and HMI: 
 
Start up VFIOBuilder to configure hardware of control station. 
 
Start up VFTAGBuilder to configure tag of control station.
--- pag 7 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
2 
 
Build or delete custom program, adjust the execution sequence of custom program 
by modifying the running cycle and phase. 
 
Build or delete custom function block, start up VFSTModule to configure. 
 
Start up VFHMICfg to configure monitoring in operation domain. 
6. Single Control Station Configuration Backup and Load of Historical Single Control 
Station Configuration: make a backup of single control station configuration and load 
the backup of historical configuration easily. 
7. Configuration Publish: opt for the operation domain and publish updated configuration 
to it. Operation node obtains updated configuration from configuration server. 
8. Online or Start up/Stop Custom Program: connect with custom programs to view 
running status, running time, inactive/ active status of input/ output, etc of all custom 
programs; stop/ start up any program. 
9. Phase Load: view the phase load and running time of current controller. 
10. Global Tag Search: search and accurately locate tags and domain variables in all 
control domains and operation domains of current project. 
11. Control Station Read-only: when the control station is locked by some engineer 
stations, engineers with configuration authority can view the configuration in normal or 
online debug status, but can not configure or write value. 
12. Download Log: view latest 500 download log of selected controller. 
13. Page Footer Settings: set the template of page footer in printing of custom program. 
14. Status View: select a node in project configuration tree in the working area, then the 
information of selected node would be showed in property bar on the right. 
15. Simulation: debug configuration without real controller. 
1.2 Technical Specification 
The minimum unit of parallel configuration: 
 
Single control station for control configuration. 
 
Single operation domain for HMI configuration 
 
Single file for resources such as graphics or schedule. 
The minimum unit of block compilation and download: 
 
One (or a redundant couple) module for hardware configuration. 
 
One tag for tag configuration. 
 
One program for custom program. 
 
One parameter for the initial value of function blocks parameter. 
 
All function blocks in the control station for custom function block. 
 
The configuration of the whole module for Profibus master communication module.
--- pag 8 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
3 
 
The configuration of the whole module for serial communication module. 
Control scheme 
 
When the controller is FCU711-S or FCU712-S, a single control station supports at most 
200 custom programs. When the controller is FCU713-S, a single control station 
supports at most 500 custom programs. 
 
Space, \, /, and single quote mark, double quote mark, comma and colon in English 
status are not allowed in custom program name; name can not be repeated and is in at 
most 64 English characters; descriptions can use any character and are in at most 256 
English characters. Both name and descriptions can be modified. 
 
The number of custom function blocks in single station is at most 250, and the sum of 
code can’t exceed 512k byte. 
 
At most 16 English characters are in custom function block name, which must start with 
letter and consist of English letter, number and underline. No repeated name (can’t have 
the same name with system function block), no modification are allowed and try to use 
the least characters to express the meaning of function block; at most 64 English 
characters or 32 Chinese characters are in descriptions and modification is available; the 
length of parameter name is at most 8 characters. 
 
Custom function blocks that have been used can’t be deleted, and the modification of pin, 
parameter name and memory shift is not allowed. 
 
Search and locate tag in whole project, check renamed tag in whole project.
--- pag 9 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
4 
1.3 Configuration Procedure 
When you use VFExplorer, refer to the following figure to configure the project. After configured 
the project, you can start at any step in the following figure to modify the configuration . 
 
Figure 1-1Configuration management flowchart
--- pag 10 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E

Section 2 Launch the Software 
Before starting VFExplorer, please make sure that the project has been created and the system 
structure configuration has been completed. VFExplorer does not support new projects, but only 
supports opening the system structure configuration software to create and set the default project. 
 
Tip: 
For the detailed operation of system structure configuration software to create and set 
default project, please refer to VFSysBuilder User Manual. 
 
2.1 Open the Project 
The configuration management software cannot create a new project, it can only connect to the 
configuration server, and copy the project created by the system structure configuration software 
and set as the default on the server to the local configuration directory on the engineering station. 
The specific operations to connect to the configuration server and open the project are as follows: 
Start the configuration management software, and the login window will pop up automatically, as 
shown in the figure below. (Click the "Open Project" button on the toolbar, and the login window 
will pop up) 
 
Figure 2-1 Login 
Among them: 
 
The project to be opened is the project that is set as the default project in the system 
structure configuration software (for the operation of setting the default project, please
--- pag 11 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
2 
refer to the VFSysBuilder User Manual), and the name of the project is displayed on the 
title bar of the dialog box. 
 
The user is an engineer added in the system structure configuration software (when an 
engineer has logged in to the configuration management software, the last logged in 
user name will be displayed in the user name); if the entered user name does not match 
the password, it will be prompted to log in failure. 
 
The configuration database path is the configuration database path set when the 
VisualField software is installed or in the menu command 
[Start/Programs/VisualField/System Tools/System Global Options]. 
Note: When the multi-item switching function is selected, the login interface is different, as shown 
in the figure below. In the configuration server option, you can select the configuration server of the 
remote node. The login method is the same as that of the local operation node. 
 
Figure 2-2 Login
--- pag 12 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
3 
2.2 Introduction to Interface 
After successfully logging in to the configuration management software, the main interface shown 
in the figure below will be displayed. 
 
Figure 2-3 Interface of VFExplorer 
The configuration management software interface mainly includes the following parts: 
 
Title Bar---displays the name of the software and project. 
 
Menu Bar---includes menus of File, Edit, Debug, View, Help, etc, and each menu 
contains several sub-menu items. 
 
Toolbar---lists frequently used menu function in the form of icon, in order to make it easy 
to use. Click the menu [View/Toolbar] to decide whether to show the bar or not. 
 
Configuration Tree--tree diagram used to display configuration information. 
The function block library/program template library, control configuration, and monitoring 
configuration can be managed in the configuration tree. 
The control configuration contains all control domains, and each control domain contains several 
control stations (the number in front of the control station name indicates the address of the 
corresponding controller). The monitoring configuration includes all operating domains. 
 
Property Bar--displays the basic property of the current selected content.
--- pag 13 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
4 
 
Output Bar---displays output information such as configuration check of control station. 
Click [View/Output Bar] to decide whether to show the bar or not. 
 
Status Bar---displays current operation information and some prompt information. Click 
[View/Status Bar] to decide whether to show the bar or not.

Through the configuration management software, you can manage the system function block 
library, the global function block library, the Phase function block library, and the program template

required. 
 
When exporting industrial library, the authorization of “VFGlobalFB” or 
“FBDPassView” is required.

3.2 Manage Global Function Block 
During field configuration, the same configuration is often used in multiple user programs. In order 
to reduce the workload of field configuration and improve engineering efficiency and engineering 
reusability, frequently used configurations can be extracted as global function blocks. The global 
function block can be used by any control station and operation station in this project, and its use 
method is consistent with the system function block and user function block.
--- pag 26 ---
Config Explorer User Manual M41S55-E 
17 
3.2.1 Technical Index 
 
The global function block library supports 50 function block sub-libraries, and each sub-library 
can support up to 255 global function blocks. Global function block sub-libraries do not allow 
duplicate names. The global function block cannot have the same name as the system 
function block and the user function block. 
 
The number of all parameters of global function block is limited to 512. 
 
The number of aliases is limited to 128. 
 
The global function block can have multiple panels and support up to 256. 
 
The global function block can have multiple symbols and support up to 256. 
 
A single control station can support up to 255 user-defined function block types, including user 
function block and global function block. 
 
Support FBD, St, SFC three types of global function block. 
 
The maximum memory of global function block is 6K. 
 
The multicast data of global function block is limited to 100 bytes, and the redundant data is 
limited to 300 bytes. 
 
The number of global function block panels opened at the same time is 8, which is the same 
as the limit of the number of system panels. 
3.2.2 Structure Illustration 
Global function block can be used in any control station. There are three layers in the global 
function block library 
 
Global function block library 
 
Global function block folder 
The global function block folder can contain multiple global function blocks, which realizes the 
management of global function blocks. 
Support the operation of adding function block, deleting folder and importing function block. 
 
Global function block 
Global function block is composed of parameters, logic, symbols and panels, and supports 
multiple symbols or panels.

7.1 Global Tag Find 
Function "Find Global Tag" can find and locate all tags and variables in all control domains and 
operation domains in current project. 
7.1.1 Illustration for Content and Scope 
When searching for a global tag, the content and scope of the search are: 
 
Content: ECS-700 tags. 
 
Tag name supports“ * ”and “?” Wildcards. “*” can represent multiple characters, and “?” 
represents one character. Wildcards can be used multiple times in a search, such as "A*1*", 
"A?1*", etc. 
 
Scope: Including flowcharts (including dynamic data source expressions), flowchart scripts, 
pop-up flowcharts, background templates, scheduling, point groups, function block alias 
variables, pop-up alarms, and historical trends. 
7.1.2 Find Download logs 
1. As shown in the figure below, enter the tag name in find bar and click “Find Tag” button to 
find the current tag entered.

displayed. 
 
Figure 7-2 Output information of global tag find

Detailed information includes which controller the tag belongs to, which custom program it is 
referenced by and which resource files (graphics, scheduling, etc) it is used in which operation 
domain, etc. Users can open corresponding software by double-clicking listed information. 


If the custom program has been opened, it will be shown as default size, 
and the “Find Tag” will be selected. 


Tag” will be selected. 
 Press F3 to find next tag, select it to view.

screen and the tag graph object will be selected, and the selected graph 
object will be shown in edit area. 
 
If the graphics isn’t opened, it will be opened and the tag graph object will 
be selected, and the selected graph object will be shown in edit area.

If there are several tags with same name, it locates tag by priorities, from 
high to low: Datalink> button> text> other. 
7.2 Refresh 
Users can refresh the project without login again. For example, when partial content of project is 
added or modified by system structure configuration software, or control station or operation 
domain is locked by other engineers, project information can be refreshed with real-time but 
without login again. 
Select menu command [File/ Refresh] or "Refresh Project" button in the tool bar or use shortcut 
key of "F5" to refresh the project.

Configuration and Monitor Guide of 3D 
Section 1 Overview 
At present, with the development of 3D positioning technology, more and more manufacturers 
build 3D factory models for production equipment. Through the 3D images, the virtual 3D factory, 
2D DCS operation screen and physical factory can be combined to quickly and conveniently 
obtain digital factory design information, and improve the safety and intelligence of factory 
operation and maintenance, and polling. 
 
Tip: 
This document mainly introduces the configuration and monitoring method of 3D 
positioning function in VF. For the production of the 3D positioning function, the 
construction of the server and other 3D positioning operations, please refer to the DMS 
materials.

Section 2 Configuration and Monitor 
This section mainly introduces how to complete the 3D positioning data access and 3D positioning 
data related monitoring configuration in the VF system software after completing the connection 
between the 3D positioning server and the VF configuration server. 
2.1 Start 3D Positioning 
Operational Steps 
Before using the 3D positioning function in the VF system software, you need to enable the 3D 
positioning function first. 
1. 
In the VF installation directory, open the configuration file “UserSettings\3D.ini”, the 
default content of the configuration file is shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 2-1 Start 3D positioning 
2. Enable the 3D positioning function, and configure the address and port number of the 
server associated with the 3D positioning function according to the following table. 
Configuration item 
Configuration instructions

 Configuration “ b3DPOS = 1 “, disable 3D function. 
3DServer 
Used to configure the IP address of the 3D function association 
server . 
3DServerPort 
The port number used to configure the communication between the 
3D function association server and the VF configuration server. The 
default is 80 . 
sleepTime

opening the 3D model, the unit is s , and the requirement is not less

Section 2 System Application Overview 
The network device can be compartmentalized to master station and slave station on the basis of 
PROFIBUS-DP specifications. The master station can initiate communication with salve stations. 
The communication module connects standard PROFIBUS-DP slave station device into system. It 
can also connect PA device via link and DP/PA coupler or by means of DP/PA coupler only. Utilize 
SCnet II inter-station communication protocol, in-system control station and operation station can 
realize message both-way communication with other control system and intelligent device, make 
heterogeneity device as subsystem of SUPCON DCS. 
2.1 System Structure 
The structural diagram of the ECS-700 system equipped with PROFIBUS device is shown in 
Figure 2-1. 
 
Figure 2-1 Structural Diagram of Network Equipped with PROFIBUS Device 
 
2.1.1 System component 
As shown in the figure above, this system is consisted of parts below: 
 
Master Controller 
2
--- pag 7 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
Master controller supports PROFIBUS protocol and collect data from PROFIBUS 
communication modules in real time and send them to the data server. 
 
PROFIBUS Communication Module 
As a PROFIBUS-DP master station interface, which serves to connect standard 
PROFIBUS-DP slave station device to the DCS system and it can also connect to 
PROFIBUS-PA by Siemens couplers and linkers. 
 
PROFIBUS Device 
It refers to devices supporting PROFIBUS protocol in the field by which the system can 
collect the on-site data and execute production and control. 
 
 
It refers to devices supporting PROFIBUS protocol in the field by which the system can 
collect the on-site data and execute production and control. 
 
Different DCS systems require different types of PRODIBUS communication module and 
configuration software: 
 
ECS-700 system's PROFIBUS communication module is COM722-S and the 
complementary software is VisualField (V3.2 and above). 
 
ECS-100/JX-300XP system's PROFIBUS communication module is XP239-DP\ 
FW239-DP, and the complementary is AdvanTrol-Pro (V2.80 and above). 
 
GCS-G5 system's PROFIBUS communication module is COM522-S and the 
complementary software is GCSContrix (V1.10 and above). 
 
2.1.2 Introduction of Redundant Modes 
The PROFIBUS states the two modes of slave redundancy: System Redundant Mode (SR) and 
Fast Redundant Mode (FR), while the master redundancy and its operation is not stated, as shown 
in following figure. 
 
Figure 2-2 Diagram for PROFIBUS Redundant Modes 
3
--- pag 8 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
The difference between them is the redundancy. 
 
For FR structure, as the bus is not redundant, the masters and slaves can be redundant 
separately or together, and the structure can be redundant master connecting with 
non-redundant slave, non-redundant master connecting with redundant slave, or 
redundant master connecting with redundant slave. 
 
For SR structure, both the masters and slaves need to be redundant.

5.2.2 Programming for Communication 
When using CP342-5 to connect PROFIBUS-DP, CP342-5 uses 16 bytes address area to 
exchange data with CPU. The address of 16 bytes hardware address is distributed to CP342-5 by 
CPU, which is the buffer memory for data exchange between CPU and CP342-5. CPU uses this 
hardware address to access CP342-5 module. There is another independent data storage area 
used for data exchange between CP342-5 and PROFIBUS node. The input area and output area 
are 2160 bytes respectively. When CP342-5 is used as DP slave, there can be max. 240 bytes 
input data and 240 bytes output data. 
When using DP communication port of CP342-5 module to communicate, it can not use 
Load/Transfer command (sentence table programming), Mov command (ladder diagram 
programming) to directly access I/O data of DP slave. Using CP342-5 to carry out PROFIBUS 
communication has two steps: 1. CPU transmits data to the data register of CP communication 
card; 2. Write data stored in data register of CP342-5 to the Output data area of PROFIBUS slave 
(the opposite process is CPU reading Input data from slave). The communication process 
between CP342-5 and the Input/Output data area is automatic, but function area FC1 (“SEND”) 
and FC2 (“RECV”) is transferred manually to finish the data exchange between CP342-5 and 
CPU. 
1. FC1 and FC2 parameter 
“SEND” parameter of DP_SEND(FC1) function area is a data area needs to be defined. 
This data area is the data source sent to COM722-S by CPU. "RECV" parameter 
definition of DP_RECV(FC2) function area is used to store the data sent by COM722-S 
in some data address area of CPU. 
“SEND” and “RECV” parameter requires filling of a needle type data, e.g. 
"P#DB1.DBX3.0 BYTE 37", its meanings are: 1. As for the “Send” parameter of sending 
function area, it means sending the data in data block DB1 from the 0 bit of the 3rd bytes 
and of 37 bytes long to CP342-5 module; 2. As for “RECV” parameter of “DP_RECV” 
receiving function area, it means storing the data received by CP342-5 in data block 
DB1 from the 0 bit of the 3rnd bytes in a data area of 37 bytes long. Although needle 
type parameter allows other data type defined length (byte type and bit type etc.), e.g. 
P#DB1.DBX3.0 WORD 37. "SEND" and "RECV" parameter of "DP_SEND" and 
"DP_RECV" must be needle type defined by byte, i.e. "P#DB1.DBX3.0 BYTE 37". 
64
--- pag 69 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
 
Figure 5-22 Fill parameter of "SEND" and "RECV" 
2. Fill the return value of FC1 and FC2 
“DP_SEND” function area include "DONE", "ERROR" and "STATUS" three parameters 
used to indicate the data transmission status and result. "DP_RECV" function area has 
"NDR", "ERROR", "STATUS" and "DPSTATUS" four parameters used to indicate the 
data transmission status and result. You can define corresponding data address area for 
storing these return values, analyzing them and evaluate the data exchange status of 
CPU and CP342-5. The return data is stored in M address area as shown in Figure 5-23. 
 
Figure 5-23 Store the output return value of the function area in M zone. 
As for these two function areas, when Error= False, STATUS=0, DONE=True and 
NDR=True, it means the data exchange between CPU and cp342-5 succeeds.

When one bus segment of PROFIBUS-DP excesses the distances in the above table, use RS-485 
repeater to expand the bus segment. One PROFIBUS-DP network can at most use 4 RS-485 
repeaters. 
We can select Siemens products for RS-485 repeater with order No. of 6ES7 972-0AA01-0XA0 (or 
the updated version). 
When it is longer than the length of Table 6-1 or in environment with much electromagnetic 
interference, we can extend the PROFIBUS-DP bus segment by optical fiber cable. When using 
optical fiber to connect PROFIBUS-DP, optical link module is necessary. The system structure is 
shown in Figure 6-2. 
We can select Siemens products for optical link module. The OLM with one –route optical fiber 
interface is model OLM/G11, OLM two–route optical fiber interface is model OLM/G12. (User can 
71
--- pag 76 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
contact the local Siemens supplier for latest product model and details.) 
 
Figure 6-2 Use Optical Fiber to Connect PROFIBUS-DP 
Shielding and Grounding 
When connecting PROFIBUS-DP bus, it must strictly guarantee shielding and grounding. If 
possible, it is recommended that all devices have equipotential design; otherwise we will specify 
single-point grounding at the PROFIBUS Master Communication Module (Interface Module). 
Single-point grounding must ensure that there is no connection to the earth with any part of bus 
cable beyond PROFIBUS Master Communication Module. 
When the repeater carries out bus expansion during practical application, the single-point 
grounding of the expanded bus segment is as close as the repeater of PROFIBUS Master 
Communication Module. 
6.3 PROFIBUS-PA Bus Topology Structure 
Tree Topology (Paw Shape) 
Tree topology comprises of the single independent fieldbus that connected with the public junction 
box. This topology can be applied to terminal of the main cable. If the devices on the same bus 
segment are mutually separated but they are still within the junction box area, this topology is 
feasible. When adopting this topology, it is necessary to consider the maximum length of the spur, 
which will be discussed later. The tree topology structure is as in Figure 6-3. 
72
--- pag 77 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
 
Figure 6-3 Tree Topology Structure of PA Bus (Paw Shape) 
When applying tree topology structure, please select corresponding junction box as per quantity of 
spur. 
The tree topology structure is applied to the following conditions: 
 
Reconstruction project 
 
Special rear with high density of field devices 
Spur Topology 
The fieldbus device connects with the multi-station bus segment with one cable with spur, forming 
the topology. Technically, this topology is feasible but is not economic solution. 
For first installation, and in low-density of field devices, it should adopt bus topology with spur. 
 
Figure 6-4 Multi-Station Spur Topology Structure of PA Bus 
73
--- pag 78 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
Mixed Topology 
Combined topology comprises of tree and multi-station topologies. This topology can combine the 
advantages of the two topologies and overcome their limitations respectively. 
 
Figure 6-5 Combined Topology Structure of PA Bus 
6.4 PROFIBUS-PA Device Connect 
PROFIBUS-PA uses PROFIBUS-DP extended protocol, so PROFIBUS-DP master interface 
module can connect PROFIBUS-PA device to SUPCON DCS. 
PROFIBUS-DP master interface module connects PROFIBUS-PA device by using connecter and 
DP/PA coupler or by using DP/PA coupler singly. Link work as a DP slave and dispatch PA device, 
DP/PA coupler is used to transform type of physical signal and supply power for PA bus. 
In application, according to following principle to specify the DP link (like IM157) number extended 
by one DP system, and specify the DP/PA coupler extended by one linker 
There are following principle to configure PA device, taking IM157 as example. 
Basic Principle 
The configuration principles of using connecter and DP/PA coupler are: 
 
In upper-layer DP system, link is used as DP slave station and gateway connected to 
under-layer bus system (i.e. PA field devices). 
 
Maximum of PA salve stations supported by link is 61, and maximum of slots is 236-PA 
slave stations. 
 
Maximum of DP/PA couplers connected to one IM157 is 5. 
 
Generally, one intrinsically non-safety DP/PA coupler supports 8~9 PA instruments, one 
intrinsically safety DP/PA coupler supports 3~4 PA instruments. Please connect after 
understand PA instrument and user requirements. 
 
PA system supply current can be increased by added coupler. 
74
--- pag 79 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
 
Maximum configure data, maximum parameter data, and maximum I/O data supported 
by every IM157 is 240 bytes. 
The configure principles of using DP/PA coupler are: 
 
PA instruments only can be connected when the baud rate of bus is 45.45bps. 
 
PROFIBUS-DP does not need high speed, and all DP devices support baudrate of 
45.45Kbps. 
 
The count of all DP slave stations and PA instruments is less than 123, and the count is 
less than 64 in ECS-700 system. 
 
Generally, one intrinsically non-safety DP/PA coupler supports 8~9 PA instruments, one 
intrinsically safety DP/PA coupler supports 3~4 PA instruments. Please connect after 
understand PA instrument and user requirements. 
 
PA system supply current can be increased by added coupler. 
Spare Parts Principle 
The principle is to provide capacity for further expansion. 
 
25% spare capacity is designed or a control loop is reserved for a transmitter or a valve. 
 
The spare capacity should consider the bus energy drive capability, full load cable 
voltage and corresponding cable length etc. 
Voltage Drop Principle of Bus Section 
The working voltage of field instruments of PROFIBUS-PA is within the scope of (9-32) V DC. 
Therefore, to control voltage drop is to ensure all field instruments could get at least 9V DC 
working voltage. 
The output voltage of the distribution ware affects the allowable voltage drop of the bus section. 
For example, if the output voltage is 24V DC, the allowable voltage drop is 15V; if the output 
voltage is 17V DC, the allowable voltage drop is 8V. The output voltage of the DP/PA Coupler used 
is 24V. 
The resistance of field bus A-type cable is 44Ω/km. 
The consuming current of the registered PA field instruments is within scope of (13-30) mA. When 
the branch has short circuit, the current in the branch is (40~60) mA (the short circuit protection 
device has clear stipulation of this index. The sum of the consuming current of all field instruments 
plus the supplementary current of at least one branch is the maximum working current of network 
section. 
6ES7 157-0AD82-0XA0 (Ex[i]), Ex intrinsically safe DP/PA Coupler. 
6ES7 157 0AC83-0XA0, Ex non-intrinsically safe DP/PA Coupler. 
The maximum working current of the bus section × cable resistance = the maximum voltage drop 
of the bus section. 
75
--- pag 80 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
The maximum voltage drop of the bus section should be less than the allowable voltage drop. 
 
Figure 6-6 PROFIBUS-PA configuration and power supply 
Max. cable length, connecting cable 
If there is no repeater installed, the allowable total bus length is 1900m. 
The bus section consists of trunk and branch. Trunk is the longest cable route by which the 
equipments connected to the bus section, and branch means other cable channel connected. The 
total length of the network section equals to the sum of the length of the trunk line and that of all 
branch lines. The maximum length of each branch is shown in the following table:

Shielding and Earthing 
To acquire good electromagnetic compatibility, shield of connection lines of system is very 
important. This kind of shield provides a strong electric protective shell. As for the site bus, the 
ideal condition is to connect the cable shield layer to the shell (which is usually made of metal) of 
site equipment. Because the shells are usually connected to the earth or protective lead, the bus 
cable shield equals to several times several points (several instruments) earthing. This method 
provides optimal electromagnetic compatibility and protects personal safety (shown in Figure 6-7). 
It can be used in the system requiring realizing optimal equal electric potential earthing. 
76
--- pag 81 ---
DPCon User Manual IM41S94-E 
 
Figure 6-7 Earthed of cable shielded layers and shells of instruments 
When the system can not have equal electric potential earthing, if unfavorable condition causes 
current generated in the shielded layer, the frequency compensation current between two earthing 
points will damage cable. To avoid the system without equal electric potential shield earthing 
generating low frequency compensation current, it is recommended to one end of the cable 
earthing and capacity ground of other earthing points. A feasible solution is shown in Figure 6-8, 
but it can not provide electric protection to the most extent. 
 
Figure 6-8 One end of shielded cable earthing and capacity ground of other earthing points

Diagnosis Software User Manual 
Section 1 Function Feature 
System Status Diagnosis is a significant function of the VisualField System Software, and is an 
important tool for system debugging and status analysis. System status diagnosis mainly consists 
of 2 parts: real-time status supervision and history record query. The main objects of real-time 
status supervision include the running status and communication situation of system components 
such as operation domain, control domain, process control domain, control station, controller, 
communication node, I/O module, etc. History record query can check the faults which occur in the 
control station during a certain time, and display their information including occurring moment, 
device, address, diagnosis result and recovery time, etc.
--- pag 6 ---
Diagnosis Software User Manual IM41S74-E 
2 
Section 2 Introduction to View 
Select “System Status” command in toolbar of real-time monitoring software and the main view of 
the system status diagnosis will be displayed, as shown in Figure 2-1. The history records of 
system network structure, control station, operation station, controller, process control network, 
communication node, I/O module status as well as the whole system status can be observed in 
each view of system status diagnosis. 
As the figure below, ECS-700 control system uses the network of SCnetIIIA and SCnetIIIB to 
communicate with operation domain. Thus, network line mark and network topology in the figure 
only display the network of SCnetIIIA and SCnetIIIB. 
 
Figure 2-1 Main View of the System Status 
System diagnosis software supports to diagnose the network in project configuration, ECS-700 
system and various node devices subordinated to the system and operation domain.
--- pag 7 ---
Diagnosis Software User Manual IM41S74-E 
3 
2.1 View Description 
 
Network Structure view (main view of the system status) 
User can check the whole operation status and the communication among all system 
nodes connected to current operation domain. 
 
Control Station view 
User can check the information of each node (cabinet) about the power supply, fan, 
temperature and the like within the control station. 
 
Controller view 
User can check the information of running status, hardware, configuration, 
communication, version, statistics, time record and local I/O connection module. 
 
Process Control Network view 
User can check the diagnosis data of controller network port, hardware address and 
protocol address of the controller, protocol address of the network time synchronization 
server, network connection status, network node overloaded alarming, and IP node 
conflict alarm. 
 
Communication Node view 
User can check devices type, request communication, configuration status, startup 
status, redundancy configuration, work status, power supply status, L-BUS 
communication status, E-BUS communication status. 
 
IO module view 
User can check the work status of IO modules, level of module faults, module auxiliary 
power supply, Module link check, module address check, module bus communication 
status, module type consistency check, module configuration consistency check, and 
channel status. 
 
Operator Station (Engineer Station) view 
User can check types, currently running configuration information, computer operation 
information of the operator station (engineer station). 
 
History view 
User can check the history record of system status, shown as figure below.

Section 3 System Status 
Automatic self-diagnose function exists in processes from signal channel to I/O module, from I/O 
module to controller, and from control station to operator station (engineer station). Diagnosis 
results can be displayed by LED lights on the hardware module. Also, these diagnosis results will 
be transmitted to the operator station (engineer station) immediately to be alarmed, displayed and 
recorded, in order to assist user in finding and solving the system problems as soon as possible. 
The control system mainly consists of various types of I/O module, I/O link module, process 
control network, main controller, operator station (engineer station), and sever. The following parts

Section 4 System Diagnosis Tags Provided by OPC 
VF supports OPC communication. VFOPCSvr, VF internal installed OPC server, supports 
transmitting tag and domain variables to OPC client. And VFOPCSvr supports cross-domain 
referred, that is, the referred tags also can be transmitted to OPC client. 
Besides the analogy input, analogy output, digital input and digital output, VFOPCSvr also can 
provide the system diagnosis tags. 
 
Attention: 
System diagnosis tags do not support cross-domain referred. 
 
4.1 Enable System Diagnosis Tag 
Before OPC sever transmitted, system diagnosis tags should be enabled manually by following 
steps: 
1) In VF installed path, for example "C:\VisualField4\", double click the configuration file 
"OPCConfig.ini". 
2) Modify the item value of "SYSOPENENABLE" as 1, as shown as figure below, save 
and close the file.

3) Right click the icon 
 in system tray and select the command "Exit", and reconnect 
OPC client with VFOPCSvr. Or restart VFOPCSvr by double click VFOPCSvr.exe in 
VF install path(for example C:\VisualField\).

4.3 Diagnosis Tag Type 
VFOPCSvr can connect with multiple OPC client programs at the same time, and each connection 
can exchange multiple dynamic data (tags) at the same time. 
VFOPCSvr supports the transfer of diagnostic data of controllers, operating 
stations, IO connection modules and IO modules.

address + station address + attribute name". For example, " _CS_017_002.SCNETA ", 
where: _CS means the tag is the controller diagnostic tag, 017 means 
the 17th domain, 002 means the No. 2 control station, and SCNETA means the control A network

4.3.2 Communication Module’s Diagnosis Tags 
In the VF system, the diagnostic tag of the communication module uses the format "diagnostic 
name + domain address + station address + communication module address + attribute name", 
such as " _CM_017_002_000.WORK ", where: _CM indicates that the tag is a communication 
module The diagnostic tag, 017 indicates the 17th domain, 002 indicates the No. 2 control 
station, 000 indicates the communication module address, and WORK indicates the working 
status of the module.

Electronic Signature Management 
Section 1 Introduction 
Through the electronic signature in VisualField, you can manage the permission of users during 
the software operation. The permission management includes operation permission and 
verification permission. Through electronic signatures, the VF system can record important 
operations. 
1.1 Main Features 
The electronic signature function of VF system software mainly includes: 
 
Operation signature 
Operation signature, that is, the operator needs to perform electronic signature 
verification during the tag operation. 
 
Operation and verification signature 
Operation and verification of signatures, that is, operators and verification users are 
required to perform electronic signature verification separately during tag operation. 
1.2 Configuration and Execution Procedure 
When the electronic signature is applied in the VF system, you can configure the electronic 
signature according to the following process and apply the electronic signature in monitoring. 
 
Figure 1-1 Electronic signature flowchart
--- pag 5 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
2 
 
 
Tip: 
Only when the software dongle with electronic signature permission is obtained, can you 
configure and apply the electronic signature above.
--- pag 6 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
3 
Section 2 Configuration 
The configuration of the electronic signature is generally divided into two parts, one is to enable 
the electronic signature, and the other is to enable the user’s electronic signature. 
2.1 Enable Electronic Signature in VxSysBuilder 
In the VFExplorer, you can configure the enabling status of electronic signatures according to the 
alarm level, the type of signature required for batch processing of the configuration status table, 
the type of signature required for batch acknowledgment of the current page of the configuration 
process alarm, and the predefined information. 
Through the following operations, the attribute configuration of the electronic signature in the 
system structure can be completed. 
1) Click "Global Default Configuration> Security Settings> Electronic Signature", the 
electronic signature configuration page shown in the figure below will be displayed in the 
configuration property bar on the right. It contains three tabs, namely "Tag Operation", 
"Other Operations", and "Predefined Remarks". Detailed electronic signature 
permissions can be configured on these three tabs. 
 
Figure 2-1 Electronic signature example 
 
2) Tag operation 
In the "Tag Operation" tab, you can configure the operation of different levels of tag 
number, alarm confirmation electronic signature authority configuration. According to the 
following table, you can configure the electronic signature authority for tag operation.
--- pag 7 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
4 
 
Configuration 
Item 
Configuration Description 
Option Description 
Tag level 
It lists the tag level. 
It is unnecessary to configure. 
Operation signature, that is, the operator needs to perform 
electronic signature verification during the tag operation 
Operation and verification of signatures, that is, operators 
and verification users are required to perform electronic 
signature verification separately during tag operation. 
Type 
It is used to specify the 
operation authority of different 
levels of tags. Including three 
options: operation signature, 
operation and verification 
signature, no signature. 
No signature, that is, no electronic signature verification is 
required for tag operation. 
If checked, it means that the same electronic signature 
authority as "Type" is required for the alarm confirmation. 
ACK 
It is used to configure the 
electronic signature authority 
of the tag alarm confirmation 
operation. 
If it is not checked, it means that no electronic signature 
authority is required for alarm confirmation. 
 
3) Other operations 
The electronic signature also supports permission management for the "process alarm 
confirmation current list" and "status table batch processing" operations in real-time 
monitoring. 
In the "Other Operations" tab shown in the figure below, you can configure the electronic 
signature permissions for "Process Alarm Confirm Current List" and "Status Table Batch 
Processing". 
 
Figure 2-2 “Other operation” tab in electronic signature 
Configurable operations are listed in the "Function" column, and the electronic signature 
requirements corresponding to "Function" are selected in "Type". 
 
Select "None", the operation in "Function" does not require electronic signature 
verification. 
 
Select "Operation Signature", then the operation in "Function" requires the 
operator's electronic signature verification. 
 
Select “Operation and Verification Signature”, then the operation in “Function” 
requires the electronic signature verification of the operator and verifier. 
4) Predefined remarks 
In the monitoring operation, the bit log operation and other operations need to be written 
into the operation log. Pre-defined comments refer to the contents that can be written to 
the operation log when the operation signature is verified. 
In the "Predefined Comments" tab shown in the figure below, you can pre-define the
--- pag 8 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
5 
comment information for the electronic signature operation. 
 
Figure 2-3 “Predefined remarks” of electronic signature 
Enter the remark information into “Predefined remarks”. 
2.2 Configure User’s Signature Permission in VFExplorer 
When the tag meets the following conditions, the monitoring user needs to have the "electronic 
signature operation" or "electronic signature verification" authority. 
 
In the VFExplorer, "operation signature" or "operation and verification signature" 
corresponding to the tag is enabled. 
 
In the VFLaunch, you can execute writing value or alarm acknowledgment operations on 
tags. 
 
 
Attention: 
The electronic signature dongle permission is required to authorize “Electronic signature 
operation” and “Electronic signature verification”. If there is no authorization, you cannot 
adopt the electronic signature and verification to execute the double check. 
 
Through the following operations, you can complete the user's electronic signature authority 
configuration. 
1) Open the VFLaunch. 
2) Select the "Monitoring Operation Authority" tab, which contains the authority 
configuration items of the electronic signature, as shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 2-4Electronic signature permission 
3) Configure the operation authority and verification authority of the electronic signature. 
 
Configure user's electronic signature operation authority
--- pag 9 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
6 
After checking the "Electronic Signature Operation", the "Electronic Signature" 
dialog box will pop up in the real-time monitoring software to perform tag operation, 
alarm acknowledgment and other operations. Only after the user's electronic 
signature information is entered in the "Operation Verification" in the "Electronic 
Signature" dialog box can the tag operation be successful. 
 
Configure user's electronic signature verification authority 
After "Electronic signature verification" is checked, signature verification is required 
when performing tag operations, alarm acknowledgment and other operations in the 
real-time monitoring software.
--- pag 10 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
7 
Section 3 How to Use Electronic Signature in 
VFLaunch 
When the electronic signature function is enabled in the VF system project, and a user who 
performs an electronic signature operation is created, the user can apply the electronic signature 
after logging in to theVFLaunch. 
In the following cases, an electronic signature needs to be applied to complete the operation. 
 
Write value operation to the specified tag 
 
Acknowledge the alarm of the designated tag level 
 
Batch acknowledgment of process alarms 
 
Batch processing the status table 
For operations such as tag writing or alarm acknowledgment, according to the settings of the 
"Electronic Signature" sub-node under the "Security Settings" of the system configuration software, 
an electronic signature dialog box will pop up requesting a second confirmation. 
Please confirm and verify the electronic signature according to the following description: 
 
Acknowledgement of electronic signature operation: in the dialog box that pops up after 
performing operations such as tag writing or alarm confirmation, select the 
corresponding predefined comment item according to the operation, enter the user and 
password, and click OK to complete the operation. Electronic signature confirmation. As 
shown in Figure 2-4.
--- pag 11 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
8 
 
Figure 3-1 Operation permission of electronic signature 
 
Electronic signature verification confirmation: After the operator confirms it, the left 
interface of the dialog box turns gray, and the verifier performs the verification 
confirmation operation on the right interface. As shown in Figure 3-2. Select the 
corresponding predefined remark item according to the operation, enter the user and 
password, and click Confirm to complete the electronic signature verification 
confirmation of the operation.
--- pag 12 ---
Electronic Signature Management User Manual IM41S47-E 
9

Export Tool 
1 
Export Tool 
Section 1 Overview 
VFExport is one component of VisualField software package, and it exports the required 
information automatically by reading the configuration archive information, which facilitates the 
engineering application. 
VFExport exports information in the unit of control station, including "Cabinet Layout", "Terminal 
Board Wiring Diagram" and "Tag List". "Cabinet Layout" indicates the cabinet number in the 
system and the module layout in each cabinet;” Terminal Board Wiring Diagram " indicates the 
terminal wiring of each module; "Tag List" indicates the statistic data of the tags used by system. 
All the information can not only facilitate engineers, but also be submitted to users as the delivery 
information. 
 
Tip: 
This tool can only be applied in configuration server. 
 
1.1 Technical Specification 
 
The maximum cabinet number exported by "Cabinet Layout": 32 
 
The maximum module number exported by " Terminal Board Wiring Diagram": 512 
 
The maximum tag number exported by "Tag List": 2000 
 
Time of exporting all the information of single station: ≤ 4min 
1.2 Configuration Criterion 
The hardware configuration should conform to the following criterion before exporting "Cabinet 
Layout", “Terminal Board Wiring Diagram " and "Tag List". 
The actual address of the rack should be written in the rack remark in hardware configuration 
software, shown as follows. 
The remark format of the rack: "SC cabinet number-rack number: actual remark ", Such as"SC0-0: 
No.0 cabinet No.0 rack".

Global Function Block Configure Guide 
 
Tip: 
When using this manual, if need to check detailed operation steps, refer to VFSTModule User 
Manual. 
Section 1 Overview 
Global function block is the kind of block that can be created, edit and delete. The kind of the 
global function block is the unique, and the global function block can be used in any control station 
and operation station in the same local project, and the usual of the global function block is same 
to the usual of the system function block and user-defined function block. 
In real application, the same configuration may be used in numerous programming. The common 
configuration can be edited as the global function block, which can be re-used to reduce the 
configuration load and improve configure efficient and configuration reuse. 
1.1 Main Feature 
 
Support applied in the all control station, and modified after applied. 
 
Support three types of programming languages FBD, ST and SFC. 
 
Support user-defined panel for the global function block. 
 
Support user-defined symbol for the global function block. 
 
Support user-defined panel for the global function block. 
 
Support using STModule, and support user-defining parameters and logical. 
 
Support configured for monitoring and alarm rule. 
 
Support online publish 
When adding (adding incrementally import method), modifying (apart from alarm property) 
and deleting global function blocks, only online publish is necessary. 
 
Support offline publish 
When the alarm properties in the global function block are changed, or users import 
global function blocks in a overwriting way, the offline publish is necessary. 
1.2 Technical Specifications 
 
Global function block supports 50 function block sub-libraries, and each can support 255
--- pag 5 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
2 
global function blocks. The names of global function blocks sub-library cannot repeat. 
The names of global function blocks cannot repeat, and cannot be the same as the 
names of system function blocks and custom function blocks. 
 
The limit No. of all global function block parameters is 512. 
 
The alias No. limit is 128. 
 
Global function block can have several panels, the maximum is 256. 
 
Global function block can have several symbols, the maximum is 256. 
 
A single CS can support 255 custom function block types, including custom function 
block and global function block. 
 
It supports 3 types of global function blocks FBD, ST and SFC. 
 
The maximum memory of global function block is 6K. 
 
The global function block multicast data limit is 100 bytes, and the redundant data bytes 
limit is 300 bytes. 
 
The No. of global function block panels open in supervision simultaneously is 8, the 
same as system panel No. limit.
--- pag 6 ---

Section 3 Create Global Function Block 
Configure tree in VFExplorer has the item of "Global Function Block Library", below which global 
function block sub-library can be created, and below sub-library global function block can be 
created. Global function block is constructed by parameter, logic, panel and symbol. After created 
global function block, the new global function block should be synchronized in control station to 
make sure that the new global function block can be applied in programming. 
3.1 Create Global Function Block Sub-library 
Global function block supports 50 function block sub-libraries, and every sub-library can be used 
as system function library in FBD programming. 
By following steps, the global function block sub-library can be created: 
1) Open the VF configure explorer software (VFExplorer). 
2) Right-click "Global Function Block Library" in configure tree, and select “New Function 
Block Library” to popup the dialog box "New Custom Function Block Library". 
3) Input "Name" and "Description" in the following dialog box, and click "OK" to finish the 
creation of global function block sub-library. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-1 Dialog box of "New Custom Function Block Library" 
 
"Name" should be the combination of English letter, Chinese letter, number and "_", 
and the maximum of the “Name” is 16 characters. 
 
"Description" should be the combination of English letter, Chinese letter, number 
and "_", and the maximum of the “Name” is 64 characters. 
The new global function block library will be show under "Global Function Block" show as 
following figure.
--- pag 8 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
2 
 
 
Figure 3-2 Example of New Global Function Block Sub-library 
3.2 Create Function Block 
Every global function block sub-library supports 255 global function blocks, and every global 
function block can be used in each control station of one project. 
 
Tip: 
Creating a new global function block can be enabled only with dongle authority, while 
operations like edit, view and import can be performed without the dongle authority. 
By following steps, global function block can be created. 
1) Right-click one global function block sub-library, select “New” in right-click menu to popup 
"New Function Block" dialog box shown as below. 
2) Input "Name" and "Description" of the global function block, and select its type in the 
dialog box shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-3 New global function block dialog box 
 
“Name” contains at most 16 characters including letters, numbers or "_", and "G_" is 
the defalut beginning of the name. 
 
“Type” can choose from “FBD”, “ST” or “SFC”. 
 
“Description” contains at most 64 capital letters, numbers, Chinese character or "_". 
The new global function block will be added below the global function block sub-library, and the 
configure item of the global function block, including "Parameter" and "Logic", displayed at the 
right area shown as below.
--- pag 9 ---

3.3 Configure Logic of Global Function Block 
Global function block supports 3 programming language including FBD, ST and SFC. For detail of 
the programming instruction, refer to VFSTModule User Manual. 
Global function block should be configured with one input pin and one output pin. 
3.3.1 Create Logic in FBD Programming Language 
By following steps, logic of global function block in FBD programming language can be created. 
1) Select "FBD" in "Type" of "New Function Block" dialog box as shown in Figure 3-1. 
2) Select "Edit" in the right menu of global function block property "Logic", or double click 
"Logic" to enter in the programming interface of the VFSTModule software. 
3) By the command "Add" in the right menu of "Input Parameter", new input parameter can 
be added, as shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-6 Right Menu of Input Parameter 
4) By the same operation, add all the parameters for the global function block. 
5) Select function blocks from the frame of "Function" in the right area, and construct the 
logic for the global function block. For detail of the function block programming, refer to 
VFFBDBuilder User Manual. 
6) Compile and view the compile result in the "Output Window", which is at the bottom of the 
interface and is shown as the below figure.
--- pag 11 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
5 
 
Figure 3-7 Succeed to Create Global Function Block (FBD Type) 
7) Save and exit from the programming interface, return to the VFExplorer software. 
8) In VFExplorer software, Select the edited global function block and select the command 
of "Save to Configuration Server" in its right menu. 
9) Select the control station used the global function block, and select the command of 
"Synchronize Function Block Library". 
The name of the applied function block should not be repeated to other applied function block, the 
parameter name and system retain field in the FBD global function block. The name of the applied 
function block in the FBD global function block should be less than 24 characters, only can be 
consisted of letters and numbers and started with letter. 
By following method, the pin of internal function block can be used as external pin of FBD global 
function block: 
 
Connect the output pin of the internal function block with the output parameter, as shown 
as Figure 3-7. 
 
Set one parameter of the internal function block as the relevant parameter of the input 
parameter for the global function block, as shown as below figure.
--- pag 12 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
6 
 
 
 
Figure 3-8 Set Relevant for the Global function Block Pin with Internal Function Block Pin 
By relevant parameter, parameters in the internal function block can be related to the parameters 
in global function block. The parameters set as the relevant parameters should be in the same 
type, and the format of the relevant parameters is "function block instance name. parameter name 
of function block". 
Before set relevant parameter, FBD should be instanced.

By following steps, the global function block in ST programming language can be created. 
1) Select the "Type" as "ST" while creating global function block, as shown as below.

3) By the command "Add" in the right menu of "Input Parameter", new input parameter can 
be added, as shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-10 Right Menu of Input Parameter 
4) By the same operation, add all the parameters for the global function block. 
5) Program with ST programming language in the right area. For detail of ST programming, 
refer to VFSTModule User Manual.

1) Select "SFC" in "Type" of "New Function Block" as shown in Figure 3-1.

be added, as shown as below.

Program in the right area to construct the logic in SFC programming language. For detail

Compile and view the compile result in the "Output Window", which is at the bottom of



 
Save the new global function block to the configuration server. 
 
Select the control station used the global function block, and select the command 
"Synchronize Function Block Library". 
3.4 Configure Parameters of Global Function Block 
Refer to VFSTModule User Manual, to get the parameter configuration detail of global function 
block.
--- pag 15 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E

3.4.1 Parameter Overview 
Parameters of global function block can be created and edited in VFSTModule software, and 
before configuring program of global function block, whose parameters should be configured. 
Parameter names of global function block should not be repeated, and should not be repeated to 
the system retain field. Parameter name of global function block should be defined by the name

Custom function block do not support using global function block, and applying tags of global 
function block by adding as reference variable. 
Global function block do not support debugging online, and it will be triggered by custom program.

10 characters, and only supports 
letter, number and "_". Marco name 
should not be repeated to the existed 
parameter and keyword. 
- 
 
 
Tip: 
 
SFC global function blocks do not support array type parameters. 
 
Support two dimension settings on array parameters, and each dimension supports 
maximum 32, settings of dimension 1 and dimension 2 must exceed or be equal to 2. 
 
3.4.2 Set Parameter Rule 
Users can set parameter rule to define the limit and relation between parameters of global function 
blocks. The rule can be set for multicast data. Only global function block contains the function of 
rule setting. 
1) Select “Parameter”, right-click and select “Parameter Rule Settings” to open the 
“Parameter Rule Settings” dialog.

2) Select the parameter name in the pull-down menu. Parameter names can not repeat, or a 
prompt will pop up. 
3) Select parameters for “Maximum Parameter”, “Minimum Parameter” and “Unit 
Parameter”. Maximum parameter and minimum parameter must be configuration 
parameters. Unit parameter can only be configured in configuration parameter. Select 
EUNIT for the configuration parameter to be set. 
4) Repeat step 2 and step 3 to complete the configuration of all parameter rules. 
5) Click “OK” to complete the operation. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-14 Parameter Rule Settings Dialog 
 
3.5 Configure Alarm of Global Function Block 
The global function block supports self-defined alarms, and the maximum self-defined alarms 
supported by global function block is 20. 
3.5.1 Self-defined Alarm 
In VFSTModule software, click "Program/ Self-defined Alarm" in menu bar to pop up the dialog 
below, in which can add self-defined alarm type for global function block.
--- pag 18 ---

Name, description and alarm priority can be set in the figure above. Name of new alarm cannot 
repeat with system alarm or existed custom alarm in this global function block. 
After setting the self-defined alarm type, user can view and select the self-defined alarm in alarm 
parameter settings. Its features are same with system alarm. 
Please publish and compile after creating or modifying the self-defined alarm to validate it. 
 
Tips: 
New self-defined alarm is in level “Low” in default. 
 
3.5.2 Set Alarm 
Users can use the alarm parameter in supervision by setting alarm. 
1) Select the “ENALM” in “Parameter”, right-click and select “Alarm Settings” to open the 
“Alarm Settings” dialog. Right-click “Parameter” or select the “FLAG” in the “Supervision 
Parameter” of global function block can also perform the alarm settings. 
2) Select the alarm name in the pull-down menu of “Name” in the “Alarm Settings” dialog, 
including the custom alarm, and the “Description”, “Type” and “Show Alarm Enable” will 
be shown automatically. The alarm cannot repeat in the alarm settings dialog, which 
means the same character strings are not allowed for names. 
3) Select the alarm type in “Show Alarm Enable”. The selected parameter will be shown in
--- pag 19 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
13 
the alarm parameter settings of properties settings when invoking the global function 
block. 
4) Select the parameters of alarm in drop-down menu of “Associated Parameter”. 
Note: parameters in the drop-down menu are multicast, the settings are shown in 
VFSTModule User Manual. 
5) Repeat step 1 and step 2 to finish the settings of all alarm parameters. 
6) Click “OK” to complete the operation. 
 
Figure 3-16 Alarm Settings Dialog 
In the figure above, the 0~2 bits of FLAG refer to the three states of function block, AEH, AEL and 
ALM, 3~31 bits have no meanings. If users name it as G_A when invoking the global function 
block, the state information AEH/AEL/ALM will be generated when some values of the 0~2 bits of 
FLAG are 1 in using the global function block. As shown in the figure above, during the logic 
configuration process of G_A , if only AEH and ALH are enabled, then when you are setting its 
property, only AEH and ALM’s alarm are displayed. If AEH and ALM are set as alarm enabled 
(combo is checked), when the value of FLAG’s 0/2 bit is 1, AEH or ALM is generated.
--- pag 20 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
14 
 
Figure 3-17 Alarm Settings Example 
As shown in Figure 3-17, at this time, the 0th to 2nd bits of the FLAG parameter represent the 
three states of the function block, respectively: AEH, AL, ALM. The global function block is called 
in the user program, and it is assumed to be G_A, and the corresponding status information 
AEH/AEL/ALM are generated when the value of several bits in the 0 to 2 digits of the FLAG 
parameter of the global function block is 1. 
As shown in the figure above, in the global function block G_A logic configuration, only AEH and 
ALM are displayed when the G_A property is configured only when AEH and ALMs are enabled. If 
AEH and ALM are set to alarm enable (check box is ticked), the AEH/ALM alarm is generated 
when the value of the 0/2 bit of FLAG is 1. 
3.6 Configure Global Function Block Panel 
Global function block panel of is similar to the tag panel, which can be viewed in the real-time 
monitoring software. Global function block panel can be defined by created new one or imported 
an existed panel. One global function block support 256 panels at most, and the panel's name 
should not be repeated. Panel's name should be a string no more than 20 bytes, and only supports 
Chinese letter, English letter, number and "_". 
By adding Datalink in global function block panel, it can display the tag's real-time value. And the 
Datalink only can be the parameter or Marco of global function block, not can be tag's information. 
Datalink also can be actions, such as popup panel, popup trend, and so on.
--- pag 21 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
15 
3.6.1 Create Panel 
By following steps, global function block panel can be created. 
1) Select "New Panel" from the right menu of global function block, as shown as figure 
below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-18 Right Menu of Global Function Block 
2) Pop up the “New Panel” dialog box shown as below, input the “Name” and “Description”. 
The panel name can contain at most 12 characters. It cannot be empty or contain any 
blank space and symbols like \/:*?\"<>|!@#$%^&=,.';[]+-~. 
 
Figure 3-19 "New Panel" Configure Dialog Box 
3) After configured new panel's properties, click "OK" to popup panel edit software 
"VFPanel" as shown as below.

--- pag 23 ---

17 
 
 
 
Figure 3-22 Design Panel 
5) If inner parameter of global function block required displayed, the format of DataLink 
should be [@THIS@. Parameter Name] as shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-23 Configure Datalink Related to Global Function Block Parameter

click trend controller to popup the dialog box of "TrdGraphic Properties" shown as below, 
and the tag should be in the format of [@THIS@.Parameter Name].
--- pag 24 ---

18 
 
 
 
Figure 3-24 "TrdGraph Properties" Dialog Box

panel's page, as shown as figure below.

--- pag 25 ---

configuration.

Global function block supports importing panel in the format of .pnl file, the operation steps are: 
1) Select "Import Panel" in the right menu of global function block as shown as below.
--- pag 26 ---

Figure 3-28 "Import Panel" Dialog Box

3.7 Configure Global Function Block Symbol 
Global function block symbol can be applied in it's panel. Every global function block support 256 
symbols at most, and which can be exported, imported. Name of global function block symbol 
should not be repeated, and it is a string no more than 12 characters including Chinese letter, 
English letter and "_". 
Global function block symbol can display parameter real-time value by adding Datalink, which can 
only be parameters and Marco of global function block. Datalink in global function block supports 
actions such as popup panel, popup trend, and so on. 
3.7.1 Create Symbol 
By following steps, global function block symbol can be created.
--- pag 28 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
22 
1) Select "New Symbol" in the right menu of global function block as shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-30 Right Menu of Global Function Block

23

Global function block supports importing symbol that in the format of .syb file. The operation steps 
are:
--- pag 32 ---

1) Select "Import Symbol" in the right menu of global function block as shown as Figure 
3-30. 
2) Popup the dialog box "Import Symbol", and select the .syb file to import, as shown as 
below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-37 "Import Symbol" Dialog Box

6) Modify page property in the "Page Properties" dialog box as shown as Figure 3-35. 
7) Save and exit the symbol editing software, and return to VFExplorer software. 
8) In VFExplorer software, right click the global function block and select the "Save to 
Configuration Server" command in its right menu. 
9) In VFExplorer software, save the operation domain configuration to the configuration 
server. Check that the symbol had saved to the "VisualField Template Manager" as 
shown as the figure below.
--- pag 33 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
27 
 
 
 
Figure 3-39 Check the VF Template Manager 
3.8 Synchronize Global Function Block 
Synchronize global function block is the action that the global function block configuration will be 
synchronized to the control station. After modified global function block, the new configuration 
should be synchronized. And by synchronization: 
 
The global function block cited in the control stations can be updated and compiled, and 
the result will be saved to the system library of global function block. 
 
The synchronized global function block can be used in custom program. 
3.9 Import/Export Global Function Block 
3.9.1 Import Global Function Block 
VF supports import the global function block in the format of file with the suffix ".ex", and the file is 
the global function block exported file. If the exporting global function block existed in the library, 
the prompt information "Function Block *** already exists, Replace existing file?", and "***" is the 
name of global function block. 
By following steps, global function block can be imported: 
1) Right click the global function block library in the configure tree, and select "Import 
Function Block" command in its right menu. 
2) In the popup dialog box of "Import Function Block", select the .ex file, and click "Open" to 
import the selected global function block. 
3.9.2 Export Global Function Block 
The file suffix of the exported global function block is ".ex". By exporting global function block, the 
configured global function block can be imported to other projects. 
By following steps, global function block can be exported. 
1) Right click the exporting global function in the configure tree, and select the command 
"Export Function Block" in its right menu. 
2) Popup the dialog box of "Export Function Block", input the file name and select the export 
file saved path.
--- pag 34 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
28 
3) Click "Save" to export the selected global function block.
--- pag 35 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
29 
Section 4 Application of Global Function Block 
Global function block can be used in all the stations of the same project, and the other projects can 
used the global function block by export and import. 
By following steps, the global function block of PID interlock can be created and used. 
1) Start the software VFExplorer. 
2) Create global function block library. 
3) Create a global function block named "G_Lock_PID" and set the type as "ST". 
4) Edit the logic for "G_Lock_PID". 
Add parameters as shown as figure below. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-1 Add Parameters for Global Function Block 
Edit the global function block login in ST language as shown as figure below.
--- pag 36 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
30 
 
 
 
Figure 4-2 Edit the Logic of Global Function Block "G_Lock_PID" 
5) Compile, save and exit the logic edit software VFSTModule. 
6) Create monitoring panel for the global function block parameters as shown as figure 
below. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-3 Monitoring Panel of Global Function Block Parameter

8) Save the new global function block "G_Lock_PID" to configuration server.

Function Block Library" in its right menu. 
10) Edit custom program as shown as figure below.
--- pag 37 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
31 
 
 
 
Figure 4-4 Edit Custom Program Using Global Function Block "G_Lock_PID" 
11) Set the instant name and panel of global function block as shown as figure below. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-5 Set Property for G_Lock_PID 
12) Set the Marco for global function block "G_Lock_PID" as shown as figure below.
--- pag 38 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
32 
 
 
 
Figure 4-6 Set "Marco" for Global Function Block "G_Lock_PID" 
13) Complie and save the editing custom program, and return to VFExplorer. Right click the 
control station edited the custom program, and select "Save to Configuration Server" in 
its right menu. 
14) Modify name and dynamic property of buttons in the panel of the global function block, as 
shown as below. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-7 Modify Button of Global Function Block Panel 
Modify the buttons' dynamic property as shown as figure below.
--- pag 39 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
33 
 
 
 
Figure 4-8 Modify Button's Dynamic Property of Global Function Block Panel 
Set tag information of button in the panel of global function block. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-9 Set Tag Information of Button
--- pag 40 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
34 
15) Exit panel editing software, and return to the VFExplorer. Right click the edited global 
function block and select "Save to Configuration Server" command in its right menu. 
16) Right click the control station used the global function block, and select the command 
"Save to Configuration Server" in its right menu. 
17) Right click the control station used the global function block, and select the command 
"Synchronize Function Block Library" in its right menu.

return to VFExplorer.

Server" in its right menu. 
21) Right click the edited operation domain, and select the command "Publish Configuration" 
in its right menu. 
22) Start the real-time monitoring software, and view the graphic added the global function 
block panel. 
 
Tip: 
Global function block can also execute monitor by function block tag, and logic diagram. 
When users execute monitoring through function block tags, its method is similar to it of 
other tags. Users need to create a logic diagram in the custom program that referenced 
global function block as they want to monitor by logic diagram.
--- pag 41 ---
Global Function Block Configure Guide IM41S86-E 
35 
Section 5 Notes 
The differences between the global function block and custom function block are: 
 
Global function block can be used in all the stations of the same project, and the custom 
function block only can be used in the same station. 
 
Global function block supports multi-people configuration. 
The differences between the global function block and system function block are: 
 
Global function block only can be used in the project which has the global function block. 
 
Global function block name can be repeated in the different projects. 
 
Global function block can be edited by custom, but the logic and parameters of the 
system function block can not be edited. 
 
Besides parameter and logic, global function block also has panel and symbol.
--- pag 42 ---

36
