Section 1 Overview 
After installed "HP HMI" packet, the Radar Plot control, Profile control and HP Bar control can be 
used in graphics. 
This section describes the usage of the Radar Plot control, Profile control and HP Bar control, for 
detail of graphic drawing refer to Graphics Builder User Manual. 
Section 2 Radar Plot 
It is used to draw a radar plot. The radar plot uses the range of tag values as the coordinate axis, 
and can display the change information of multiple tags in the same plot.

The core position of the radar plot is the lower limit of the tag measuring range and the outermost 
scale (or border) of each axis is the upper limit of the tag measuring range. The value of the tag is 
marked proportionally at the corresponding position of each axis of the radar plot. The instruction 
of various parts of the radar plot are shown in the figure below. The associated tags information is 
displayed in the radar plot in the unti-clockwise direction in the numerical order as shown in the 
figure below.

Section 3 Profile 
It is used to draw a profile. The profile view is used to display polyline comparison figure between 
multiple tag values and their desirable values. 
3.1 Configuring control properties 
1. Select 
 in the “Graphic”, the cursor will appear as 
. At the same time, hold down the left 
mouse button to change the size of the profile, then release it to complete the creation. 
Each segment line represents the tag range. The real-time value of the tag is marked as a 
percentage on the segment line, and multiple tag values are connected to form a polyline graph. 
 
When the direction is vertical, the left border is the lower limit of the range, the right 
border is the upper limit of the range, and the display order of the tag values is from top 
to bottom; 
 
when the direction is horizontal, the lower border is the lower limit of the range, and the 
upper frame is the upper limit of the range and the tag value display order is from left to 
right.

Hardware Module Builder User Manual 
 
1 
Hardware Module Builder 
Section 1 Overview 
Hardware module builder (VFIOBuilder.exe) is an important part of VisualField system software 
package for system hardware configuration. A friendly man-machine interface is built with simple, 
clear pull-down menus and pop-up dialog boxes. A great deal of standard ActiveX in Windows is 
adopted to maintain the consistence of operation, making it easy to learn and use. 
Tree structure is employed to manage the configuration information, ensuring users well-informed 
about the whole system configuration status. All information of hardware module configuration is 
described in files with good expansibility. 
1.1 Function Feature 
Main function features of VFIOBulider: 
 
Conveniently and quickly edit hardware configuration information 
 
Hardware configuration import 
 
Supply the configured hardware information of hardware address (I/O channel 
address, etc) and channel type to tag builder 
 
Hardware configuration scan and upload (no need for customized configuration, 
information of hardware configuration can be scanned and generated automatically 
from control station) 
 
I/O module real-time data and diagnose data debug 
 
Power consumption statistics of controller, I/O link module, rack, I/O module 
 
Communication module configuration 
1.2 Technical Specifications 
 
Maximum amount of I/O modules: 7 
 
Maximum amount of racks in single controller: 32 
 
Maximum amount of modules in single rack: 16 for long rack and 8 for short rack 
 
Maximum amount of channels in single module: 16 for analog and 32 for digital 
 
Maximum undo steps: 32 
 
Longest time for scanning and uploading all modules in whole station: 2 minutes

Configuration Server" in right-click menu. Double-click "Hardware Configuration" in configuration

2-1.

station.

menu contains several sub-menus. 


easy to use. Click the menu [View/Tool bar] to decide whether to show the bar or 
not. 


cut and paste can be directly carried out to the "configuration tree". Click the menu

current selected device

3.10 Power Consumption Statistics 
Power consumption of the module would be shown in the Properties Settings Area. The power 
consumption includes system power consumption and auxiliary power consumption. 
 
Power consumption statistics of single I/O module is determined according to its 
type and the type of channel power distribution. 
 
The power consumption of one rack is the sum of the power consumption of all its 
subordinate I/O modules. 
 
The power consumption of one I/O link module is the sum of the power consumption 
of itself and all its subordinate I/O modules. 
 
The power consumption of one controller is the sum of the power consumption of all 
of its modules. 
Power consumption statistics varies according to the configuration. VFIOBuilder can display the

History Alarm Viewer 
Section 1 Overview 
VFHAView is also called history alarm viewer. Users can view local history alarm information in 
stand-alone mode when network and history alarm server are not available. 
VFHAView can select a project (operation domain of the project) to view history alarm (process 
alarm, status alarm and system alarm included). It also has functions of filtering, locating and 
searching and turning page, etc. 
The records of history alarm are in ms level, while the filter and location is in s level.
--- pag 4 ---
History Alarm Viewer User Manual 
2 
Section 2 Interface Introduction 
Select [Programs/VisualField/System Tools/History Alarm Browser] in the Start menu or double 
click VFHAView.exe
 (C:\VisualField\VFHAView.exe) in the installation directory to open 
VFHAView, and enter VFHAView interface, as shown in Figure 2-1 VFHAView interface includes 
title bar, menu bar, toolbar, list header, list content, status bar and function button, etc. 
 
Figure 2-1 History Alarm Browse Interface 
 
Tips: 
 
VFHAView can view all the alarm of the specified operation domain in the off-line status, 
not confined by alarm data region. 
 
Selecting the project (operation domain of the project) again actually is a process of 
reloading the history alarm. Users should avoid starting it up with the supervision 
software at the same time.

The title bar displays configuration directory, software name, etc.

right bracket of each menu indicates the shortcut key manner. Open the menu and display content
--- pag 5 ---

support shortcut key operation.

same, as shown above. But because the database structure of FF is different, the 
viewing method of FF database is different too.

operation.



 
View System Alarm: when [Type/System] is selected, the system alarm is displayed. 


VFHAView.

VFHAView provides print function of the alarm information in the current page. Click the function

 and pop up the dialog box of “Printer Settings”. Select the printer, and output to the 
configured printer after confirmation.

After the printer setting, click "OK" and pop up the prompt dialog box "Print Pages: X, Rows in One 
Page: M, Do you want to print?". Click "OK" to print the alarm in the current page. 
 
Tip: 
Print width is standardized by A4 landscape orientation width and it is preferred to set sheet 
width not shorter than A4 landscape orientation width (29.7 cm). 
 
3.2 Filter 
VFHAView provides the alarm filter function. It can filter the alarm according to setting conditions, 
such as tag name, alarm priority, range, time, etc. The displayed alarm differs according to filter
--- pag 12 ---

10 
conditions. 
3.2.1 Process Alarm 
Select to display process alarm. Click the function button
, and pop up the alarm filter setting 
dialog box, as shown in Figure 3-2. 
 
Figure 3-2 History Alarm Off-line Browse Filter Setting Process Alarm 
Alarm filter conditions include: 
 
Range: Search "All" or "Part" of the alarm information. Tick off "All" to display all the 
process alarm. Tick off "Part" and tag name, alarm priority, alarm time, alarm type, tag 
type, alarm acknowledge and eliminate and alarm group will be in optional status. If all 
alarm conditions are not set, the effect will be the same with that when ticking off "All". 
 
Tag name: When "Part" is selected in range, "Tag Name" is in optional status. Tick off 
"Tag Name", click "Select" and pop up "Tag Selector". Select the tag name to be filtered 
and click "OK", the tag name will be displayed in the edit box. (You can also input tag 
name in the edit box). 
When performing query filtering of process alarms, the query interface supports "," as a 
separator to perform query of multiple tag. The tag selector supports multiple selections 
and tag in the previous text box is not cleared and just appended after tag is added, 
 
Alarm priority: Include filter search of alarm priorities between 0 and 31.The start priority 
value should not be bigger than the end priority value. If the start priority is set as 5, the 
end priority should be set as a positive integer between 5 and 31.
--- pag 13 ---
History Alarm Viewer User Manual 
11 
 
Tag type: List all the tag type. Select one or several tag types and filter all the alarms of 
the tag of the selected types (When the alarms are conformed to other filter conditions, 
display them in several pages). 
 
Alarm type: List all the possible process alarm that tags of all types may generate. Select 
one or several tag types and filter the alarms of selected types (When the alarms are 
confirmed with other filter conditions, display them in the several pages). 
 
Acknowledge and eliminate: Select the alarm acknowledge or eliminate status. The 
default status is "Ignore". That is, ignore all the alarm that is 
acknowledged/unacknowledged and eliminated/not eliminated. 
 
Alarm time: Set time range of alarm filter. The start time should be less than the end time. 
 
Tip: 
The range of alarm time should be between 1970 and 2038. In view of the filter speed of the 
alarm, it is suggested to set alarm time filter less than three months. When alarm time span is 
too long, pop up the prompt dialog box "Time span is too long and it may cost a lot of time to 
search. It is suggested to set search range in three months." 
 


regions in each alarm group at most. Click the button

and pop up "Alarm Region Selection" interface, as shown in Figure 3-3. Click "Region

current list. Click "Clear" to select none.

 in the process of locating, filtering and turning

--- pag 3 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
1 
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
Section 1 Overview 
History fault diagnosis offline viewer (SCDiagHisView), which is also called fault diagnosis 
history data viewer, is an auxiliary function of VisualField, and can browse history fault 
diagnosis offline. History fault diagnose offline browser can provide various types to 
browse history fault diagnosis when not running the monitoring software, to analyze 
history data convenient.
--- pag 4 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
2 
Section 2 Application Procedures 
Operation steps of SCDiagHisView are shown below: 
Start
Select File or Database
Set Query Conditions
View History Data
End
 
Figure 2-1 Application procedures of SCDiagHisView 
2.1 Startup 
1. Select [All Programs/ VisualField/ System Tools/ History Fault Diagnose Viewer]. 
2. Pop up the main interface of SCDiagHisView, as shown in Figure 2-2. 
 
Figure 2-2 Main interface of SCDiagHisView 
2.2 Select File or Database 
2.2.1 Precondition 
SCDiagHisView associates with history fault diagnosis database file.sdh of VisualField.
--- pag 5 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
3 
The database file is required for viewing history data. 
 
Tip: 
Save path of database file can be customized and has no special requirement. 
Generally, select the default path [D: / ECSRun/ Project Name/ HMI/ Operation 
Domain Name/ Run/ DiagRecord]. 
 
2.2.2 Open Database File 
Select [File/ Open/ Database (File)] in Figure 2-3. If only checking the history fault 
diagnosis data of a certain period, user can select the corresponding .sdh file. If checking 
all history fault diagnosis records, please select the corresponding directory. 
 
Figure 2-3 Select database file 
Select Single .sdh File 
Select "File" as shown in Figure 2-3, and select single .sdh file, as shown in Figure 2-4.
--- pag 6 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
4 
 
Figure 2-4 Select .sdh file 
Select the diagnosis history file to be viewed. Click "Open" to view history data. 
Format of .sdh file name: Date_Domain Address_Station Address_Document Number. 
The detail instruction is shown in Table 2-1. 
Table 2-1 Naming rules of .sdh file 
Items 
Instruction 
Date 
Generation date of fault records in file. 
Date format: YYYYMMDD, such as 20141030 means Oct. 30th, 2014. 
IP Address 
Code 
For example: the IP of an operation station is 172.30.0.190, and the domain address 
is 0, station address is 190. Therefore, user can view the .sdh file according to the 
operation station, or check operation station has fault according to the .sdh file. 
File No. 
When the fault records generated one day exceed 64000, a new .sdh file will be 
generated. The file No. starts from 0, and add successively. 
 
Select Database Directory 
Select "Database" as shown in Figure 2-3, and select the database directory of history 
fault diagnosis, as shown in Figure 2-5. 
 
Figure 2-5 Select database directory 
Click "Browse" to select the database directory, to open the default database directory, as 
shown in Figure 2-6. If selecting other path to save database file of .sdh, so open the other 
database directory.
--- pag 7 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
5 
 
Figure 2-6 Select database directory 
2.3 Set Query Condition 
User can check the time range, station address and so on by query toolbar, as shown in 
Figure 2-7. 
Input address of station address is in format of X.Y, as shown in Figure 2-7, the station 
address is 0.254. 
 
Figure 2-7 Set query condition 
After setting the condition, click "Display Record" to display the records. 
Click "Advanced Search" to pop up the interface shown below, in which user can check 
more details for fault diagnosis.
--- pag 8 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
6 
 
Figure 2-8 Fault diagnosis history query 
Diagnosis Information 
History fault supports filtering display according to the node subordinating to diagnosis 
information. The specific operation steps are: 
1. Select "Diagnosis Information", the node below will be under the selectable 
status. 
2. Click “+” in front of the node. Various diagnosis items will be displayed under the 
specific node as shown below.
--- pag 9 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
7 
 
 
 
Figure 2-9 Select detail diagnosis information 
3. According to the actual need, select diagnosis type to be viewed. 
Diagnosis Position 
Select "Diagnosis Position", select specific fault diagnosis position, including the controller, 
operation node, cabinet, node and IO module. 
 
Figure 2-10 Select diagnosis position 
Fault Level 
Select "Fault Level", and choose a specific fault level, including serious fault, fault, warn 
and prompt. 
 
Figure 2-11 Select fault level 
After selecting, click "OK" in Figure 2-8, to complete the operation.
--- pag 10 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
8 
2.4 Export History Data 
Click “Export” button. History data of fault diagnosis can be outputted as the form of CSV 
file. The outputted CSV file can be opened directly as shown below. 
 
Figure 2-12 Exported History Fault 
You can view the file in .CSV format that the history fault exported by the text view tool and 
Excel. When view it by Excel, configure the time format to view the right time. The 
configuration is as follows: 
1) Select the time bar, and select "Format Cell…" in its right menu and the cell 
format setting interface will pop up. 
2) Select "Custom" in the "Category" and input "yyyy-m-d h:mm:ss.000" in the 
"Type" as shown as figure below. 
 
Figure 2-13 Format settings of cell when exported 
2.5 View Historical Data 
View the historical data displayed, as shown in Figure 2-14.
--- pag 11 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
9 
 
Figure 2-14 Display records 
History data of fault includes following information: 
 
Generate Time: generation time of fault. 
 
Diagnose Device: device with fault 
 
Device Address: address code of device with fault. 
 
Diagnosis Description: Detail description of fault. 
 
Diagnosis Parameter: detail reason or information of the fault. 
 
Record Status: current fault status. 
 
Restore Time: restore time of the fault.
--- pag 12 ---
History Fault Diagnosis Offline Viewer 
10 
Section 3 Revision 
Table 3-1 Revision 
Document Version 
Applicable Model 
Remarks

Publish for the first time. 
V1.1(20150512)

Change the software figures. 
V1.1(20190805)

Add the instruction of configure time format 
of the export file.

--- pag 3 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
1 
 
History Trend Viewer 
Section 1 Overview 
SCTrdHisView, which also can be called history trend viewer, is one of the accessorial functions in 
the VisualField system software and users can view the history trend off-line via it. The function of 
history trend off-line view can provide various history trend view modes to users when the 
supervision software is not running, so that it is convenient to analyze the history data.
--- pag 4 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
2 
 
Section 2 Interface Introduction 
Select the [Programs/VisualField(V3.20)/System Tools/History Trend Browser] in the Start menu 
or click the SCTrdHisView.exe
 (C:\VisualField3\SCTrdHisView.exe) in the installation directory, 
and then open the view software and enter into the history trend off-line view interface as shown in 
the Figure 2-1. 
The view window can be divided into title bar, menu bar, system tools bar, trend tools bar, trend 
page, trend window, tag information page and status bar, etc. 
 
Figure 2-1 Trend History Data View Interface 
Right click the blank place at right of menu bar, users can set the display or hide the “Trend page”, 
“Configuration information”, “Trend tools bar”, “System tools bar” and “Status Bar” in the pop-up 
right-key menu. 
2.1 Menu Bar 
File, View, Operate menu options are displayed in the menu bar and the letter in the bracket at the 
right of each menu option expresses the shortcut key. Press “ALT+shortcut letter” can open the 
relevant option and display the content of sub-menu.
--- pag 5 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
3 
 
2.1.1 File 
File menu includes the options of Open, Save, Print, Print Preview, Print Setting, exit and Recent 
Files. 
Open: It is used to select the project of history trend to be viewed and set the project directory. 
When select the [File/Open] option, or click the button 
, the “Configuration Selection” setting 
dialog will be popped-up. When click the 
 button, the “Open” dialog used to select project 
file will be popped-up, and then choose “ECSRun/Project name/Project.scp”. After clicking the 
“Open”, selected path is displayed in the input frame under the “Configuration Selection”, as show 
in the Figure 2-2 Click the “OK” after selecting an operation domain. 
 
Figure 2-2 Effect of project path setting 
 
Save: It is used to save free configuration file. Select the option [File/Save], or click the 
button 
 on the “System tool bar” and save the information of “Free configuration”. 
Furthermore, “Free configuration” will be saved when close the software normally either. 
 
Print: Select the menu option [File/Print], or click the button 
, and the print setting 
window will pop-up as show the Figure 2-3. Time setting, curve setting and tag setting 
can be operated respectively in this window.
--- pag 6 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
4 
 
 
Figure 2-3 Print Setting Window 
Time Settings 
Time setting includes “Current Page Time” and “Time Adjusting”. No need to set others if select 
“Current page time”, and the print content is trend diagram current page in the current coordinate 
time of each tag. It needs to set the “Start Time”, “Total Span”, “Each Page Span” and whether 
“Unify Start Time” respectively if select the option “Time Adjusting”, as shown the Figure 2-4. The 
detail operations as followings:
--- pag 7 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
5 
 
 
Figure 2-4 Time Adjusting Setting (Select unify start time) 
 
Start Time: Click the increase/decrease button or input the time by keyboard can 
set the starting time. 
 
Total Span: Click the list button of “day(s)”, “hour(s)”, “min(s)” to selecting. Range of 
Day: 0~3 
 
Each Page Span: Click the list button of “day(s)”, “hour(s)”, “min(s)” to selecting. 
Range of Day: 0~3 
 
Unify Start Time: If select “Unify Start Time”, “Tag” can not be operated and only 
one time coordinate will be displayed in history trend diagram. If don’t select this 
option, “Start Time” of each tag can be set in the option “Tag”, as shown in the Figure 
2-5. Detail operation: Click the list button beside the “Tag” and select a tag (only set 
the configured tag in the current off-line trend page), and then modify the starting 
time; After that, click the list button beside the “Tag” again to select another tag, and 
modify the starting time, repeat the above operations, and click the “OK” to finish the 
starting time setting. If the starting time setting of each tag is different, each tag will 
have a corresponding axis as show the Figure 2-6. 
 
Total Page: Display the number of current pages printed. Software will calculate it 
automatically according to the setting, no need to set by users.
--- pag 8 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
6 
 
 
Figure 2-5 Time Adjusting Setting (Not select unify start time) 
 
Figure 2-6 Multi-Time Coordinates
--- pag 9 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
7 
 
Curve Settings 
Curve setting are used to set the line shape, width and color of trend curve. 
 
Line shape and Width: Click corresponding list button to select suitable line shape 
and width. 
 
Color: Click Color frame to open the color plate and select suitable color. Besides. 
User can enter the customized color setting window via clicking the button 
 at 
the right-bottom of color plate to set, add and use customized color, as shown in the 
Figure 2-7. 
 
Figure 2-7 Curve Setting 
 
Tip: 
8 curves in the Curve Setting window are corresponding to the 8 tags from up to down in the 
trend configuration page respectively. Users can set different line shape, width and color to
--- pag 10 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
8 
 
distinguish different trend curves in the same trend window. 
 
Tag Settings 
Tag Settings are used to select the trend curve to be printed and set the maximum and minimum of 
its coordinate, whose expression has two types: value and percentage. 
 
Maximum and Minimum of Coordinate: Input value into the corresponding 
position of each tag directly or input value after selecting “%”. 
 
“Select” Tag Name: print the trend curve of this tag 
 
“Not select” Tag Name: no need to print the trend curve of this tag 
 
Print Preview: Select [File/Print Preview] option on the menu bar, and print preview 
setting window will pop up, as show the Figure 2-8. Set print firstly and the method of 
print setting can be found in the introduction of menu command “Print”. 
 
Figure 2-8 Print Preview Setting 
After setting print, click “OK” and the print preview window will pop-up shown as in 
Figure 2-9. The specifications of button functions of the toolbar in this window are shown 
as followings: 
 
Click 
 button (its function is same as the 
 on the system toolbar) and 
pop-up the print setting panel. 
 
Click 
 button to page down.
--- pag 11 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
9 
 
 
Click 
 button to page up. 
 
Click 
 button to display one or two pages in the same window. 
 
Click 
 button to zoom in. 
 
Click 
 button to zoom out. 
 
Click 
 button to close print preview. 
 
Figure 2-9 Print Preview Window 
 
Print Setting: Set properties of printer and paper 
 
Exit: Exit SCTrdHisView 
2.1.2 View Menu 
View menu can choose whether trend page, configuration information, trend toolbar, system 
toolbar or status bar will be displayed in the history trend off-line browse window. 
2.1.3 Operation Menu 
Operation menu includes window setting, time setting, coordinates restore, data point, page 
turning and zoom in/out. Details can be found in the introduction of “Trend Toolbar”. 
2.2 System Toolbar 
System toolbar lists part of menu functions in “File” as icon shortcut.
--- pag 12 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
10 
 
 
: Open File. The same as [File/Open] 
 
: Save free configuration. The same as [File/Save] 
 
: Print trend. The same as [File/Print] 
2.3 Trend Toolbar 
Trend toolbar lists all the submenu functions in “Operation” as icon shortcut. 
 
: Previous Screen 
 
: Previous Half Screen 
 
: Next Half Screen 
 
: Next Screen 
 
: Zoom out. Enlarge the time span of X axis (time axis) in the visible trend display 
window. 
 
: Zoom in. Reduce the time span of X axis (time axis) in the visible trend display 
window. 
 
: Zoom Benchmark: Select the benchmark line of curve zoom. (it can 
be Starting time, cursor time, finish time) 
 
: Display Settings. It can set “coordinates limit”, “coordinates setting”, “curve 
section” and “display setting”. 
 
 
: Time Settings. Set starting time, time span and data interval of trend curve 
displayed in the trend display window. 
 
 Data List. Tag data list, which lists all the tags data displayed on the window. 
 
 Reset Coordinate. Reset the maximum and minimum of all the tags to the 
setting same as configuration 
 
: Export Data: Export the history data of tag as the format .CSV for easy to view 
the history value of one tag at one time. 
2.3.1 Page Turning 
Click the icons on the “Trend Toolbar” to achieve the trend page turning operation, as show the 
Figure 2-10.
--- pag 13 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
11 
 
 
Figure 2-10 Page Turning Buttons 
2.3.2 Curve Zoom 
Select the buttons 
 on the “Trend Toolbar” can zoom the trend curve in the visible time 
range of X axis. Select button “Zoom out”
to enlarge the time span of X axis (time axis) in the 
visible trend display window. Select button “Zoom in” 
 to reduce the time span of X axis (time 
axis) in the visible trend display window. 
2.3.3 Curve Zoom Benchmark Line Selection 
When set “Curve Zoom”, users can select benchmark line in 
on the Toolbar. 
Start 
When select “Start” as zoom benchmark line, trend window will set “start time” as benchmark and 
double the whole time span of time axis. Suppose that original starting time is 2006-1-5 9:00:00 
and the whole time axis span is 10 minutes. After clicking this button, the starting time will not 
change, but the time span will be 20 minutes. When click the icon one time, the time span will be 
doubled. The maximum span is 3 days. The same as zoom in, when click
, trend window will 
set the starting time as benchmark and reduce the time span to half. The minimum time span is 2 
minutes. 
Cursor 
When select “cursor” as benchmark for zoom, trend window will be zoomed based on “Cursor 
time”. Selecting one time and clicking icon
, “Cursor time” will be the middle line of trend 
window, and based on it, double the time span. Figure 2-11 and Figure 2-12 corresponding picture 
before and after clicking the icon
. Similarly, clicking icon
, the time span will be reduced as 
half of original one. Therefore, zoom by using “Cursor” as benchmark line is convenient for viewing 
the trend around cursor time.
--- pag 14 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
12 
 
 
Figure 2-11 Before clicking zoom in button 
 
Figure 2-12 After clicking zoom in button 
Cursor also used to locate time. Drag cursor by mouse left key, or scroll up or down the mouse 
wheel, cursor moves left or right. Time of the location displayed in the bottom of cursor (near the 
time axis), user can view the trend data in some time easily. 
Stop 
When select “Stop” as the benchmark for zoom, the principle is the same as “Start”, but the effect 
is converse, meaning that the stop time will not be changed and starting time will move forward or 
backward which makes the span of whole time axis zoom in or zoom out. The maximum of time 
span is 3days and minimum is 2 minutes. 
2.3.4 Interface Setting 
Clicking icon
, “Display Settings” will pop up and users can operate the “Coordinate Limit”, 
“Coordinate Settings”, “Curve Area” and “Display Settings”. 
Coordinate Limit
--- pag 15 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
13 
 
It is used to set the maximum and minimum of Y axis of each tag current trend page. Coordinate 
limit can be displayed by “value” or “percentage”, as show the Figure 2-13. Y axis maximum and 
minimum in the trend window will be the value which had been modified in the interface setting. 
The setting effect here is the same as the setting effect of maximum and minimum in the tag 
information setting window. 
 
Figure 2-13 coordinate limit setting window 
Coordinate Settings 
It is used to set “data precision, display location, display interval, background color, data color and 
scale color” of the value coordinate (Y axis) and “time format, display location, display interval, 
time color, scale color and background color” of the time coordinate (X axis). 
Value Coordinate 
It is used to set “data precision, display position, display interval, background color, data color and 
ruler color” of the value coordinate. 
 
Data Precision: It refers decimal digits of the value displayed at each scale. The 
data can only be set any one integer between 0~5 else a dialog “Please input an 
integer between 0 and 5” will pop-up. 
 
Display Location: It refers value are displayed to “inside” or “outside” of the trend
--- pag 16 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
14 
 
window; 
 
Display Interval: It refers how many scales displaying a value. The value to be set 
must be positive integer, or a dialog “Please input a positive integer” will pop-up. 
 
Background Color: It depends on the display position. When the position is 
“outside”, it means the background color of Y axis; when the position is “inside”, 
background color can not be seen, because the background color of Y axis is the 
same as the background color of trend window. 
 
Data Color: It refers the color of the data on the Y axis. 
 
Scale Color: It refers the color of scales. 
If the value coordinate as show in the Figure 2-14, and the effect after setting is shown as Figure 
2-15 (a). Figure 2-15(b) is the effect which the display position is set as “inside”. 
 
Figure 2-14 value coordinate setting
--- pag 17 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
15 
 
 
Figure 2-15 value coordinate setting effect 
Time Coordinate 
It is used to set “time format, display position, display space, time color, ruler color and background 
color” of the time coordinate 
 
Time Format: It can be displayed by two modes. (HH:MM:SS and yy:mm:dd 
HH:MM:SS) 
 
Define of other items are the same as the relative define in the value coordinate 
setting. Details can be found in the “Value Coordinates”. 
Curve Area 
In “Curve section”, users can set “Curve diagram (Trend diagram), grids, line information (the font 
color of the tags in tag section)”. 
Curve (Trend diagram) 
Users can set “background color, slide bar width, slide bar color” of the curve (trend diagram), 
where the slide width only can be an integer between 1~3, or a dialog” Please input an integer 
between 1 and 3.” Figure 2-16 is the setting of curve diagram and the effect is shown as Figure 
2-17.
--- pag 18 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
16 
 
 
Figure 2-16 curve diagram setting 
 
Figure 2-17 curve diagram setting effect 
Grid Line 
Users can set “color, line shape, X axis/Y axis segments” of grids, where the sectoring of X/Y axis 
should be an integer between 1 and 10, or a dialog “Please input an integer between 1 and 
10”.The effect of Figure 2-18 is as Figure 2-19.
--- pag 19 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
17 
 
 
Figure 2-18 grids setting 
 
Figure 2-19 Grid setting effect diagram 
Line Information 
It is used to set the font color of the tags in tag information bar. Except the color of the selected tag 
will be different, rest of them will be the color that be set. The effect of Figure 2-20 is as Figure 
2-21.
--- pag 20 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
18 
 
 
Figure 2-20 font color setting 
 
Figure 2-21 font color setting effect diagram 
Display Setting 
Display setting includes the setting of “display information” and “tag information”. 
Display information 
It is used to set whether display the value axis (Y axis), time axis (X axis), grids, slide bar, and tag 
information bar. Set the display information by “Selected” or “Not selected”. 
Tag Information 
It is used to set the number of tags displayed in each row. Click the list button besides the 
information frame, users can select the number, the range of which is the integers between 1 and 
4. The effect of setting as Figure 2-22 is as Figure 2-23.
--- pag 21 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
19 
 
 
Figure 2-22 Display Setting
--- pag 22 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
20 
 
 
Figure 2-23 Display setting effect diagram 
2.3.5 Time Setting 
Clicking the icon
 on the “Trend Toolbar”, the time settings interface shown as the figure below 
will pop-up. Users can set “Start Time”, “Time Span”, “Data Interval” and whether “Unify Start Time” 
respectively. 
 
Figure 2-24 Time Settings 
 
“Start Time”, refers the starting time of trend curve for each tag in the current trend
--- pag 23 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
21 
 
page displayed in the trend window. 
 
“Time Span”, refers span of X axis of trend curve for each tag in the current trend 
page displayed in the trend window. 
 
“Data Interval”, refers the time interval between two adjoin data points. Programs will 
select one suitable value as the parameter automatically, and users don’t need to 
set it generally. However, if users want to obtain different trend curves at the same 
period time, they need to set it, E.g., time segment is 2000s, when the parameter is 
2s, 1000 points can be got; when the parameter is 4s, only 500 points can be got. 
The setting of this parameter needs to make the data amount is a number between 
120 and 1200, allowed by the window. When setting it, select corresponding 
positions (Hour, Min or Sec), and click the increase/decrease button besides the 
“Data interval”. 
 
“Unify Start Time”, refers the starting time of X axis for each tag in current trend page 
is the same one, time span of X axis is same and data interval is same as well. 
Details for “Time setting” please see the “Time setting” in 2.1.1. 
2.3.6 Data Point 
Click the button 
 on the “Trend Toolbar”, “Tag Data List” shown as Figure 2-25 will pop-up. Tag 
data displayed on the window is listed in the list. If one point data is empty, it refers there is no data 
at that point. 
 
Figure 2-25 Tag Data List
--- pag 24 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
22 
 
 
Tip: 
Time interval of two adjoin data points of one tag depends on “Time Settings -> Data 
Interval”, details can be seen in relative specification “Trend Toolbar->Time Settings->Data 
Interval”. 
 
2.3.7 Coordinates Restore 
Click the button
 on the “Trend Toolbar”, maximum and minimum of all the tags will restore to 
the setting same as configuration. 
2.3.8 Data Export 
Click the button
 on the “Trend Toolbar”, “Data Export Settings” will pop up, as shown in the 
Figure 2-26. 
 
Figure 2-26 Data Export Setting Window 
 
Add: Click “Add” button, select the tag to be export history data in the pop-up trend 
tag selector. 
 
Delete: Select one tag and click “Delete” button. 
 
Clear: Click “Clear” button to delete all tags. 


each tag. 
Part of data exported is shown as the diagram below.

23

2.4 Trend Page 
Trend page can be divided into trend configuration page and free configuration page. 
2.4.1 Trend Configuration 
Click icon
to enter trend configuration page. After opening specified file, 
“Trend configuration page” will show its trend configuration, and then click the node
 to expend 
trend configuration tree. Click one “Trend page”, all tags of trend curves in this page will be 
displayed in the trend window; the information of tags including in this trend page will be displayed 
in tag information page. Meanwhile, part of trend window information will be displayed in the status 
bar: whether unify the Starting time, (X axis) time span and current cursor time. 
2.4.2 Free Configuration 
Click icon
 to enter free configuration page. Free configuration page can 
put tags in different trend pages into one trend window to be displayed, so that it is convenient to 
analyze. Right click” Trend window configuration”, users can “Add”, “Modify” or “Delete” trend 
configuration of free page. 
Add free page trend configuration 
Operation Steps: 
 
Right click “Trend window configuration” and click “add”, “Trend page setting” 
window will pop-up, as shown in the Figure 2-28.
--- pag 26 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
24 
 
 
Figure 2-28 free page trend configuration 
 
Fill in “Page name” in the trend page setting window (“Page name” can be empty. In 
order to distinguish easily, recommend to fill in the “Page name”). 
 
Input “tag name” into edit box besides “Tag name” directly, or click the button
, 
select the tag in the pop-up “Tag selector”. 
 
Tips: 
Select one tag in the tag selector and press “Shift” key, and then select another tag, which 
means it can select several continuous tags. 
Select any one tag and press the “Ctrl” key, which can select several discontinuous tags. 
 
 
Select the color of trend curve for the tag. Color settings please see the relative 
introduction in 2.1.1 “Curve Setting”. 
 
Click “Coordinate” button, “Value coordinate maximum and minimum setting” will 
pop-up. Set the maximum and minimum of the coordinate in this window, and the 
display mode is percentage, as shown in the Figure 2-29.
--- pag 27 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
25 
 
 
Figure 2-29 coordinate limit setting in the free configuration trend page 
 
Click the “OK” button to finish adding free trend configuration page. 
 
After adding, free configuration trend page window is as Figure 2-30. 
 
Figure 2-30 free configuration trend page
--- pag 28 ---
History Trend Viewer User Manual 
26 
 
 
Modify trend configuration of free page: Right click one configuration page to be 
modified in free configuration, and then click “Modify” and modify in the pop-up 
panel of “Trend page setting”. 
 
Delete trend configuration of free page: Right click one configuration page to be 
deleted in free configuration, and then click “Delete” to delete it. 
 
Save trend configuration of free page: Click the button
 on the “System 
toolbar” to save the modify information in “Free configuration”. 
2.5 Tag Information Page 
Select one trend page and corresponding configuration information will be displayed in the tag 
information page. Configuration information content should be consistent with the tag information 
in the tag list (or domain variable configuration). 
2.6 Trend Window 
Trend window can be divided into X axis (time coordinate), Y axis (value coordinate), trend display 
window, zoom slide button, up/down slide button and tag information bar. 
 
Figure 2-31 Trend Window 
 
X axis (time coordinate): After dividing equally the time span, a horizontal axis with 
equal dividing scale will be generated. 
 
Y axis (value coordinate): After dividing equally the range of maximum and minimum of 
a tag, a vertical axis with equal dividing scale will be generated.
--- pag 29 ---

27 
 
 
Trend display window: Display all the trend curves of selected tags. 
 
Zoom slide button: Slide upwards the button can zoom in the trend display window, 
while slide downwards will zoom out the window. Figure 2-32 shows the comparison of 
one trend window with normal, zoom in and zoom out status. 
 
Figure 2-32 trend diagram zoom in and zoom out effect

display window, while slide downwards will move down the window.

 
Tag information bar: Display all the tag names and current value of the data point 
where the trend curve cursor is in current trend window. 
 
Figure 2-34 Tag information bar 
In the tag information bar, user can carry out following operations: 


I/O Tag 
Section 1 ECS-700 Tag 
I/O Tag can be managed in the Tag Builder software. It (and part of its parameters) can be 
referenced in programming software like FBD, ST, etc. 
 
 
Tips: 
When the tag is the independent domain tag, domain address will be displayed as “/” in 
address information of tags. 
 
1.1 AI Tag 
Signal of general AI input module, temperature signal input module (such as RTD, thermocouple 
and so on), pulse input module can be input to AI tag. The input signal is processed according to 
tag configuration and the actual value is got. 
Communication AI signal can be input to AI tag and the actual value can be got directly or by 
conversion. 
1.1.1 Tag Panel 
As shown in Figure 1-1, AI tag panel of ECS-700 system includes Tag Name, Alarm ACK Mark, 
Alarm Level Mark, Alarm Level, Real-time Value and Window Jumping Button.
--- pag 5 ---

status:

tag property. For example, real-time of the tag in the figure above is 0, alarm level of the 
tag is NEDV, L and LL. 
 
Decimal digits of the tag are conformed by the configuring in system configuration. By 
default, decimal digits are 2 bit. 
 
The mark and color of the tag alarm level is related to the configuring of “Global Default 
Settings > Alarm Priority” node in system structure configuration software.

1.1.6 AI Tag Member 
Parameters in AI tag can be referenced in user program according to the format of tag name and 
parameter except inner parameters. 
1.1.7 Function Description 
1. Signal send over 
 
Sample data linearly from -25% of span to 125% of span at most. 
 
Even if the measurement range of the module is more than or equal to -25%~125% 
of the span, sampling values in the range of -25%~125% of the span can be sent
--- pag 9 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 6 
back because the maximum of the extended span can be set 25% and the minimum 
of the extended span can be set -25%. 
 
If the extended span range is less than ±25%, linear sampling values are sent in the 
extended span range. If the sampling values are over the extended span range, the 
maximum or minimum of the extended span are sent back. 
 
The span range of thermocouple and thermal resistance is set by the measurement 
range of the sensor. 
2. Input signal conversion 
Input signal conversion of AI tag includes: 
 
No conversion 
No conversion mode is only for communication tag, in which not convert the sent data, 
and output data in 2 types: output unsigned integer COMMASK equaling to 
communication value (controller FCU711-S doesn’t has this function); or output float PV 
equaling to communication value 
 
Linear conversion 
PV = (actual measurement code value – code value low limit)/(code value high limit – 
code value low limit)*(range high limit – range low limit)+range low limit 
1) Convectional signals (type II, type III and -10V~10V, -20mA~20mA and so on) 
2) Temperature signal (thermocouple , thermal resistance) 
The actual temperature value is calculated in AI module according to measurement 
principle. Span range should be specified for signals in hardware configuration. For 
example, the span of thermocouple of E type is set 200~500 . The high limit of the 
span is 500 and the low limit of the span is 200 in the hardware configuration. The 
span of actual value of E type thermocouple must be set 200 ~500 in the tag 
configuration software. 
 
Sqrt 
The input can be converted to actual value output by sqrt conversion. 
Calculation formula: 
 
3. Small signal cutting 
If the small signal cutting switch SWLCUT is ON, the small signal is cut. The small signal cutting 
value is set as percent. When percent of input signal is less than positive small signal cutting value, 
the small signal is cut and AI value is 0% of the span, equal to low limit of the span.
--- pag 10 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 7 
4. Single period change rate alarm 
Judge single cycle change rate overrun for inputed AI signal. 
When |inPV(n)- inPV(n-1)| <=DPV: tag value is PV(n) when change rate of adjacent input values is 
not over the set rate limit DPV. 
When |inPV(n)- inPV(n-1)| >DPV: PV(n) is equal to PV(n-1) when change rate of adjacent input 
values is not over the set rate limit DPV. 
DPV is the most change value in single period when it is configured. inPV(n) and inPV(n-1) are 
data sent by AI module in two adjacent periods. PV(n) and PV(n-1) are tag value in two adjacent 
periods. 
If input signal change values in two adjacent periods are over the most change value in running 
process, the output value in the last period is maintained and the single period change rate alarm 
is set. When the alarm is generated, if PV of the two new adjacent periods are less than or equal to 
DPV, the jump reaches new balance position and alarm is eliminated. 
5. Filter function 
FV(n) =*FV(n-1)+(1-)* PV(n) 
Tc
Tc
Ts


 
FV(n) is value of first-order filter,  is filter smoothing coefficient, Tc is filter time constant, Ts 
is sampling time. 
6. Extended span limit process 
Data send by AI module can be over 25% of the span at most. Data can be sampled linearly in the 
range of -25%~+125% at most. When data is over high or low limit of the extended span, high limit 
or low limit of the extended is sent back. The high and low limit of the extended span are set in the 
tag configuration software. 
 
When PVCALC>=SCH+(SCH-SCL)*HORLIM/100.0, PVCALC= 
SCH+(SCH-SCL)*HORLIM/100.0 
 
When PVCALC<=SCL-(SCH-SCL) *LORLIM/100.0, PVCALC= SCL-(SCH-SCL) 
*LORLIM/100.0 
HORLIM and LORLIM are percent of high and low limit of the extended span. The maximum is 
25% when it is configured. 
If over-range occurs in non-forced status, ORL or ORH will be generated, and set ERR at the 
same time. In auto mode, output by fail-safe mode. 
7. Forced process
--- pag 11 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 8 
In non-force status, AI input signal comes from AI module or simulation input, from which the 
current actual value is attained after a series of operation. 
In force status, actual value PV of AI tag is set by users. In force status, high and low limit alarm, 
small signal cutting and over span process are same as in non-force status. 
In FCU712, communication tag non-conversion mode has no force status. 
8. Alarm process 
 
Fault alarm 
When the module or communication is faulty, AI tag fault alarm ERR is displayed (In the 
status of controller debugging, ERR alarm is not generated). FBD can reference 
parameter, tag status sign ERR=ON. 
 
Over range alarm 
When over max/min limits, alarm is set in alarm enable and PV is over max/min of 
extended span, over range alarm flag is set in the quality code. FBD can reference 
parameter, tag status sign ERR=ON. 
 
Change rate of single period over limit alarm 
When change rate over limit alarm is set in alarm enable and change rate of single 
period of PV is over limit, corresponding alarm flag is set in quality code. 
 
High/Low alarm 
HHH, HH, high, low, LL, LLL limit of PV can be processed by the tag. Each alarm can 
has hysteresis function. 
 
Alarm shield 
If the function of tag alarm shield is set, corresponding alarm will only be recorded but 
not displayed in real time. 
 
Alarm enable 
In alarms above, each alarm in high and low limit alarm, over span alarm and rate alarm 
can be set enable or disable separately. Alarm limit reversal alarm and tag fault alarm 
always work. When an alarm is generated, corresponding flag is set in quality code. 
 
Delay alarm 
When the heterogeneous communication module (COM741) loses communication 
connection with its I/O modules (including 485 communication channel disconnects, 
communication timeout and data package verification error), it issues delay alarm. 
When module lost (insert and extract COM741), inconsistent module types (configuration 
is inconsistent with the actual I/O) and module major fault appear on its I/O device, the
--- pag 12 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 9 
delay alarm will occur immediately. 
9. Fault setting 
In status of non-force and non-simulation, tag values are from AI module. When data sent by AI 
module is suspicious, tag value is maintained. When data sent by AI module is bad, tag value is 
output according to configuration setting, which includes maintain, set span high limit and set span 
low limit. 
Details of fault safety, refer to '1.5 Fail-safe". 
10. Format conversion of communication signal 
The data format is low bytes forward and high bytes backward. If data format of communication 
signal is different from system data format, corresponding conversion mode can be selected. 
If communication data format is two bytes integer, "No conversion" or "Byte conversion" can be 
selected. 
If communication data format is four bytes integer or four bytes float, "No conversion", "Byte 
conversion", "Word conversion" and "Conversion in word" can be selected. 
For example,

11. Communication data types 
Communication signal configuration data types can reflect the mode applicated when getting 
communication data. 2-byte integer and 4-byte integer are “signed” or “unsigned”. For example, 
2-byte integer, the communication memory value is 0x8000. When signed, negative number can 
be obtained; when unsigned, positive number can be obtained.

Analog operated in control strategy is output to AO module by AO tag to control field executor.

1.2.7 Function Description 
1. Validity check of parameters 
Check whether configuration data is right. The output low limit set should be less than the output 
high limit when tags are configured. Otherwise, low limit is equal to high limit. 
When the output limit is more than the high limit of the extended span, the output limit can be set 
high limit of the extended span at most. 
When the output limit is less than the low limit of the extended span, the output limit can be set low 
limit of the extended span at least. 
2. Output track function 
When SWTR is ON, output of AO module tracks TV value and marks track status. When the field 
device is in handheld status, it can be connected with TV by readback AI signal of device position 
in order that output of AO tag can track actual position of field device. 
The priority of track status is sub-status of non-force status and lower than the force status.
--- pag 16 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 13 
3. Output limit 
The output value is set between maximum output a minimum output. 
If output value of AO is more than maximum output, the output value is restricted to the maximum 
output and the maximum output limit flag is set. 
If output value of AO is less than minimum output, the output value is restricted to the minimum 
output and the minimum output limit flag is set. 
If high limit is larger or equal to low limit, the output value is limited no matter in force status or 
non-force status. 
Otherwise, limit is invalid, and report CFGERR configuration error, while extended range limit is 
still valid. 
4. Output inversion calculation 
Inversion calculation output value BKOUT is equal to input value which is acquired byf reverse 
calculate currently AO block output value OUT: BKOUT = OUT - Bterm. When AO block is in force 
status, think it is in open loop status. BKOUT linked inversion calculation value of previous block, 
and the output of previous block track this inversion calculation input value. 
BKOUTERR should link BKINERR of previous block. When AO is OOS, trackin, force, fault sage 
status, BKOUTERR equal ON, and can make previous control block turn into IMAN status by 
BKOUTERR. 
5. Force status process 
When SWAM is OFF, it is in force status and output OUT is set manually not according to input IN. 
When SWAM is ON, it is in non-force status, output OUT is attained from input IN after process. 
In FCU712, communication tag non-conversion mode has no force status. 
6. Conversion type (controller FCU711-S doesn’t have the function) 
The configuration is for communication tag. Output AO output value after converted by high/low 
limits of output original code in linear conversion mode. In no conversion mode, output unsigned 
integer COMMASK directly. 
7. Positive output/negative output 
For general tags and communication tags as below: 
 
4-byte float and the data is percentage. 
 
4-byte integer （signed / unsigned） 
 
2-byte integer （signed / unsigned）
--- pag 17 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 14 
When positive output, output value of AO module = dimensionless output value of AO tag. 
When negative output, the output value of AO module = dimensionless output value which is AO 
tag range high limit subtraction OUT value. 
For communication tags, when they are 4-byte float and actual value output, no matter positive 
output or negative output, output is equal to actual value, while it still limits the output. 
8. Output with extended span 
Output of AO signal supports extended span and maximum is 25%. High and low limit of the 
extended span can be configured. 
9. Alarm process 
 
Fault alarm 
When the module or communication is faulty, tag fault alarm ERR is displayed (In the 
status of controller debugging, ERR alarm is not generated). 
 
Output H/L Limit Alarm 
When the output is over max./min. of output, the output will be limited and 
corresponding maximum output /minimum output alarm flag is set. Maximum 
output/minimum output limit alarm can be shielded separately but the limit function can 
be shielded. The function is available in force or non-force status. 
 
Over span alarm 
When the input value is out of the range of extended span, over span alarm is 
generated. 
 
Alarm shield 
If the function of tag alarm shield is set, corresponding alarm will only be recorded and 
not displayed in real time. 
 
Alarm enable 
High limit/low limit alarm and over span alarm can be enabled or disabled separately. 
The tag fault alarm always works. When the alarm is generated, corresponding flag will 
be set in the quality code. 
10. Fault safety status 
If the controller is in non-debugging status and the channel which the tag corresponds to is 
configured under "Output according to the preset value", AO tag will be in fault safety status 
automatically, the tag value displays the fault safety value and SAFESTA after the controller 
disconnection with AO module for five minutes. The tag is in "Fault safety status" displayed in the 
bar "Fault safety list" in the system status list of supervision. In the status, the tag value can't be
--- pag 18 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 15 
modified. 
If communication between controller and AO module restores or AO channel connection restores, 
AO tag exits fail-safe status automatically. 
When AO channel is disconnected or in short circuit, AO tag Flag is set as OOP (open loop) 
status. 
Please refer to "1.5 Fail-safe" for details. 
11. Communication signal format conversion 
The data format is low bytes forward and high bytes backward. If data format of communication 
signal is different from system data format, corresponding conversion mode can be selected. 
If communication data format is integer of two bytes, "No conversion" or "Byte conversion" can be 
selected. 
If communication data format is integer of four bytes or float of four bytes, "No conversion", "Byte 
conversion", "Word conversion" and "Conversion in word" can be selected.

1.3.6 Function Description 
1. Select output source 
Simulation input is available for DI tag. 
When the simulation input switch SWSIM is ON, the input signal is from SIMIN. SIMIN can be set 
manually in the panel or FBD debugging interface or from other function blocks. 
When SWSIM is OFF, input signal is from corresponding DI module. Original status of input is 
recorded in RAWAL parameters no matter input signal are from simulation input or DI module. 
2. Negate DI input 
When IVO is ON, negate raw value RAWVAL but RAWVAL is not changed; When IVO is OFF, 
output the original status of DI without processing. 
 
Tip: 
In the status of force, negating is unavailable. 
 
3. Process in force status 
When SWAM is OFF, it is in force status. In this case, DI output value is set manually by operators, 
not according to the value sent by I/O module. 
4. DI accumulator of rising
--- pag 22 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 19 
DI tag can count positive jumps of input digital. If the rising edge accumulation switch AVSTRT is 
ON, AV is added by 1 when a positive jump is checked. If the rising edge accumulation switch 
AVSTRT is OFF, rising accumulation is stopped. 
If rising edge accumulation is reset, i.e., rising edge of AVRST occurs, accumulated value AV is set 
0. 
5. Alarm processing 
 
Fault alarm 
When the module or communication is faulty, tag fault alarm ERR is displayed (ERR 
alarm is not generated in the status of controller debugging). 
 
Status alarm 
If ON status alarm is enabled, when DI tag value is ON, the tag is in the status of ON 
alarm and ON status alarm bit of corresponding quality code is set 1; When DI is 
changed from ON to OFF, the tag is in normal status and ON status alarm bit of 
corresponding quality code is set 0. 
If OFF status alarm is enabled, when DI tag value is OFF, the tag is in the status of OFF 
alarm and OFF status alarm bit of corresponding quality code is set 1; When DI is 
changed from OFF to ON, the tag is in normal status and OFF status alarm of 
corresponding quality code is set 0. 
 
Jump alarm 
If positive jump alarm is enabled, when DI jumps from OFF to ON, positive jump alarm is 
generated (RJUMP). 
If negative jump alarm is enabled, when DI jumps from ON to OFF, negative jump alarm 
is generated (FJUMP). 
 
Alarm shield 
When the function of tag alarm shield is set, corresponding alarms are only recorded but 
not displayed in real time. 
6. Set in fault status 
If the status of non-force and non-simulation is selected, i.e., tag value is from DI module, when 
data sent by DI module is suspicious, tag value is maintained and dithering alarm is marked. When 
data sent by DI module, tag value is set according to configuration. Tag value can be set Maintain, 
ON and OFF.

1.5 Fail-safe 
ECS-700 system has powerful functions of fault self-test and processing. The fault diagnosis can 
reach channel level directly and the troubleshooting is set when configuring. 
1.5.1 Troubleshooting 
 
AI tag: 
When AI tag fails (module failure, channel failure or communication failure) and fail-safety 
is enabled, according to the configuration of fail-safety, AI tag outputs can be set as: hold, 
set upper limit and lower limit of the measuring range, set the preset value of faults and 
proximity extended range limits. 
 
Selects “Hold” and enters fault mode , then PV value of AI holds the value of last 
cycle. 
 
Selects “Set upper limit of the measuring range” and enters fault mode, then PV 
value of AI will be set as the upper limit of the measuring range. 
 
Selects “Set lower limit of the measuring range” and enters fault mode, then PV 
value of AI will be set as the lower limit of the measuring range. 
 
Selects “Set the preset value of faults” and enters fault mode, then PV value of AI will 
be set as the preset value of faults. 
 
Selects “Set proximity extended range limits” and enters fault mode, if the sent 
original code is smaller than the lower limit of the extended measuring range, PV 
value of AI will be set as the lower limit of the extended measuring range. If it is 
greater than the upper limit of the extended measuring range, PV value of AI will be 
set as the upper limit of the extended measuring range. If it enters fault mode due to 
module lost while the value is held within the normal measuring range, PV value of 
AI tags will be set as the lower limit of the extended measuring range. 
 
For DI 
In VFIOBuilder, Hold, ON or OFF can be selected in troubleshooting. 
 
For AO 
In hardware configuration software, “Hold” and “Output the preset value” can be selected 
from the channel fail-safety mode. 
 
For DO 
In hardware configuration software, “Hold” and “Output the preset value” can be selected 
from the channel fail-safety mode. 
Different faults have different processing modes. The fault types can be listed as below:
--- pag 28 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 25 
 
Fault in channel level of I/O module 
 
Fault in module level of I/O module 
 
Fault in the communication between I/O module and controller. 
Fault in channel level of I/O module 
Fault in channel level of I/O module means only one channel of the module fails (like 
disconnection and short circuit). 
When this kind of fault occurs, the solution is shown as below: 
 
AI tag: troubleshoot immediately, generate ERR alarm and output fault value. 
 
DI tag: troubleshoot immediately, generate ERR alarm and output fault value. 
 
AO tag: delay for 8 seconds and enter the fault safety status, generate the ERR 
alarm and output holding or output the pre-setting value. 
 
DO tag: delay for 8 seconds and enter the fault safety status, generate the ERR 
alarm and output holding or output the pre-setting value. 
Fault in module level of I/O module 
Fault in module level of I/O module includes module lost, model difference, configuration 
difference and severe fault 
When the Fault in module level of I/O module occurs, the tag troubleshooting is shown below: 
 
AI tag: troubleshoot after delay for 8 seconds, generate ERR alarm and output fault 
value. 
 
DI tag: troubleshoot after delay for 8 seconds, generate ERR alarm and output fault 
value. 
 
AO tag: delay for 8 seconds and enter the fault safety status, generate the ERR 
alarm and output holding or output the pre-setting value. 
 
DO tag: delay for 8 seconds and enter the fault safety status, generate the ERR 
alarm and output holding or output the pre-setting value. 
Fault in the communication between I/O module and controller. 
After the communication between the AO/DO module and the controller is broken for 5 seconds. 
the module will enter the fault safety status and output holding or output pre-setting value 
according to the configuration. 
The reasons of the communication breaking include L-BUS communication fault between I/O 
module and the controller or remote nodes, the E-BUS communication fault between the controller 
and remote nodes, and the fault in remote nodes. 
In the operation mode, if communication of the controller with AO/DO module is broken.
--- pag 29 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 26 
 
When the communication is broken for less than 5 seconds: AO/DO module will 
hold the output during the breaking time, and output the program calculation value 
as soon as the communication is normal. 
 
When the communication breaking time is between 5 and 8 seconds: AO/DO 
module will hold the output value firstly and then output the fault safety value after 5 
seconds during the breaking time, and output the program calculation value as soon 
as the communication is normal. 
 
When the communication breaking time is greater than 8 seconds: AO/DO module 
will hold the output value firstly, output the fault safety value after 5 seconds, enter 
the fault safety status and output the fault safety value after 8 seconds. When the 
communication is normal, the AO/DO tag will exit the fault safety status 
automatically. If the upriver is connected to loop or handholder, then it will enter the 
MAN mode and output the fault safety value. If the upriver connection does not exist, 
then output program calculation value immediately. 
The fault safety value mentioned above includes output holding and output the pre-setting value 
these two modes. 
1.5.2 Output specifications of controller in different start modes 
Start modes of controller 
According to different start conditions, there are 3 start modes as below: 
 
Cold Startup 
 
Instantaneous Power-off 
 
Hot Startup 
Cold Startup 
Definition: the controller restarts in the case of which the controller is power-off for 5 seconds or 
power-off protecting battery is useless. 
In the latter case, the system needs to load configuration again. 
If the power-off protecting battery works well in the cold restarting mode, then the controller will 
read back the output value of I/O module within 8 seconds after restart. When it is over, the output 
specification of the controller is shown below: 
 
If the AO tag is under non-Force mode before power-failure, controller will output the 
read-back value when the upriver of the AO tag is connected to the controlling 
function block. When there is no connection, then output the program calculating 
value. 
 
When AO tag is under the force mode before power-off, then the controller will 
output the read-back value. 
 
When DO tag is under non-force mode before power-failure, then output the
--- pag 30 ---
IO Tag User Manual 
 27 
program calculating value. 
 
When DO tag is under the force mode before power-off, then the controller will 
output the read-back value. 
Instantaneous Power-off 
Definition: controller restart when the power-off time is less than 5 seconds and the power self-test 
is normal. 
The power-off protecting battery is normal and data stays still around the instantaneous power-off 
point, the controller will read back the output of I/O module after start for 8 seconds. When it is over, 
the output specification of the controller is shown below. 
 
When the upriver of the AO tag is connected to the controlling function block and the 
AO tag is under non-Force mode before power-off, if it is set to the manual-back 
mode, controller will output the read-back value; if it is set to automatical back mode, 
then output the program calculating value. 
 
When AO tag is under the force mode before power-off, then the controller will 
output the read-back value. 
 
When DO tag is under non-force mode before power-off, then output the program 
calculating value. 
 
When DO tag is under the force mode before power-off, then the controller will 
output the read-back value. 
Hot Startup 
Definition: the controller restart in the condition of non-power-off which is caused by resetting. 
The data inside controller will keep fixedness during hot-startup. After restart, controller continues 
to calculating and output according to status of before reset, thus ensure the control continuity and 
stability.
