Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and 
TCS-900 
Section 1 Introduction 
The TCS-900 system configuration and tag can be integrated into the ECS-700 system through 
VisualField (hereinafter referred to as VF) software, so as to realize the monitoring of the TCS-900 
system by the VF system software. 
1.1 Function 
VisualField can integrate TCS-900 system configuration and its tags into the VF system software, 
realizing the reduction on the operation and maintenance of equipment by users, and the 
uniformed management and monitor of alarm, trend, and SOE. 
 Support adding TCS-900 controller to VF system configuration 
 Support the import and export of SafeContrix configuration in VF system software 
 Support TCS-900 system for clock synchronization according to ECS-700 system clock 
 Support the integration of TCS-900 system data into VF system software through 
SISPatch 
 Support one SOE server to record SOE information of TCS-900 and ECS-700 
1.2 Application Scenario 
The following figure shows a typical network diagram of the integration of the TCS-900 system and 
the ECS-700 system.
--- pag 5 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 3 
 
Figure 1-1 Typical network of TCS-900 integrated into ECS-700 system 
 
The TCS-900 system shown in the figure above is integrated into the typical networking of the 
ECS-700 system: 
 
SISPatch, SafeContrix software, SOE software, OPC software are installed in the VF 
engineer station in ECS-700 to obtain the tag data, SOE record and OPC data of the 
TCS-900 system. 
 
SOE is installed on the SOE server in ECS-700 to access the SOE data from ECS-700 
and TCS-900 systems. 
 
The TCS-900 system performs clock synchronization according to the clock 
synchronization server in the ECS-700 system.
--- pag 6 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 4 
Section 2 Preparation 
Before the ECS-700 system is integrated with the TCS-900 system, the following tasks need to be 
completed in the VF engineer station: 
 
Install SafeContrix V1.10.05.01-M 
 
Install SISPatch. The SISPatch program is saved in the "Add-On" path of the SafeContrix 
software installation package by default. 
 
 
Tip: 
When the TCS-900 system is integrated into the ECS-700 system, there is no need to install 
SafeContrix clock synchronization software, SOE software, OPC software during the 
installation of the SafeContrix software. Please install the software as needs.
--- pag 7 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 5 
Section 3 Configuration Flow 
When integrating TCS-900 to ECS-700 through VF software, you need to operate according to the 
following flowchart. 
 
Figure 3-1 Operation flow diagram of integrating VF with TCS-900
--- pag 8 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 6 
Section 4 Configuration 
This section mainly introduces how to add TCS-900 control station in VF software, add TCS-900 
system tag and add TCS-900 system monitoring screen. 
4.1 Add TCS-900 Control Station in VxSysBuilder 
In the VF project, after adding the control domain of the TCS-900 system, you can jump from the 
VF software to the TCS-900 system configuration software SafeContrix. After completing the 
configuration, saving and downloading in the SafeContrix software, the TCS-900 system 
configuration can be published to each node of the ECS-700 system. 
Through the following steps, you can add the TCS-900 control station: 
1) Open the VF system structure configuration software, and open the VF project. 
2) Select "Control Domain Configuration" in the navigation tree of the VF project, and select "Add 
Control Domain" in the right-click menu. 
3) Right-click the added control domain in the navigation tree, and select "Add Control Station" in 
its right-click menu. The configuration interface shown in the figure below will be displayed in 
the right configuration area. 
 
Figure 4-1 Select controller type 
4) Select SCU9010 or SCU9020 in the “Type”.
--- pag 9 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 7 
 
Attention: 
 
A control domain can contain both ECS-700 control station and TCS-900 control 
station. 
 
After configuring the TCS-900 controller type and controller address, if you open 
the TCS-900 configuration software SafeContrix for configuration in subsequent 
operations, you cannot modify the controller type, project name, and controller 
address. 
 
After importing SafeContrix configuration or modifying the address of the 
address of the control station of TCS-900 in VFSysBuilder, if the address of 
TCS-900 controller is different from that in VF, users can open Safecontrix 
through VFExplorer, then the address of control station in TCS-900 in the 
SafeContrix will be automatically updated to the address set in VFSysbuilder. 
 
4.2 Configure Clock Synchronization Server 
When the TCS-900 control station is integrated into the ECS-700 system, the TCS-900 control 
station will synchronize its clock in accordance with that in the configured clock synchronization 
server in the ECS-700 system. 
1) Select "Global Default Configuration" in the navigation tree in the VFSysBuilder, and the clock 
synchronization server configuration interface shown in the figure below will be displayed in 
the configuration area on the right. 
 
Figure 4-2 Example 
As shown in the figure above, When VF project includes TCS-900, users can select “Software 
clock synchronization server (ECS-700)” or “Hardware GPS (ECS-700)”. 
 
Tip: 
If the clock synchronization server’s address in TCS-900 is different with that of VF 
project, TCS-900 configuration software will automatically update the address of the clock 
synchronization server in TCS-900 configuration.
--- pag 10 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 8 
4.3 Manage TCS-900 Configuration 
When the TCS-900 system is included in the VF software, the TCS-900 system configuration can 
be carried out by import, or it can be directly jumped to the SafeContrix software for the TCS-900 
system configuration. 
After adding the TCS-900 system configuration to the VF project, the TCS-900 system 
configuration can be published to each operation node in the VF project. 
4.3.1 Import/Export TCS-900 Configuration 
The VF system software supports the import and export of the TCS-900 configuration in the form 
of a .zip file, thereby simplifying the configuration process. 
Export configuration 
TCS-900 configuration in VF project can be exported as .zip files by the following steps: 
1) Select TCS-900 control station in the navigation tree in VFSysBuider, and select "Export 
Control Station" in its right-click menu. 
2) In the pop-up "Save As" dialog box, select the file name and path of the TCS-900 system 
configuration export file. 
Import configuration 
The VF system software supports the import of two kinds of configuration files and the control 
station configuration in TCS-900 exported from VF software. 
Through the following operations, you can import the TCS-900 system configuration in .zip format 
to the VF project. 
1) Select TCS-900 control station in the navigation tree in VFSysBuilder, and select "Import 
Control Station" in its right-click menu. 
2) In the pop-up "Open" dialog box, select the zip file and click "Open". 
 
Tip: 
Please enter TCS-900 controller type is as the same as that in the file you want to import, 
otherwise the import fails. 
 
4.3.2 Configure TCS-900 System Configuration 
Open SafeContrix in VF software, create or edit TCS-900 configuration. 
Preparation
--- pag 11 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 9 
Before opening the TCS-900 configuration in VF, you need to make sure that the TCS-900 
configuration has been compiled and passed. 
1) Open the VFExplorer software. 
2) In the configuration tree, select the control station where the TCS-900 system is located, 
and select "Open from Configuration Server" in its right-click menu. The configuration 
area on the right will be displayed as 
. 
3) Click “Edit” to open SafeContrix. In SafeContrix, users can do configuration. 
 
Create configuration 
If the TCS-900 control station doesn’t be imported with the configuration before opening 
the software, then open SafeContrix and create TCS-900 project configuration. At the 
same time, users need to configure administrator’s account and password. 
 
Open the configuration 
If one TCS-900 configuration is imported into the control station before opening the 
SafeContrix software, open the TCS-900 project corresponding to the imported 
configuration. 
4) when SafeContrix is opened, in SafeContrix software, edit the TCS-900 configuration, 
compile, debug and download. 
5) Select the edited TCS-900 control station in the VFExplorer software navigation tree, and 
select "Save to Configuration Server" or "Save to Configuration Server and Keep 
Locked" in its right-click menu. Through this operation, the TCS-900 configuration of the 
local engineering station will be saved to the configuration server. 
 
Tip: 
 
When editing the TCS-900 configuration, up to 4 SafeContrix programs can be 
opened at the same time for TCS-900 configuration. 
 
When SafeContrix software is called in VFExplorer, the configuration operation 
functions of SafeContrix software such as "Open", "New", "Backup", and 
"Recent File" are invalid. When the SafeContrix software is used alone, the 
TCS-900 configuration created in the VF project cannot be opened. 
 
4.4 TCS-900 Tag Configuration 
The tag of the TCS-900 system needs to be connected to the VF system through SISPatch and 
loaded into the VF system in the form of a TCS-900 driver. The TCS-900 tag loaded into the VF 
system can be used for monitoring configuration.
--- pag 12 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 10 
4.4.1 Preparation 
Before performing TCS-900 tag configuration in the VF system, the following tasks need to be 
completed. 
 
Install SISPatch correctly 
 
Complete TCS-900 system configuration 
4.4.2 Download TCS-900 Configuration into VF System 
Through the following operations, you can import the TCS-900 tag into the VF system and 
manage it. 
1) Open the domain variable configuration software, select "Edit> Operation Domain Driver 
Configuration" in the menu bar, and the interface as shown in the figure below will pop up. 
 
Figure 4-3 I/O driver settings 
 
2) Click "Add IO Driver" on the pop-up I/O driver configuration interface, and the I/O driver 
configuration wizard interface will pop up.
--- pag 13 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 11 
 
Figure 4-4I/O driver settings wizard 
3) Select "TCS-900 Driver" in the driver list, and click "Next".
--- pag 14 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 12 
 
Figure 4-5 Drive program name prompt 
4) Click "Finish" to end the driver configuration and enter the TCS driver configuration interface. 
 
Figure 4-6 TCS-900 driver configuration 
5) Click the toolbar icon 
 to open the open folder, where you can select the TCS-900
--- pag 15 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 13 
configuration to load. 
 
Figure 4-7 Download TCS-900 configuration 
 
 
Tip: 
When TCS-900 system is integrated into VF software, TCS-900 project under VF configuration 
saving path should be selected. By default, the TCS-900 system is saved in the path of "D: 
ECSdata: Project Name: control: control domain name: control station name" with the suffix 
of. Sisprj. 
 
6) Select the TCS-900 configuration to load and click open, and return to the TCS drive 
configuration page to add the loaded TCS-900 configuration to TCS driver, as shown in the 
following figure.
--- pag 16 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 14 
 
Figure 4-8 TCS driver configuration interface 
The control station after importing is identified as "the last 2 bits of TS + IP address", such as ts0.2. 
7) After loading the TCS-900 configuration, the TCS-900 configuration information can be 
configured according to the following table. 
Table 4-1 TCS-900 configuration’s property 
Configuration Item 
Configuration Instruction 
Control station name 
The name of the control station can only contain numbers / English 
letters and symbols " - ", " _ ", " . ", up to 128 characters, and the name cannot be 
repeated. 
Configuration path 
Added note about not supporting SAMS and PAT cards 
Tag prefix 
Users can avoid tags with duplicate names as importing multiple TCS-900 
configuration. Users can add a prefix to the TCS-900 tags by stations in VF software.. 
Tag name case 
conversion 
In the drop-down list, select whether to perform case conversion. 
 
lowercase is selected, the TCS-900 tag names (except the suffix) imported 
into VF are displayed in lowercase. 
 
uppercase, the TCS-900 tag names (except the suffix) imported into VF are all 
displayed in uppercase. 
 
4.4.3 Configure TCS-900 Tag’s Property 
After loading TCS-900 configuration, the tags in the configuration can be configured as the domain 
variable tags of VF. 
1) On the TCS driver configuration page, select the tag tab to display the interface shown in the 
figure below.
--- pag 17 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 15 
 
Figure 4-9 TCS driver tags configuration 
2) Select the tag in the tag list and click the Save button 
 in the toolbar. 
3) Return to the domain variable configuration interface, and the selected tag will be added as 
the drive tag of VF, as shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 4-10 TCS-900 driver tag example 
4) Configure the properties of the tag. 
Double click the tag to be configured in the tag list, and configure the tag properties in the tag
--- pag 18 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 16 
configuration interface as shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 4-11 TCS-900 tag property configuration example 
 
Tips: 
For detailed configuration of tag attributes, please refer to the Domain Variable 
Configuration Software User Manual. 
 
4.5 TCS-900 HMI Configuration 
In VF software, TCS-900 control station can be diagnosed and the tag in TCS-900 system can be 
monitored. 
4.5.1 Preparation 
Before TCS-900 monitoring configuration in VF system, the following tasks need to be completed. 
 
Correct installation of sispatch 
 
Complete TCS-900 system configuration
--- pag 19 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 17 
4.5.2 Add TCS Controller Diagnosis to Graphics 
After installing the SISpatch installation package, the SIS system real-time diagnosis control can 
be selected on the flow chart configuration toolbar. Users can view SIS fault diagnosis information 
through real-time diagnosis control. 
1) Open the flowchart editing software, click the icon 
 in the quick toolbar on the left, that is 
"TCS control station diagnostic control", press and hold the mouse to drag on the canvas to 
show a rectangular box. As shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 4-12 Add diagnostics control 
2) Double click the control, or right-click to select control properties to open the window as shown 
in the following figure.
--- pag 20 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 18 
 
Figure 4-13 Diagnosis control properties 
3) Click 
 to download configuration files. 
When selecting to download configuration, users should select the TCS-900 project in the saving 
path under VF configuration. By default, TCS-900 is saved in the path of “D: \ECSData\Project 
Name\Control\Control Domain Name\Control Station Name”, and its suffix is .sisPrj. 
 
Figure 4-14 Download configuration files 
 
4) After loading the configuration file, click OK to take effect, and the schematic diagram of the 
configuration will be displayed.
--- pag 21 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 19 
 
Figure 4-15 Control station configuration 
In the monitoring, if the corresponding indicator above the card is red (such as: 
), it means 
that the card is faulty. Double click the card slot and the diagnosis information window pops up, 
with two tabs of real-time diagnosis and detailed diagnosis. There will be corresponding actual 
value after each diagnostic item. If the diagnostic item fails, it will be displayed in red. 
For detailed diagnosis information and indicator identification of TCS-900 system card, please 
refer to the SafeManager Software User Manual. 
4.5.3 Other Monitor Configuration 
After configuration of TCS-900 tag, TCS-900 tag can also be added to various monitoring 
interfaces of VF for monitoring. The monitoring configuration method of other monitoring screens 
is basically similar to that of ECS-700 tag. It will not be repeated here. For detailed operation,
--- pag 22 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 20 
please refer to the HMI Config User Manual. 
4.6 Publish Configuration 
After adding TCS-900 system configuration in VF project by importing or directly editing, TCS-900 
system configuration can be released to other nodes in VF project. 
1) Select TCS-900 control station in configuration tree. 
2) Select "save to configuration server" or "save to configuration server and lock" in its 
right-click menu. 
3) Select the menu "Edit > configuration release", TCS-900 configuration will be released to 
other nodes of VF project in the form of all release. 
 
The TCS-900 system configuration will be released to each VF node in the form of 
overall release 
 
TCS-900 monitoring configuration and tag configuration information will be 
published to each VF node in the form of incremental publish. 
 
After TCS-900 control station configuration being edited, saved to the configuration 
server, it supports to be published into the running list for diagnostic software to 
analyze.
--- pag 23 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 21 
Section 5 Monitor TCS-900 
When TCS-900 system is integrated into VF, TCS-900 system can be monitored through tag panel 
and alarm list. For detailed operation, please refer to SISPatch User Manual.
--- pag 24 ---
Management of the Integration of ECS-700 and TCS-900 IM41S06-E 
 22

Section 1 Overview 
VisualFiled system software supports two types of OPC servers. 
 
OPC servers installed with VisualField system software include VFOPCSvr and 
VFOPCAEServer. 
VFOPCSvr is used to transmit the real-time data from tags of top and bottom machines 
from ECS-700 to the OPC clients. 
VFOPCSvr and VFOPCAEServe respectively provides data to up to 30 clients. 
 VFOPCAEServer is used to transmit the process alarms in the local domain and 
crossed domain, system alarms, SOE and operation logs of ECS-700 to OPC clients. 
In which, the process alarms include the fied tag alarm in ECS-700, added alarms of 
field tags and domain variable tags of JX-300XP/ECS-100. 
 
OPC server installed with OPC independent package: independent OPC server. 
PC installing the software package can be OPC DA (Data Access) server or OPCAE 
(Alarm& Event) server. 
The real-time data of control station tag in ECS-700 system can be sent to OPC client via 
OPC DA server. 
Alarm information and operation log of control station tag in ECS-700 system and SOE 
records in ECS-700 system and TCS-900 system can be sent to OPC client via OPC 
A&E server. 
ECSDASvr and ECSAESvr respectively provides data to up to 30 clients. 
By VFOPCSvr and ECSDASvr, tag's information will be transmitted to OPC client. And 
the tag's information includes: 
 
Analogy tag provides tag's type, value, timestamp, access right, scan rate, unit and 
range. 
 
Digital tag provides tag's type, value, timestamp, access right, scan rate. 
Tag's access right can be configured in VFOPCSvr and ECSDASvr, for detail refer to "2.2.2 
Configure Writing Tag" and "3.3.1Configure DA Server".

Section 2 VF OPC Server 
This section describes VF OPC server's usage including application and instruction. 
2.1 Application of VF OPC Server 
VF OPC server can be applied in independent project and joint project. 
 
In independent project (the project without inter-domain), VF OPC server acquires the 
tag information in the current project and sends to the OPC client. 
 
In joint project(the project with inter-domain), VF OPC server acquires the tag 
information in the current project and referenced domain and sends to OPC client.

Figure 2-1 shows the typical application of VF OPC server in independent project.

from controller via SCNetA/B network. 


control station and its domain variable information collected by VF OPC server via OPC 
private network.

 
Data Source Configuration 
Use OPC client to connect with VFOPCAESvr and start VFOPCAESvr. Select the 
right-click menu "Data Source Configuration" in the system tray after VFOPCAESvr 
starts, to bring up the dialog shown below. User can configure the SOE data server 
address in dialog. After the configuration is successful, the SOE information in 
VFOPCAESvr will be obtained from the server. 
 
Figure 2-10 Data source configuration 
 
Reload Configuration 
When VF is configured and released, VFOPCAESvr will acquire configuration 
information synchronously and obtain alarms based on the configuration information. 
When the configuration in VFOPCAESvr is inconsistent with VF, user can select the 
right-click menu "Reload Configuration" of VFOPCAESvr to synchronize the latest VF 
configuration. 
 
Push or not push suppress alarms 
In the VF system, it is supported to pre-process the nuisance alarm by suppressing the 
alarm, so as to avoid the influence of the nuisance alarm on the system. When 
VFOPCAESvr pushes alarms to the OPC client, you can choose to push or not push 
suppressed alarms. 
By default, VFOPCAESvr pushes suppressed alarms to the OPC client. 
If you do not need to push to suppress alarms, you can right-click VFOPCAESvr in the 
system tray and uncheck "Push to suppress alarms" in its pop-up menu. 
 
Display the domain alias

Section 3 Independent OPC Server 
OPC independent package includes OPC DA and OPC A&E functions. OPC independent package 
can be installed and applied either independently, or with VisualField, their functions will not 
influence each other. 
 
Server for OPC DA is SUPCON. ECSDASVR, for OPC A&E is SUPCON. ECSAESVR. 
 
ECSDASVR conforms to OPC DA V1.0 standards and OPC DA V2.0 standards. OPC DA 
client can read/write tags of ECS-700 control station in the operation domain. 
 
As the OPC A&E server, ECSAESVR conforms to OPC A&E V2.05 standards, and can 
provide the alarm information, operation log and SOE record (ECS-700or TCS-900) of 
tags in ECS-700 control station to OPC A&E client. 
3.1 Application of Independent OPC Server 
 
Figure 3-1 Typical Application Network of Independent OPC Server 
In the application as shown as Figure 3-1, the independent OPC server in ECS-700 system 
collects the information (including data and alarm) of tags of ECS-700, and sends the tag 
information to the OPC client in the third party system. 
Besides, this section introduces 2 configuration ways for independent OPC server.

Install OPC independent package 
 
Start "OPC Standard A&E Server" or "OPC Standard DA Server". 
 
Import configuration in the format of ZIP file. 
 
Select operation domain 
After installed OPC independent package, ECSDASvr can get the controller's real-time data and 
A&E data, and ECSDASvr can get the operation log from the operation record server through the 
SCNet.

configuration.

Section 1 Start Supervision 
1.1 Responsibilities of Operator 
 
Monitor the running of DCS to prevent potential dangers. 
 
Intervene in the system operation at any time to ensure s safety and normal production. 
 
Modify system authorized operation parameters. 
 
Alarming treatment: There will be sound prompt in technical index alarming, and the 
alarming information will be displayed in alarm bar and process alarm table. After the 
alarm is accounted for, turn off alarm sound by silence button and confirm the alarm. 
 
Discover abnormal events and inform system maintainers to address. 
1.2 Steps for Supervision Software Startup 
1. Double click the shortcut icon
of VFLaunch or click [Start/ Program/ 
VisualField/ VFLaunch], and the dialog box for operation domain configuration 
selection will pop up, as shown in Figure1-1. 
 
1
--- pag 5 ---
Operator Guide 
 
Figure1-1 Configuration Selection dialog box 
2. Select the operation domain to login. Current operator station (engineer station) can 
only login the domain (set in system structure configuration software) it belongs to. 
3. Select supervision start mode. Three start modes are as follows: 
 
Data Server: current node will provide history data query service to operation 
domain as data server after startup. 
 
History Data Server: current node will serve as history data server to collect history 
trend data after startup. 
 
Supervision Software: the operator station (engineer station) will start up real-time 
supervision software if user selects this mode, otherwise it won’t. 
 
Tip: 
At least one startup mode should be selected to start up supervision. 
The startup mode of server is the same as that in configuration. 
 
4. Configuration version check: If inconsistency of between local configuration and that 
in the configuration server is found, a prompt asking for configuration 
synchronization will pop up. Click “Yes” to synchronize the configuration. 
Furthermore, the Update button can also be used for configuration synchronization. 
 
2
--- pag 6 ---
Operator Guide 
 
Tip: 
“Update” means to update modified configuration files, which is more efficient. “Update All” 
means to update all configuration files, which is more reliable. 
 
5. The dialog box will not be displayed during next startup if user selects “Don’t show 
configuration selection dialog box next time”. To display it again, click the icon 
 
on toolbar and select “System Information” in the pull-down list, the dialog box of 
system information will pop up, and click the button “Options”. 
Then the dialog box of “VisualField Global Options” will pop up. Cancel the selected 
option “Not display configuration selection dialog box when starting supervision 
software”. 
 
Figure 1-2 VisualField Global Options 
6. Login supervision after confirmation. The default user here is “Observer” in all cases, 
and there’s no operation team by default, the supervision interface is shown in 
Figure 1-3.

“Login” in the pull-down menu. The user login dialog box is shown in Figure 1-4.

shown in Figure 1-5.

Section 3 FAQ 
3.1 IIS Install Process Problem under a Windows Server System 
Error Description 
Progress Bar Not Loading or Suspended for a Long Time When Installing IIS under a Windows 
Server System 
This is because of the higher security level of a Windows Server system than a non-server 
Windows system. In case where the software installs services by a script, the system performs a 
series of security configurations and related security checks, which is likely to cause a slow or 
even suspended installation. 
 
Figure 3-1 Progress Bar Not Loading or Suspended for a Long Time When Installing IIS 
Solution 
Left click the commands shown above in CMD, and then quickly press “Enter” key to continue the 
installation process manually. 
3.2 PID Service Unavailable 
Error Description
--- pag 16 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software Installation User Manual IM41S11-C 
13 
This is usually caused by improper installation or manual uninstallation. 
Solution 
Please run the Service Manager (enter services.msc in CMD to open it) to confirm if a service 
named APC-PIDService exists; if it does not exist, you need to fix the issue by using the 
installation package. 
3.3 Failed to Start PID Service 
Error Description 
Failed to Start PID Service, the Executable Program Corresponding to the Service Does Not Exist 
This is usually caused by the loss of the service file or the tampering of its file name when a 
service is not started. 
Solution 
1) Run the Service Manager (enter services.msc in CMD to open it) to select the service 
whose service name is “APC-PIDService”. 
2) confirm if the exe file corresponding to the service exists (right click to open the attribute 
page, find the path of the executable file under the normal page, and go to the path to 
check if the file exists). If it does not exist, it means the file has been deleted or moved, 
and the issue should be fixed by re-installation. 
3.4 Failed to Start PID Service 
Error Description 
Failed to Start PID Service, the IP Address Configured Does Not Match the Local Address 
This is usually caused by the change of the local IP address, making it inconsistent with the IP 
address specified in the system configuration file. 
Solution 
 
Click the menu Start menu-> All programs-> PID performance evaluation-> Tools-> IP 
setting tool to open the IP setting tool, where you can reset the IP address and make it 
consistent with the one specified in the configuration file. 
 
It is recommended to use a fixed IP address as the local address, otherwise the system 
cannot be used normally.
--- pag 17 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software Installation User Manual IM41S11-C 
14 
3.5 Failed to Start APC-PIDService in Service Manager 
 
This is usually caused by the change of the local IP address, making it inconsistent with 
the IP address specified in the system configuration file. The cause of this issue can be 
verified in the Event Viewer. Enter “eventvwr” in CMD to open the Event Viewer and find 
the error message sourced from APC-PIDService. If error message as shown in the 
figure below are found, it means that the local IP address has changed, and that of the 
PID system needs to be re-set (click the menu Start menu -> All programs -> PID 
performance evaluation -> Tools -> IP setting tool to open the IP setting tool, where you 
can reset the IP address and make it consistent with the one specified in the 
configuration file). 
 
It may be caused by the loss of the exe file corresponding to the service (right click to 
open the attribute page, find the path of the executable file under the normal page, and 
go to the path to confirm if the file exists. If it does not exist, it means that the file has 
been deleted or moved, and the issue should be fixed by re-installation). 
 
Proxy service VFSDKWRAPPERHOSTING doesn’t start. 
3.6 VF Monitor 
The PID evaluation service agent running log shows: VF monitoring is not turned on, please turn it 
on! 
This problem occurs mainly because when the service agent reads the real-time value through the 
C++ interface provided by VF, it needs to call the runtime interface, that is, the VF monitoring 
startup software needs to be turned on. 
3.7 Open PIDWeb Monitor Failure 
This problem can be checked from the following two points: 
 Whether IIS has been installed, and whether the Web site has been successfully 
deployed to IIS during the installation process. 
 If the deployment of the previous site is normal, further check whether 
NETFRAMEWORK in IIS has been checked for installation. 
After the two points are finished, restart PIDWeb. 
3.8 No Net Framework Installed on New PCs or Servers 
This problem will detect whether the system has installed the .Net Framework plug-in during the
--- pag 18 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software Installation User Manual IM41S11-C 
15 
PID service installation process. If not, it will automatically install the plug-in that comes with the 
system installation package (for detailed .Net Framework installation, please refer to "Installing 
PID Performance Monitoring Evaluation on the Server Side" software"). If it has already been 
installed, you can click to cancel the installation of the plug-in during the PID service installation 
process. 
3.9 Modify PID Service’s IP Address 
If the PID service address is configured incorrectly or the default IP address is selected during the 
PID service installation process, as shown in the figure below. After successfully installing the 
software, you can modify the address through the software installation path: 
1) Double-click ProjectSavePathSetting.exe under "C:\Program Files 
(x86)\SUPCON\VFPIDCPA-LOOP\Tools\" to pop up the configuration interface as shown 
in the figure below. 
2) After reconfiguring the IP address and saving path of the evaluation results in the pop-up 
interface, click "OK". 
3) Restart the PID service. 
3.10 CPU Overload as PID Performance Evaluation Runs 
CPU overload is usually caused by too many users online simultaneously. According to the VF 
work station’s requirement to the CPU load performance, it is recommended to limit the number of 
online users within 2 to avoid that the CPU is overload.

PID Performance Evaluation Software 
Section 1 Glossary 
Glossary 
Description 
PID Loop 
Process industrial fundamental automation control loop name 
Section 2 Overview 
PID performance evaluation software is aiming to PID controller in terms of performance 
evaluation, optimization and monitoring. 
2.1 Main Function 
PID performance evaluation software mainly includes: 
 
Real-time monitoring of the performance of the control loop, evaluation of 
comprehensive indexes of control loop performance, display of intuitive evaluation 
reports. 
 
In addition, the user can selectively adjust the control loop according to the loop 
evaluation report. 
 
The software can also generate the evaluation report periodically, so that the user can 
query the historical evaluation report, which has greatly improved user-friendliness and 
saved the time of searching for the historical evaluation report. 
 
PID Performance Evaluation Software obtains workshop and equipment statistical 
reports and loop evaluation results from the client and displays them on the web page 
through the evaluation service, and provides online modification and real-time evaluation 
for such parameters as reference time, loop level, and evaluation standard. 
2.2 Software Structure 
Each module of PID performance evaluation software is described in the table below:
--- pag 6 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
2 
Table 2-1 Module list 
Module Name 
Description of Functions 
Configuration module 
Its functions include the management of loop information, loop grouping, 
evaluation plan and equipment template. 
Overview module 
It shows the overall running status of the loop and the equipment. 
Assessment module 
It shows the list of loop evaluation results and a detailed evaluation 
report. 
Statistical report module 
It shows loop reports, including the daily report, weekly report, monthly 
report and the custom report. 
 
2.3 Software Authorization 
When user starts PID performance evaluation software, software authorization is required.
--- pag 7 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
3 
Section 3 Start to Configure 
The configuration process of PID performance monitoring needs to be carried out on the 
equipment with PID configuration software installed. PID configuration software provides functions 
such as loop management, loop grouping management, and evaluation plan management. 
 
Loop information management 
Before performing PID new energy monitoring, you need to add a PID loop first. 
 
Loop group management 
Considering that there are often more loops in the field, this software supports loop grouping to 
facilitate daily management. 
 
Evaluation plan management 
In order to realize online regular evaluation, this software provides the function of 
creating evaluation plan, allowing users to push the created evaluation plan online to the 
background evaluation service. 
 
This software supports the creation of a single loop evaluation plan 
 
Support the creation of an evaluation plan for the entire workshop or the entire plant 
 
Support the creation of standard evaluation plans such as daily, weekly, and monthly 
reports 
 
Support the creation of customized evaluation plans
--- pag 8 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
4 
3.1 Manage the Loops 
This section mainly introduces the configuration methods of loops that need to be monitored 
before PID performance monitoring, including creating loops, modifying loops, and deleting loops. 
3.1.1 Software Interface 
After configuring the PID loop, you can create a new loop in the PID performance monitoring 
evaluation module through the following operations. 
Open the VF configuration management software VFExplorer. 
Select “Monitoring Configuration> Operation Domain” in the navigation tree. 
Select “Loop Evaluation” in the navigation tree of the VFHMICfg software that pops up, as shown 
in the figure below. 
 
Figure 3-1 Start Operation Domain in VF menu 
In the PID performance evaluation configuration software shown, select the address where the 
PID performance evaluation server is located. Once the server address is entered and the 
connection is successful, it will be automatically saved. 
After selecting the server address, the configuration interface pops up.
--- pag 9 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
5 
 
Figure 3-2 PID Performance evaluation configuration interface 
 
Status: online configuration, indicating that the current mode is online configuration; 
 
Total: 18, indicating all current loops; 
 
Authorize: 5,000, indicating the total number of loops authorized to be available for 
evaluation; 
 
Used: 15, indicating the number of loops for which an evaluation has been available. 
3.1.2 Create a New Loop 
As adding monitoring loops in the PID performance evaluation software, two modes including 
manual creation and import in batches are supported. 
Manual creation 
1. 
Click “Loop > New Loop” in the menu bar and the dialog box pops up.
--- pag 10 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
6 
 
Figure 3-3 Window for Creating a New Loop 
2. 
Enter the loop name for monitoring in “Name” and select device templates. System can 
fast create a new loop according to the basic information and suffix of tags. It is noted 
that: 
 When policy is “constant”, tag cannot be modified yet values can be modified. 
 When policy is “Tag read”, tag can be modified yet values cannot be modified. 
3. 
Click “Evaluation Parameters” tab and configure these parameters as shown in the figure 
below.
--- pag 11 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
7 
 
Figure 3-4 Page of Evaluation Parameters 
4. 
Advanced settings 
Click “Advanced settings” and the interface pops up.
--- pag 12 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
8 
 
Figure 3-5 Advanced Settings of Evaluation Parameters 
5. 
Configure it according to the actual requirement and click “OK” and then save it. 
Import in batches 
1. 
Click “Loop > Add loop” in the menu bar . 
2. 
Click “OK” to obtain PID loop tags form VF software. 
3.2 Loop Grouping Management 
Considering that there are often more loops in the field, this software supports loop grouping to 
facilitate daily management.Rules 
3.2.1 Rules 
When grouping, you need to pay attention to: 
 
There is no restriction on the level of grouping, users can create a multi-level grouping 
structure
--- pag 13 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
9 
 
You can add another group under the group, but only the leaf node group can add a loop, 
and the group that already contains sub-groups cannot add a loop. 
3.2.2 Configuration Steps 
1. Select “Management> Loop Group Management” in the menu bar, and the interface 
shown in the figure below pops up. 
2. Configure the grouping structure in the left area of the interface shown in the figure 
above. 
First select a grouping node and click “Add”, a new sub-node named “New Group 1” will 
be created under the selected grouping node, and the number will be counted up. If the 
selected grouping node already contains loops, then it is not allowed to add For 
sub-groups, the following prompt message will pop up, “The group that has been added 
to the circuit can no longer add sub-groups.” 
In addition, the group structure can be modified through the delete, move up, and move 
down buttons. 
3. After selecting the group in the grouping structure, configure the properties of the group 
in the right area and add the PID loop to which it belongs. 
First select a group node and click “Edit”. If it does not contain subgroups, a loop 
selection window will pop up, as shown in the figure below. 
4. In the list shown in the figure above, select the circuit to be monitored and tick it. 
5. Click “OK” to add the checked circuit list to the group and close the window. 
3.3 Evaluation Plan Management 
The evaluation plan is divided into three types: standard evaluation plan, custom evaluation plan 
and loop correlation analysis plan. 
1. Select “Management> Evaluation Plan Management” in the menu bar, and the 
“Evaluation Plan Management” interface pops up. 
2. Select the evaluation type and configure the evaluation plan. 
 
Select “Standard Evaluation Plan” in the “Evaluation Plan” navigation tree to display the 
evaluation configuration interface dialog box shown in the figure below. In the “Standard 
Evaluation Plan”, daily, weekly, and monthly reports can be configured according to 
actual needs. 
 
The standard evaluation plan cannot be deleted, the name cannot be modified, and the 
properties of the related report can be modified. 
 
Select “Custom Evaluation Plan” in the “Evaluation Plan” navigation tree to display the
--- pag 14 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
10 
evaluation configuration interface dialog box shown in the figure below. Select the group 
or loop to be evaluated in the “Customized Evaluation Plan” on the right, and enter the 
evaluation cycle period. 
It should be noted that the name of the custom evaluation plan cannot be repeated or 
empty. The configuration items with * must be filled in. 
 
Select “Loop Correlation Analysis Plan” in the “Evaluation Plan” navigation tree to display 
the evaluation configuration interface dialog box shown in the figure below. Select the 
group or loop to be evaluated in the “Customized Evaluation Plan” on the right, and enter 
the evaluation cycle period. 
It should be noted that the name of the custom evaluation plan cannot be repeated or 
empty. The configuration items with * must be filled in. 
3. After the loop is managed and the evaluation plan is specified, it is necessary to start the 
loop evaluation. 
As shown in the figure below, select the circuit to be evaluated in the evaluation list, and 
select “Enable Evaluation> Yes” from the right-click menu to add the desired circuit to the 
evaluation plan
--- pag 15 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
11 
 
Section 4 View the Evaluation Report 
After configured the PID loop to be evaluated, you can view the report. 
4.1 Preparation 
Before the client monitor the PID loops, the following tasks should be finished. 
 
Install Chrome and configure PID monitor interface 
 
Install VF software and configure PID loop tags 
 
Configure the PID performance evaluation 
4.2 Configure Evaluation Properties 
Select the icon 
, and the “Generate evaluation report” dialog box shown as figure below will 
popup.
--- pag 16 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
12 
 
Figure 4-1 Generate Evaluation Report 
4.3 View the Evaluation Report 
 
View the evaluation report. Open the PID evaluation report WEB window via “PID 
CONTROL” button in VF menu, enter the evaluation report interface.
--- pag 17 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
13 
 
 
 
Figure 4-2 Entrance to PID Evaluation Report 
 
Start the Chrome browser and enter “http://localhost:6601/” in the browser address to 
jump to the evaluation report display interface shown in the figure below. 
 
 
 
Figure 4-3 View the Generated Evaluation Report 
 
The main interface consists of the top menu region, the left navigation region and the 
content display region, etc. Their functions are described below in turn.
--- pag 18 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
14 
 
Figure 4-4 Each Region of the Main Interface 
Top menu 
The top region of the software mainly displays the software name, company logo, user information, 
common operating buttons and module switching buttons, as shown in Figure below. The meaning 
of each button is as follows: 
 
Figure 4-5 Top Menu 
 
“Help” is to view the system manual; 
 
“Overview” is to switch to the overview functional module; 
 
“Assessment” is to switch to the evaluation functional module; 
 
“Statistical report” is to switch to the statistical report functional module. 
Left navigation tree map 
The navigation tree map on the left side of the system mainly shows the grouping of PID controller 
loops, and the interface is shown in Figure below. When the user clicks a node, the overview 
report corresponding to this node will be displayed in the system content region.
--- pag 19 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
15 
 
Figure 4-6 PID Controller Loop Grouping 
 
Content display region 
As shown in Figure below, the content display region mainly shows the overview reports of 
different groups (grouping can be customized by the user, e.g. workshop, and equipment) and 
switches to the content display regions of different modules.
--- pag 20 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
16 
 
 
 
Figure 4-7 Content Display Region 
4.3.1 Overview Module 
Enter the home page of controller performance assessment software and the grouping of PID
--- pag 21 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
17 
controller loops is displayed under the left navigation tree. A refinery in this example has a control 
domain, a control domain has a control station, and a control station has dozens of PID loops. 
Left-click the refinery, and the comprehensive performance index about its PID loops will be 
displayed on the overview page on the right. Similarly, left-click a control domain or control station 
name, and the comprehensive performance index about the workshop or the equipment will be 
displayed on the overview page. 
Left-click to select different nodes (physical structure of the loop, refinery→ control domain→ 
control station) in the left navigation menu, and count the overview report of the node. The report 
mainly includes the basic situation, self control rate, steady rate and comprehensive performance 
of the loop, comprehensive loop status and loop status statistics. 
 
Figure 4-8 Overview Module 
4.3.2 Real-time Statistics of the Equipment 
The overview interface shows the real-time statistics of the equipment by default, including all 
loops of the current software, equipment self control and steady rates of child nodes and 
comparative information, which will be refreshed automatically every 2min to facilitate users to 
monitor and understand the operation of loops and devices in real time.
--- pag 22 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
18 
 
Figure 4-9 Equipment Real-time Statistics 
4.3.3 Real-Time State of the Loop 
The interface of real-time state of the loop shows the real-time self control, steadiness and 
operations of all loops, number of alarms and the longest time with no alarm. In addition, filtering 
can be carried out based on the child node to which the loop belongs and sorting or induction can 
be conducted in accordance with different indexes to help users accurately find loops with different 
operation problems. 
 
Figure 4-10 Real-time State of the Loop 
4.3.4 Basic Situation of the Loop in the Past Day 
Enter the home page of controller performance assessment software and the grouping of PID 
controller loops is displayed under the left navigation. A refinery in this example has a control
--- pag 23 ---
PID Performance Evaluation Software User Manual IM41S12-C 
19 
domain, a control domain has a control station, and a control station has dozens of PID loops. 
Left-click the refinery, and the comprehensive performance index about its PID loops will be 
displayed on the overview page on the right. Similarly, left-click a control domain or control station 
name, and the comprehensive performance index about the workshop or the equipment will be 
displayed on the overview page. 
Left-click to select different nodes (physical structure of the loop, refinery→ control domain→ 
control station) in the left navigation menu, and count the overview report of the node. The report 
mainly includes the basic situation, self control rate, steady rate and comprehensive performance 
of the loop, comprehensive loop status and loop status statistics.

PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
Section 1 Overview 
In the function block library provided by the VisualField system software, the PID function block 
(PID) and the extended PID function block (PIDEX) support parameter self-tuning functions, and 
provide two solutions: quick tuning, and identification tuning. 
 
Quick tuning 
It is generally used for tuning the PID parameters of the loop by using the expert 
experience library when the site has not been started or the data is insufficient. 
 
Identification tuning 
For the single-input single-output system, the current mature model identification and 
tuning methods are adopted to realize the self-tuning of PID parameters through four 
parts: data preselection, model identification, credibility evaluation, and model-based PID 
parameter calculation. 
This function block supports two model forms, namely “second-order inertial model” and 
“adaptive model”. PID parameter calculation also supports two methods: “internal model” 
and “amplitude phase margin”.
--- pag 5 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
2

1.2 Function Block Panel 
1.2.1 Switch 
The PID function block and PIDEX function block panel does not open the self-tuning function by 
default, and it can be turned on or off by modifying the configuration file. 
1) Find the “UserSettings\GlobalUserSettings.ini” file in the installation directory (if the file does 
not exist, you can open VFSetup.exe and click OK to generate the file); 
2) Add or modify the configuration item “PIDShowTune=1” under the “[GlobalUserSettings]” 
node (a value of 1 means turning on the tuning function, a value of 0 means turning off the 
tuning function); 
3) After saving the modification, you need to restart the VF monitoring to take effect. 
After enabling the auto-tuning function, complete the parameter-tuning settings in the “Auto-
tuning” and “Settings” tabs shown in the figure below, taking the PID function block as an 
example.
--- pag 6 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
3 
 
Figure 1-1 PID function block “Self-tuning” and “Tuning settings” tab example 
 Self-tuning: used for PID self-tuning. 
 Tuning settings: When PID self-tuning is performed, it is used for detailed self-tuning 
parameter setting. 
During the tuning process, the alarm information of the tuning status of each time is displayed at 
the right lower corner on the function block panel, including: 
 Stop Tuning; 
 Start Tuning; 
 Waiting Stable; 
 Relay Surge; 
 Finish Tuning; 
 Tuning Failed.
--- pag 7 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
4 
Section 2 Parameter Self-Tuning 
When using it on site, you can first use the quick tuning to achieve quick-tuning. If the effect is 
found to be unsatisfactory after tuning, identification tuning can be used. 
2.1 Quick Tuning 
Quick tuning is generally used to set the parameters of the loop by using the expert experience 
library when the site is not started or the data is insufficient. Through the following steps, quick 
tuning can be achieved. 
1) Click the “Enable Tuning” button in the Auto Tuning tab to turn on the quick tuning function. 
2) In the “loop type” drop-down list, select the current detection type, including flow, pressure, 
liquid level, temperature and others. 
3) In the “loop characteristics” drop-down list, select the characteristics of the current loop. 
 
When the loop type is flow, the loop characteristics support unknown, gas flow, liquid flow, 
and others. 
 
When the circuit type is pressure, the circuit characteristics support unknown, liquid 
pressure, gas pressure, steam pressure, fuel gas pipeline or others. 
 
When the circuit type is liquid level, the circuit characteristics support unknown small 
container liquid level (higher than 1.5 meters), medium container liquid level (higher 1.5-2 
meters), large container liquid level (higher than 2 meters), and others. 
 
When the loop type is temperature, the loop characteristics support unknown, heating 
furnace, heat exchanger/, reaction tower, column temperature, and others. 
4) Click “Quick Tuning”, the system will automatically form the setting data according to the 
selected “loop type” and “loop characteristics”. 
5) Click “Update” to download the generated setting data to the controller. 
 
 
Attention: 
When the user has the write authority for the PID parameters “PB”, “TI” and “TD”, he 
has the authority to perform the “update” operation, otherwise the “update” button 
cannot be operated. For detailed configuration instructions of panel permissions, please 
refer to HMI Config Software User Manual.
--- pag 8 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
5 
2.2 Identification Tuning 
Identification tuning is for single-input single-output systems, using historical data in the trend 
(SV/MV/PV, etc.), using the current mature model identification and tuning methods, through data 
preselection, model identification, parameter calculation, and credibility evaluation Four parts 
realize the self-tuning of PID parameters. 
1) Add historical data server, add SV/MV/PV in PID loop to historical trend tag library. 
2) Click the “Enable Tuning” button in the Auto Tuning tab to turn on the PID identification and 
tuning function. 
3) Data pre-selection 
Data pre-selection refers to the data pre-processing of historical data (SV/MV/PV, etc.), quality 
codes, and tag names in the trend, and the selection of data for model identification. Data pre-
selection supports two methods: automatic pre-selection by the system and manual pre-selection. 
 
Automatically select data 
Click “Data Pre-select”, and the system automatically filters out sufficient incentive data. 
 
Manually select data 
By right-clicking a data pre-selection area, select “Delete Auto-tuning Range” to delete a 
section of parameter setting data pre-selection area. As shown in Figure 1-1, the data 
preselection area selected in the trend screen is marked as a yellow shaded area. The 
left and right sides of this area are the data preselection lines, and the specific start and 
end times are marked above the preselection line. 
You can drag the left and right borders of the data pre-selection area to adjust the start 
time and end time. 
 
Tip: 
 
The length of a single piece of data must be at least 1 time of the open-loop steady-
state time. For general circuits (such as liquid level circuits), the data length can be 4-8 
hours. 
 
For loops with longer response times, the time range of the data should be increased 
accordingly. 
 
The length of time for data preselection shall not exceed 30 days at most, otherwise it 
will easily lead to data reading timeout and failure 
 
After performing data pre-selection in the above two ways, you can drag the pre-selection line to 
adjust the data pre-selection area.
--- pag 9 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
6 
Generally, the richer and longer the data segment contains, the better the recognition effect is. 
4) Click “Tuning” to perform model identification, credibility evaluation, and PID parameter 
calculation based on pre-selected data segments to generate a first-order or second-order 
model, model credibility parameters, and PID tuning parameters. The PID tuning parameters 
include PB Value, TI value, TD value. 
5) (Optional) Detailed settings of PID auto-tuning 
For more detailed configuration such as response speed and smoothness of the tuning results, 
please refer to the next section for details. 
6) After confirming the credibility, click “Update” to download the generated PB value, TI value 
and TD value to the controller. 
2.3 Detailed Settings for PID Self-Tuning 
For high-level users, you can adjust the results of PID auto-tuning to achieve a tuning result that 
is more in line with site requirements. The detailed settings of PID auto-tuning are completed in 
the “Tuning Settings” tab shown in Figure 11. The specific settings include: 
 
Adjust response rate and stability 
Adjust the “Response Speed” and “Stability” through the slider to complete the PID tuning 
in real time. You can view the preview of the response effect of the PID tuning below. 
Note: When the “setting method” is “internal mold”, the “stability” slider cannot be 
operated. 
 
Configure identification method and tuning method to realize PID tuning 
According to the type of field application, select the type that matches the field application 
in “Identification Method” and “Setting Method”. 
“Identification method” includes second-order inertial model and adaptive model. 
 
The system defaults to select the “second-order inertia model”, which is suitable for 
most industrial application sites. If an experienced user wants to identify by 
comparing multiple model forms, you can choose the “adaptive model” option. This 
method will automatically obtain a first-order model with lag, a second-order 
underdamped model with a lag, or a second-order model based on the identification 
results. Over-damped model with hysteresis. 
 
“Setting method” includes “internal model” and “amplitude phase margin”. 
The default option is “internal model”. The internal model PID is suitable for systems 
with no lag or small lag. The response of the system with large lag is slow, but there 
is almost no overshoot. If an experienced user judges the system as a system with 
large lag, it is also You can select “Amplitude and Phase Margin” for PID tuning.
--- pag 10 ---
PID Self-Tuning User Manual 
7 
This tuning method is faster than “Internal Model”, but there will be a certain amount 
of overshoot.

Section 2 System Application Overview 
The network device can be compartmentalized to PROFINET IO controller and PROFINET IO 
device on the basis of PROFINET specifications. PROFINET IO controller can manage and 
initiate communication with PROFINET IO device. The communication module connects standard 
PROFINET slave station device into system. Through E-BUS and controller communication, in-
system control station and operation station can realize message both-way communication with 
other control system and intelligent device, and make heterogeneity device as subsystem of 
SUPCON DCS. 
PNCon software is the software to configure PROFINET communication module (interface 
module). And the PNCon software is mainly used to configure hardware of PROFINET module in 
ECS-700 system. Table 2-1 indicates the match software and communication module in system. 
Generally COM723-S are used as communication modules.

stations are connected by one communication module (interface module). 


User can configure the PROFINET site, view and set the basic properties of station, add 
submodules to the slave station and set the parameter information of module with the PROFINET 
configuration management software (PNCon).

PROFINET communication module acts as the master station of PROFINET and the various 
PROFINET IO devices act as slave station of PROFINET.

Phase Class Function Block User Manual 
Section 1 Introduction 
The Phase class is the smallest element of SFC of the task to complete the process. In the 
sequence control logic, the Phase class constitutes elements such as operation, unit, etc., and is 
used to perform operations such as opening the valve and stirring, as shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 1-1 The Comparison Figure between VF System Software and S88.01 Standard 
The VF system software follows the ISA S88.01 standard and the IEC-61131-3 standard, and 
utilizes Phase function block edited in SFC to achieve sequence control logic. 
1.1 Main Features 
 
The Phase function block supports the call from each control station, and is allowed to 
modify the structure after being referenced. 
 
Phase class function block supports custom parameters and uses SFC language editing 
logic. 
 
Phase class function blocks support monitoring and alarm rules. 
 
Supports 5 Phase function block folders, each folder can support up to 255 Phase 
function blocks. Phase class function block folders do not allow duplicate names. Phase 
class function blocks do not allow duplicate names and cannot be duplicated with system 
function blocks and user function blocks. 
 
Support online publish
--- pag 6 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
2 
When adding (adding incrementally import method), modifying (apart from alarm property) 
and deleting Phase function blocks, only online publish is necessary. 
 
Support offline publish 
When the alarm properties in the global function block are changed, or users import 
Phase function blocks in a overwriting way, the offline publish is necessary. 
1.2 Technical Features 
Performance 
Description 
The maximum steps RUNNING supports 
128 steps 
The maximum steps HOLDING supports 
32 steps 
The maximum steps PAUSING supports 
32 steps 
The maximum steps RESTARTING supports 
32 steps 
The maximum steps ABORTING supports 
32 steps 
The maximum steps STOPPING supports 
32 steps 
The maximum conditions Transition supports 
16 
The maximum characters FAILMONITOR supports 
10000 characters (including space and enter) 
The maximum characters for single step code 
10000 characters (including space and enter) 
The maximum items of messages 
50 
The maximum custom parameter 
512 
The maximum custom alias 
128 
*The maximum memory of custom data (parameters, alias) is 1420 bytes. 
1.3 Status Illustration 
Phase function block supports three status and it executes different actions under different status. 
1.3.1 Status in Phase function block 
Phase function block supports static status, transient status and FailMonitor status. 
 
Static status 
Static status is a status Phase function block will enter when a program ends normally. 
The initial status of a program is Idle and then it enters Complete status when the 
program ends normally. 
 
Transient status 
Transient status includes Running, Stopping, Pausing, Restarting and Aborting, They are 
used to configure the logic related to the operations in field, corresponding to the 
Operation in ISA S88.01. 
 
Exception Handling Status FailMonitor
--- pag 7 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
3 
It is used to monitor the status of programs. When a program is in Running, Pausing and 
Restarting, the program will enter Holding status after FailMonitor finds it with an 
exception. Only the exception is eliminated in Holding status can the program enter 
Restarting status. 
1.3.2 Status-switching Rules 
In normal conditions, status will be automatically switched according to the order: IDLE > 
RUNNING > COMPLETE. When you need to debug programs, you can manually switch status by 
the command buttons on the Phase panel. Status switching is controlled by Start, Stop, Hold, 
Pause, Restart, Abort, Reset and Resume. 
The switching rules of Phase status are shown in the table below. 
Table 1-1 Status-switching rules of Phase Status

Section 2 Add Phase Class Library and Phase 
Function Block 
Before applying the Phase function block, you need to firstly create a Phase function block folder 
and a Phase function block. 
2.1 Add new Phase Class Library and Function Block 
Operational Steps 
You can create a Phase class library and a Phase class function block by the following operations. 
1. Open the configuration management software VFExplorer. 
2. Right-click “Phase Class Library” in the system tree, and select "Create Phase Library" 
from the right-click menu. The “New Phase Library” dialog box will pop up. 
3. Enter “Name” and “Description” in the dialog box, and click “OK” to complete the creation 
of the Phase class folder. 
 
“Name” is a combination of Chinese and English, numbers, and underscores. It 
supports up to 16 characters. 
 
“Description” supports up to 64 characters. 
4. Click the created Phase class folder and select “New” in the right-click menu command. 
The “Create new phase function block” dialog box will pop up. Enter “Name” and 
“Description” in the dialog box, and click “OK” to complete the creation of the Phase 
Function Block. 
 
“Name” is a combination of letters in uppercase, numbers, and underscores. The 
default setting is to start with “G_”. It supports up to 16 characters. 
 
“Description” supports up to 64 characters. 
 
 
Attention: 
When creating Phase function blocks, it is noted that its name cannot be the 
same as those of Phase Library, function blocks in medical system, global 
function blocks and ST keywords.
--- pag 10 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
6 
Status Instruction 
The newly created or imported Phase function block will be displayed under the Phase Function 
Block Library folder as shown below. 
 
Figure 2-1 View the Phase Function Block in the Navigation Tree 
 
The navigation tree displays the status of the Phase function block: 
 
The function block corresponding to 
 is in the local editing lock status (can be 
edited in the local). 
 
The function block corresponding to 
 is in the unlocked status (non-editable 
status). 
 
The right area shows the Phase function block is composed of two parts in the VF 
system, and the two parts are “logic” and “parameter”. After creating a Phase function 
block, you need to configure its parameters and logic. 
 
“Logic” is used to configure the logic of Phase function blocks. 
 
“Parameter” is used to view the basic parameters of Phase function blocks and to 
configure macro. 
2.2 Import Phase Class Function Block 
In addition to creating a new Phase function block, the VF system software supports the import of 
the Phase function block in the form of an .ex file. Therefore, the Phase function block can be 
reused to simplify the configuration process. 
Import 
You can import the Phase class function block by the following steps: 
1. 
In the navigation tree, select the function block library you need and select “Import 
function block” from the right-click menu. 
2. In the pop-up “Import Function Block” dialog box, select the .ex file to be imported and 
click “Open” to complete the import of the Phase function block. 
The imported Phase function block shall be a Phase function block exported from VFExplorer and
--- pag 11 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
7 
the file format is “.ex”. If the Phase function block to be imported already exists in the Phase 
function block library, you will be prompted whether to replace it. Please act according to the actual 
situation. 
Export 
The Phase class function block can be exported by the following operations: 
1. Select the Phase function block to export in the navigation tree and click “Export Function 
Block” from its right-click menu. 
2. Select the specified path in the “Export Function Block” dialog box, and enter the name of 
the exported Phase function block in “Name”. 
3. Click “Save” in the “Export Function Block” dialog box to export the specified Phase 
function block. 
 
Tip: 
The configuration of phase function block password, panel and icon as well as the upgrading 
of function block is similar to those of global function block. For details, please refer to Global 
Function Block Guide.
--- pag 12 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
8 
Section 3 Edit Phase Function Block 
In VF system software, Phase function block is edited by VFSTModule software. By the operations 
below, you can enter VFSTModule. 
1. Select the Phase class function block in the editable status in the navigation tree of 
VFExplorer. 
2. Click “Logic” in the right area and select the right-click menu command “Edit”. The 
“VFSTModule” program configuration interface in the figure below will pop up. 
 
Figure 3-1 “VFSTModule” Program Configuration Interface 
“VFSTModule” program configuration interface mainly consists of the parts shown below: 
 
Screen-switching list, click the area displayed in the right bottom corner. Select “status 
transition graph” and the right bottom corner will display the status transition graph of the 
current Phase. Select “Running” and other transient status, then the program editing 
interface will be displayed on the right bottom corner. 
 
Parameter List. It is used to display each parameter of the selected types in “Parameter 
Type Navigation Tree”. 
 
Parameter Type Navigation Tree, it is used to select the parameter types you need 
check. 
 
Status change view/transition program editing interface 
Status change view, it is used to display all the status and changing relationship Phase
--- pag 13 ---
Phase Class Function Block User Manual IM41S49-E 
9 
Function Block. Double click the transient program to enter transient editing interface. 
Transient program editing interface is used to edit the specific transient logic. 
3.1 Configure Program Parameters 
The parameters of the Phase function block include fixed parameters and custom parameters. 
 
The fixed parameter is the built-in parameter of the Phase function block. For details, see 
“Fixed Parameters”. 
 
Custom parameters. You can configure the parameters to be used in the Phase logic 
according to actual needs. 
3.1.1 Configure Custom Parameters 
Custom parameters such as recipe parameters and report parameters, etc phase function block 
supports are shown below. 
1. In the Parameter Type Navigation Tree, select the type to which the parameter belongs 
and select the right-click menu command Add ** Parameter. The new parameter will be 
displayed under the selected parameter type. 
2. Double-click the newly added parameter to bring up the parameter configuration dialog 
shown in the figure below.
--- pag 14 ---

is noted that “Operating Parameters” and “Recipe Parameters” support the configuration

1) 
In the property configuration interface of “Operating Parameters” and “Recipe 
Parameters”, check “Enable Range”, “Range Upper Limit”, “Range Lower Limit” and 
“Unit” will be in a configurable state. 
2) 
In the editable state, configure the upper range limit, lower range limit, and unit of the 
parameter. 
It is noted that as parameter is configured as “array”, parameters won’t support

3.1.3 Built-in Timer Description 
Time pausing, restarting and resetting can be realized by the built-in timer in Phase. 
VF system provides 4 Phase timers, which are TIMER1~TIMER4. Each timer has 4 parameters, 
which are CMDTn, TIMERSn, TIMERMn and TMRPTNn. n represents the corresponding timer, 
such as TIMERS1, which means a parameter of TIMER1 in a second level. 
The use of corresponding parameters is shown in the table below: 
Parameter 
Value 
Function 
CMDTn 
This parameter is used to specify the operation mode of the timer. The value range of 
this parameter is 0 ~ 4: 
CMDTn = 0, reset the nth timer, if CMDT4 = 0 means reset timer TIMER4 
CMDTn = 1, start timer n, such as CMDT1 = 1 means start timer TIMER1. 
CMDTn = 2, suspend timer n, such as CMDT2 = 2, it means suspend timer TIMER2. 
CMDTn = 3, the n-th timer synchronizes minutes to seconds, for example, CMDT3 = 3 
means the synchronization timer TIMER3 minutes to seconds. 
CMDTn = 4, the n-th timer synchronizes seconds to minutes. For example, CMDT4 = 4 
means the synchronization timer TIMER4 seconds to minutes. 
TIMERSn 
This parameter is used to indicate the second-level timing parameter of the specified 
timer. The value of n ranges from 1 to 4. 
TIMERMn 
This parameter is used to indicate the graded timing parameters of the specified timer. 
The value of n ranges from 1 to 4. 
TMRPTNn 
This parameter is used for the working mode of the timer. The value of n ranges from 1 to 
4. 
0 means accumulative timing mode, such as TMRPTN1 = 0 means timer TIMER1 works 
in accumulative timing mode If TMRPTN1 = 0, TIMERM1 = 10, it means time 10 minutes.
1 indicates the countdown mode, such as TMRPTN1 = 1 indicates that the timer TIMER1 
works in the countdown mode. If TMRPTN1 = 1, TIMERM1 = 10, it means the countdown 
is 10 minutes.

Section 4 Apply and Monitor Phase Class Function 
Block 
This section mainly introduces how to use Phase function blocks in the user program after 
configuring Phase function blocks, and how to view Phase function blocks in monitoring. 
4.1 Apply Phase Function Block in Custom Program 
After configuring the Phase function block, the Phase function block can be applied to the user 
program to realize the sequential control strategy. The phase function block after instantiation can 
monitor its running status in real-time monitoring. 
4.1.1 Application Steps 
After configuring the Phase function block, you can apply it to the user program by the following 
steps. 
1. Save to the configuration server 
To ensure that the Phase function block is used throughout the project, you need to save 
the configured Phase function block to the configuration server. 
Select the Phase class function block in the navigation tree and select “Save to 
Configuration Server” or “Save to Configuration Server (Locked)” in its right-click menu. 
2. Synchronize the Phase class function block at the control station. 
Before the control station uses the Phase function block, in order to ensure that it is the 
latest Phase function block, the operation of updating function block should be performed 
first. 
Select the Control Station in the navigation tree and select "Synchronize Function Block 
Library" in its context menu. 
It is noted that the Phase function block can be applied only when the controller type in 
the control station is FCU713-S. 
3. Instantiate the Phase function block in the custom program 
1) Select the control station which needs to apply Phase function block in the navigation 
tree and open the custom program. 
2) Select the Phase function block library in the “Function Block Library” and select the 
Phase function block to be added to the custom program in the function block list to
--- pag 44 ---

add it to the custom program. 
3) Double click the added custom program to bring up the property configuration box, 
and configure the tag name of the Phase function block in the “Function block tag 
name”.

function block is applied in custom programs.

Section 5 Appendix—SFC Introduction 
5.1 SFC Introduction 
Phase function blocks use SFC to program. 
SFC is an acronym for Sequential Function Chart and a kind of programming language in 
IEC61131-3. It is used to edit sequential control programs such as the program controlling motor 
to start and stop. 
5.2 Program Composition 
The SFC program in the VF system software supports sequence diagrams of multiple structures, 
and the sequence diagrams of multiple structures are composed of steps, conditions, branches, 
transitions, and etc. 
5.2.1 Basic Elements 
The basic elements of the SFC program include the start step, step number, selecting branch, 
transition, action description, selecting branch-selecting junction, parallel branches-parallel 
junctions, and end step, as shown in the following figure. SFC programs include the following 
elements, but not every element is required.
--- pag 55 ---

The structure of the program is divided into: sequential structure, parallel structure, selection 
structure, jump structure, and loop structure, as shown in the following table. 
Structure Illustration 
Structure Name 
The sequential structure consists of steps and 
conditions. 
Step is used to perform production-related 
operations. 
Condition is used to configure the conditions for 
entering the next step.
--- pag 56 ---

 52

Structure Name 
Parallel branches can operate simultaneously 
in the same cycle, and their execution is 
independent of each other. 
The transition condition under the parallel 
branch can operate only if all the steps at the 
end of the parallel branches are activated and 
their transition conditions are all satisfied. 
Selection branches are usually added after the 
step. 
The execution order of the selected branches is 
starting from the branch where the condition is 
satisfied first and going into next in turn. 
If multiple transition conditions are met at the 
same time, the leftmost condition in the SFC 
diagram is activated, as 002 shown in the figure 
on the left side. 
A jump consists of an initial transition condition 
and an arrow symbol specifying a jump target. 
If the transition condition of the jump is satisfied, 
the jump will be performed. If there are multiple 
jumps at the jump source location (003), the 
jump where the transition condition is firstly 
satisfied operates firstly. If multiple transition 
conditions are satisfied at the same time, the 
leftmost transition condition is activated.

Report Software 
 1
Report Software 
Section 1 Overview 
In industrial control system, report is a very important and frequently used data record tool. It is 
usually used to record important system data and field data for engineers to check system status 
or technical analysis. 
Report software is one of VisualField software components, including three parts: report 
configuration software, report browse and report server. 
Report configuration software (Normal mode and Excel mode) has window graphic user operation 
interface. The configured report file should be saved in the “rtRpt” subfolder of the system 
configuration folder. 
Report system generates reports by the report server, and it starts up automatically following the 
supervision software by setting the report server 
Report browse supports browsing and editing the generating/generated reports. 
1.1 Performance Specification 
 
The system exports (exports in several seconds in turn) or prints ten pieces of 
reports in one minute at most. 
 
One operation station configures and generates 100 pieces of reports at most when 
data acquisition and report export are both staggered. 
 
The whole report acquires 1000 statistic items at most, and data of 500 tags at most. 
 
One report project supports 200 events or expressions at most. 
 
If there is only one report in the project, the number of rows of the report should not 
be more than 1000 and number of columns should not be more than 100. 
 
One report acquires data of 200 tags at most simultaneously, and each tag only has 
one filling item. If the minimum acquisition interval is not more than 5 seconds, it 
only acquires data of tags not more than 50. 
 
VF supports hot-backup of report 
By hot-backup of report, VF can record from the last record in the report while the 
real-time monitoring restarted after exit. 
By default, report supports hot-backup only if the real-time monitoring restarted in 10 
minutes.
--- pag 5 ---
Report Software 
 2
1.2 Report Configuration Steps 
1. Create the report file: Add the report configuration and set the report filename in the 
designated operation team to enter report editor. 
2. Edit the report format: Design and edit the whole format of the report and the report 
text. 
3. Definite the event: Set the data recording event and exporting event of the report.

new rows into the table.
