Section 2 Overview 
2.1 Introduction 
SCMasterRUS is a tool for managing the dongle authority, by which user can view the current

2.2 Features

The dongle has the function of viewing the current authority, by which user can view the current 
authority of dongle conveniently. 
High Flexibility 
The dongle has the function of upgrading the new authority, by which user can upgrade the new 
authority of dongle remotely by updating file whenever and wherever.
--- pag 4 ---
SCMasterRUS 
2 
Section 3 Manage Dongle Authority Remotely 
This chapter introduces how to manage the dongle authority remote via SCMasterRUS. 
3.1 Steps 
 
Tip: 
User can only add new authority to the dongle when upgrading remote, but cannot delete 
the current authority. 
 
The flow of upgrading dongle remote via SCMasterRUS is shown in Figure 3-1. 
 
Figure 3-1 Flow of upgrading dongle remotely 
 
The feature file of dongle is in the format of “.scc2v”. 
 
The updated file of dongle is in the format of “.scv2c”, which includes the new authority 
of dongle. 
3.2 Startup 
3.2.1 Precondition 
These 2 preconditions below should be satisfied before starting SCMasterRUS:
--- pag 5 ---
SCMasterRUS 
3 
 
The host running SCMasterRUS should only have one dongle inserted. 
 
The version of dongle should not be earlier than HASP HL Pro 3.25. 
If no dongle is inserted or the dongle version is earlier than HASP HL Pro 3.25, a prompt as shown 
in Figure 3-2 or Figure 3-3 will pop up. 
 
Figure 3-2 Prompt when the dongle version is HASP HL 2.16 
 
Figure 3-3 Prompt when the dongle is illegal in other situation 
Details of viewing the dongle version please refer to 4.1View Version and ID. 
3.2.2 Startup Steps 
Follow steps below to start the SCMasterRUS: 
1. Select the start menus [Start/ VisualField / System Tools / SoftwareDog Upgrade 
Tool]. 
2. A decryption prompt of the software will pop up, as shown in Figure 3-4. 
 
Figure 3-4 Decryption prompt 
3. After decrypted successfully, the SCMasterRUS interface shown in Figure 3-5 will open.
--- pag 6 ---
SCMasterRUS 
4 
 
Figure 3-5 SCMasterRUS interface 
3.3 Check Current Authority 
After inserting the dongle to the host and starting SCMasterRUS successfully, follow steps below 
to check the current authority of dongle: 
1. Click the button “Check Features” in the SCMasterRUS interface to pop up the prompt 
of checking progress, as shown in Figure 3-6. 
 
Figure 3-6 Prompt of checking progress 
2. After checking completed, the dongle current authorities checked will be shown in Figure 
3-7.
--- pag 7 ---
SCMasterRUS 
5 
 
Figure 3-7 Checking results 
3.4 Get Feature File 
Follow steps below to get the feature file of dongle: 
1. Click the button “Get C2V File” in the SCMasterRUS interface to pop up a dialog of 
saving C2V feature file, as shown in Figure 3-8. 
 
Figure 3-8 Dialog of saving C2V feature file
--- pag 8 ---
SCMasterRUS 
6 
2. Select the saving path and enter the name of feature file, then click “Save”. 
In default, the file name will be the “saving date and time”. After sending the feature file 
to the vendor, the vendor will generate the updated file according to the feature file and 
the new authority required. 
3.5 Get and Apply Updated File 
Follow steps below to get and apply the updated file of dongle: 
1. Click the button “Get V2C File” in the SCMasterRUS interface to pop up a dialog shown 
in Figure 3-9. 
 
Figure 3-9 Select updated file 
2. Select the updated file and click “Open”, and the SCMasterRUS interface will be shown 
as Figure 3-10.
--- pag 9 ---
SCMasterRUS 
7 
 
Figure 3-10 SCMasterRUS interface after selecting updated file 
After updating the file, the button “Get V2C File” in the interface will become “Apply 
V2C File”. 
3. Click “Apply V2C File” to pop up the success prompt as shown in Figure 3-11. 
 
Figure 3-11 Success prompt 
4. Click “OK” to complete the authority upgrading of the dongle. 
 
Tip: 
Click the underlined words in the icon in upper right corner of the SCMasterRUS interface 
to switch the Chinese and English versions of the software.
--- pag 10 ---
SCMasterRUS 
8 
Section 4 View Dongle Information 
4.1 View Version and ID 
Follow steps below to view the version of dongle: 
1. Insert the dongle to the host. 
2. Open IE, enter the address as http://localhost:1947 and press the “Enter” key. 
3. Open the website shown in Figure 4-1, click “HASP Keys” to view whether the “Key 
Type” is “HASP HL Pro”, and whether the “Version” is later than 3.25. 
 
Figure 4-1 Website showing the dongle version 
 
Tip: 
If the prompt shown in Figure 3-2 or Figure 3-3 still pop up when there is a dongle inserted 
in the host running SCMasterRUS, the dongle version is earlier than HASP HL Pro 3.25. 
Please connect the vendor and change the dongle. 
 
4.2 View Operation Record 
4.2.1 View All Operation Records 
If the SCMasterRUS runs normally, follow steps below to view the operation record of managing
--- pag 11 ---
SCMasterRUS 
9 
dongle authority: 
1. Click the button “Records” in the SCMasterRUS interface to pop up a dialog shown in 
Figure 4-2. 
 
Figure 4-2 Operation Records 
2. Click “Query” to show all operation records in the list below, as shown in Figure 4-3.
--- pag 12 ---
SCMasterRUS 
10 
 
Figure 4-3 Searching results 
4.2.2 Search by Dongle ID 
SCMasterRUS supports to search the operation record by dongle ID, the steps are shown below: 
1. Input the dongle ID in the “Key ID” box of the “Operation Records” interface. 
2. Click “Query” to show all operation records of the dongle in the list below, as shown in 
Figure 4-4.
--- pag 13 ---
SCMasterRUS 
11 
 
Figure 4-4 Search operation record by dongle ID 
Please refer to 4.1View Version and ID to view the dongle ID. 
4.2.3 Search by Operation Type 
SCMasterRUS supports to search the operation record by the operation type, the steps are shown 
below: 
1. Input “Check Features” in the “Operation Type” box of the “Operation Records” 
interface. 
2. Click “Query” to show all operation records of checking dongle authority in the list below, 
as shown in Figure 4-5.
--- pag 14 ---
SCMasterRUS 
12 
 
Figure 4-5 Search operation record by operation type 
Section 5 Notes 
 
Only one dongle can be inserted in the host running SCMasterRUS. 
 
SCMasterRUS supports the remote authority upgrading of software in VisualField series, 
Advantrol-Pro series, GCS/SCADA series etc., but doesn’t support the software stopped 
production or in very old versions, such as the software in AdvanTrol series, 
Advantrol-GCS2 series and SupView etc. 
 
Please make sure that the “hasplms” service is started when using the SCMasterRUS.

Document Version 
Applicable Product Version 
Remarks

SCMasterRUS(V1.00.00.01) 
The first version.

SISPatch 
Section 1 Overview 
SISPatch is a patch package that connects SIS data to VF and achieves centralized monitoring. 
Connect SIS TAG to VF system via domain variable, to monitor the real-time data, diagnosis data 
and trend data, etc. 
 
Section 2 Connect SIS Driver 
Run installation program of SISPatch to install SISPatch Driver. After that, TCS-900 Driver can be 
added when configuring VF domain variable. 
SIS Driver supports to import several SIS projects via domain variable configuration, and import 
SIS project configuration to import SIS project configuration to VF domain variable configuration in 
batch. 
2.1 Configure SIS Driver 
Open domain variable configuration software, select [Edit/Operational Domain Driver Settings (R)] 
in menu bar to pop up the interface below. 
 
Figure 2-1 I/O Driver Settings 
Click "Add IO Driver" in the IO driver settings interface, to pop up the I/O driver settings wizard.
--- pag 5 ---
SISPatch 
2 
 
Figure 2-2 I/O Driver Settings Wizard 
Select "TCS-900 Driver" and click "Next". 
 
Figure 2-3 Input driver program name
--- pag 6 ---
SISPatch 
3 
Click "Finish" to complete the driver program configuration and open the TCS driver configuration 
interface. 
2.2 Configure SIS TAG 
 
Figure 2-4 TCS Driver Configuration 
Click [Edit/ Load(M)] or click 
 in toolbar to load SIS configuration, which should be completed 
in SafeContrix first.
--- pag 7 ---
SISPatch 
4 
 
Figure 2-5 Load SIS configuration 
Double-click to open the selected configuration, and the configuration information will be shown in 
“TCS Driver Configuration” interface. SIS driver management supports to load several project 
configuration files. 
 
Figure 2-6 TCS Driver configuration interface
--- pag 8 ---
SISPatch 
5 
The imported control station will be marked by last 2 fields of TS+IP address, for example TS15.2. 
Control station name and tag prefix can be modified in the figure above. Control station name can 
only contain number, letter or "-", "_" and ".", maximum 128 characters. Names cannot be 
repeated. 
If add several configurations simultaneously, the name of configuration tag added later is repeated 
with that of added before, a tag prefix will be added, the prompt is shown below. 
 
Figure 2-7 Add prefix to tag automatically 
Switch to "Tag" to show the tag filter interface, as shown below. 
 
Figure 2-8 TCS driver tag configuration 
 
Tag filter conditions include "Name", "Data Type", "Description", "IO Address" and 
"Properties". 
 
Select the check box of each row to switch status, press keys "Shift", "Ctrl" and click to 
select several items, to switch status simultaneously, switch status of all selected tags 
with the current check box. 
 
Click "Select All" in the right lower corner of interface to select all tag in current page.
--- pag 9 ---
SISPatch 
6 
Click "Select None" to clear all selected tags. 
 
Click column title to sort the tags by alphabetical order. Click once to sort by ascending 
order, and twice by descending order. 
 
Input key word in search boxes of filter conditions and press "Enter" key to filter the tags 
in list. 
 
Click different control stations in left pane, update properties interface and tag list 
interface, clear filter conditions of tag list in "Tag" tab. 
Click 
 above status column to pop up status filter dialog below. 
 
Figure 2-9 Status Filter 
There are 3 filter conditions: "Selected", "Unselected" and "Selected OR Unselected" (select 
"Selected" and "Unselected" together). 
Click 
 of data type condition to pop up the data type condition to pop up the filter dialog of data 
type. As shown below.
--- pag 10 ---
SISPatch 
7 
 
Figure 2-10 Data Type Filter 
Select various data types from the drop-down menu to filter rows, such as "BOOL", "REAL", "INT" 
and so on. 
Click [File/ Save] or 
 to save configuration. Close driver configuration interface. All selected 
tags have been added to domain variable configuration. As shown below. 
 
Figure 2-11 Add SIS TAG to domain variable configuration 
2.3 Set Alarm Limit 
In Figure 2-11, SIS TAG has been added to domain variable configuration. User can set alarm limit 
for the tags. The setting method is same with ordinary domain variable tags. When real-time value
--- pag 11 ---
SISPatch 
8 
reaches to alarm limit, process alarm will be generated in monitoring. 
2.3.1 Configure Analog Alarm 
Configured analog alarm interface is shown below. 
 
Figure 2-12 Alarm configuration 
 
Alarm Enable: select "Enable Alarm" to enable the alarm settings. Alarm information can 
be set and modified after enable the alarm settings. 
 
Alarm Limit: include LL alarm, L alarm, H alarm, HH alarm, HYS value and change rate 
alarm. The front 4 settings cannot exceed the limited range of basic settings. Change 
rate alarm is shown as range percentage in 0~100. 
 
Alarm Level: set the alarm level for tag, to distinguish the different alarm levels of tags. 
While creating project, alarm level can be configured. In default, the value is low. And 
alarm User can adjust by 
 or input the number directly. 
2.3.2 Configure Digital Alarm 
Digital alarm configuration interface is shown below.
--- pag 12 ---
SISPatch 
9 
 
Figure 2-13 Alarm configuration 
 
Alarm Enable: select "Enable Alarm" to enable the alarm settings. Alarm information can 
be set and modified after enable the alarm settings. 
 
Alarm Mode: digital alarm modes including OFF alarm and ON alarm. 
 
Alarm Level: set the alarm level for tag, to distinguish the alarm levels of tags. Settings 
for alarm level is same with extend configuration variable of analog. 
Section 3 Real-time Diagnosis Control 
After installing SISPatch package, user can select some real-time diagnosis controls of SIS 
system from configuration toolbar of graphics. User can view the SIS fault diagnosis information 
via the real-time diagnosis control. 
Open the graphics drawing software, click 
 (Diagnosis Control of TCS Control Station) in the 
left pane, press the left button of mouse, drag and drop to form a rectangle frame. As shown 
below.
--- pag 13 ---

10 
 
Figure 3-1 Insert diagnosis control

below. 
 
Figure 3-2 Diagnosis control properties 
Click 
 to load configuration file.

11

12

)means that the module has fault. 
Double-click the slot to pop up the diagnosis information interface, which including real-time 
diagnosis tab and detail diagnosis tab. Each diagnosis item has corresponding actual value. 
Diagnosis item with fault is red. 
For detail diagnosis and indicator of TCS-900 system, refer to SafeManager User Manual. 
Section 4 SISPatch Real-time Monitoring 
This section introduces how to monitor SIS TAG, which can be achieved in VisualField real-time 
monitoring software. 
4.1 Start Real-time Monitoring Software 
Steps to start the real-time monitoring software:
--- pag 16 ---
SISPatch 
13 
Select [All Program/ VisualField/ VFLaunch] to pop up the operation domain configuration 
selection interface. 
 
Figure 4-1 Select Configuration 
Select the operation domain to be login and the startup mode of monitoring. 
Click "OK" to pop up the monitoring welcome interface. 
Select the command "User Login" in the dropdown list box of the monitoring header, and select 
"Login" from the drop-down menu, to pop up "Login" dialog shown below.
--- pag 17 ---
SISPatch 
14 
 
Figure 4-2 Login 
Select user name and input password, click "OK" to pop up the main interface of monitoring, and 
start the monitoring successfully. 
4.2 SIS Function Block Panel 
On function block panel of SIS TAG user can: 
 
Monitor and modify the status and parameters of SIS TAG. 
 
Execute parameter settings and control operation. 
 
Achieve monitoring interface jump. 
4.2.1 Panel 
Panels of SIS TAG are shown below.
--- pag 18 ---
SISPatch 
15 
 
Figure 4-3 SIS TAG panels 
The left one above is SIS analog tag panel, and the right on is SIS digital tag panel. 
 Panel pin 
On the right upper corner, the button 
 can be applied in pop-up panel. Click it to 
become 
 , so the panel will be always on top. 
 Close panel 
On the right upper corner of panel, the button 
 is on the pop-up panel, while not on the 
tuning group window. 
 Tag instance name 
Show the tag name or instance name of function block, to distinguish different function 
blocks. 
 Select, alarm, acknowledge 
- 
 Select: select panel as current operation panel. 
- 
 Alarm: tag alarm status of panel. 
- 
 Alarm acknowledge: acknowledge the tag. 
 Alarm, status display region 
Show the current alarm information of tag or function block (such as HH and LL, etc.) and 
status (manual, automatic, cascade and OOS, etc.) 
 Analog data display region 
Show the analog value and unit in tag or function block, such as the PV, MV, SV of PID 
function block. 
 Value display region
--- pag 19 ---
SISPatch 
16 
Show the current value of analog or digital. 
Analog data: show the real-time value of key parameter data dynamically by the bar 
graph. Show the limit values on both ends of scale rod, which also marks with HH, H, L 
and LL. 
Digital data: show the digital value by button, which marks by "ON" and "OFF". The button 
colors of DI and DO buttons can be shown as set in tag configuration. 
Besides, value can be assigned for tag in this region. Input new analog tag value or click 
ON/OFF button of digital. 
Jump Button region 
There are 5 jump buttons at the bottom of panel, 
 are trend, 
graphics, trend, alarm viewer and turning window jump buttons from left to right. Click 
alarm viewer button to pop up the alarm viewer window of tag. 
 Tag description 
Show the description of tag or function block, maximum support 31 characters. 
4.2.2 Start Panel 
Method to start SIS TAG panel is same with starting general tag. Several methods are shown 
below: 
 
Click 
 in the toolbar of monitoring main interface, to pop up the select tag window. 
Select the SIS TAG and click "OK" to pop up the panel. 
 
Double-click the tag in monitoring main interface to start the tag panel. 
 
Double-click the SIS TAG in graphics to pop up the panel. 
 
Double-click the SIS TAG in trend window to pop up the panel. 
4.3 Query SIS alarm 
4.3.1 SIS History Alarm 
Select the command of "History Alarm" in the dropdown list box of the monitoring header to query 
SIS alarm. SIS alarm page is shown below.
--- pag 20 ---
SISPatch 
17 
 
Figure 4-4 SIS alarm interface 
Alarm list includes "Alarm Time", "Description", "Alarm Level", "Acknowledge Time", "Disappear 
Time", "Acknowledge by" and "Acknowledge Operation Node". 
Click 
 to pop up the alarm filter interface below, in which can filter SIS alarm by time range. 
 
Figure 4-5 Filter 
4.3.2 SIS System Alarm 
Select the command of "System Alarm" in the dropdown list box of the monitoring header, pop up 
the system alarm list shown below, in which show the system alarms.
--- pag 21 ---
SISPatch 
18 
 
Figure 4-6 System alarm list 
 
Show SIS alarm 
: click it and the window will not change, ECS-700 and SIS mixed 
alarm interface shows SIS alarms and mixed alarms seperately. The SIS alarms are 
shown above and mixed system alarms are shown down. Click SIS button again to 
restore to original size of mixed alarm window, in which only show mixed system alarms. 
 
Acknowledge single alarm 
: click it to acknowledge single alarm. 
 
Acknowledge current list 
: click it to acknowledge alarms in batch. If the cursor is in 
SIS alarm interface, acknowledge the 1000 system alarms with highest priorities in SIS 
alarm window. When the cursor is in mixed system alarm interface, acknowledge the 
1000 system alarms with highest priorities in mixed system alarm window. 
 
Alarm display settings 
: click it to pop up alarm display dialog of operation domain. 
The alarm of reference domain can be shown as required. If trans-domain alarm is 
configured, click the icon to pop up the window shown below. Select the operation 
domain to show its alarms in alarm list.
--- pag 22 ---
SISPatch 
19 
 
Figure 4-7 Operation domain alarm display 
 
If trans-domain alarm isn't set in operation domain configuration, click the button is 
useless. 
 
Open system status 
: for local ECS system alarm, click it to jump to corresponding 
fault diagnose interface. For remote system alarm or SIS alarm, click the button is 
useless. 
4.3.3 SIS Process Alarm 
Select the command of "Process Alarm' in the dropdown list box of the monitoring header, pop up 
the process alarms list below, in which shows all visible (process) alarms of current operation team. 
Alarms are sorted by levels in default. Please refer to System Builder Software User Manual for 
details of sorting alarms.
--- pag 23 ---
SISPatch 
20 
 
Figure 4-8 Process alarms list 
Process alarm of SIS TAG is same with common domain variable. Please refer to Real-time 
Monitoring Software User Manual for details. 
4.3.4 Query Offline Alarm 
Open the history alarm offline browser by selecting [Start/ VisualField/ System Tools/ History Alarm 
Browser]. Select [Type/ System SIS] in menu bar to view the history records of SIS TAG alarm.
--- pag 24 ---
SISPatch 
21 
 
Figure 4-9 SIS alarm offline browser 
Export Alarm 
Select [File/ Export] to open the alarm export interface, and select "SIS System Alarm" from the 
drop-down menu of alarm type, as shown below. 
 
Figure 4-10 SIS alarm export settings
--- pag 25 ---
SISPatch 
22 
This function can export all alarms conforming to current filter conditions to .CSV files. Export 
settings include "Time Specified" and "Export Path". 
The setting method is same with exporting process alarm in ECS-700. Please refer to History 
Alarm Viewer User Manual for details. 
Specify History Alarm Import/ Export Interface 
Select [Database Management/ Import/Export Specified History Alarm] to pop up the dialog below, 
in which can import specified history alarm records. 
 
Figure 4-11 Import/Export Specified History Alarm 
Data process method can select "Export History Alarm" or "Import History Alarm", and specify 
"History Alarm Library" and "Save File". After installing SISPatch, alarm types include "Process 
Alarm", "System Alarm", "Status Alarm" and "SIS System Alarm". Specify the time period and start 
to import or export history alarm. 
4.4 SIS History Fault Diagnosis 
 
Attention: 
IP addresses of SIS and VF controllers cannot be same, or the SIS fault diagnosis will be 
wrong. 
 
Select the command of "System Diagnose" to display system diagnose system. Click 
 to 
open the query window below.
--- pag 26 ---
SISPatch 
23 
 
Figure 4-12 Fault diagnosis query window 
Click "Find" to pop up the filter condition settings dialog below. 
 
Figure 4-13 Filter condition settings 
 
Time Range 
set the start time and end time for filtering. 
 
Detail Fault Position 
select "TCS-900" from the drop-down menu of system bar, and the filter results will be 
SIS TAG. Filter conditions include station, redundancy and IO module, etc. Click "Add" to 
add a record to filter list. 
 
Diagnosis Information 
Check "Diagnosis Information" and select the diagnosis information to view in the below 
check box. 
 
Fault level: select one or several fault levels as filter condition.
--- pag 27 ---
SISPatch 
24

Applicable Model

"Configure alarm". And modify the interface by the software;

Section 2 Introduction 
SOE software includes SOE server and SOE browser. It is an important part of the VisualField 
system software package. It is mainly used to collect and record on-site ON and OFF events, such 
as operations of circuit breaker and switch trip. The SOE server can record information such as 
the time, status, type, and location of the events. Based on the above information, users can take 
corresponding measures based on the on-site situation to achieve the purpose of solving on-site 
process control problems. 
2.1 Main Features 
In the VF system software, SOE event management is carried out through SOE server and SOE 
browser, and its main functions are as follows. 
 SOE server collects and records data. 
 SOE browser to browse and query SOE data. 
The SOE server can record up to 800,000 pieces of data by default. After more than 1 million 
pieces of data, the oldest records will be automatically deleted, and only the latest 800,000 
records will be retained. 
2.2 Typical Scenario 
In the VF project, SOE data can be collected in the following scenarios through SOE software: 
 
Directly collect SOE data generated by the ECS-700 system. 
 
Directly collect SOE data generated by the TCS-900 system.

structure is shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 3-1 SOE in system structure 
The whole system consists of four parts, SOE server, SOE browser, controller, and SOE module. 
 SOE server: complete system SOE data collection and recording, and provide SOE 
historical data query service. 
 SOE browser: complete viewing and querying of SOE data. 
 Controller: The controller collects the SOE records in the SOE module in real time, and 
sends the event records to the SOE server through master-slave communication. 
 SOE module: The SOE module scans the status of the DI or DO channel at high speed. 
When the channel status changes, the original SOE record is formed and sent to the 
main controller in real time.

Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
Simulation Controller Software 
Section 1 Overview 
VFCon can simulate all functions of ECS-700 system controllers (including FCU711, FCU712 and 
FCU713), and provides functions of breakpoint settings, step and archive, etc. Therefore, it can 
meet the demands of project configuration debugging and operator training. 
1.1 Functions 
Users can realize functions below by VFCon: 
 
Configuration debug without real controller. 
 
Compose complete simulation system to perform configuration debug or user 
training with the assistance of object simulation model. Simple object simulation 
model can be realized by custom program configuration software and custom 
function block configuration software. 
 
By archiving and load archive function of VFCon, users can stop controller operation 
and save all information at any time. When being started again, software can carry 
on operating from status and data saved last time. 
 
By breakpoint setting function of VFCon, users can set the function that when a data 
meets certain conditions, for example, a tag's real-time value reaches set value, 
VFCon operation will pause in order to debug configuration and program logic. 
 
By step function of VFCon, VFCon can run and pause by scan period. 
 
By period time control function of VFCon, controller running can be accelerated or 
decelerated to meet the demand of debugging. 
 
 
Attention: 
 
This software is only applicable for system without real controller. 
 
Please don’t apply this software if real controller is connected. 
 
1.2 Instruction of Software Dog 
After met one condition of following conditions, station can run the simulation controller software： 
 
With a dog including simulate authority, then simulate controller can be run. And the 
1
--- pag 4 ---
Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
count of running simulate controller in the same time is decided by the software dog, 
memory size and CPU capability. 
 
Only with a dog including engineer authority, one simulate controller can be run. 
 
 
Tips： 
If the station’s dog with simulate authority and with out engineer authority, download only 
can be execute to simulate controller but not real controller. 
 
1.3 Precondition 
1) Network card preparation 
Both the real and the virtual network cards can be used for the device to communicate 
with the simulation controller. 
 
If the real network card is adopted, 172.20/21 network is required. 
 
If the virtual network card is adopted, Microsoft Loopback Adapter (windows 7 
operational system） or Microsoft KM-TEST Loopback Adapter (Windows 10 
operational system） is required to be added. The specific steps are shown below: 
a. Enter Windows operational system and device manager. 
b. In device manager, select “Add outdated hardware” And goes to the next step. 
c. In the “Add hardware” dialog box, select “manually select hardware (Advanced)” 
and then goes to the next stop. 
d. Select ”Microsoft––Network Adapter Microsoft KM-TEST Loopback 
Adapter/Microsoft Loopback Adapter”。 
2) Configure the IP address of network card 
This step is to configure the IP address for the prepared network card in the last step. 
“172.20/21.X.Y” shall be adopted during the configuration process, in which X represents 
the integer in 0~59 and Y represents the integer 129~253. 
 
2
--- pag 5 ---
Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
 
Attempt: 
 
After the device communicates with the simulation controller by the virtual 
or real network cards, other network cards shall be disabled. 
 
the address range of the simulation controller s are respectively: domain 
address 0~59 and station address 2~126. The domain and station addresses cannot 
be configured as the maximum at the same time (59.126 cannot be configured). 
 
3) Reboot the device and ensure that the modification takes effect. 
 
3
--- pag 6 ---
Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
Section 2 Start Up VFCon 
 
Attention: 
 
Before using simulation controller, please make sure that computer has network module 
and is connected to network, and there is an operation node IP on network module 
(172.20.*.*or 172.21.*.*) 
 
When simulating a control station (such as domain 0 station 2), please make sure there’s 
no controller actually connected to it, otherwise, simulation cannot be carried out. 
 
1. Select a control station in VFExplorer and open it from configuration server. Right 
click the control station, and select "Simulation" in the right-click menu. 
VFCon is started up and minimized on the task bar with an icon
 at the bottom right 
corner. At this time, the icon of the control station becomes
.

has been downloaded and online download is allowed, users can also select the 
control station by selecting menu command [Edit/Download Online] or selecting 
download on-line in the right-click menu. 
The download dialog box pops up and the operation of download is consistent with that 
of real controller. Please refer to Config Explorer User Manual for details. 
3. After download, click the icon 
 at the bottom right of taskbar to display the main 
interface of VFCon, as shown in the figure below.

3.3 Breakpoint 
Breakpoint function is that simulated controller will pause after it finishes the cycle during which the 
breakpoint condition is satisfied, and it will prompt which breakpoint is satisfied. 
Click button

Figure 3-6 Magnification settings 
By gliding glide block on the glide bar, the executing period of simulated controller can be chosen 
as several times longer than normal period; the magnification number can also be inputted in the 
input dialog box directly. 
The magnification range of execution period can be set between 0.5 and 10 (when it is set to 0, 
software adjusts it to 0.5 automatically) which means that simulation controller can run with period 
0.5~10 times of normal period. That is, it can be accelerated to 2 times of normal speed at most or 
be decelerated as one tenth of normal speed at least. 
3.5 Memory Browser 
In order to facilitate debugging, VFCon provides memory browser to browse memory value of 
simulated controller. 
Click button 
 on the tool bar or select menu command [View/Memory Browser] and the 
memory browser will pop up, as shown in Figure 3-7. 
12
--- pag 15 ---
Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
 
Figure 3-7 Memory Browser 
Controller memory can be viewed in memory browser to assist debug. Memory browser can 
display content with size of 768(0x300) bytes at one time. 
 
Tip: 
 
Users don't need to use the function. 
 
Error prompts will pop up if the input address is not HEX; when the input address is 
over address range, memory browser data section will not be updated. 
 
3.6 Minimal Mode/Normal Mode Switch 
VFCon also provides switchover of interface display modes. Minimal mode only contains toolbar, 
as shown in Figure 3-8. Click button 
 on the tool bar to switch between minimal mode and 
normal mode. Select menu command [View/Minimal mode] to make software interface enter 
minimal mode. 
 
Figure 3-8 Simplest mode 
13
--- pag 16 ---

3.7 Simulation Battery 
By selecting or not selecting menu command [Set/Simulate Battery], whether to simulate battery 
function can be chosen. When simulation battery is selected, simulation controller will proceed as 
follows: 
 
When simulated controller is stopped (or closed), software will save the status and 
data automatically, i.e. save all data of current controller as designated file. 
 
After an IP address is set in simulation controller (i.e. select a control station to 
simulate from configuration management software), software will automatically 
search current directory for the automatically saved file of controller with the same IP 
address. If such a file exists, it will be imported to the simulated controller memory 
automatically. In this way, even if program is closed, the configuration data won’t be 
lost after opening it again. 
When menu command [Settings/Simulation battery] is not selected, the abovementioned two 
actions will not be executed.
--- pag 17 ---
Simulation Controller Software User Manual 
Section 4 Simulation Controller Status 
Simulated controller has three basic states, and their switchover relationship is shown as Figure 
4-1. In the figure, blue font part is caused by user operation. 
 
Figure 4-1 Controller Status 
 
Ready status: IP address has already been set in simulated controller and it is ready 
to run. 
 
Running status: Simulation controller is running and equates to actual controller is 
running after it is powered on 
 
Pause status: When simulation controller is in running, it can pause by manual 
setting. Simulation controller will no longer execute after it finishes current period. All 
internal and external data will be held, and network communication will be 
suspended and won’t process network command of changing controller internal data. 
When virtual controller is in pause status, it can be changed to the running status 
manually.

SyCON User Manual 
Section 1 SyCon Software Installation 
1.1 Summary 
SyCon software is the application software of PROFIBUS master module, and it is used to 
configure PROFIBUS communication. 
1.2 Environment 
SyCon software is applicated in Windows XP Professional SP2 (32bit). 
1.3 Steps of Installation 
SyCon software can be installed by following steps: 
1. Put the installation disc of the SyCon software into the CD-ROM. The Windows system 
will run the setup procedures automatically, as shown in following figure. 
 
Figure 1-1 Installation Interface 
2
--- pag 5 ---
2. Click “System installation” to start installing SyCon, as shown in following figure. 
 
Figure 1-2 SyCon Installation Interface 1 
3. Configure options of “Installation settings” as following figure, and select “English” in 
“Language” frame. 
Note: if local PC has installed SyCon software, then the following figure will be omitted. 
 
Figure 1-3 SyCon Installation Interface 2

3

4

7. Click “Next>” to enter in installation interface. 
 
Figure 1-7 SyCon Installation Interface 6 
8. After installation, the interface shown as following figure display. 
5
--- pag 8 ---
Figure 1-8 Installation Interface 3 
9. Click “Finish” to finish installation of SyCon. 
10. Register SyCon. 
Only after registered, all the functions of SyCon can be valid. Else, only the system with 
one master and one slave can be configured. 
Double-click icon of SyCon to run SyCon. 
Select “Help/licensing” to popup dialog box as shown in following figure. 
 
Figure 1-9 SyCon Register Interface 
6
--- pag 9 ---
Input “Name”, “Company”, “Address” and other information, then click “Enter License 
Code” to input license cod. 
Restart SyCon to validate the register number. 
 
Tips: 
“Name”, “Company” and license code must be matched and inputted correctly. Other 
information is optional. 
 
Section 2 Usage of Software 
The types PROFIBUS-DP stations include masters and slaves. In system configuration, 
PROFIBUS communication module is used as the master of the PROFIBUS, while DP linkers and 
various PLCs are used as the slave. PROFIBUS-PA bus devices are connected to the DP bus 
through couplers/linkers. 
2.1 Preparation before Configuration 
Before configuring the PROFIBUS communication module, please prepare the GSD file provided 
by DP device supplier and carefully read the device operation manual. If the connecting device is 
the PA bus device, corresponding GSD file of linker should be produced. 
Input the GSD Files of DP Devices 
To connect PROFIBUS-DP device, there should be GSD file for connecting PROFIBUS-DP which 
is provided by device supplier or can be download from the database in www.profibus.com. To 
ensure the GSD file used matching the device, it is recommended to use the GSD file provided by 
the device supplier. 
For the convenience of configuration and further maintenance, please copy GSD in DP device to 
the folder (Program Files\Hilscher\SyCon\other\GSD) before configuration, which is created after 
SyCon software setup. 
For the convenience of user to study and practice, some relative GSD files of certain DP device 
are copy to the folder (Program Files\Hilscher\SyCon\other\GSD) in advance. 
Generating GSD Files of Linkers 
 
 
Tip: 
If you don’t need to connect PROFIBUS-PA device, you can skip this section. 
 
To connect PROFIBUS-DP device, there should be GSD file for connecting PROFIBUS-DP which 
is provided by device supplier or can be download from the document base in www.profibus.com. 
To ensure the GSD file used matching the device, it is recommended to use the GSD file provided 
7
--- pag 10 ---
by device supplier. 
Because PA device communicates with DP device through linker, GSD file of linker should be 
created. 
Take Siemens IM157 linker as example. For configuration of IM157, Siemens Company provides a 
template for creating GSD file of DP/PA link. This template does not include module ID of any PA 
device. The module ID of PA slave should be added into the GSD file of DP/PA link. All these can 
be accomplished by GSD tools. 
All versions of GSD tools (GSDTOOL.JAR) require Java operation environment (JRE) version 
1.3.0 or higher version running in all MS -Windows operation system. The JRE can be obtained 
from internet for free. 
To ensure normal operation of GSD tools, the GSD file of field device should meet one 
requirement that the first 22 bytes of different module used in one GSD file should be different so 
GSD tools can identify them by different module names. If the difference only exits in the bytes 
after the first 22 bytes, user will get error message and can not process GSD file of the field device. 
User can edit the GSD file of the field device and change or shorten the corresponding module to 
make simple remedy. Changing the module name of GSD file does not affect the actual function of 
the field device. 
The operation procedures of generating GSD file of linker are as bellow: 
1. Create a folder under the D disk (e.g. D:\IM157). 
2. Copy GSDTOOL.JAR and IMLINKV1.DAT (address “Program 
Files\Hilscher\SyCon\other\Tools”) to file D:\IM157. 
3. Copy the GSD file of PROFIBUS-PA device used to a same folder D:\IM157 as shown in 
following figure. 
8
--- pag 11 ---
Figure 2-1 Copy the GSD file of PROFIBUS-PA device to a same folder

9

Figure 2-4 GSD-TOOL for IM157 interface 3

options in following figure, and click generate GSD-file to generate the GSD file obtaining 
the device information of PROFIBUS-PA. The file is in the automatically created folder 
Output with the name of si048052.gsd.

2.2 Add COM722-S in Hardware Configuration 
Click “Start\Program\ VisualField (V3.1)\configuration management software” to run system 
configuration software, or click 
 on the desktop to run the software directly. 
After run the “Configuration Management Software”, load the corresponding project, select the 
corresponding controller and double click “hardware configuration” to enter into hardware 
configuration interface.

the menu or directly click the 
 in the tool bar, then a dialogue box shown in Figure

corresponding address, then click “Add” to finish the adding process.

E-BUS node is the same as the address jumper in the base. The scope is 1~7. 
 
2.3 DP Communication Configuration 
In this section a PROFIBUS communication module as a PROFIBUS master with a module type 
slave ET200M and a compact type slave IM184 is taken as an example to explain how to use 
SyCon to configure PROFIBUS. 
Entering DP Communication Configuration Interface 
In hardware configuration, to select COM722-S, select “Communication Configuration” by left click 
or select “Operate (O)/Communication Configuration” in the menu to enter SyCon software as 
shown in following figure. 
 
Figure 2-8 DP communication configuration interface SyCon software 
 
Configure DP Master 
Double click the master icon and open the “Master Configuration” dialogue box as shown in 
following figure. The default address of the master is 31. If you need change it, edit it directly in 
“Station” editing box as shown in following figure. 
13
--- pag 16 ---
Attention:

Confirm the selection of the check box before “Auto addressing”.

following figure.

in the path of “Program Files\Hilscher\SyCon\Fildbus\PROFIBUS\GSD” automatically.

Configure DP Slaves 
 
 
Attention: 
Since different DP slaves have different characters, please refer to the relative application 
manual when configuring DP slaves. Furthermore, on the configuration method, please refer to 
the module manual when the S7-300, CP342-5, IM157, etc are as slaves.

Add modules one by one in the following order:

--- pag 19 ---
17

Another example, 8-channel analog input module SM331 with the order number of 6ES7 
331-7SF00-0AB0, the module has input data of 8 bytes. As shown in Figure 2-14. 
 
Figure 2-14 Slave Configuration Interface 
Configure Bus Parameter 
Click the master icon. Select “Settings/ Bus Parameter” in menu. Set baud rate, such as 
1.5Mbps. 
Save the file. 
Save Configuration File and Exit 
After finishing DP communication configuration in the SyCon software, select 
 button or click 
“File/ Save” to save the configuration. Finally, exit the SyCon software back to hardware 
configuration software “VFIOBuilder”. 
Some GSD files provided by manufacturers should to generate GSD files of corresponding linker 
first if the connected by PA bus device.
--- pag 20 ---

SyCon 
Select IM157 slave by the left key of the mouse, select “Settings/Slave Configuration” or double 
click IM157 slave icon to open IM157 slave configuration interface. 
 
Attention： 
The configuration of link used as DP slave in DPCon is similar to the configuration of this

The configuration structure of IM157 depends on the number and type of PA slaves. It is

Add a module “Begin of Device_0B25” and add another module “= =Analog Input” as shown in

Figure 3-1 Add modules

Section 1 Overview 
VFSysBuilder is used to build system structure frame. It is usually installed in System 
Configuration Server (Chief Engineer Station), and used to build and maintain system structure 
frame by engineers with project management authority. 
The network structure diagram of system is shown in Figure 1-1. 
 
Figure 1-1 System structure 
VFSysBuilder is used to build and maintain the real project system structure as shown in Figure 
1-1. After building system structure frame, each engineer station can specifically configure each 
control station by opening the default project in VFExporer when it is connected with Configuration 
Server. 
1.1 Function Feature 
New project 
Users can build a new project, and then build a system in this project by configuring control 
domains, operation domains and engineers. 
While creating project, amount alarm priority and project creator information should be configured.

1.2 Technical Specification and Naming Criterion 
System scale 
 
The system supports 250 nodes at the maximum. (number of control stations, 
operation nodes and servers. Control stations are viewed as redundancy by default, 
so each control station counts for two nodes); 
 
The system supports 16 control domains at the maximum and 16 operation domains 
at the maximum; 
 
The single control domain supporting control stations is maximum 60; the single 
operation domain supporting operation nodes is maximum 60 and the amount of 
server is one at the least and two at the most. 
Network address 
 
In the ECS-700 system 
SCNet is redundant network by default, its node address is "172.20.X .Y" and 
"172.21.X .Y". X is the domain address of network with an address range of 0~59; Y is 
the host ID of node with a control node ID range of 2~127 and an operation node ID 
range of 129~254. 
 
The node address is "172.Z.X.Y" in SONet. 
X is the domain address of the network with an address range of 0~59. 
Y is the node address of network with an address range of 129~254. 
Z can be configured as 21, 30 or 31 according to the configuration of information 
network. 
Naming criterion 
 
All names cannot include the following characters: \ / : * ? " < > | ! @ # $ % ^ & = . ; ~ 
`, and cannot be blank. In addition, project names cannot use windows reserved 
characters which are con, aux, com1, lpt1, prn and nul; 
 
Names of projects, control domains, operation domains, control stations, operation 
nodes, servers and engineer group cannot be blank, and the name length is 
maximum 64 English characters(32 Chinese characters); 
 
Names of engineers cannot be blank, the maximum name length is 32 English
--- pag 10 ---
System Builder User Manual IM41S54-E 
5 
letters (16 Chinese characters); 
 
The name length of tag groups can be 1~64 English letters (1~32 Chinese 
characters); 
 
The maximum length of descriptions is 128 English letters (64 Chinese characters). 
 
Time synchronization server specification 
The time synchronization server host ID must be 254. 
Engineer group and engineer 
Users can configure at most 31 engineer groups and at most 32 engineers for each engineer 
group. Users can configure at most 32 engineers with no engineer group. 
Alarm priority 
The default of alarm priorities is 6, and the maximum of alarm priority is 32.

Section 2 Configuration Flow 
System configuration consists of control domain configuration, operation domain configuration and 
engineer group configuration. 
Control domain configuration: users can set control domain name, description, domain address 
and group name of tags in the domain; set control station name, description, address, system, 
type, and authorized users. 
Operation domain configuration: users can set operation domain name, description, control 
domain that can be supervised and authored users; set server name, description, address; set 
operation node name, description, address, operation node type and connection type of SCNet. 
Engineer group configuration: users can set the distribution of project management authority of 
engineers, maintainable control stations and operation domains. 
In addition, users can also set some global parameters, such as decimal digits, alarm indicator 
colors on the panel, time synchronization server, panel which need confirmed, alarm priority, 
information network connection, etc. 
Before configuring the project, users must build the system structure frame in System Builder, and 
then configure hardware, tags and control schemes of each control station in the project by 
Configuration Explorer and configure operation domains by HMI builder. The whole configuration

configuration in operation domain and operation node configuration. It provides settings of name, 
description, address of server and operation node, and the distribution of control domains that can 
be supervised and engineer authority.

Section 5 Engineer Authority Management 
The authority of engineer in System Builder is classified into 3 types: 
 
Project management authority: it includes the authority to open/close the project, 
and set the authority of control station configuration and operation domain 
configuration. 
 
Control station configuration authority: it includes the authority to specify the control 
station that can be configured. 
 
Operation domain configuration authority: it includes the authority to specify the 
operation domain that can be configured. 
These 3 authorities are independent of each other: engineer who has project management 
authority does not necessarily have control station configuration authority or operation domain 
configuration authority; engineer who has control station configuration authority does not 
necessarily have project management authority or operation domain configuration authority; 
engineer who has operation domain configuration authority does not necessarily have project 
management authority or control station configuration authority. However, engineer with project 
management authority can set its own control station authority and operation domain authority by 
System Builder, while the other two authorities can't. In a project, there must be at least one user 
who has the project management authority.

Tag Builder User Manual 
 
1 
Tag Builder 
Section 1 Overview 
VFTAGBuilder is a component of VisualField System Software, which is used to implement tag 
configuration. VFTAGBuilder must be invoked by VFExplorer. 
1.1 Function Feature of VFTAGBuilder 
 
Configure tags in single control station. 
 
No need to close the software when downloading configuration. 
 
Provide convenient editing functions of tag configuration information, including tag 
adding, tag deleting and tag modifying and modifying of tag parameters (includes 
tag name) in batch. 
 
Support multiple modes of tag search like search by tag name, description and, 
channel address and Support wildcard query. 
 
Real-time save the tag configuration automatically. 
 
Provide a function of initializing value of custom tag. 
 
Import and export configuration in EXCEL format. 
 
Compile and download single unit as the minimum unit. 
 
Scan and upload the channel tag ( No need manual configuration, and generate the 
corresponding tag to the finished hardware configuration) 
 
Check the validity of total tags or single tag. 
 
Check the using information of the tags in custom program. 
 
Provide setting of the digital tag in SOE record.

Section 2 Introduction to Interface 
Select the control station (not locked by other engineer stations) needed to be configured in 
VFExplorer, and click "Open from Configuration Server" in right-click menu. Double-click "Tag 
Table" in property bar of the control station (or select "Tag Table" in property bar and click "Edit" in 
right-click menu) to open VFTAGBuilder, and its interface is shown as Figure 2-1. 
 
Figure 2-1 Interface of VFTAGBuilder 
Interface of VFTAGBuilder mainly includes three parts: tag list area, locating on the left of the 
interface and used to display the configured tags; tag property setting area, locating on the right 
and used to set and view all properties of selected tag; and output bar, locating at the bottom and 
used to display the result of operation, which can be closed if necessary. 
 
Title Bar-Display the program title. 
 
Menu Bar-Include File, Edit, Operate, View, and Help. Each menu item contains 
submenu items. 
 
Toolbar-List frequently used menu functions in icon, making it convenient to use. 
Click the menu [View/Toolbar] to decide whether to show the bar or not. 
 
Tag List-Display the tag list conformed to the designated conditions. 
 
Properties Settings Area-All properties of the selected tag can be set and viewed. 
 
Output Bar-Display the result of the operation and so on. Click the menu

[View/Output bar] to decide whether to show the window or not. 
 
Status Bar-Display some information of the current operation and some prompts. 
Click the menu [View/Status Bar] to decide whether to show the bar or not.

Section 3 Introduction to Tag Property Area 
The tag property area, on the right of the tag list area, displays all properties of the designated tag. 
Properties can be modified in this area. 
 
Figure 3-1 Tag property area 
The tag property area lists all properties of the designated tag, including Number, Name, Type, 
Description, etc. All the properties can be directly modified in the property box except Type and 
Number. Property items which can't be modified are displayed in gray and others are in black. 
Text or number can be input in the edit box of properties such as Name, Description, etc. Press 
Enter after input (or move the cursor away from the current edit box). Some properties have 
pull-down menu. When one of these properties is selected, a pull-down menu pop up, like, 
 and only the items on the pull-down menu can be 
selected. 
When modifying the tag name, program will check whether the name is exclusive in the controller.
--- pag 11 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
7 
If a tag with the same name exists, program will maintain the original name and prompt name 
repeated in the output bar. 
Notes for application: 
1. Tag name is case sensitive. For example, TIC901 and tic901 are regarded as 
different tags. The maximum characters of tag name are 24. If exceeded, system will 
prompt in the Output bar. 
2. Tag name must accord with the naming criterion. Otherwise, system will prompt 
error. 
3. Tag name can only start with number or letter and consist of letters, numbers, '-' and 
'_'. When start with special characters, an error prompt "Tag name can only start with 
number or letter" will pop up in the Output bar. When modifying the tag description, 
any character can be input within the maximum characters 64. If over limit, an error 
prompt will be displayed in the Output bar. 
4. If the tag is referenced in a program section, it can't be deleted but can be modified. 
5. I/O tag: When modifying the tag number, it should be 0~31 for nodes, 0~3 for racks, 
0~15 for modules, and 0~31 for channels. 
 
Tip: 
When setting alarm value of analog tag, value with high alarm priority should be larger than 
that with low priority (for example, HHH alarm value should be larger than HH alarm value). 
Otherwise, a prompt of compiling error will pop up.

The import operation will overwrite the current tag configuration by that in the EXCEL file, so the 
matching relationship should be set first between tags in the EXCEL file and those in 
VFTAGBuilder, i.e., "Tag Import Mode" and "Intervene Condition". 
 
Tag Import Mode: The rules for matching tags in the EXCEL file with those in 
VFTAGBuilder correspondingly during the process of importing the update. 
 
Intervene Condition: the conditions on which the process of import needs to be 
paused and engineers are allowed to intervene, i.e., certain condition is satisfied or 
certain error occurs. 
When advanced options are not set, tags will be imported according to the default settings: Tag 
Import Mode is “Import tag according to serial number" and Intervene Condition is "When there are 
no other tags having the same name as the tags to be imported.". 
 
Tip: 
If there is no special requirement (especially when tags are used by user function block),
--- pag 33 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
29
tags will be imported according to the default import mode. 
 
Tag Import Mode and Intervene Condition can be defaulted in the extension part of the dialog box. 
There are three options for "Tag Import Mode”: 
 
Import tag according to ID: This is the recommended mode, which creates the 
matching relationship according to the serial number of tags. For example, No.1 AI 
tag in the Excel file will update No.1 AI tag in VFTAGBuilder. If the tag doesn't exist, 
a new tag will be generated. 
 
Attention: 
If there are tags used by custom program in the tag configuration, it is required to import tags 
in this matching mode. 
 
 
Import tag according to tag name: It creates matching relationships according to the 
tag name. For example, a tag named "AI001" in the EXCEL file will update the tag 
named "AI001" in VFTAGBuilder. If the tag doesn't exist, a new tag will be 
generated. 
 
Import tag according to I/O channel address: It creates matching relationships 
according to the channel address of I/O channel tags. For example, a tag whose I/O 
channel address is 003-002-006-007 in the EXCEL file will update the tag whose I/O 
channel address is 003-002-006-007 in VFTAGBuilder. If the tag doesn't exist, a 
new tag is will be generated 
 
Attention: 
The import matching mode is only applicable for importing I/O tag. When non-I/O tags are 
imported in this matching mode, they will be imported as new tags. 
 
Intervene Condition is set in case of conflicts or multi-options to be chose in the import process, 
which implements the pause function for engineers to operate manually. 
 
When there are no other tags having the same serial number as the tags to be 
imported: Tags with the same serial number exist except the default matching tag. 
 
When there are no other tags having the same name as the tags to be imported: 
Tags with the same name exists except the default matching tag. 
 
When there are no other tags having the same I/O address as the tags to be 
imported: Tags with the same I/O channel address exist except the default matching 
tag.
--- pag 34 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
30
 
When not found corresponding tags (build new tag or do not import): No 
corresponding matching tag can be found in the default matching mode.

Tag Builder User Manual 
 
39
 
Figure 4-21 Communication Tag Configuration 2 
Then select "Add Strategy", and there will generate the corresponding tag information on the right, 
including tag address, tag type, and status code.
--- pag 44 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
40
 
Figure 4-22 Communication Tag Configuration 3 
Click "OK" and exit the dialog box of Communication Tag Configuration. Then select the menu 
[Operation/ Scan Tags from Channels /Scan New Added], VFTAGBuilder will generate 
corresponding communication tags according to the tag strategies of the former configuration. 
Prompts will be displayed in the output bar. 
 
Attention: 
When DP module is not configured in the hardware configuration, the function of 
Communication Tag Strategy is invalid; 
The function of Communication Tag Strategy generates corresponding tags only by DP 
module. 
 
4.10 Check All Tags 
The function of “Check All Tags” is used to implement parameters check for all tags in the current 
controller, including the tag number check, the check of tag name repeated, I/O tag address 
conflict check, tag properties check (tag type; SOE tag; signal type; module type; Max./Min.of 
parameters; items associated with Max./Min of parameters) ,alarm setting etc. , Prompt will be 
displayed in the output bar after check.
--- pag 45 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
41
 
Figure 4-23 “Check All Tags” information 
 
Tips: 
 
When implementing Check All Tags/Check Tag Properties/Exit, VFTAGBuilder will 
update SOE tag, signal type, and module parameters. 
 
Double-click the check information in the output bar to locate corresponding tags. 
 
Tags that are new or modified can be used by custom program or found in the global 
search only after checking all tags. (Check All Tags also will be implemented when exits 
VFTAGBuilder). 
 
4.11 Check Tag Properties 
"Check Tag Properties "is used to check parameters of single tag or several tags, including tag 
number check; the check of tag name repeated; I/O address conflict check; tag type matching 
check; SOE tag check; signal type check (module type check included ); Max./Min. of parameters 
check; the check of items associated with Max./Min of parameters and so on. 
Select one tag or several tags and select the menu [Operation/Check Tag Properties] information 
of tag check will be shown in the output bar, as shown in Figure 4-24. 
 
Figure 4-24Tag check information 
4.12 Default Tag Type Settings 
“Default Tag Type Settings” is used to set the configuration information of certain tag as template
--- pag 46 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
42
and make the new added tag whose configuration information is identical with it. It also supports 
template import/export. 
4.12.1 Set As Type Template 
Select Tag AI001 in the tag list area and select the menu [Operation/ Default Tag Type 
Settings/Set As Type Template], There prompts "Succeed to set the default type AI, original type is 
AI001!" in the output bar. Initial values of parameters of new tags of this type will be consistent with 
those of the template of this type. 
 
Tips: 
 
If no tag is selected or selected tags are function block tags, the item "Set As Type 
Template" is in gray and not available. 
 
If several tags are selected at the same time, as shown in Figure 4-25, and select "Set As 
Type Template", then the tag at the bottom of the list will be set as the type template. 
There will prompts in the output bar: "Succeed to set the default type AI, original type is 
AI00020166!" 
 
When selecting various types of tags, each type of tag at the bottom of the list, will be 
set as the type template of corresponding type. 
 
After the type template has been set successfully, even if the original type (tag) is 
modified by tag configuration imported from .xls file or generated by Scanning Tags 
from Channels, initial values of parameters of new tags will remain consistent with 
those of the type template before being overwritten. That is, once the type template is 
set, it is independent with original type. 
 
Before setting, please cancel "Automatically Set As Type Template". 
 
 
Figure 4-25 Select several tags simultaneously 
4.12.2 Automatically Set As Type Template 
It is used to set the tag added as template of this type automatically. Select this function, and add a 
new tag. The new tag will become the template of this type automatically and be template for tags 
added afterwards. 
 
Tip: 
Please cancel "Automatically Set As Type Template" before selecting "Set As Type Template" 
or "Restore to Original Settings to set the type template.
--- pag 47 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
43
 
4.12.3 Restore to Original Settings 
It is used to restore the type template to original template after using "Set As Type Template". After 
restoration, initial values of new tags will be consistent with original tag template. 
 
Tip: 
After restoring to original setting, values of some parameters will be restored to those of 
"Common Default Settings", like decimal digits. 
 
4.12.4 Import Default Type 
Select the menu [Operation/ Default Tag Type Settings/Import Default Type], and then pop up a 
dialog box, as shown in Figure 4-26 
 
Figure 4-26 Dialog box "Import tag Default Type" 
Select the configuration file (.TAG); click the button "Open". Initial values of tags newly generated 
will be same with those of configuration files. 
Type templates of all kinds of tags can be generated automatically by importing configuration files; 
Values of parameters of type templates can be modified by modifying configuration files.
--- pag 48 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
44
4.12.5 Export Default Type 
Select the menu [Operation/ Default Tag Type Settings/Export Default Type] in the interface of 
VFTAGBuilder, and then pop up a dialog box, as shown in Figure 4-27. 
 
Figure 4-27 Dialog box "Export tag Default Type 
After input the filename, click the button "Save". VFTAGBuilder will generate a configuration file 
according to parameters of all kinds of templates and save it in the designated directory. 
For tags of certain type without type template set, VFTAGBuilder will generate configuration files 
according to the original setting values of this type. 
If an existed filename is input, it will prompt" Do you want to replace" when the file is saved. 
4.13 Sequencing 
VFTAGBuilder supports the function of tag sorting. Tags can be sorted by "ID", "Name", "Type", 
"Description", "Unit" and "Address". 
Click one of listed titles, and the mark 
 (sort tags by ascending) or 
 (sort tags by descending) 
appears. 
 
Click title "ID", then tags will be sorted by serial number in work area: Ascending 
from 0.
--- pag 49 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
45
 
Click title "Name", then tags will be sorted by name in work area: Ascending from 0 
to 9 and from A to Z. 
 
Click title "Type", then tags are will be sorted by type in work area. 
 
Click title "Description", then tags will be sorted by description in work area: 
Ascending from none, number to characters. 
 
Click title "Unit", then tags will be sorted by unit in work area. 
 
Click title "Address", then tags will be sorted by I/O channel address in work area. 
4.14 Exit 
Select the menu [File/Exit], and then pop up the dialog box of Exit, as shown in Figure 4-28. 
 
Figure 4-28 Exit when there are errors in whole check 
VFTAGBuilder will execute “Check All Tags” of the configuration automatically when exits. When 
the configuration is invalid, for example, addresses of I/O tags conflict or IO tag doesn't conform 
with hardware configuration channel, "Failed" and error prompt will be displayed and users need to 
confirm whether to be force to exit, as shown in Figure 4-28. If names are repeated between 
stations, users cannot exit VFTAGBuilder, as shown in Figure 4-29.
--- pag 50 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
46
 
Figure 4-29Unable to exit when rename occurs in two stations 
VFTAGBuilder will exit automatically only when configurations are valid. 
4.15 Restore Tag Configuration (Used after Force UNLOCK) 
After force unlocking one control station in System Builder, users should execute Restore Tag 
Configuration, selecting the menu [Operation/Restore Tag Configuration (Used after Force 
Unlock)]. 
 
Tip: 
The function of Restore Tag Configuration should be used after forced unlock and make sure 
to restore tag configuration after forced unlock. 
If VFTAGBuilder logs out abnormally, tag configuration will be restored automatically when it 
is opened again. 
 
4.16 Parameter Upload 
Parameter Upload is used to upload important parameter information for project backup or for 
users as project information. As shown in Figure 4-30.
--- pag 51 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
47
 
Figure 4-30 Interface of Parameter Upload/Download 
 
Users can select the tag type and function block type to be set from tree diagram at 
the left in Figure 4-30. There are two labels at the right: parameter list and tag list of 
certain tag or function block be uploaded. 
 
Parameter Upload: Select parameter items to be uploaded, and upload all 
parameters by default. 
 
Tag Upload: Select tags to be uploaded. 
Parameter Upload 
It is used to filter the data uploaded and data of parameters not to upload will be ignored. In the 
interface as shown in Figure 4-30, select the label "Parameter Upload Settings", as shown in 
Figure 4-31.
--- pag 52 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
48
 
Figure 4-31 Upload parameter setting page 
Select certain item (such as AI) in the left window, all parameters of AI tags will be listed in the right 
interface where users can select parameter types to upload. 
 
Tips: 
 
Before uploading parameters, the uploading tag list should be created first. 
 
Parameter “INITVALUE” of tags in types NA, ND, NN, PA, PD and PN are not selected in 
default. 
 
Create uploading tag list 
Select a tag or several tags in the tag list area. Right-click the selected tag and select the item 
“Add” to Upload Tag List in the pop-up menu or select the menu [Operation/Add to Upload Tag 
List]. Select corresponding tag types in the pop-up interface as shown in Figure 4-32. Tags 
selected before will be added to “Tag Upload Settings".
--- pag 53 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
49
 
Figure 4-32 Tag Upload Settings 
Select tags to be upload their parameters in the interface and parameters to be uploaded are 
those of types set in the page of "Parameter Upload Settings". 
 
Tip: 
Only tags downloaded by configuration can be select to upload. 
 
Parameter Upload 
After setting parameters and tags to be uploaded, click the button "Upload" and please operate 
following the pop-up prompt. Then tag parameters will be uploaded after confirmation. Prompt will 
be displayed at the bottom of the interface of Parameter Upload/Download after upload has 
finished.
--- pag 54 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
50
 
Figure 4-33 Prompt after uploading 
 
 
Tips: 
 
Click the button "Upload", the command of parameter upload will be sent to controllers. 
 
Parameter will be uploaded in unit of tag parameter. 
 
If the current tag configuration is not consistent with that in the controller, parameter 
upload would fail. 
 
Update configuration 
 
After completing parameter uploading, select “Data operation > Update configuration” in the menu 
bar and update the uploaded parameters from the controller to the configuration. 
 
Export 
Parameters uploaded can be exported to EXCEL file (.XLS) for view and analysis. 
4.17 Tag Usage 
It is used to check the usage information of tags in custom program. 
Select a tag and then select the menu [Operation/Tag Usage]. Information that in which programs 
the tag is used will be listed in the output bar.
--- pag 55 ---
Tag Builder User Manual 
 
51
 
Figure 4-34Usage of Tag PT1117 
4.18 Vacant Channel Information 
It is used to get statistics of module channels without corresponding tags. Select the menu 
[Operation /Vacant Channel Information] and corresponding prompts will be displayed in the 
output bar, as shown in Figure 4-36. 
 
Figure 4-35 Vacant Channel Information

It is used to get statistics of I/O tags without corresponding channels. Select the menu

User Access Software User Manual

User Access Software User Manual 
Section 1 Overview 
VFAccess is an important component of VisualField system software package which is used to set 
supervision operator and relevant operation authority.
--- pag 6 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
1 
Section 2 Startup Mode 
Two startup modes of VFAccess: 
 
Double-click the “Supervising User Authority” node in left tree of VFExplorer. 
 
Right-click the “Supervising User Authority” node in left tree of VFExplorer, then click 
“Edit”. 
VFAccess interface is shown as Figure 2-1. 
 
Figure 2-1 VFAccess interface 
There are only two users in the User List, one is “Admin” with “Privilege +” , and the other is 
“Observer” with authority of "Observer" (Both users are system reference project users and can't 
be deleted.
--- pag 7 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
1 
Section 3 Interface 
The software interface as shown in Figure 3-1. The whole interface consists of title bar, menu bar, 
toolbar, user list tree, information display area and status bar. 
 
Figure 3-1 VFAccess interface 
3.1 Title Bar & Status Bar 
 
Title bar displays the name of the software. 
 
Status bar displays the prompt message where the cursor is and information of 
current user. 
3.2 Introduction to Menu Bar & Toolbar

3.3 User List Tree & Information Display Area 
3.3.1 User List Tree 
User List Tree displays the name and authority of users. 
 is level icon and 
 is user icon. 
 
Figure 3-2 List Tree 
3.3.2 Information Display Area 
Information display area consists of 5 tabs below.
--- pag 9 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
3 
 
Figure 3-3 Switch tabs 
 
Select level in user list tree to show “User List” tab in information display area only. 
 
Select user in user list tree to show all 5 tabs in information display area.
--- pag 10 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
4 
Section 4 Operation Instruction 
This section introduces main operations of VFAccess, including add user, add referenced user, 
configure user authority, etc. 
4.1 Add User 
Right-click a user in user list tree on the left of the interface, then choose “Add” in the right-click 
menu as shown in Figure 4-1 ( or select the menu command [ Manage/Add User ], or click the 
button 
 in the toolbar ), pop up dialog box of “New User”. 
 
Figure 4-1 Right-click menu ->Add User 
4.1.1 Add VF User 
Dialog box of “New User” as shown in Figure 4-2:
--- pag 11 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
5 
 
Figure 4-2 Dialog box “New User” 
If add VF regular users, don’t click the right option “Use Windows users”. Input User Name, User 
Level, User Description, Password, and then click "OK" to complete the operation. Click “Cancel” 
and the operation will be canceled. 
 
Tip: 
 
User Name should within 30 single characters that consist of number, underline, letter, 
SBC case character and Chinese; the description should be within 128 single 
characters; Password should be within 20 characters. 
 
There is only one user as observer and one user as “privilege +”, the user of observer is 
“observer”, while the user of “privilege +” is “Admin”. 
 
4.1.2 Add Windows User 
If add Windows users, click the right option “Use Windows users”. Enter in new Windows user 
dialog box as shown below.
--- pag 12 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
6 
 
Figure 4-3 Dialog box “New Window User” 
Enter User Name, User Description, Domain Name, no password, click “OK”. 
Windows users and VF regular user can’t use the same name. Windows user login needs to set. 
After setting a new user, Windows users and VF regular users can’t switch each other. 
Windows users are consistent with VF users in packet, supervisory control, configuration of 
operation group. 
 
Tip： 
 
Username should be the username of configured Windows domain user in domain 
server. 
 
Windows user don’t write domain name. Windows domain user need to write 
corresponding domain name. 
 
Windows user can not be used as user of cross-domain referred. 
 
4.1.3 Specify User-binding Card 
In VF system software, it supports to bind IC card or ID card for the existed users. After binding the 
card, the user can log in to the monitoring system for operation through password verification, card 
verification or complex identification.
--- pag 13 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
7 
Specify card type 
Card type should be firstly specified before binding cards for users. After the card type is specified, 
inside the project only supports this type card. 
You can specify card type by the following steps: 
1. 
Select “User management > card identification > card type” and then the dialog box pops up. 
 
Figure 4-4 Card module setting dialog box 
2. 
In the drop-down menu of “select card type”, you can select card type the current project 
supports, ID card or IC card. 
3. 
Click “OK” to save the settings of card type. 
Bind cards for users 
Through the following operations, bind cards for the existed user. 
1) Select the user in the user list and select "Properties" in the right-click menu. The "User 
Properties" configuration dialog box will be displayed, as shown in the figure below.
--- pag 14 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
8 
 
Figure 4-5 “User Properties” dialog box 
2) Click the button 
 on the right corner and the card identification dialog box will pop up. 
 
Figure 4-6 "Manage Card" dialog box 
3) Click “Bind” and verify the card in the card reading device. 
When users need to bind multiple cards, they need to repeat step 2) ~ step 3). 
After the user binds the card, if you need to delete the specified card, you can select the card to be
--- pag 15 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
9 
deleted in the dialog box shown in the figure above, and click “Unbind” without verified the card. 
After binding a card to a user, you can configure the identification method for user login monitoring. 
For detailed configuration instructions, see Configure Card . 
 
Tips： 
 
One user can bind the multiple cards, and the maximum of the card is 10. 
 
After binding a card to a user, the card is only valid in the user's local domain, and the card 
will be invalid in the cross-domain. 
4.2 Configure Referenced Project User 
4.2.1 Add Referenced Project User 
Operation domain references other operation domain, and users in that operation domain only 
have read authority for the tags in referenced domain. The write authority can be obtained by 
adding referenced project user (in referenced domain). 
Steps to add referenced project user: 
1. Select user to be configured in user list. 
2. Right-click and select “Add Referenced Project User” to pop up the dialog shown in 
Figure 4-6. 
 
Figure 4-7 Add referenced project user 
3. Select the operation domain from the drop-down menu of “Referenced Operation 
Domain”. 
4. Select the referenced project user from the drop-down menu of “User”. 
5. Input password of referenced project user in the box of “Password”. 
6. Click “OK” to save the reference user. 
After adding referenced project user successfully, its user name, reference domain and alaias of
--- pag 16 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
10
reference domain will be shown in the information area. 
Figure 4-7 shows that the user “Admin” is added into the referenced domain “Operation Domain0”. 
 
Figure 4-8 Admin information (after adding referenced project user) 
4.2.2 Notes 
 
Observer cannot add referenced project user and the command is grey, as shown below. 
 
Figure 4-9 Right-click “Observer” 
 
Select the observer in “User” in Figure 4-9 will pop up the prompt below, which prompt 
that the observer cannot be referenced project user. 
 
Figure 4-10 Prompt (1) 
 
Other users except observer can add referenced project user, or be added as referenced 
project user, without level limit. For example, engineer can add “Admin” (which has 
higher authority than it). 
 
Different user can add the same referenced project user. For example, the local users 
“Admin” and “Engineer 1” can both add the remote user “Admin” as referenced project 
user. 
 
A domain can reference several referenced domains. While a referenced domain can 
only have one user been added. As shown below, user “Admin” has been existed, so no 
other user in the domain can be added. Click “Yes” to replace user “Admin”.
--- pag 17 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
11 
 
Figure 4-11 Prompt (2) 
4.2.3 View/ Modify Properties of Referenced Project 
Steps to view/ modify properties of referenced project user. 
1. Right-click a referenced project and select “Properties” to pop up the dialog shown in 
Figure 4-11. 
 
Figure 4-12 Referenced User Properties 
The referenced operation domain, user name and password are shown in the 
“Referenced User Properties” dialog. 
2. Select “Modify Reference User” to enable the boxes of “User” and “Password”.
--- pag 18 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
12
 
Figure 4-13 Modify Reference User 
3. Select the referenced project user from drop-down box of “User”, and input password of 
referenced project user. 
4. Click “OK” to save the modification. 
4.3 Configure Data Group Management authority for User 
Click “Data Group”, and information display area will display the tag group of each control domain, 
and users can select tag groups with "√" to obtain the operation authority of tags in the selected 
tag group. 
 
Figure 4-14 Data Group 
“Combustion” and “Turbine” here are control domain name. 
Current user only has operation authority in monitoring for tag in tag group selected in data group 
tab. Otherwise, the user has no operation authority in monitoring for tag in tag group unselected. 
Right-click the control domain name in Figure 4-13, pop up a menu including "Select All, Clear All, 
Invert Selection", as shown in the Figure 4-14. "Select all" means to select all the tag groups in this 
control domain; "Clear All" is all the tag groups in this control domain will be unselected; "Invert 
Selection" means the selected tag groups will be cleared and the unselected tag groups will be
--- pag 19 ---
User Access Software User Manual 
 
13
selected. 
 
Figure 4-15 "Select All , Clear All, Invert Selection" in tag group 
Enable tag of the selected tag group (the enable tag should be digital) can be set in the “Enable 
tag” column. When the enable tag is ON, current users can operate tags in this tag group, else the 
operation of the tags in this tag group would not be available. If select analog for enabled tag, 
analog value will always be same as not enable tag (even if enable tag is invalid). 
4.4 Configure Alarm Acknowledge Authority for User 
After configuring the “Alarm ACK” authority in user monitoring operation authority, user can 
configure the alarm acknowledge authority for user, and specify the alarm acknowledge authority
