User Setting Guide of Windows Domain 
Section 1 Overview 
ECS-700 system includes operation domain and Windows domain. 
A Windows domain is a collection of computers that share common domain databases and 
security policies. The Windows domain is managed by the domain server, which authenticates the 
domain logon and maintains the domain's security policy and master account database. Each 
domain and each computer in the domain has a unique name. 
The ECS-700 system can be divided to one or multiple control domains and operation domains by 
the scale and structure of actual instruments. Every operation domain can monitor multiple control 
stations at the same time,or monitor the control stations jointly. By the domain management, the 
system network load of ECS-700 system can be effectively reduced to ensure the real-time 
performance of the large-scale system network. 
1.1 Typical Network 
The actual network can be configured according to the following figure, each VF operation domain 
is configured with a group of master-slave VF domain servers, and a number of operation stations 
and engineer stations. The windows domain server and the VF operations domain server can be 
the same device, with one server deployed as the windows domain server and the VF master 
domain server, another server deployed as the VF slave domain server and windows domain 
client, and the other device deployed as the windows domain client and the VF operation station. 
 
Figure 1-1 Typical Network of ECS-700 Domain and Windows Domain
--- pag 4 ---
User Setting Guide of Windows Domain 
2 
1.2 Network Instrument 
As shown as figure above, the upper part is the Windows domain, and the lower part is the VF 
operation domain network. 
 
In the windows domain, the operation system in the windows server should be server 
version, such as Windows Server 2008, Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2019. 
 
While multiple operation domains in the ECS-700 system, the Windows domain server 
can be configured for each operation domain or for multiple operating domains. If there 
are multiple Windows domain servers in the network, the Windows domain name must 
be unique, for example the windows domain can be distinguished by vf1.com, vf2.com, 
or oa1.com, oa2.com. Each Windows domain server manages the domain users in it. 
 
 
Caution: 
 
For Windows domain servers, please restart and log on with the domain account 
(generally vf\Administrator) after configured the domain server. For Windows domain 
clients, please restart and log on with the local account (generally Administrator) after 
added the computer to the windows domain. 
 
Switching user in Windows OS will caused the failure of starting VF monitoring, 
switching user in windows OS is not recommended. If switching user in windows OS, 
please restart PC to restore the failure. 
 
Please don't modify domain server's IP address after the configuration of domain 
service is finished. That's purpose is to prevent the configuration of Windows domain 
from losing its efficacy and leading to the client unable to log in.

Intelligent Management of Alarm 
1 
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
Section 1 Overview 
VisualField (hereinafter referred to as VF) provides an alarm management function including 
latching alarm management, shelving alarm management, merging alarm management, operating 
state management, regulation and procedure files management, and so on. This function makes it 
easier to manage the alarms occurring in DCS (Distributed Control System). 
1.1 Introduction of Alarms 
This section mainly introduces the basic concept, classification, states and the rules of switching 
states. 
1.1.1 Alarm Classification 
Alarms would warn operators to pay attention to the special events and adopt the corresponding 
actions. Generally, the system supports users pre-defining the triggering conditions of alarms as 
well as the warning methods. For instance, in production field, users need to observe the tank 
liquid level, so they can customize the HIGH alarm of the tank liquid level and set the system to 
broadcast sound for warning. 
 
Systematic alarm 
This kind of alarm refers to the alarms from the instruments connected to DCS or alarms 
only coming from DCS, such as the cabinet fan in DCS. 
 
Process alarm 
The device parameters may take effects on the production technology in the field shall be 
pre-defined in DCS. When the real-time device parameter exceeds the limit, the alarm is 
generated. After its occurrence, DCS would adopt a way of outstanding display or sound 
warning to remind operators to deal with the alarms. Therefore the loss in field would be 
averted. 
For instance, the temperature value of a certain sensor in field determines the production 
environment safety. This temperature is set as an analog input AI1 and its High alarm 
value is configured as 30. When AI1>30 is satisfied, DCS will make this tag alarm. 
Therefore the operators would be aware that the production environment needs chilling.
--- pag 6 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
2 
1.1.2 Alarm Levels 
VF supports alarm management according to levels. In application, users can customize alarm 
levels as per the alarm severity. Alarm levels in VF are form 0 to 32 and 32 is the most serious 
one. 
When configuring alarm levels, users need to consider production environment, factory 
applications, devices, and safety. After the configuration, the tags with different alarm levels have 
differing light and sound effect. 
1.1.3 Alarm State 
The figure below shows the rules of alarm-switching in VF. 
 
Figure 1-1 Alarm State Switching 
The figure above includes the alarm state as follows: 
 
Normal 
Normal state refers to a state where the system is operating in a good condition. After the 
checked alarms are clear, the system would also be in a good condition. 
 
Unacknowledged Alarms 
The unacknowledged alarms refer to the ones that are beyond the normal range and 
satisfy the alarm conditions. The acknowledged alarms would also go into this state 
when they again reach the alarm conditions. 
 
Acknowledged Alarms 
The acknowledged alarms refer to the alarms whose alarm conditions are still being 
satisfied while operators have already received and checked.
--- pag 7 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
3 
 
Unacknowledged Latching Alarms 
Latching alarm is a kind of selective alarming state. Only when the system enabled latching 
alarm function, alarms can have an alarming state of unacknowledged latching alarm. One 
unacknowledged alarm with alarming conditions already unsatisfied is exactly in the 
alarming state of unacknowledged latching alarm. 
1.2 Function Introduction of Alarm Management 
VF supports the unified alarm management, including latching alarm management, alarm 
suppression management and merging alarm management. VF mainly has the following alarm 
management functions: 
 
Grouping/area management 
Grouping alarms/area alarms makes tracking and managing alarms easier. Groups shall 
be created according to the field area, device parts, and operator responsibility or 
production process. 
 
Latching alarm management 
Latching alarms refer to alarms which have been cleared before being acknowledged. By 
latching alarm management, users can avoid overlooking the vital alarms. When a 
latching alarm occurs, this alarm can recover the normal condition only when operators 
check the alarms. In VF, users can enable or forbid latching alarms as per differing 
levels. 
 
Re-triggering alarms 
VF periodically detects alarms as per the preset re-triggering time. During the detecting 
process, if the alarms have been acknowledged but alarm conditions have been not 
cleared, then the alarms would be marked with a re-triggering symbol and start light and 
sound warning again. 
 
Merging alarms 
Merging alarms means to sort out the same type of alarms of one tag from all types (for 
example, when H and HH alarms occur concurrently, only HH alarm is displayed). After 
the classification, alarms would display in the alarm list and alarm column. By merging 
alarms, the items in the alarm list and the alarm number in the alarm column would be 
reduced. 
 
Shelving alarms 
By shelving alarms, operators can temperately shelve the annoying alarms. 
VF supports to shelve alarms. The shelved alarms would be displayed in shelving alarm 
list rather than in the process alarm list. Alarms displayed in the shelving alarm list could 
return to the process alarm list by canceling the shelving. In addition, the shelved alarms 
would also return to the process alarm list as the shelving time expires.
--- pag 8 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
4 
 
Suppressing alarms 
By suppressing alarms, users could preset the annoying alarms in order to avoid the 
impact on the system from the annoying alarms. VF supports to suppress the individual 
alarm as well as multiple alarms by operating state. 
 
Operating state management 
Operating state refers to common work scene in field, such as startup and shut-down, 
etc. By operating state management, users can define the operating state of devices in 
field in any particular moment, and manage devices by the operating state. 
 
Regulation and procedure files management 
VFHMICfg supports to define tag’s alarm regulation and procedure files. The files are 
in .doc format, whose content depends on the actual field requirement, generally 
including tag alarm cause, operational suggestion and possible results. After configuring 
files in VFHMICfg, and at the same time the alarms happening in real-time monitoring 
contain the one in the files,, the file related to the tag would pop up by manually selection. 
Section 2 Configuring Alarms 
Before configuring alarms, it is necessary to make sure the alarm levels, grouping and 
management strategy. Further, users need to continuously optimize each configuration related to 
the alarms according to the actual alarms occurring in field. 
2.1 Configuring Alarm Levels 
The number of alarm levels shall be preset once users create a project. After users designate a 
project name, the "Amount of Alarm Priority Settings" dialog box shown as follows will pop up. 
 
Figure 2-1 Number of Alarm Levels 
Alarm priority shows the urgency of different alarm levels. User can set the number of the alarm 
levels in the dialog above. System supports 6 alarm levels in default. Project in VF can support 
minimum 6 and maximum 32 alarm levels. 
After configured the number of the alarm levels, "Alarm Priority" in "Global Default Settings" will be
--- pag 9 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
5 
displayed by the preset number. For example, if there are six alarm levels by default, the alarm 
from level 0 to the alarm level 5 will be displayed in the alarm priority list. Color, icon, and other 
information can also be configured. Please refer to “2.2.2 Configuring Alarms by Alarm Priority” for 
details. 
2.2 Configuring Global Alarm Functions 
Users can uniformly configure the alarms in the system by setting the global alarm configuration in 
the project. The uniform alarm management mainly includes latching alarm sound, re-triggering 
time, merging alarms, shelving alarms, operating state management and alarm levels. 
2.2.1 Enable and Forbid Alarms 
By following steps, global alarm configuration can be completed: 
1) Select "Global Default Settings" in configuration tree and the "Alarm Setting" shown as



2.2.2 Configuring Alarms by Alarm Priority 
Alarm color, alarm shelving, alarm latching and re-triggering alarm for alarms can be configured by

The amount of alarm priority cannot be modified after setting while creating project, but other

 
Shelving and re-triggering alarms 
Configure re-triggering alarms and continue to perform re-triggering computation after

Latching and shelving alarms 
Latching alarms can be shelved. 
Alarms in shelving alarm list will stay if entering the latching state. 
The shelved latching alarm will disappear after being acknowledged. If the alarm is 
generated again and is added into the multiple-shelving shelf, it will enter alarm shelving 
list. 
The shelved alarm will return to the process alarm list when the shelving time expires. 
 
Shelving and alarm shield 
After the alarm is shelved, if tag alarm is suppressed, shielded or shielded by group or 
region, the alarm will no more be shown in the shelving list until alarm suppression, 
shield or group and region shield are eliminated. 
For either single-shelving or multiple-shelving, the alarms will be still in the shelving list 
only if the actions above occur during the shelving time. If exceeding the time, alarms will 
go back to alarm list. 
 
Shelving and user switch 
If configuring "User Switch" in the shelving shelf as "Auto Cancel", the shelved alarm 
after user switching will be eliminated. Only the shelving of current operation station can 
be eliminated, but not for shelved alarms in operation domain. 
If configuring "User Switch" in shelve shelf as "Non-auto Cancel", the shelved alarm is 
not influenced by user switching. 
 
Shelving and operation team switch 
After users switching operation team, shelved alarms of local station will stay, but only 
display the intersection with current operation team. For example, Team01 in computer A 
has A, B and C alarm regions, corresponding to tags A1, B1 and C1. Alarms A1, B1 and 
C1 is single shelved, and then switched to Team02 (with B, C and D alarm regions). 
Single shelving shelf only shows that alarms B1 and C1 are shelved, shelving 
accumulated time of B1and C1 resumes from the point of switching.

As for the acknowledged and eliminated alarms, VF will store them in the history alarm list. Click 
history alarm in the menu of the real-time monitor software, the history alarming list will pop up as 
shown in the figure below.
--- pag 42 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
38 
 
Figure 3-6 The Example of History Alarm Lists 
Users can filter history alarms by clicking 
 as per time, groups, levels and types. 
3.4 Handle Alarms 
When VF recognizes alarms, it will warn operators to handle alarms in specific ways, such as 
alarm acknowledgment, alarm shelving, viewing operating states and so forth. 
3.4.1 Merging Alarms 
VF supports alarm merging. It means alarms of differing levels of a tag would be merged to one 
alarm of the highest level. For example, if a tag generates HHH alarm, HH alarm and H alarm 
concurrently, after system merging alarms, only HHH alarm is displayed in the alarm list. After the 
alarm-merging function is enabled in the VxSysBuilder, VF will automatically merge alarms. 
Alarm operation, alarm recovery, alarm shelving such functions may influence the merged alarms 
as per the table below. 
Operational types 
Influence 
Alarm 
acknowledgment 
After the highest level alarm is acknowledged, all alarms being merged will be 
acknowledged. The acknowledged alarm cannot merge with the non-acknowledged 
alarms. 
Alarm recovery 
After the highest alarm recovers, whether to display the merged alarms depends on its 
inferior alarm. If HHH alarm recovers but HH alarm exists, H alarm would continue to 
merge with the HH alarm. 
Alarm re-triggering 
If HHH alarm doesn’t enable the re-triggering while HH does, after alarms are merged, 
HHH alarm will display re-triggering warning.
--- pag 43 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
39 
Operational types 
Influence 
Alarm shelving 
After the highest level alarm is shelved, all the merged alarms would be shelved. If HH 
alarm is shelved, the merged H alarm will be shelved as well. However the alarms in the 
shelving list will not be merged. If HH alarm recovers without acknowledgment, two 
alarms would be displayed in the shelving list, respectively HH alarm and H alarm. 
If merged low-level alarms are shelved, they will not influence high-level alarms. If HH 
alarm is generated after H alarm is shelved, HH alarm will not be shelved. 
Alarm suppressing 
If merged low-level alarms are suppressed, it will not influence the high-level alarms. 
After the high-level alarm is suppressed, whether to generate alarms will depend on the 
inferior alarms. For example, if HHH alarm is suppressed, H alarm will merge with HH 
alarm and only HH alarm will be displayed. 
Alarm latching 
If latching alarm is enabled, latching alarm will not be merged. If HH alarm is latched 
and H alarm is under generating state, alarm list interface will respectively display 2 
items of alarm information. 
 
3.4.2 Re-triggering Alarms 
VF detects two kinds of alarms shown below every re-triggering time: 
 
If the acknowledged alarms undergoing the re-triggering time didn’t disappear, the 
alarms will be generated again. 
 
If the eliminated alarms undergoing the re-triggering time are generated again, the 
alarms will go into the alarm list again. 
In VxSysBuilder, if alarm re-triggering function is enabled and re-triggering time is configured, VF 
will automatically execute the re-triggering detection as per the re-triggering time. When alarms 
are undergoing the re-triggering detection, the recognized alarms will be displayed in the alarm list 
with 
 symbol. Every time the alarms are re-triggered, a new item of alarm will be generated, 
which means the alarm list will display the same alarm re-triggered at different time. Other display 
rules are the same with the newly generated alarms, with no more detailed description. 
Impact on re-triggering alarms from other functions 
Operational types 
Influence 
Alarm shelving 
Alarms are displayed in the shelving list and it keeps the light warning and also 
keeps the re-triggering time accumulated continuously. 
Cancel, suppression and 
shielding after shelving 
After alarms are shelved, suppression, shelving and shielding would be 
canceled. The re-triggering time would continue. 
alarm operations under 
operating state 
It doesn’t influence the re-triggering time accumulation. Once the re-triggering 
time is up, alarms will be generated as per the original alarm level. 
Delta release 
The re-triggered alarms would be delta released after being modified, which will 
not influence the re-triggering calculation of the generated alarms. Alarms 
would be effective only after being re-generated. 
After the re-triggering period is modified, the system will compare the new 
re-triggering period with the current accumulated value. After delta release, the 
system will configure the triggering count value of all the acknowledged and 
non-recovered alarms as the smaller value in the comparison result. E.g. If the 
new re-triggering period is 10s while the left re-triggering time is 15s, then the 
new remainder of the re-triggering time.
--- pag 44 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
40 
3.4.3 Alarm Shielding and Releasing 
In real-time monitor software, as for the alarms not requiring attention temporarily, VF supports 
alarm shielding by alarm groups or control stations as well as releasing shielding as per the 
following requirement. 
By the following steps, users can set alarm shielding and releasing: 
 
Process alarms 
In the process alarm interface, click 
 in the toolbar and the following interface will pop 
up, where users can shield alarms or release shielding according to the alarm groups. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-7 The example of the Process Alarm 
 
System alarms 
Shielding of system alarm and releasing shielding will be displayed in the system alarm 
interface. The detailed steps are similar to the process alarm, with no more detailed 
description.
--- pag 45 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
41 
3.4.4 Alarm Acknowledgment 
After checking the alarms generated in the system, operators can execute acknowledgment to 
them. The acknowledged alarm will not flash or sound. By the following operations, each type of 
alarms can be acknowledged. Take the process alarm as an example to introduce how to 
acknowledge alarms. 
1) Open the process alarm interface as shown in the figure below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-8 The Example of Process Alarm 
2) Acknowledge alarms 
 
Item acknowledgment: after selecting an alarm, click “acknowledge” in the right-click 
menu to acknowledge alarms. “Process alarm”, “pop-up alarm”, “alarm list” and “system 
alarm” all support item acknowledgment. 
 
Batch acknowledgment: clicking 
 in the toolbar can acknowledge alarms in the 
current display interface in batch. “Process alarm”, “pop-up alarm” and “system alarm” all 
support batch acknowledgment. 
After acknowledging alarms, click 
 to view the acknowledged alarms. When the alarms are 
eliminated, alarms will disappear from the acknowledged alarm list. 
3.4.5 Alarm Shelving 
In the real-time monitor software, users can temporarily shelve alarms to avoid the negative 
impact from the annoying alarms. 
Shelving alarms 
In each type of alarm lists, users can execute the single shelving by the following steps. 
1) Select one alarm and click “shelve” in the right-click menu. The dialog box below will pop
--- pag 46 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
42 
up. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-9 The Example of the Single Alarm Shelving 
2) Select the corresponding shelf to the shelving in the “shelf name”, and then the 
configured alarm shelf type will appear. 
 
The shelving type of the selected shelf is single shelving, which means the alarm is 
single shelving. 
 
The shelving type of the selected shelf is multiple shelving, which means the alarm is 
multiple shelving. An alarm configured as a multiple shelved alarm which will stay in 
the shelving alarm list even though it is re-triggered during the shelving period. 
3) Input the reason of executing the operation in the “operation reason”. 
4) Click “OK” to complete the single alarm shelving. 
After executing alarm shelving, click “shelving alarm” page in the process alarm to view the current 
shelving alarm as shown in the figure below.
--- pag 47 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
43 
 
Figure 3-10 The Example of the Shelving Alarm List 
Select one alarm in the shelving alarm list and manage it by the right-click menu: 
 
Cancel shelving the shelved alarm. 
After shelving is canceled or shelving time is up, alarm will go back to the process alarm 
list again. 
If the alarm is not acknowledged, the alarm flashes and makes sound. Pop up again if 
pop-up alarm is configured. 
 
Re-shelve the shelved alarm 
Re-shelve alarms by right-click menu to keep alarms continuously shelved. 
Preset shelving alarm 
After configuring “multiple shelving” shelf in the configuration, users can create a preset shelving 
alarm to shelve the annoying alarms in advance. 
1) In the “shelving alarm” page in the process alarm interface, click 
 then “the preset of 
multiple shelving alarms” dialog below pops up.
--- pag 48 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
44 
 
 
 
Figure 3-11 Presets of Multiple Shelving 
2) Select one shelf configured in the “shelving shelf” and the “add” on the right side is 
enabled to use. 
3) Click “add” in the pop-up “alarm selector” dialog. 
The “alarm selector” will list all alarms with shelving enabled and alarms without 
presetting shelving. 
The enabling and dis-enabling of alarm shelving is configured as per alarm levels. For 
detailed information, please refer to 《system configure user manual》. 
4) Select the alarms requiring preset in the “alarm selector” and click “OK”, and then the 
“multiple shelving time setting” dialog will pop up as shown in the figure below. 
 
 
 
Figure 3-12 “Time Settings of Multiple Shelving” Dialog Box
--- pag 49 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
45 
5) In the dialog box above, users can configure the start time of the alarm preset shelving 
and the multiple shelving intervals 
 
Select "Set confirming time as the shelving start time", pre-shelve time starts from 
clicking "OK". 
 
Select "Set preset time as the shelving start time" to show the dialog below, in which 
can set the "Shelving Interval" and "Shelving Start Time" for continuous shelve. 
After selecting the shelving start time, user can input the alarm shelving reason in 
“Operation Reason” box as required. 
6) After setting the pre-shelving condition, click "OK" to add pre-shelving to list. Repeat the 
steps above to add pre-shelving alarms for each shelf. 
3.5 Manage Alarms by the Operating States of Devices 
After configured device's state, device's state can be viewed and alarm operation can be executed 
in the real-time monitoring software. Click 
 in alarm bar and the device state list below will 
pop up. 
 
Figure 3-13 Device Operating State List 
All configured device states and alarm operation are shown in device state list. There are 3 kinds 
of state information in device rows: 
 
Current state shows the current running state. 
 
Calculation state means the state is calculated out by the expression of the operating
--- pag 50 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
46 
state. 
 
Calculation state mode shows the mode of device state switched to. 
3.5.1 Switching Operating States 
State can be switched automatically by configured expression and switch mode, and supports 
forced switch. 
Auto Switch Rules 
Device state switches automatically by rules below: 
 
A state expression is satisfied and the switch mode is "Auto", enter into the state 
automatically. 
 
A state expression is satisfied and the switch mode is "Manual", state icon 
 in each 
operation station monitoring interface will flash. Open state status table, all operation 
stations will switch to the state after acknowledged, and state icon will no more flash. 
 
A state expression is satisfied and the switch mode is "Only Detect", both "Current State" 
and "Calculation State" are shown as "Calculation State", but not perform alarm 
operation in state, i.e. not perform configured alarm suppression, alarm threshold 
modification and alarm priority modification. 
Force and Un-force 
A state can be forced to enter by following steps in state list. 
1) Right-click a state and select "Force" and the dialog below will pop up. 
 
 
 
 
 
Figure 3-14 “State Force” Dialog Box
--- pag 51 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
47 
Figure above lists the current states, selectable force states and all the alarm operations 
of devices. "Alarm Operation List" has listed all the configured alarm operating status. 
 
"Operation Mode" shows configured alarm operation, generally shows suppress, 
threshold or priority. 
 
"Alarm Value" shows target of alarm operation, such as "Suppress", "95" and "High". 
 
"Current Alarm Value" shows current information of tag. 
2) Select forced status from drop-down menu of "Force State" 
3) Click "OK", force to switch the device state. 
After forced to state, "Current State"of device shows "Force State Name" with yellow bottom color, 
as shown below. 
 
Figure 3-15 The Example of the Operational Results of “State Force” 
User can select "Unforce" in right-click menu of device forced to state as required. 
3.5.2 Alarm Suppression 
Alarm suppression, i.e. eliminate alarm dynamically. In VFHMICfg, after users configuring the 
alarm suppression in the device operating state, the executive condition of alarm suppression will 
be displayed in the real-time monitor. In the table of operating state, click the 
 button next to the 
“device” to view the executive condition of the device alarms (alarm suppression, modification of 
alarm limit values and the modification of alarm authority). Refer to the figure below, taking the 
operating state of device 1 as an example, multiple tag alarms are under the suppression state.
--- pag 52 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
48 
 
Figure 3-16 The Alarm States under the Device Operating State 
After suppressing alarm or eliminating suppression, changes below will be shown in monitoring 
windows such as alarm list and graphics, etc. 
 
Alarm sound 
After suppressed, alarm stops to make sound. After suppression is eliminated, alarm 
makes sound again. 
 
Alarm in alarm list 
After suppressed, alarm will no more be shown in list. After eliminating suppression, 
alarm will be shown in the alarm list again. 
 
Alarm in graphics 
After suppressed, tag alarm in graphics will not flash any more. After suppress is 
eliminated, tag flashes again. 
 
Alarm statistics 
After suppressed, suppressed tag will not be counted in alarm statistics. After 
suppression is eliminated, tag alarm statistics will be restored. 
Suppressing alarm by rules below: 
 
Support suppressing alarms in operation domain and referencing domain, i.e. after alarm 
in referenced domain is suppressed, it is also be suppressed in referencing domain. 
 
Support suppressing latching alarm. Suppressed latching alarm will not be shown in 
process list (pop-up alarm) until the suppression is eliminated. After latching alarm is 
shielded or shielded by group and region, it will not be shown in process list.
--- pag 53 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
49 
3.5.3 Modify Alarm Threshold 
Modify alarm threshold, i.e. modify alarm threshold from X to Y, and it will become effective when 
alarm generated next time. After users modifying alarm threshold, alarm will be generated in 
monitoring by new alarm threshold. 
Alarm threshold modification is similar to the alarm suppression, which both are executed in the 
real-time monitor software as per the configuration in the VFHMICfg, with no more detailed 
description. 
 
Tips： 
 
Global function block tag does not support modifying alarm threshold. 
 
Suppressed alarm supports modifying alarm threshold. 
 
Modify Alarm Priority 
Modify alarm priority, i.e. modify alarm priority from X to Y, and it will become effective when alarm 
generated next time. After alarm priority is modified, changes below will happen in the monitor: 
 
After modifying priority, tag alarm generated later will be shown and make sound by 
modified priority. 
 
Alarm re-triggering will be performed by new alarm priority. 
 
Alarm latching will be performed by new alarm priority. 
Alarm authority modification is similar to the alarm suppression, which both are executed in the 
real-time monitor software as per the configuration in the VFHMICfg, with no more detailed 
description. 
 
Tips： 
Users can configure re-triggering alarm and alarm latching by level. Please refer to "2.2.2 
Configuring Alarms by Alarm Priority" for details. 
 
3.6 View the Regulation and Procedure Files of Alarms 
Click alarm bar or other station to open alarm list in real-time monitoring software, and the alarm 
with the icon 
 in the alarm list is the alarms configured procedure. By the command "Pop-up
--- pag 54 ---
Intelligent Management of Alarm 
50 
Alarm Procedure" in the alarm right menu, the alarm's procedure will be shown as below.

VFFBDBuilder 
Section 1 Overview 
VFFBDBuilder is one of the most important control strategy configuration tools in control system. It 
provides functions of FBD programming and debug. 
1.1 Software Features 
Control software conforms to IEC61131-3 standard. By combining with function block library, it 
provides powerful functions of FBD user program editing and debug, and supports single program 
compiling and online download. 
FBD software supports configuration of the initial values of function block parameters, online 
parameter download and editing, displayed or non-displayed input/output pin settings, function 
block parameter settings as displayed input/out pin, user-defined function block execution order, 
debug technology based on truncated information flow, activation and close down. 
1.2 Function Features 
 
Initial values of function block parameters can be configured; 
 
The input/ output pin of function block can be set to displayed or invisible; function 
block parameters can be displayed as input/ output pins; 
 
The execution sequence of function block can be determined by users; 
 
Implement the redundancy and multicast of function block data automatically; 
 
Support online modification of function block data in user program; 
 
Provide online debugging and support activation and close down of function block’s 
input and output; 
 
The HMI properties (display decimal digits, etc) of function block’s tag can be 
configured. 
 
Modify the basic properties (description, tag level and tag group) of function block 
tag in batch.

Section 3 Create/ Import a New FBD Program 
User can create a new FBD program in VFExplorer, or import one as CSV file. Different controller 
types support different number of programs. FCU711-S and FCU712-S controllers support up to 
200 pages of user programs, and FCU713-S controller supports up to 500 pages of user 
programs. 
3.1 Create a New FBD Program 
Open the Configuration Management Software. Select corresponding controller in the 
configuration tree on the left of interface. Click “Open” from menu of “Control Scheme”, or click 
button 
 on the tool bar, a dialog box “New Custom Program” pops up, as shown in Figure 3-1. 
 
Figure 3-1 Dialog box of “New Custom Program” 
Click “OK” after input the name and descriptions to create a new FBD custom program, as shown 
in Figure 3-1.
--- pag 8 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
4 
 
Figure 3-2 Interface of Configuration Management Software 
Double click the new program to open editing interface. 
3.2 Configure FBD Program Properties 
3.2.1 Set FBD Program Properties 
Users can set the phase and period of FBD program. Phase and period will affect the running time 
of the custom program. 
1) Select any program and then right click it, select “Property” and the custom program property 
dialog box pops up as shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 3-3 Dialog box of program property setting (the left graph shows FCU712-S and the right graph 
shows FCU711-S) 
1. 
Configure the basic properties according to the table below. 
Configuration 
Item 
Configuration Description
--- pag 9 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
5 
Configuration 
Item 
Configuration Description 
Name 
A string of no more than 64 th English characters or 32 Chinese characters, only 
begin with a letter and be letters, numbers and underscores, it can not be duplicated 
(the system also can not be duplicated function blocks) . 
Description 
A string of no more than 128 th English characters or 64 Chinese characters. 
Cycle 
The supported cycles are fast cycle, 1 times, 2 times, 5 times and 10 times. 
When the cycle of the user program is “fast cycle”, the fast scan cycle of the 
controller is used to execute the user program, and the phase configuration is not 
supported. 
Starting phase 
Setting the starting phase is a function set for distributing the program running load 
of the controller in each phase. After downloading, each program cyclically runs 
according to the set initial phase. 
Priority 
When the user programs have the same starting phase, the controller will determine 
the user program to be executed first according to the priority. 
 
3.2.2 Set FBD Program Password 
Follow steps below to set password for FBD program: 
1. Right-click a FBD program, and select “New Password” and the dialog below pops up. 
 
Figure 3-4 Create Password 
2. Input the password and confirm it in boxes “Password” and “Confirm Password”. 
3. Click “OK” to save the password of FBD program.

, and pop up the following dialog when opening 
FBD program.

The folder “\data\FBDTemplate” in installation directory includes 2 FBD program module as 
CSV files. 
 
CSV file with the postfix “loop” is single loop or cascade loop FBD program applying PID 
and PIDEX function blocks. 
 
CSV file with the postfix “motor” is valve FBD program applying DIO21V, DIO01V, 
DIO11V, DIO22V, DIO11M, DIO21M, Motor, Valve function blocks. 
3.3.1 Operation Steps 
Operation steps to import CSV file: 
1. Right “Custom Program” and select “Import”. 
2. Select CSV file from the “Open” dialog pops up and click “Open”. 
FBD program will be created automatically in the right pane after importing FBD program 
successfully, as shown below. The top 2 are FBD programs created by CSV file with the 
postfix “motor”, and the rest 4 are created by CSV file with the postfix “loop”. 
 
Figure 3-6 FBD programs created after importing CSV file

System prescribes that when invalid function block exists in current program, adding of 
function block examples won’t be allowed, and compile won’t pass. 
 
Auto Upgrade of Invalid Function Block 
When starting the program, dialog box of “Invalid Function Block Auto-upgrade” will pop up if 
invalid function block exists in current program, and current invalid function block will be upgraded 
automatically after clicking “Yes”. If click “Cancel” now, users can also upgrade function block latter 
by “Auto Update” command in the right-click menu in editing area. The invalid function block can 
be auto updated while compiling in Configuration Explorer Software. 
 
Tips: 
 
When upgrading function block, if pin parameter does not exist or parameter is modified 
(either parameter name or parameter data type), lines corresponding to the parameter 
will be deleted by system, therefore, program should be re-checked after auto-upgrade 
to guarantee correct logic. 
 
When alias function block becomes non-alias function block, or non-alias function 
block becomes alias function block by adding an alias to this block, function blocks of 
this type can’t be upgraded automatically. 
 
Auto-upgrade may change the address of function block. 
 
When it is found by upgrade check that upgrade may cause any item of data area, 
multicast data area and redundancy data area off limit, upgrade will be unavailable. 
 
6.2.10 Set Display Mode of Function Block 
The programming software of FBD supports the display mode of function block as needed. 
 
Display/ hide default values of input parameters 
Select [View>Function Block Input Parameter Initial Value] in the menu bar. If this 
configuration item is checked, the default value when the function block input pin is not 
connected is displayed. 
 
Display/ hide some pins or parameters 
Select [View>Function Block Configuration Parameter Initial Value] in the menu bar. If the 
configuration item is checked, some pins or parameters of the function block are 
displayed. If the item is not checked, some pins or parameters of the function block will be 
hided. 
6.2.11 Create and Configure Logic Diagram 
Click the icon 
 “Logic Diagram Select Frame” in toolbar, press the left key of mouse and drag
--- pag 43 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
39 
into a frame, in which the graphics will be generated automatically. 
 
Figure 6-31 Logic Diagram Select Frame 
1. Several graph objects can be put in a FBD program. VFFBDBuilder can generate several 
logic diagrams according to the frame graph objects. 
2. The “Edit” box is in the lower right corner of frame. The name cannot be empty (and 
should conform to the naming rules of graphics), Frame names in the program page 
cannot repeat, cannot contain characters “\\/:*?\”<>|!@#$%^&=,.';[]+-~(){}`”. The length 
cannot exceed 24 characters. 
3. The graph object can be moved by selecting. User can select copy, paste, delete and 
properties settings by right-clicking the frame. The size of frame can be set in properties 
settings dialog, which cannot be less than pixel 200*400. 
4. Click the “Show/Hide Select Frame” button in toolbar to show or hide the select frame. 
Save the settings, so the select frame will be shown as set when open again. 
5. Right-click the select frame and select “Properties Settings” and the dialog below pops 
up.
--- pag 44 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
40 
 
Figure 6-32 Properties Settings 
Select a function block “PIDEP” in select frame, as shown below. 
 
Figure 6-33 Draw select frame 
In the real-time monitor, users can open this function block, click “Pop-up logic” button to view the 
logic shown in the selection box. If the logic contains data reference, it displays the real-time data 
according to the type of data reference. 
 
If the data reference is normal tags, it normally displays the real-time value of tags. 
 
If the data reference is data tags, it only displays the real-time values of array tags in this 
local control domain. The real-time values of array tags in the reference domain doesn’t 
be displayed. 
6.3 Connection line 
6.3.1 Connect Function Blocks 
Lines between function blocks should come from output to input, users should first select the 
output of a function block (a blue box will appear around the output when it is selected) and keep 
the mouse button pressed until it is dragged to the input of another function block, and in this way,
--- pag 45 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
41 
the line between output and input is created. 
6.3.2 Set Special Line 
Connection line can be set as special line in the mode of Auto Queue to eliminate the circle. When 
Auto Queue is executed, the special line will be ignored by the program. 
The method of setting special line: select the specified connection line and click the icon 
 in 
the Toolbar. The selected line will be brown (the line has been brown will not change), which 
means the line has been turned into special line. 
6.3.3 Set Ordinary Line 
Special line can bee restored as ordinary line in the mode of Auto Queue, and then it will be 
included by the program when Auto Queue is executed. 
Special line can be restored to the ordinary line by the buttons in toolbar. Select the special line 
(displayed as brown) and select to restore it the ordinary line (displayed as black) . 
 
Tip: 
 
Only the lines from output pin of upstream function block to input pin of downstream 
function block are allowed. 
 
Software will check the consistency of data types of objects connected by the line 
automatically, and connection will not be allowed if data types are not consistent (line 
will become red in this case, normally it is blue). 
 
When the line connected the BOOL data, the line will be the broken black line. 
 
One output pin of function block can be connected to several input pins of other 
function blocks, but one input pin of function block can only be connected to one 
output pin of another function block. 
 
6.4 Compile 
 
Tip: 
Users can debug the function blocks with simulation controller when real controller is 
absent or concerning of security. 
 
Compilation is used to check whether the reference tag exists, whether tag name conflicts exist on 
program page, and the compilation result will be displayed on output bar. 
A completed FBD program should be saved, compiled and downloaded before online debug. If the 
program passed compilation, but hasn’t been downloaded, prompt box will pop up after clicking
--- pag 46 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
42 
“online” to prompt “Program need download”. 
If the compilation is not passed, the program can be saved, but cannot be downloaded. 
6.5 Online Debug 
After the compilation and download of FBD, click “Online” button in the toolbar for online debug, 
and “Program Debug”, “Function Block Debug”, “Variable Debug” and “Save the Real-time Value 
of Function Block” keys become enabled, in addition, option “activate all input parameters” and 
“activate all output parameters” will be enabled. 
Instructions to function keys are shown in Table 6-2. 
Table 6-2 Instruction list of function keys 
Online 
Program Debug 
Function Block Debug 
 
 
Tip: 
Users can set input and output to Active or Inactive according to requirements when 
debugging. Users can select “Activate All Input Parameters” and “Activate All Output 
Parameters” in “Program”. 
 
6.5.1 Program Debug 
Click “Program Debug” button and the real-time value of each function block pin in program area 
will be displayed. If the user function block or global function block in the program area contains 
array parameters, the array parameters do not display real-time values. 
 
Figure 6-34 Real-time value of function block pin
--- pag 47 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
43 
As shown in the figure below, the real-time value of each pin of the PID function block is displayed 
in the program area. IN1 and OUT1 in G_SF are array-type parameters, so their real-time value is 
not displayed. If you need to view the real-time value of the parameter of this type of function block, 
you can click the “Set” button in the parameter real-time value column in the function block 
parameter debugging interface, and the real-time value of the array member will be displayed in 
the pop-up interface. 
In the debugging process, if the program didn’t run or the result wasn’t correct, the possible cause 
is the program has been shielded. You should check the status of the program for confirming 
whether or not it is shielded. For details, refer to “Online” section in VFExplorer User Manual. 
6.5.2 Function Block Debug 
Click “Function Block Debug” button, interface of function block parameter debug will pop up. 
Select any function block and the real-time data of all parameters of the function block will be 
displayed in debug bar, and modification on-line is allowed (except for configuration parameter). 
 
Figure 6-35 Function block parameter debug
--- pag 48 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
44 
If the control scheme would be changed if a parameter is modified in real-time status, the 
parameter is called configuration parameter. For example, Direct/Reverse action selection switch 
(SWPN), control output type (OUT_OPT) in PID function block, etc. 
 
Tips: 
For FF function block, parameter values in different status are in different colors. 
 
Blue question mark refers to that the parameter status is uncerten. 
 
Red cross refers to that the parameter status is bad. 
 
Black refers to that the parameter status is good. 
 
6.5.3 Variable Debug 
Click “Variable Debug” button, variable debug column will pop up, as shown in Figure 6-37. 
 
Figure 6-36 Variable debug bar 
Double click reference tags connected to each function block pin in debug status, the real-time 
value of corresponding tag will be displayed in variable debug column (as shown in Figure 6-38, 
double click reference tag AI00040001 connected to IN1 pin in function block ADD, and the 
real-time value of the reference tag is displayed in variable debug column).
--- pag 49 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
45 
 
Figure 6-37 Variable debug bar displays real-time value 
6.5.4 Save the Real-time Value of Function Block 
Select any function block and click “Save the Real-time Value of Function Block” button, dialog box 
for saving parameter will pop up. The real-time value of function block can be saved by this 
function, making it convenient for parameter upload. When uploading real-time data of function 
blocks, software record closes data at the point where data is uploaded and then upload them.
--- pag 50 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
46 
 
Figure 6-38 Parameter save 
If the real-time value of parameter is modified in online state (parameter value is modified in 
parameter debug window shown in Figure 6-36), it will be distinguished by red, as shown in Figure 
6-40.
--- pag 51 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
47 
 
Figure 6-39 Parameter save 2 
 
Tips: 
 
In debug state, Input/ Output of function block can be activated by right-click menu of 
the function block. 
 
Parameters that can’t be modified in debug state can only be adjusted in function block 
parameter column in function block properties settings interface.
--- pag 52 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
48 
Section 7 Other Operations and Prompts 
7.1 Modify Basic Properties in Batch 
User can modify the description, tag group and tag level of complex function block in batch via the 
information bar. 
Steps to modify basic properties of function block in batch: 
1. Select the function block whose basic properties should be modified in batch in the edit 
area. 
2. Select [View/ Information Bar] in menu bar to pop up the “Information Bar” below. 
 
Figure 7-1 Modify function block properties in batch in information bar 
3. User can modify function block properties in batch in “Information Bar”: 
 
After cancel the “Auto Sorting for Function Block”, user can right-click to change its 
execution sequence. 
 
Right-click to pop up the function block properties dialog, in which user can change the 
function block properties. 
 
Support copy and paste. 
 
Support pasting contents in Excel for description, tag group and tag level of function 
block: normal format of tag group is “Tag Group N”. There is a space between “N” and 
“Tag Group”. Description of custom tag group should conform to this rule too. 
 
Tips: 
 
Execution sequence and tag name of function block don’t support modification in 
batch. 
 
Basic properties are unnecessary for normal function block. As the function block ADD 
shown in the figure above. So it is not editable.
--- pag 53 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
49 
7.2 Object Movement and Object Zoom 
7.2.1 Object movement 
FBD programming software supports dragging function blocks, users can click the selected 
function block with the mouse button pressed, release the mouse until it is dragged to required 
location, and the line is moved correspondingly. 
7.2.2 Object zoom 
All diagram objects can be zoomed, and the zoom rate is 0.6~1.5, users can implement operation 
of Zoom in, Zoom out and recover to function blocks in work area by clicking corresponding icons 
in toolbar, please refer to Introductions to Toolbar Icon Functions for specific information. 
7.3 Print Properties settings 
FBD programming software supports the general functions of Print, Print preview, and page layout 
setting. In addition, print information of footers can also be set. Click the item of “Print page footer 
setting” in “file”, window of footer setting will pop up, as shown in Figure 7-2. 
 
Figure 7-2 Footer Setting 
Some specific information of configuration program (i.e. program function name, Designed, 
Reviewed, version and other information) can be set. Click the place corresponding to a certain 
item to implement setting, and select “Yes” to complete the setting. The printed footer is same as 
set. 
7.4 Diagram Settings 
The software can execute Diagram Settings. Select “File” and click “Page Settings” to pop up the 
following dialog.
--- pag 54 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
50 
 
Figure 7-3 Diagram Settings 
 
Diagram: select the diagram size, Diagram 1#(S), Diagram 2#(M) or Diagram 3#(L) 
from the pull-down menu. 
 
Orientation: select the diagram orientation, landscape or portrait. 
 
Footer: select whether to enable the footer. 
The diagram setting will change the print effect. Different diagram settings will result in different 
print effects. 
7.5 View the Logic of Global Function Block 
Users can view the logic of global function block conveniently after invoking global function block. 
The view steps are: 
1. Select the global function block to be viewed in the edit area, right-click it and select 
“View Logic”. 
2. Pop up VFSTModule software, in which the global function block is shown. 
7.6 Import/ Export 
The import or export functions of FBD program can be achieved by this operation. 
Click [File/ Export], dialog box of “Save As” will pop up, select save path and click “Yes” to save 
current FBD program (save in .fbdi form). 
Click [File/ Import], dialog box of “Open” will pop up, select needed file (in .fbdi form) to import 
program saved in the file.
--- pag 55 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
51 
7.7 Supervision Parameter of Function Block Example Update 
When some parameter data of current advanced function block example is modified, users should 
save configuration to configuration server in configuration management software so that 
information of local configuration can be uploaded to server completely. 
Supervision parameter of function block example update includes: add function block tag, update 
supervision parameter of function block, etc. 
7.8 Delete 
All delete confirmation in FBD is No by default. 
7.9 Alarm Priority Setting 
The priority of alarm is arrayed at tag (or function block) level, the priorities of all alarm items within 
one tag or function block is consistent. Users can modify the priority of tag or function block, but 
can’t configure the priority of each alarm item of a tag or function block.
--- pag 56 ---
VFFBDBuilder User Manual IM41S59-E 
52

VFFFBuilder User Manual 
Section 1 Overview 
VFFFBuilder is a part of ECS-700 System software, by which the system can support FOUNDATION 
fieldbus and users can configure FOUNDATION fieldbus H1 segment. 
1.1 Functions 
VFFFBuilder is designed basing on Microsoft Windows and can be used by users with the basic 
Windows operation knowledge. Up to now, VFFFBuilder supports the Device Description (DD) file 
interpretation of fieldbus device registered by the FOUNDATION, and the online and offline 
configurations. 
Users can configure and modify the parameters of fieldbus device easily and connect fieldbus 
device with ECS-700 System to monitor the PD-TAG in system monitoring software. 
1.2 Terms 
Terms 
Instruction 
Capabilities File 
Describe the functions of function blocks in FF device and their 
initial values. Its suffix is .cff. It forms drive file of device with DD 
file. Capabilities file is provided by device supplier. 
Device Description File 
FF device description file, which is provided by device supplier, 
including .ffo and .sym files. It forms device drive with CFF file. 
DD Tool 
Import DD file of manufacturer to installation directory of 
VisualField by DD tool.

Section 2 Startup 
2.1 Precondition 
The VFFFBuilder uses the AM712-S and AM716-S of the ECS-700 system as the FF H1 interface 
module to realize the FF H1 network segment configuration software platform. Before starting the 
FF configuration software, the following two tasks must be completed: 
 
Install FF software 
When installing the VF system software, check "FfSystem", and the FF software will be 
installed synchronously during the software installation process. 
When installing the VF system software, if "FfSystem" is not checked, the FF installation 
package can be obtained in the installation package for independent installation. 
 
Add FF interface module in the configuration 
In VFIOBuilder, add AM712-S or AM716-S. 
Please refer to the VF Installation Guide for specific installation methods and precautions, 
and refer to the Hardware Module Builder User Manual for detailed operation methods of 
AM712-S and AM716-S configuration. 
2.2 Getting Started 
1. Add AM712-S/AM716-S in VFIOBuilder or scan all system hardware modules (including 
AM712-S/AM716-S). 
2. Select AM712-S/AM716-S in Hardware Configuration Tree, right-click the 
Communication Configuration. Then the interface of VFFFBuilder pops up as 
shown in Figure 3-1.

Operations such as segment property setting and device configuration can be implemented in the

3.2.1 Composed Parts 
Device Configuration Window is composed of:

shown in Figure 3-4, and ordered by names of manufacturers. 
The window is initially in dock state and locates in the interface of VFFFBuilder. Double-click the 
title bar to alter it to float state. Double-click again or select Dock in the right-click menu to restore it 
to dock state. 
 
 
Figure 3-4 Manufacturer List 
 The Manufacturer List includes: 
 
Manufacturer name and code 
 
Device model and name 
 
 Details of the device, which are composed of 6 digits and respectively represent for 
device version (the first 2 digits), device DD version (the medium 2 digits) and 
device CFF version (the last 2 digits).
--- pag 14 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
11 
Section 4 Configure Fieldbus H1 Segment & Device 
VFFFBuilder can implement operations including: 
Setting 
 
Assign and manage the node address of the fieldbus device automatically; 
 
Set the PD-Tag and the FB-Tag; 
 
Modify and configure the device block parameters. 
 Configuration 
 
Configure the link between fieldbus devices, and the link between device tag and 
main controller; 
 
Set the macrocycle and subcycle of segment, and optimize the function block 
schedule. 
Monitoring 
 
Get the device alarm diagnostic information and block alarm diagnostic information. 
4.1 Add Fieldbus Virtual Device to Commissioned Segment 
 Configuration flow of FF devices is shown in Figure 4-1. 
 
Figure 4-1 Configuration flow of FF devices 
4.2 Add FF Devices 
After adding and commissioning the devices in the commission segment, the mapping relationship 
between the virtual device in the configuration and the field device can be established to realize
--- pag 15 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
12 
the online parameter configuration, monitoring and other functions of the device. 
4.2.1 Preparation 
If the system already contains the DD file of the device to be added, the "unmatched segment" of 
the FF network segment will display the FF device connected to the site in real time, and the initial 
status of the device is "Spare". 
If the FF device has been connected to the site but there is no display in the "unmatched segment", 
it means that there is no DD file of the device or the DD file of the device has been updated, and 
the DD file needs to be re-imported. Operation method: In Figure 21, click "Advanced> DD Tools" 
to re-import the DD file of the device, and then click "Advanced> Refresh" to refresh the 
manufacturer list. 
4.2.2 Add FF Virtual Devices 
In the commission segment, a virtual FF device can be added. This task can be achieved by the 
following two methods: 
 
In the device configuration window, select the network segment to be added (such as 
network segment 1), and select "Add Device" from the right-click menu, and the 
"Properties" setting dialog box shown in Figure 4-1will pop up. 
 
Select the device to be added from the "Manufacturer List" window (specified to the 
specific version, that is, the device version with the 6-digit identification). 
 
Figure 4-2 Set the Property Dialog of Fieldbus Device 
The specific parameter settings are shown in Table 4-1. 
Click "OK" to add the specified device to the "Commission Segment" in the "Virtual" state.
--- pag 16 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
13 
Table 4-1Device property configuration table 
Parameter 
Configuration Illustration 
Node address 
No need to set, when matching the device, the system will 
automatically allocate according to the node where the device is 
located; 
Device tag 
Enter the tag number of the device, that is, PDTag format 
Device ID 
The device decides by itself, no need to set 
Working mode 
The device decides by itself, no need to set 
Manufacturer 
Device Model

version 
DD version

adding the device by dragging, and it is optional when you

Capacity level 
Some devices have this function, which can be set when the 
device is instantiated. For details, please refer to 
"Instantiate/Delete the Function Block of an Instantiated FF 
Device" 
 
 
Tips: 
The maximum length of PD-Tag is 31 characters, and it cannot be set as NULL. Status devices 
and their function blocks in one VisualField configuration must have different PD-Tags. 
Users are suggested to choose the device with the latest Capabilities File Version if the DD 
Versions are the same. 
 
4.3 Set the Properties of Fieldbus Device 
Users can set the PD-Tag and the block tag after adding virtual device according to the 
application. 
4.3.1 PD-Tag Setting 
PD-Tag is a sign of fieldbus device of Fieldbus H1 segment and cannot be repeated. 
Steps to set PD-Tag: 
1. Select the device in Device list and select “Property” in its right menu, pop up the following 
dialog of “Property”.
--- pag 17 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
14 
 
Figure 4-3 Set the Property Dialog of Fieldbus Device 
2. Enter the PD-Tag name, the example is PDT1. 
3. Click OK and save it. 
4.3.2 Device Block Tag Setting 
Users can monitor the fieldbus device by setting block tag of device. 
1. Click 
 to display all blocks. 
2. Select the block, right-click and select Set Block Tag, pop up the following dialog. 
 
Figure 4-4 Set Block Tag 
3. Enter the Block Tag name. 
4. Click OK and save it. 
4.3.3 Reset Block Tag 
Normal name of block tag in device is in form of “FF Device Name_FF Block Name”. After 
modifying FF device name, the block tags in device can be modified in batch
--- pag 18 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
15 
Steps to reset block tag: 
1. Select device in the device list. 
2. Select the command of "Reset Block Tag" in the device's right-menu, pop up the dialog 
shown in Figure 4-5. 
 
Figure 4-5 Reset Block Tag 
4.4 Commission/ Decommission Device 
4.4.1 Commission 
 
Tip: 
Commission can be implemented when the virtual device version of commissioned segment 
is consistent with standby device of decommissioned segment. The DD version of Virtual 
device must be greater or equal to the DD version of Standby device. 
 
Device commission includes configuration device commission and field device commission. 
1. Select device in the state of Spare in DeCommissioned Fieldbus Devices, right-click and 
select Put in Standby. This step can be skipped if the device is in Standby state. 
2. Select the configuration device in Virtual state in the Commissioned Fieldbus Devices, 
right-click and select Commission, pop up the following dialog. 
 
Figure 4-6 Select Device Dialog 
3. Select the field device in Figure 4-5 and click OK, pop up the following dialog.
--- pag 19 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
16 
 
Figure 4-7 Commission Dialog 
4. Select the Whether Write Down Params according to the application. 
 
Attention: 
 
If select the Whether Write Down Params, parameters of the field devices will be modified 
as consistent as configuration device after commission. 
 
Select the Whether Write Down Params only when the project required. 
 
 
Not select the Whether Write Down Params and click Start Commission, pop up 
the following dialog. 
 
Figure 4-8 Not Select Whether Write Down Params 
 
Select Whether Write Down Params and click Start Commission, pop up the 
following dialog.
--- pag 20 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
17 
 
Figure 4-9 Select Whether Write Down Params 
 
Click Read Params, pop up the following dialog. 
 
Figure 4-10 Uploading the Params 
 
Pop up the following dialog when uploading finished.
--- pag 21 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
18 
 
Figure 4-11 Start Commission 
 
Click Select Parameters, pop up the following “Select Parameters to Update” 
dialog, in which select the parameters needed. 
 
Figure 4-12 Select Parameters to Update Dialog 
 
Select parameters and click OK to return to the Commission dialog.
--- pag 22 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
19 
 
Figure 4-13 Commission Dialog 
 
Click Start Commission and begin to commission the configuration device with the 
field device, and modify the parameters according to the configuration. 
4.4.2 Check the Commission Result 
The commission result can be view in the Operate page in Output window. If the commission failed, 
users can find and process the reason causing failure and commission again according to the 
information shown in the Output window. 
4.4.3 Decommission 
Decommission can be implemented for commissioned configuration devices, include 
commissioned online device and commissioned offline device. 
Operational steps of decommission are as follows: 
1. Select the device in the Commissioned Fieldbus Devices, right-click and select 
Decommission, pop up the following dialog. 
2. Click Start and decommission the configuration device and field device. 
4.5 Configure Device Parameters 
After the configuration is downloaded, if the user needs to view or modify the parameters of each 
function block of the field device, he can open the corresponding function block parameter window 
to configure the parameters. 
The FF device contains three types of user application blocks, namely resource blocks, 
conversion blocks and function blocks. The parameter configuration of the resource block and the 
conversion block is completed in the FF configuration software, and the parameter configuration of 
the function block is completed in the function block diagram programming software. 
There are two types of device states that can be configured with parameters:
--- pag 23 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
20 
 
Online 
 
Standby 
Select the device, right-click and select Device Configure, pop up the Device Configure window 
as below, in which the parameter configuration can be achieved. 
 
Figure 4-14 Device Configure Window 
4.5.1 Introduction 
The Device Configure window is composed of: 
 
Device Information Display Area 
It can display the information of fieldbus device, including device manufacturer, device 
model and device version, etc. 
The device property only can be configured while adding device. Details of property 
configuration refer to 4.1 Add Fieldbus Virtual Device to Commissioned Segment. 
 
Block Parameter Selection Area 
It can display blocks of the fieldbus device, include Resource Block
, Transducer 
Block
 and Function Block
. 
Users can click 
 to extend and configure the parameters. 
 
Block Parameter Configuration Area 
It can configure the block parameter of the fieldbus device. 
The parameter can only be read and cannot be written when the area is in grey. The 
parameter can be read and written or modified when the area is in black. 
 
Parameter Instruction Area 
It can display the instruction of a certain parameter.
--- pag 24 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
21 
4.5.2 Configuration Steps 
1. User can modify the parameter value by double-click it, then the parameter will become 
orange. As the “STRATEGY” parameter in Figure 4-14. 
2. Click Apply after modification. 
 
Tip: 
Users can refer to device user manual or ask manufacturer for the Fieldbus Foundation device 
parameter configuration. 
 
4.5.3 Steps for Parameter Configuration 
 
 
Tips: 
 
Users should change the block mode to OOS before modifying the parameters of device 
resource block and function block. 
 
Information of the parameter will be shown at the bottom of the window when it is 
selected. 
 
Only one function block parameter window can be open at a time in VFFFBuilder 
configuration software. 
 
After modifying the parameter of online decommissioned device, if users select Whether 
Write Down Params in commission, then all parameters selected Whether Write Down 
Params of online decommissioned device will be modified as same as the parameter of 
decommissioned device. 
 
Normal block parameters and configuration steps are shown below: 
Resource Block Mode 
Here take “Auto” as the target mode of resource block, to introduce the configuration of block 
parameter: 
1. Extend the resource block in the parameter selection area, double click Parameter. 
2. Select Contained page and extend “MODE_BLK” parameter, select “TARGET” for the 
resource block.
--- pag 25 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
22 
 
Figure 4-15 MODE_BLX Parameter 
3. Select “Auto”. 
Configuration of other mode (such as PERMITTED) is same to the configuration of TARGET 
mode. 
Please refer to the resource block mode. 
Transducer Block and Function Block Mode 
Configuration of function block mode and transducer block mode is same to the configuration of 
resource block mode. 
Please refer to the resource block mode. 
4.6 Instantiation/ Delete Instantiation of Fieldbus Device Function 
Block 
4.6.1 Function Block Instantiation of Fieldbus Device 
Instantiation can be implemented on the fieldbus device with instantiation function block. 
1. Select the fieldbus device in Manufacturer List and drag it to the Commissioned Fieldbus 
Devices, pop up the Property dialog.
--- pag 26 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
23 
 
Figure 4-16 Property Dialog 
2. Click Custom and pop up the Select Capability Level dialog. Select the number of 
instantiation for the function block. 
 
Figure 4-17 Set the Instantiation Number of the Function Block 
3. Click OK and save the setting.
--- pag 27 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
24 
4. Commission the instantiated virtual fieldbus device and the online fieldbus device. 
5. Select the instantiated fieldbus device after commission, right-click and select 
Instantiation. Pop up the Device Operating dialog. 
6. Click Start to process instantiation. 
 
Tip: 
It need a while for instantiation, users can view the process in operate page of Output window. 
When instantiation finished, it will show as "Operate Completely" in the Operate page in 
Output window. 
 
4.6.2 Delete Instantiation of the Fieldbus Device Function Block 
The FF device function block that has performed the instantiation operation can perform the 
operation of deleting the instantiation according to actual needs. 
Users can delete instantiation for the instantiated function block of fieldbus device. 
1. Select the instantiated function block, right-click and select Delete Instantiated Block. 
 
Figure 4-18 Delete Instantiated Block 
2. A prompt box pops up whether to delete the instantiation operation of the device, click 
"Start" to delete the instantiated FF device function block. 
4.7 Set Fieldbus Device as Master/ Basic Device 
The fieldbus device with Link Active Scheduler (LAS) can be set as master device, then it can 
perform LAS function instead of AM712-S. 
 
Tip: 
Only the Fieldbus Device in the state of Standby can be set as master device. 
 
4.7.1 Set Fieldbus Device as Master Device 
The FF device can be set as the master device through the following steps. 
1. Select the Fieldbus device in Standby state and supporting LAS function, right-click and 
select Set to Master.
--- pag 28 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
25 
2. Pop up following dialog, click Start to set the master device. 
 
4.7.2 Set Fieldbus Device as Basic Device 
Steps to set the fieldbus device as basic device: 
1. Select the fieldbus device which has been set as master device, right-click and select Set 
to Basic. 
2. Pop up the Alter to Basic dialog. Click Start to set the basic device. 
3. Pop up the Hide dialog and users can click it in application. 
4.8 Control Strategic Configuration 
The control strategy configuration of the FF device is completed in the VF function block diagram 
programming software. For details, please refer to the "Engineering Instruction Manual". For the 
detailed use of the FF function block, please refer to the Function Block Reference.
--- pag 29 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
26 
Section 5 Diagnostics 
The diagnostic information of the FF device can be viewed in the FF configuration software 
VFFFBuilder and the real-time monitoring software. Through the diagnostic information of the 
device, it can be determined whether the current state of the device is normal. The following 
introduces the device diagnostic information contained in VFFFBuilder. For the acquisition of 
diagnostic information in real-time monitoring, please refer to the Diagnosis Software User 
Manual. 
 
Tip: 
 
Only the device in state of Online or Standby can perform diagnostic. 
 
Different devices have different diagnosis information, please refer to the device manual 
for details. 
 
5.1.1 Operation Steps 
1. Select the device in the Device Configuration window, right-click and select 
Diagnostic. 
2. Pop up the Condition window as shown in Figure 5-1, by which users can view the alarm 
information of the device. 
Alarm can be displayed by 2 ways: 
 
Tab with alarm will be shown as red text, as shown in Figure 5-1, the tab “Alarm” has 
alarm, 
 
The light of alarm item will be come red, i.e. 
 
 means alarm in that type. 
 
 means no alarm. 
Alarm types and contents of different devices are different, as shown below. 
5.1.2 Alarm 
Block alarm is an important alarm type of FF alarm, which can indicate the system problems of 
configuration, hardware, connection and device in block. Figure 5-1 shows the block alarm tab.
--- pag 30 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
27 
 
Figure 5-1 Condition-“Alarm” tab of transducer block 
Different blocks have different alarm information. Figure 5-2 shows the alarm tab of resource 
block. 
 
Figure 5-2 Condition-“Alarm” tab of resource block

the generation reason of process alarm and configuration of device parameters.
--- pag 31 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
28

5.1.4 Alerts 
错误！未找到引用源。 shows the “Alerts” tab of FF transducer block, which including 3 kinds of 
alarms, FAILED, MAINT and ADVISORY. 
 
Figure 5-4 Condition-“Alerts” tab of transducer block 
5.1.5 Dynamic Variables 
错误！未找到引用源。 shows the “Dynamic Variables” tab of FF transducer block, which including

--- pag 32 ---

5.1.6 Advance
