Figure 5-6 Condition-“Advance” tab of resource block 
5.1.7 Other 
错误！未找到引用源。 shows the “Other” diagnosis information tab of FF transducer block, which 
including the self-diagnosis information of FF device.
--- pag 33 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
30 
 
Figure 5-7 Condition-“Other” tab of transducer block 
5.2 Segment Property Setting 
Segment property setting includes basic property setting and advanced property setting. 
5.2.1 Segment Basic Property Setting 
Users can set the segment basic properties such as Segment Disable, Macrocycle, etc. 
Steps to set the segment basic properties: 
1. Select the segment, right-click and select Property, pop up the following dialog. 
2. Users can select Segment Disable to disable the segment in application. 
3. Select the Macrocycle.
--- pag 34 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
31 
 
Figure 5-8 Segment Basic Property Setting 
Besides, users can view the Virtual Communication Relationship (VCR) of the segment in the 
dialog. 
5.2.2 Segment Advanced Property Setting 
Users can set the System Management Parameters and Link Master Information by setting the 
segment advanced property. 
1. Click Advanced in the Menu Bar and select Segment Setting, the following dialog will 
pop up as follows.
--- pag 35 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
32 
 
Figure 5-9 Segment Setting Dialog 
2. Set the SM Params, LM Info and Cfg Settings. 
The parameter definition and value range will be displayed in the interface. 
5.3 Schedule 
 
Tip: 
Generally, the function block of Fieldbus H1 segment in VFFFBuilder will execute the control 
strategy based on the best schedule mode automatically, users do not need to change it. 
 
Schedule function can be used to modify the sliced time, set the run times of configuration function 
block and configure the schedule area. 
Icons in Function Block Information List: 
 
: Function block module or Host controller 
 
Network data publish time 
Icons in Schedule Configuration Area:
--- pag 36 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
33 
 
: Function block module 
 
: Selected function block module 
 
: Network data publish module 
 
: Selected network data publish module 
 
: Function blocks internal data transmission module 
in the same physical device 
 
: Running time of the Host controller 
 
: Conflict 
 
: Conflicted function block module 
 
: Conflicted network data publish time 
 
: Shadow of the redraw part 
 
: Redraw function block module 
 
: Redraw network data publish module 
 
Tip: 
Redraw means that part of function block module and network data send package module 
running repeated after setting the sub-cycle. 
 
5.3.1 Schedule Steps 
1. Select the segment in Device Configuration Window, right-click and select Show 
Schedule, a Segment Schedule Viewer dialog appears. 
 
Figure 5-10 Segment Schedule Viewer Dialog 
2. Users can modify the schedule configuration information in the Segment Schedule 
Viewer dialog.
--- pag 37 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
34 
5.3.2 Parameter Configuration and Instruction 
 
Macrocycle 
It shows the cycle of control strategy executed once in the segment. 
Macrocycle can configure in the segment basic property, details of the configuration refer 
to 4.8.1 Segment Basic Property Setting. 
 
Sliced Time 
Users can configure the sliced time in the Segment Schedule Viewer dialog and can 
select 20ms, 50ms, 100ms and 500ms. 
Configuration method: click 
 and select the sliced time. 
 
Run Times 
It shows the run times of a certain function block in one macrocycle. 
Modification method: select the fieldbus function block in the VFFBDBuilder, double-click 
it to open the Properties Settings dialog and modify the FFCycle. 
Details of configuration refer to FBD Programming Software User Manual. 
 
Adjust the execution time of the function block manually 
Select the function block and drag it to the required time. 
5.3.3 Automatic Optimization 
VFFFBuilder can optimize the schedule configuration automatically. Right-click in the 
Segment Schedule Viewer dialog, and select Optimize to optimize the schedule 
configuration. 
5.3.4 Notices 
 
Users can select and drag the function block module, except the OUT Internal 
Transmission Module and Host Controller Run Time Module. 
 
Conflict between modules appears when: 
 
Different modules overlap in one device; 
 
Function block module overlaps with the network data publish module in one 
device; 
 
Different network data publish modules overlap. 
 
Schedule configuration by dragging function block module or network data publish 
module may cause conflict between modules. Conflicted module will be marked with 
the icon 
 and cannot download the configuration. Users can eliminate the conflict 
by dragging the function block or optimizing it automatically. 
 
Automatic optimization may cause modules conflict in some special situation, and 
users can drag the modules to adjust it.
--- pag 38 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
35 
 
Function block module and the network data publish module will be displayed as 
normal and redraw these two parts in the schedule configuration area, if the users 
do not select “1” for its Run Times. The redraw part is covered by the shadow. 
 
Tip: 
Users can only select and drag the modules of normal part, and the modules of redraw part 
will be adjusted with them. 
 
5.4 Delete the Configuration Device 
5.4.1 Operation Steps 
Users can delete the unused configuration device from the Commissioned Fieldbus Devices. 
 
Tips: 
 
Device performed with link configuration can only be deleted after deleting its links. 
 
Users should decommission the configuration device before delete it. 
 
1. Select the configuration device, right-click and select Delete, a Delete dialog opens. 
2. Click OK to delete the device. 
5.4.2 Notices 
 
Device of DeCommissioned Fieldbus Devices and in the state of Standby cannot be 
deleted. 
 
Device of Commissioned Fieldbus Devices and in the state of Virtual can be deleted. 
 
Device of Commissioned Fieldbus Devices and in the state of Online can be deleted 
after decommission and ensuring that the device is not assigned in configuration. 
 The physical device of fieldbus device in the state of Online will be online again in the 
DeCommissioned Fieldbus Devices, after the fieldbus device is decommissioned. 
 And the decommissioned fieldbus device in the state of Offline can only appear in the 
DeCommissioned Fieldbus Device after being online. 
5.5 Compile 
Users can check the correction of the fieldbus device configuration by compiling. 
5.5.1 Compile Steps 
Select Advanced | Compile in the Menu Bar after the device configuration finished.
--- pag 39 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
36 
The error of compiling will be shown in the Error Page in the Output Window. 
 
Figure 5-11 Error Prompt Dialog 
If compile successfully, it will be shown in “Output” pane in Figure 5-12. 
 
Figure 5-12 Compile Successfully 
5.5.2 Reasons for Compiling Failure 
Please compile again if compiling failure occurs after solving problems prompted by the software. 
Following reasons can cause compiling failure: 
 
Decommissioned fieldbus device exists in the segment 
 
The VCR number of a fieldbus device in the segment exceeds the maximum VCR 
number. 
 
The acyclic schedule time of a macrocycle is less than 50%. 
 
Publishing VCR number of the segment exceeds 80. 
 
Subscribing VCR number of the segment exceeds 40. 
 
Total VCR number of a single segment exceeds 50.
--- pag 40 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
37 
Section 6 Device Maintenance 
This chapter introduces the regular maintenance and replacement of device. 
If users want to replace a commissioned fieldbus device while keep the configuration information, 
they should apply different operations basing on the new devices. 
6.1 Replace Device 
Only the new device having the same model and version of one manufacturer can replace the old 
device. 
If the new device is in same type with the old one, use “Replace” command to replace it 
automatically. 
1. Connect the new device with H1 segment. 
2. Ensure that the new device is in the state of Online in the DeCommissioned Fieldbus 
Devices. 
3. Select the device to be replaced in the Commissioned Fieldbus Devices, right-click 
and select Replace to open the Device Replace dialog. 
 
Figure 6-1 Device Replace Dialog 
4. Click Next according to the prompt. 
6.2 Update DD Files 
Users can update the DD Files of the fieldbus device, which is not registered by the Foundation 
when the software published, through importing DD Files by DD Tools in engineering station.
--- pag 41 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
38 
The DD file import function can be realized through the DD tool, so as to realize the DD file update 
of the FF device. 
The operation steps of the DD tool are as follows: 
1. Select Advanced > DD Tools in the Menu Bar to open the DD Tool dialog. 
2. Select “Import” in the Menu Bar. 
3. Click Import after select the directory of DD File to be imported. 
 
Figure 6-2 DD Tool Dialog
--- pag 42 ---
VFFFBuilder User Manual 
39

 
 For fieldbus device in the state of Mismatch

 VFLDBuilder User Manual 
Section 1 Overview 
Ladder Diagram (LD) derives from relay control schematic diagram. The most important functions 
of Ladder Diagram are logic operation and interlock control. As one of the standard languages, 
Ladder Diagram is not only used as programming language for programmable controller, but also 
widely used in many other fields, for example, Sport Control System, Distributed Control System, 
PLC Control, SCADA, etc. 
VFLDBuilder is one of the main control strategy configuration tools of the VisualField software 
package, which provides function of Ladder Diagram programming and debugging.
--- pag 4 ---
VFLDBuilder User Manual 
 
3
Section 2 Software Features 
VFLDBuilder conforms to IEC61131-3 standard. By combining with function block library, it 
provides powerful functions of graphical logic processing and interlock control, making it 
convenient for program editing and debugging, and supports single program compiling and online 
download. 
Features of the Ladder Diagram Builder: 
 
Ladder Diagram supports all contacts, coils, jumps and some system function blocks 
of standard type. 
 
Ladder Diagram program can be divided into segments which are not related to 
each other, and each segment has a auto-numbered label and a editable text 
description. 
 
Ladder Diagram supports the jump to the beginning of the segment corresponding 
with the label. 
 
There is no special restriction for the placements of elements except left/right 
convergence. 
 
Upward parallel branches and cross without connection are not permitted in the 
ladder diagram. 
 
The maximum amount of program elements in each segment (excluding amount of 
links) is 32.
--- pag 5 ---
VFLDBuilder User Manual 
 
4
Section 3 Function Overview 
VFLDBuilder is mainly used to can deal with switch signal processing, interlock control and simple 
sequence control logic. 
VFLDBuilder serves as an integrated development environment for ladder diagram program. It 
provides four main functions: edit, compile, online and debug. 
1. Edit: edit the elements (segment, contact, coil, jump and function block), zoom the 
view, search & replace, print, import & export, etc. 
2. Compile: Compile the diagram and create relevant files, prompt succeed or error 
messages (it can locate the relevant element). 
3. Online: Communicate with controllers to debug the program logic after the program 
is complete and downloaded. 
4. Debug: Debug the program, variables and function blocks in online state. 
 
Program debugging: display the value of analog variables and boolean variables in 
real time and mark them with different colors, making it convenient for observation. 
 
Variables debugging: display status and value of the tags in real time, and modify 
the tag status and value. 
 
Function block debugging: display and modify the relevant parameters of function 
block in real time, close or activate input / output pins real timely.

VFSFCBuilder User Manual 
Section 1 Introduction 
SFC (Sequential Function Chart) is a type of module operation that controls the sequence of time 
events, such as start, operation, stop, and so on. 
SFC consists of steps and transition conditions. The step consists of a series of actions. When the 
transition condition is satisfied, the order is from the current step to the next step. For each SFC 
scan, the system determines the activated step and transition conditions. When the transition 
condition is satisfied, the step before the transition condition is no longer activated, and the step 
after the transition condition becomes activated. 
1.1 Working Process 
All status of the SFC program and commands related to status switching are illustrated in the 
status transition diagram shown below. 
 
Figure 1-1 SFC Status Transition Diagram 
 
1.1.1 Supported Status 
SFC program contains two kinds of status, namely: 
 
The RUNNING status is transient and supports custom programming. 
 
The IDLE, COMPLETE, and STOPPED are final status and do not support programming.
--- pag 5 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
2 
1.1.2 Status-Switching Rules 
The status of the program will automatically change state in the order of IDLE > RUNNING > 
COMPLETE under normal conditions. During the monitoring or debugging process, the program 
status can be manually switched via the command button on the SFC program panel. The status 
switching is controlled by the START, STOP and RESET commands. 
The switching rules for program status are listed in the following table. 
Table 1-1 SFC Program Status Switching Rules 
Current Status 
Command 
Estimated Status 
Remark 
IDLE 
START 
RUNNING 
IDLE is the initial status of the program. 
After it enters IDLE status, data of all 
programs will be initialized. 
- 
COMPLETE

RUNNING 
STOP 
STOPPED 
After it receives STOP command in 
RUNNING status, the program will 
switch to the STOPPED status.

After it receives START command in the 
STOPPED status, program will continue

RUNNING status. 
STOPPED

the initial status that is IDLE status. 
COMPLETE

After it receives RESET command in the 
COMPLETE status, program will restore 
to the initial status that is IDLE status. 
 
1.2 Program Composition 
The SFC program in the VF system software supports sequence diagrams of multiple structures, 
and the sequence diagrams of multiple structures are composed of steps, branches, transitions, 
and etc. 
1.2.1 Basic Elements 
The basic elements of the SFC program include start step, step number, selection branch, 
transition condition, action description, selecting branch-selecting junction, parallel 
branches-parallel junctions, and end step, as shown in the following figure. SFC programs include 
the following elements, but not every element is required.
--- pag 6 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
3 
 
Figure 1-2 SFC Basic Elements 
During the execution of the typical SFC program shown in the above figure, the following rules are 
followed: 
 
The program starts from step 
Step supports three states, namely initialization state (not activated, not executed), 
activated state and complete state. 
The initial state means that the step is not activated and has not been executed, the 
active state means that the instruction or code is being executed, and the completion 
state means that it has been executed and is no longer executed. 
 
Transition condition judgment after step 
The judgment starts when the previous step of the transition condition is activated. When 
the entire transition condition passes, the establishment status of each expression in the 
transition condition is recorded, and the update of the satisfaction status of the transition 
condition is stopped, that is, the satisfaction condition of the transition condition is a 
historical data. 
 
Step jump
--- pag 7 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
4 
During program execution, you can jump through the steps on the panel or according to 
the jumps configured in the transition conditions. The jumped step should be the parallel 
branch of the currently activated step. 
1.2.2 Program Structures 
Program structures include sequential structure, parallel branch, selection branch, jump branch 
and loop branch as shown in the table below. 
Structure 
Structure Name 
The sequential structure consists of steps and 
transitions. 
Step is used to perform production-related operations. 
Transition is used to configure the transition for entering 
the next step. 
Parallel branches can operate simultaneously in the 
same cycle, and their execution is independent of each 
other. 
The transition condition under the parallel branch can 
operate only if all the steps at the end of the parallel 
branches are activated and their transition conditions 
are all satisfied. 
Selection branches are usually added after the step. 
The execution order of the selected branches is starting 
from the branch where the condition is satisfied first and 
going into next in turn. 
If multiple transition conditions are met at the same 
time, the leftmost transition in the SFC diagram is 
activated, as 002 shown in the figure on the left side. 
A jump branch consists of an initial transition condition 
and an arrow symbol specifying a jump target. 
If the transition condition of the jump is satisfied, the 
jump will be performed. If there are multiple jumps at 
the jump source location (002 and 003), the jump where 
the transition condition is firstly satisfied operates firstly. 
If multiple transition conditions are satisfied at the same 
time, the leftmost transition condition is activated. 
In the jump structure, the jump only operates at the end 
of the selection branch and cannot jump into the 
parallel branches.
--- pag 8 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
5 
Structure 
Structure Name 
Loop branch is a special condition of the jump branches 
and its jump objective is the step prior to it. As shown in 
the figure on the left, the jump objective in the loop 
branches is the step “002”, which is the previous step of 
the jump branch. 
 
1.2.3 Program Running Rules 
 
SFC program supports two modes, automatic and manual modes. 
In automatic mode, the step starts immediately after activation. 
In manual mode, the step starts after it is activated and waits for “Continue” command for 
next transition’s result. After the step execution is completed, if the next transition 
condition of the step is satisfied, the transitioned step will be activated and wait for the 
“Continue” command. If the next transition condition of the step is not satisfied, continue 
to keep the current step active and wait for the transition condition to be satisfied. 
 
When the transition condition prior to the branch is not satisfied, the currently activated 
step will be executed in each scan cycle until the transition condition is satisfied. Then, 
the currently activated step will fail, and the next step is activated. If you select “Execute 
once” (set in step property settings), it will be scanned during the first cycle during which 
the custom function block is called, and will not be scanned any more. 
 
In the selection branch, the branch that first satisfies the transition condition operates 
first, the other branches will not operate. When there are more than two selection 
branches satisfying the condition at the same time, the leftmost branch operates first. 
 
In the parallel branch, when the transition condition prior to the branch is satisfied, all 
branches under the parallel branch will start running at the same time. When all the 
branches finish running and the transition condition is met, the parallel branches end 
operation. 
 
When the transition condition prior to the jump is satisfied, the program logic jumps 
directly to the target step and continues operating from that step. When the transition 
condition is satisfied, the program goes to the next step. If it is not satisfied, each control 
period needs to scan this transition.
--- pag 9 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
6 
Section 2 Configure SFC Program 
When the controller in the ECS-700 system is FCU713-S and FCU712-S, the SFC program can 
be created by VFExplorer and the SFC program can be edited by VFSFCBuilder. 
2.1 Workflow 
 
Figure 2-1 SFC Program Configuration Flowchart of VF Software 
2.2 Create and Configure SFC Program 
Before starting SFC programming, create a SFC program at first. The specific steps are as follows. 
1. Open the VFExplorer. 
2. Select “Control Station > Custom Programs” in the project navigation tree and select 
“New” from its right-click menu. 
3. In the pop-up dialog box, select “SFC” in the “Type” drop-down list and configure “Name” 
and “Description” for the SFC program. 
 
The program name supports 64 characters and cannot contain the characters 
“\”\’\\/,:<>|?*%\r\n”. 
 
The program description supports 128 characters. 
 
The cycle supports fast cycle, 1 time, 2 times, 5 times, 10 times cycle multiples, the 
default is 1 time. 
 
Start phase 0~9, default 0. 
4. Double-click the newly created SFC program to open the VFSFCBuilder program and the 
program configuration interface is displayed as shown in the figure below.
--- pag 10 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
7 
 
 
 
Figure 2-2 Initial Interface of VFSFCBuilder Software 
5. Configure the tag name of the SFC program. 
Choose “Edit > Properties” in the menu. The SFC tag configuration dialog box is 
displayed as shown in the following figure.
--- pag 11 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
8 
 
 
 
Figure 2-3 Configuration Interface of SFC Tags 
6. Configure SFC program property as per the table below. 
Configuration 
Item 
Function Description 
Tag Name 
Used to specify the tag name of the current program. In real-time monitoring, the 
SFC program can be controlled through the tag monitoring panel of the SFC 
program. 
It supports up to 24 characters and can only be composed of numbers, letters, "-", 
"_", and cannot be duplicated with the name of the function block in the station. 
Tag Description 
It is used to configure the description information of the current program and 
supports up to 64 characters. 
Tag Group 
The tag group used to specify the tag of the program. 
Tag Level 
The tag levels are divided from 0 to 9 (0 is the lowest, 9 is the highest). Tag levels 
are selected from the drop-down menu. Tag level is used to set whether or not it 
needs to double check before values of tag panel are changed. 
Decimal digitals 
Decimal digital range is from 0 to 7. It is selected from the drop-down menu. 
Auto/Manual 
Status 
It is used to specify the initial manual automatic state of the program. 
Select “Auto”, the program will start to run automatically after the program starts. 
Select “Manual”. After the program starts, it needs to be triggered manually to start 
running.
--- pag 12 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
9 
Configuration 
Item 
Function Description 
Auto Start 
Status 
It is used to specify whether the program will automatically restart after running to 
the COMPLETE state. It is only valid in the manual mode. 
Select “Open”, which means that the program will automatically restart after 
running to the COMPLETE state. 
Select “Close”, which means that the controller will automatically enter RUNNING 
status to restart after the program runs to the COMPLETE. 
Cold Start Status
It is used to specify whether the program continues to run after a cold start of the 
controller. 
Select “Open”, the program will enter IDLE status after the controller is cold 
started. 
Select “Close", the controller will keep the current running status after the cold 
start before the program. 
 
7. Click “OK” to complete the creation and configuration of SFC program. 
2.3 Add and Configure Sequential Step 
The steps in the SFC program can be configured by the following operations. 
1. Enter the SFC program configuration interface shown in Figure 2-2. 
In the initial status, SFC program includes one step001. If new steps need to be added, 
please firstly select one step and then select “Edit > Add sequential step”. The newly 
added step will display after the selected step. 
2. Double click the sequential step you need to configure and the “Step property” dialog box 
will pop up as shown below.
--- pag 13 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
10 
 
 
 
 
 
Figure 2-4 “Step Property” Dialog Box 
3. Configure the property values for the step according to the table below. 
Configuration Items 
Description 
Describe 
The description for the step
--- pag 14 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E 
11 
Configuration Items 
Description 
Command 
To appoint how the step is performed, selecting from the drop-down list: 
 
N: Execution repetitively. 
 
P: Execute only once (rising edge of pulse). 
 
L: Repeated execution within a limited time. After L is selected, you 
need to configure a limited time next to the configuration item. 
 
D: Repeat after a delay. After selecting D, you need to configure the 
delay time next to this configuration item. 
 
S class command/R: S class command occurs with R command in 
pairs. S class command includes S, SL, SD and DS. After the step 
configured with S class command is activated, this step action will 
continue to execute until it receives the command that the signal R step 
sent. When configuring R step, you need to specify the step with S 
class command. 
For example, if 001 step is set to S step, 003 to R step, then only after 
003 step is executed, can the action of 001 step stop. 
 
SL: Keep executing within a limited time. After you select SL, you need 
to configure a limited time next to the configuration item. The unit of the 
limited time is second. 
DS: The step holds running after it is activated and experiences the limited 
time delay; During the D (delay) process, if the current step is no longer 
activated, the D action will stop performing and no longer perform S action. 
DS action can be stopped by R command. The limited time of delay is set in 
“time” text box next to DS command and the unit is second. 
SD: The step holds running after it is activated and experiences the limited 
time delay; During the D (delay) process, even if the current step is no longer 
activated, the D action will still perform and hold S action; SD action can be 
stopped by R command. The limited time of delay is set in “time” text box 
next to SD command and the unit is second. 
Code 
Use the ST function to configure the action you need to perform in this step. 
Click “Tag Select” to add the tags of which codes need to be executed. It is 
noted that “Code” only supports writing operation on the writable parameters.
When editing codes, only normal tags and array tags are supported. 
 
Normal tags adopt “tag name, segment” such as AO11020000.IN. 
 
Array tags adopt “array parameter name. segment name[dimension1. 
dimension2]”, such as G_IMF.OUT1[2,1]. G_IMF is a global function 
block name, OUT1 is the output pin of G_IMF array, [2,1] is the array’s 
subscript of OUT1. 
 
4. Click “OK” to save the property configuration of the current step. 
2.4 Add and Configure Transition Conditions 
The transition condition is generally used to determine if a subsequent step can be activated. You 
can add and configure transition conditions by the follows. 
Configuration Step 
1. On the SFC program configuration interface, double-click the transition condition you 
want to configure, as shown in the blue area of the figure below.

12 
 
 
 
Figure 2-5 Transition Conditions in SFC Program 
2. The “Transition Properties” dialog box shown in the figure below pops up. 
 
 
 
Figure 2-6 “Transition Properties” Dialog Box 
3. Configure the “Transition properties” according to the table below. 
Configuration Items 
Description 
Name 
Name will be automatically designated in the format of Tn, and n represents 
from 1 to 128. 
Description 
It is used to configure the description of the transition condition and supports 
up to 64 characters.
--- pag 16 ---
VFSFCBuilder User Manual IM41S09-E

Configuration Items 
Description 
Check box 
It is used to configure whether the transition condition needs to 
jump to the particular step. It is noted that only when the 
transition condition is branch structure and the transition 
condition is not at the leftist side, the jump can be configured. 
If it is checked, it indicates that you need to jump. Otherwise, it 
will automatically proceed to the next step. 
Jump 
Text box 
When the check box is checked, the configuration item takes 
effect. 
It is used to specify the target step to jump to when the 
transition condition is met. When this item is configured, a 
jump arrow will be inserted below the transition condition, and 
the target step of the jump is displayed on the right side of the 
arrow. 
Transition 
It is a statement used to configure the transition condition. The judgment 
statement should be written in ST language.

After selecting the step, select “Edit > Add Branch” to add selection branches.

After selecting the branch start position or the parallel branch start position, select “Edit

You can also create sequential steps, branches, and other structures in the branch. The method is

Section 3 Compile and Debug 
After editing the SFC program, you can compile and debug the program in VFSFCBuilder. 
3.1 Compile 
VFSFCBuilder supports the compilation of logic in SFC. The specific steps are as follows. 
Select “Program > Compile” in the menu bar, VFSFCBuilder starts the syntax check of the SFC 
program, and displays the check result in the “output window”: 
 
If the syntax is correct, the compilation will be passed. 
 
If the syntax is wrong, the cause of the error will be prompted. When you double-click the 
error item, you can jump to the target object of the error syntax and select the object. 
 
 
Tips: 
If the SFC program referenced a tag, and the tag's name was modified after being 
referenced, the control station's configuration should be recompiled and downloaded. 
 
3.2 Debug 
After the SFC program is compiled and downloaded, it can be debugged online in VFSFCBuilder. 
3.2.1 Debugging 
Select “Program > Online” and the status transition diagram will switch to the debugging status as

areas:

Description 
Mode/Status 
The mode and the status of the current program. 
Manual/Auto Area 
 
Auto: By default, when the transition condition is met, the next step is automatically 
activated and executed. 
 
Manual: After the currently activated step is completed, the step continues to be 
executed. Only when the continuing command is accepted and the transition 
conditions are met, the next step is activated and executed. 


During the debugging process, you can insert a breakpoint in the transition step, so that you can

VFSTModule User Manual 
Section 1 Overview 
1.1 Fundamental Functions 
Custom function block programming software (VFSTModule.exe) is for users to create custom 
function block according to requirements of control techniques so that the logic can be reused in 
FBD programming software. Custom function block is equal to subprogram, including input, output, 
inner variable and inner program logic defined by users. 
Custom function block can be achieved by ST and SFC language, and global function block can 
be achieved by ST, SFC and FBD languages. 
The global function block is almost the same with the custom function block in compiling. This 
manual mainly introduces the custom function block programming software, and the difference of 
global function block programming software will be pointed out. 
1.2 Techniques Specification 
 
The name of custom function block must begin with letter and can only contain 
English letters, numbers and underline. It can not exceed 16 characters. Names 
can’t be repeated among custom function blocks or system function blocks. It cannot 
be modified after it is named. Descriptions cannot exceed 64 characters and can be 
modified; It is noted that the referenced parameters support to start with numbers. 
 
The name of input/output parameter can not exceed 8 characters. The name of 
inner parameter can not exceed 15 characters. The name of function block variable 
can not exceed 24 characters, and must begin with letter and only contains English 
letters, numbers and underline. The name can’t be repeated among every 
parameter. 
 
The total amount of input parameter, output parameter, inner parameter, 
configuration parameter and supervision parameter is 512. The single parameter 
number is limited by the parameters total amount. The maximum amount of 
temporary variable and alias variable is 64 and 128 respectively. There is no limit for 
the amount of reference variable. Function block variable is limited to the 8K memory 
region for one custom function block. 
 
The maximum amount of custom function block is 250 within a single control station.
--- pag 7 ---
VFSTModule User Manual IM41S61-E 
 2

The interface of VFSTModule (the following figure shows the interface of ST language 
programming software, and the interface of SFC and FBD language programming software is 
similar) is shown in Figure 1-1.

to operate.





Section 2 Introductions to Operation 
The procedure of add, edit and excerpt function block is shown as follows. 
 
Figure 2-1 Edit flow of custom function block 
 
Tip: 
The functions and corresponding figures in this section is based on ST language programming 
software, which is similar with those based on SFC language programming software. 
2.1 New Custom Function Block 
Select the node of custom function block under control station in configuration management 
software, and select “New” in the right-click menu, as shown in Figure 2-2. 
 
Figure 2-2 New custom function block

Figure 2-3.

Select ST language or SFC language. Input name and descriptions (both must conform to the 
naming rule) of custom function block, and click “OK” to create a new custom function block. Users 
can select FBD language for global function block. 
2.2 Set Custom Function Block 
Users can set properties and password of custom function block after a new one is created, please 
refer to VFExplorer User Manual for specific setting method. 
2.3 Use Custom Function Block

4.1.5 Syntax Rule 
Assignment Statement 
Assign the value of expression on the right of “:=” to variable on the left. 
Example: OUT1 := IN1; 
Function: assign IN1 to OUT1. 
Selection Statement 
 
IF statement 
IF statement defines that a group of statements will be executed only when 
corresponding logic expression is TRUE. If the logic expression is FALSE, these 
statements won’t be executed or another group of statements set in ELSE (ELSEIF) will 
be executed. 
 
Syntax 
IF condition expression1 THEN 
... (*statement serial1*) 
ELSEIF condition expression 2 THEN 
... (*statement serial 2*) 
ELSEIF condition expression 3 THEN 
... (*statement serial 3*) 
ELSE 
... (*statement serial 4*) 
END_IF 
... (*statement serial 5*) 
 
Explanation
--- pag 35 ---
VFSTModule User Manual IM41S61-E 
 30
Execution steps: 
Calculate condition expression1 follow IF, if the value is ON, then implement 
corresponding statement serial1, and then program will jump from IF block to 
statement serial5; if the value is OFF, jump to step 2; 
If the program has ELSEIF (several ELSEIF branches are available), it will calculate 
condition expression2 follow ELSEIF, if the value is ON, then implement 
corresponding statement serial2, and then program will jump from IF block to 
statement serial5; if the value is OFF, jump to step 3; 
Calculate condition expression2 follow ELSEIF, if the value is ON, then implement 
corresponding statement serial3, and then program will jump from IF block to 
statement serial5; if the value is OFF, program will implement statement serial4 
follow ELSE, and then jump from IF block to statement serial5. 
 
Example 
Find the maximum value among A, B, C which are of different value, and assign the 
maximum value to x: 
... 
IF A > B THEN 
x := A; 
ELSE 
x := B; 
END_IF; 
IF x < C THEN 
x := C; 
END_IF; 
... 
 
CASE statement 
CASE statement defines the variable values with integer type and several statement 
groups when the variable value is different. When variable value is equal to certain value, 
corresponding statement will be executed, and when there’s no matched value, the 
program will execute statement group in ELSE (ELSE branch is defined in CASE 
statement). 
 
Syntax 
CASE Integer variable OF

... (*sentence serial1*)

... (*statement serial 2*) 
ELSE 
... (*sentence serial 3*) 
END_CASE; 
... (*statement serial 4*) 
 
Explanation 
Execute corresponding statement serial according to the value of integer variable, 
when no corresponding value is found, the program will execute the statement serial 
follow ELSE. 
 
Example 
... 
CASE IN1 OF 
1: OUT1 := 1; 
2: OUT1 := 2; 
ELSE OUT1 := 3 ; 
END_CASE; 
... 
 
Loop Statements 
Loop statements includes FOR statement, WHILE statement and REPEAT 
statement. They all have end condition and a group of statements, and when the 
end condition is not TRUE, the group of statement will be executed in loop. 
Loop will end when the program executes EXIT statement. When there is nesting in 
loop, EXIT statement will only means to exit the loop of layer in which EXIT lies. 
Function of “wait for synchronization” is not allowed in loop statement. 
 
FOR statement 
 
Syntax 
FOR I := 1 TO 100 BY 2 DO 
 
 
 DOSOMETHING(); 
END_FOR; 
 
Explanation 
In FOR statement, I is control variable, 1 is initial value, 100 is end value, 2 is step 
value. Control variable, initial value, end value and step value in FOR statement 
must be integer type. Step value is 1 by default.
--- pag 37 ---
VFSTModule User Manual IM41S61-E 
 32
First assign an initial value to control variable, and then judge the end condition, and 
when the value of control variable is greater than end value, the corresponding 
statement serial won’t be executed at all. 
When the value of control variable is less than or equal to end value, corresponding 
sentence serial will be executed, and the control variable will accumulate by step value. 
And then, the judgment of end condition will continue, and once it is achieved, the loop 
will end, or operations above will be executed round and round. 
 
WHILE statement 
 
Syntax 
WHILE condition DO 
 … (*statement group*) 
END_WHILE; 
 
Explanation 
First judge the condition, and when it is FALSE, corresponding statements won’t be 
executed at all. When it is TRUE, the statement serial will be executed. 
After executing statement serial, the judgment of condition will continue, and when it 
is TRUE, the loop will continue, or it will end. 
 
REPEAT statement 
 
Syntax 
REPEAT 
… (*statement group*) 
UNTIL end condition 
END_REPEAT; 
 
Explanation 
First execute the statement group once, and then judge the end condition, therefore, 
corresponding statement group will be executed at least once. When end condition 
is TRUE, the loop will end, or it will continue to circulate. 
EXIT and EMPTY 
 
EXIT statement 
EXIT statement is used to end loop statement before the end condition becomes TRUE. 
(end the FOR, WHILE, REPEAT) 
If EXIT statement is in nesting loops, the inner-most circuit will exit (when EXIT is located 
here), then the first statement after loop will be executed. (execute the END_FOR, 
END_WHILE or END_REPEAT).
--- pag 38 ---
VFSTModule User Manual IM41S61-E 
 33
Example: if the value of FLAG is 0, SUM will be 15 after execution. If the value of FLAG 
is 1, SUM will be 6. 
... 
SUM :=0; 
 FOR I :=1 TO 3 DO 
 
 
FOR J :=1 TO 2 DO 
 
 
IF FLAG = 1 THEN 
 
 
 
 
EXIT; 
 END_IF; 
 
SUM := SUM + J; 
END_FOR; 
SUM := SUM + I; 
 END_FOR; 
... 
 
EMPTY statement 
Empty statement is produced by semicolon “;”. 
Example: 
SUM := SUM + 1; 
; (*empty statement*) 
; (*empty statement*) 
SUM1=SUM+SUM2;

5.2.2 Program Running Role 
 
Two modes are supported by SFC function block, respectively automation and 
Semi-automation mode. In automation mode, the program would be executed according 
to the program logic. In Semi-automation mode, the SFC program would transfer to 
waiting state after every step, and need to select reset command to continue the 
program. Semi-automation mode is used for single-step debug. 
 
Sequential execution. The program executes from the start step, and exit in the end step. 
 
The current activated step would keep being executed in every scan period, until the 
switch condition has been satisfied. Then the current activated step would be inactivated, 
and the next step would be activated. If Execute Once is selected (set in Set Step 
Property), the current step would be scanned in the first period after the function block 
being loaded. 
 
In selection branch, only the leftmost branch that satisfies the switch condition would be 
executed. 
 
When the switch condition before the parallel structure is satisfied, all the parallel 
branches within a parallel structure would start to run. And the parallel structure stops 
running at the time that all branches finishing their running and the switch condition being 
satisfied.
--- pag 59 ---
VFSTModule User Manual IM41S61-E 
 54
 
When the switch condition before the jump is satisfied, program logic would jump to the 
target step, and run from that step. 
 
If the switch condition is True, program logic would go to next step. Otherwise, the switch 
should be scanned in every control period.

Figure 5-16 Link of mode, command, state Figure 5-16 Connecting tag MODE_SFCUFB1 to input 
pin MODE, and output pin MODE to tag MODE_SFCUFB, achieves the input/output of function 
block SFCUFB mode from/to tag MODE_SFCUFB1. And the module mode could be modified in 
supervision interface if the tag is excerpted in graph. 
The linking mode and function of tag CMD_SFCUFB1 is similar to MODE_SFCUFB1. 
SFCUFB would keep receiving command value until the command value is canceled, and it would 
affect the function block debug and program logic execution. The linking mode shown in Figure 
5-16 solves this problem in an efficient way. After function block receives and processes the 
command coming from pin CMD, the command value would be reset, and assign to output pin 
CMD. So tag CMD_SFCUFB1 would be assigned, and reset its command value automatically.

VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and 
Monitor 
Section 1 Overview 
In order to more easily monitor the field, VisualField (hereinafter referred to as VF) developed 
Web monitor, which can monitor the field data by Web browser. In practical applications, VF uses 
the network shown in Figure 1-1. 
 
Figure 1-1 Typical network diagram of VF WebSight deployment 
In the network shown in the figure above, each role assumes different functions: 
 
VF operation station or domain server installed with VxAnywhere (hereinafter referred to as 
VxAnywhere node) exchanges data with device installed with VFWebSight (hereinafter 
referred to VFWebSight nodes) by the external network via firewall. 
 
VFWebSight node obtains VF data from the VxAnywhere node. 
 
Web client can read the VF data in the VFWebSight node and monitor it. 
 
 
Tip: 
Hereinafter the configuration items are the marked addresses in Figure 1-1. 
 
1.1 Configuration Requirement 
Table 1-1 lists the software and hardware configuration requirement of each device node in VF 
WebSight group network.
--- pag 5 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
2

1.2 Software Authorization 
When user starts VF WebSight, software authorization is required, and the authorization code is 
“VFWebSight ”. VFWebSight software authorization supports multiple-user authorization, 
namely 1, 10, 20, 30, and unlimited users. Authorization with different user numbers can provide 
data to different number of Web clients.
--- pag 6 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
3 
Section 2 Basic Settings 
This section describes that the installed configuration of VxAnywhere node, the installation and 
configuration of VFWebSight and the configuration of clock synchronization need to be completed 
before the Chrome brower performing the VF WebSight monitor. 
2.1 Install and Configure VxAnywhere 
After installing VxAnywhere and configuring the VF node, VF data can be sent 
to VFWebSight. VxAnywhere can be installed on VF 's operation station or domain server. 
Installation step 
Through the following operations, you can install VxAnywhere. 
1) After opening the VF system software installation CD, double-click “ VxAnywhere.exe ” to start 
the installation. 
2) Select “Chinese” in the language selection box, and install the software step by step according 
to the prompts. 
Configuration step 
After installing VxAnywhere, you need to specify the address of the VFWebSight device that is 
connected to VxAn ywhere to ensure that VF data can be correctly sent and received to the 
specified device . 
1) After installing the VxAnywhere program , select “ VisualField System Tools > System Global 
Options” in the start menu and the dialog box shown in the figure below pops up.
--- pag 7 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
4 
 
Figure 2-1 VF system global configuration interface 
2) Click “Web Data Service Configuration” button, and click the “Network Configuration” in the 
popped-up “Web Data Service Configuration” dialog box, then the “Configuration” pops up. 
 
Figure 2-2 VxAnywhere configuration dialog box 
3) Configure the properties of VxAnywhere according to the following table. 
Configuration Item 
Configuration Illustration
--- pag 8 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
5 
Configuration Item 
Configuration Illustration 
Local IP address 
The address is the IP address of the outside network of the local 
computer for connecting to the VFWebSight node. 
Web server IP 
address 
This is the IP address of the local computer where VFWebSight locates. 
 
4) Check “Start Web Data Service”, and the VFDataServer service process will be started when 
the monitor is started, providing various VF data to VFWebSight. 
 
Tip: 
VxAnywhere and VFWebSight only support one-to-one IP matching , that is, 
one VxAnywhere node can only connect to one VFWebSight. 
 
2.2 Install and Configure VFWebSight 
VFWebSight supports to collectn VF data and forward it to VF 's Web monitor client. 
VFWebSight needs to be installed in Win10 or siperior operation systems. 
Through the following operations, you can install VFWebSight. 
1) Double-click the VFWebSight installation program (such as 
“VFWebSight_V 1.00.00 .00-210226-C ”). 
2) After selecting “Chinese (simplified)”, install the software step by step according to the 
prompts until the dialog box shown in the figure below pops up. 
 
Figure 2-3 VFWebSight configuration dialog box 
3) Configure VFWebSight according to the following table. 
Configuration Item

local computer for connecting to the VFWebSight node.

server 
This address is the IP address for VxAnywhere device to 
connect to the computer. 
 
4) Follow the prompts to continue to install the software. 
5) After the installation is complete, restart the software according to the prompts to complete the 
software installation. 
2.3 Configure Clock Synchronization 
To ensure that the VFWebSight device can accurately obtain the VF data provided by 
the VxAnywhere device, the two devices should synchronize their clocks. The specific 
configuration steps are as follows. 
1. In the VF system configuration software, add the address configured with VxAnywhere device 
as the clock synchronization server. 
As shown in the figure below, “Clock Synchronization Server Type” is configured as “Software 
Clock Synchronization Server ( Web ) ” and “IP Address” is the IP address to install 
the VxAnywhere device. 
 
Figure 2-4 Clock synchronization server configuration of VF System Builder 
2. Configure clock synchronization in the VFWebSight device 
1) After installing VFWebSight, double-click “TimeSyncCfgClient” in the 
subdirectory “VxSipCfgSetting” of the VFWebSight installation directory, and the configuration 
dialog box shown in the figure below pops up.
--- pag 10 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
7 
 
Figure 2-5 Clock synchronization dialog box 
2) Click “Add” and the “Set Clock Synchronization Server Address” dialog box pops up, and 
enter the IP address of the VxAnywhere device. 
3) Click “Save” to complete the configuration of the clock synchronization server in VFWebSight. 
3. 
Manually synchronize the clock 
After completing the clock synchronization configuration of 
the VxAnywhere and VFWebSight devices, manual synchronization is required. 
Double click “TimeSync” at the system tray in VFWebSight, the dialog box shown in the figure 
below pops up. 
 
Figure 2-6 Dialog box of VFWebSight clock synchronization
--- pag 11 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor

Click “ Configuration Reload ” to complete the clock synchronization between the 
VxAnywhere and VFWebSight.

Section 3 Start Web Monitor 
The VF content that can be monitored on the Web client includes trend screens, graphics, single 
trend, process alarms, system alarms and tag panel. 
3.1 Task Preparation 
Before starting web monitor, you need to complete the following tasks: 
 
Complete the configuration of VxAnywhere node and VFWebSight node. 
 
Complete the user configuration of VF monitor. VF WebSight monitor’s login user name and 
password are VF monitor user's user name and password. 
 
Complete the VF operation group and monitor screen configuration. VF WebSight monitor’s 
logged-on user group is VF operation group, and the monitor screen that you can log in to 
view is various types of monitor screen in the VF operation group. 
 
Publish the configuration via VF Explorer and launch the real-time monitor software. 
 
 
Tip: 
 
For the user name and password configuration of the VF monitor user, please refer to 
the VFAccess Software User Manual. 
 
For the detailed configuration of the VF operation group and its monitor screen, 
please refer to the HMI Config Software User Manual. 
 
The monitor screens viewed by VFWebSight client are ones published by VF Explorer. 
Users must refresh web monitor client to obtain the latest monitor screens if the 
configuration is updated and published. 
 
3.2 Log into VFWebSight Monitor 
By doing the following operations, you can log into the VFWEBSight monitor. 
1) Open the Chrome browser, and type the VFWebSight address in the address bar, such as 
“192.168.1.97”. 
2) After the IP address is correct, the login interface shown in the figure below pops up.
--- pag 13 ---
VFWebSight Installation, Configuration and Monitor 
10 
 
Figure 3-1 VFWebSight Monitor’s login interface 
3) Enter the user name and password of the monitor user configured in the VF configuration in 
the “User Name” and “Password” respectively . 
4) In the “User Group” drop-down list, select the configured operation group in 
the VF configuration . 
5) Click “Login” to enter the web monitor screen shown in the figure below. 
 
Figure 3-2 VF WebSight Monitor Interface

Section 2 System Software Installation 
2.1 Installation VisualField System Software 
Installation steps of system software: 
1. Put the system installation disk in the CD/DVD-ROM and double-click it to run the 
installation program. The interface of the installing CD will pop up, as shown in Figure 
2-1. 
 
Figure 2-1 First page of installation program 
2. Click the button "Software Installation" and select "Install Software".
--- pag 7 ---

 4 
 
Figure 2-2 Interface of installing software 
3. Pop up the “Choose Setup Language” dialog, as shown below. 
 
Figure 2-3 Select installation language 
 
4. Select “English” and click “Next”. The dialog of "Welcome to the InstallShield Wizard for 
VisualField" will pop up, as shown in Figure 2-4.
--- pag 8 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 5 
 
Figure 2-4 Installation prompt of system software 
5. Click "Next" and the interface of "License Agreement" will pop up, as shown in Figure 
2-5. 
 
Figure 2-5 Software permission protocol
--- pag 9 ---

 6 
6. Click "Yes" and the interface of "Customer Information" will pop up, shown as follows. 
The installation program reads default user name and company name registered when 
installing the operating system. 
 
Figure 2-6 Client information 
7. After user name and company name have been modified, click "Next" to open the “Select 
components to install” interface below.
--- pag 10 ---

Figure 2-7 Select components to install 
VisualField is selected in default, and user can select following items as required: 
 
Select “FfSystem” to install FfSystem with the software. 
 
Select “PROFIBUS Device Online Management Diagnose Tool” to install FDTFrame 
with the software. 
 
Select “Manual” to install user manuals of VisualField with the software. Command 
“User Manual” will be shown in the path [Start/ VisualField] of operation system after 
installed. 
 
 
Note: 
 
If the “PROFIBUS Device Online Management Diagnose Tool” installed with VF system 
software without installed FFSystem, the .net4.0 program at the folder " Setup\Common" 
in VF install disk should be installed manually. 
 
“PROFIBUS Device Online Management Diagnose Tool” can be installed with VF system 
software, and can be installed independently. If installed “PROFIBUS Device Online 
Management Diagnose Tool” independently, you can run the program "FDTFrame.exe" at 
the folder "Setup\Add-on" in the VF install disk. 
 
8. After that click “Next”, “Choose Destination Location” dialog will pop up.

If it is necessary to import the configuration of the operational domain in ECS-100 to the VF project,

Section 3 Initial Configuration 
After installing VF software, configure the basic function property before the configuration and 
monitor such as whether or not to support configuration transmitting redundancy network or 
whether to support multiple screens after launching monitor. 
3.1 Configure Options 
By configuring options, users can determine whether to support the redundancy configuration of 
the configuration transmitting network or whether to support multi-project switch or configuration 
server address. 
3.1.1 Configure Server 
Select the menu command (Select [Start / All Programs/ VisualField System Tools/System Global 
Settings] in the Start menu), and a dialog box would pop up. Then set the address of configuration 
server (the information Network address of configuration server), as shown in red frame. 
 
Figure 3-1 Configuration option configuration
--- pag 16 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 13 
 
Tips: 
If unselect “Local node is configuration server”, the “Configuration Server Address” should 
be set as the SONet address of configuration server. 
 
3.1.2 Configuration Transmission Network Redundancy 
User can set whether transmit configuration data via redundant network by setting “Configuration 
Transmission Network Redundancy”: 
 
Unselect “Configuration Transmission Network Redundancy”, so connect, publish or 
download configuration in configuration management software and update configuration 
in VFLaunch will be failed when single network has fault. 
 
Select “Configuration Transmission Network Redundancy”, so connect, publish or 
download configuration in configuration management software and update configuration 
in VFLaunch will be achieved via redundant network configuration when single network 
has fault. 
 
Attention: 
 
All computers in the same project should apply the same configuration. 
 
Direct domain do not supports net redundancy. 
 
3.1.3 Configure Multi-Project Switching Property 
Through multi-project switching, users can realize remote configuration and remote monitor. 
Before executing remote configuration and remote monitor, users need to firstly launch 
multi-project switching functions. Detailed operational steps are shown as follows. 
1) In Figure 3-1, check “Support multi-project switch”. 
2) Click “Configuration” and the multiple-project switching function’s configuration interface pops 
up.
--- pag 17 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 14 
 
Figure 3-2 Multi-project switching configuration server 
3) Configure IP addresses of the remote projects you want to switch in the “Address” text box 
and click “Add”. 
4) Repeat the step 3) to add multiple IP address of configuration servers. 
All IP addresses and custom description information will be displayed in the server list after the 
addition is finished. 
3.2 Configure Monitoring Options 
Monitoring options are used to specify whether to use multiple screens, whether to go into 
simulation mode to monitor, whether to hide monitoring header and whether monitoring headers 
can be displayed in multiple columns.
--- pag 18 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 15 
3.2.1 Monitoring Options 
Select "Monitoring" tab in the "VFSetup" dialog box and the dialog will be shown as follows. 
 
Figure 3-3 Monitoring setting interface 
 
Use multi-screen when starting the monitoring software. 
It is used to configure whether the monitoring will be displayed in the multi-screens. If select 
this option, monitoring software would be run in multi-screen mode by default. Sub-screen 
mode could be chosen in this option item. 
 
Run monitoring software automatically when starting Windows. 
If select this option, monitoring software would run after Windows starting up. 
 
Don’t display Configuration Selection dialog box when starting up monitoring software
--- pag 19 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 16 
If select this option, monitoring software would directly turn into the monitoring screen when 
starting up, skip the configuration option dialog box as shown in Figure 2-1. 
 
Run monitoring software in simulation mode 
If select this option, monitoring software would run in simulation mode, don’t receive real-time 
data. 
 
Hide monitoring header automatically 
Select it and run the monitoring software again, which will hide the header automatically. 
 
Start Keyboard Alarm Tip. 
If selected this option, the alarms generated in system will also light the alarm operation keys 
of operator keyboard. Otherwise, the alarm operation keys will not be lighted. 
 
System Panel 
It is used to specify the maximum of opened panel in the real-time monitoring at the same 
time. It is an integer in the range of 1~8. If the number of opened panels is greater than the 
one user configured, the earliest opened but unpinned panel will be replaced. 
 
Language 
VF system software supports 3 languages including Chinese, English and Russian. By 
selecting from the "Language" drop-down list box, the language in the monitoring windows will 
be set. After modified the language, the real-time monitoring software should be restarted to 
make the modification valid. 
 
Monitoring header alarm configuration 
It is used to specify whether to display alarm list in the monitoring header in multiple columns. 
Check “Start multi-column mode” and configure “Column number” and the monitoring header 
will be displayed in multiple columns. The displayed columns are determined by the 
configured “column number”. Otherwise, it won’t be displayed. 
Check “Display alarm type” then the alarm list will display the alarm types. Otherwise, it won’t 
display the alarm type. In the default condition, the monitoring header’s alarm list displays 
alarm types. 
Check “Display tag description”, the alarm list of monitoring header will display the description 
information of tags associated with alarms. Otherwise, it won’t display tag description. 
 
Panel number 
It is used to specify the maximum system panel numbers and custom panel numbers. VF 
real-time monitoring supports maximum 8 systematic panels and 8 custom panels to pop up.
--- pag 20 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 17 
 
Service 
This option is used to set whether SOE server and Report Server start with the real-time 
monitoring starting. 
 
Select "Start SOE Server", the SOE server software will start at the time of the real-time 
monitoring starting next time, and the icon 
(the icon of the SOE server software) will be 
shown in system tray. 
 
Select "Start Report Server", the report server software will start at the time of the real-time 
monitoring starting next time, 
 
 
Attention: 
After select “Start Report Server”, all Excel files should be closed when monitoring software 
starting up. Otherwise, the Excel file that being edited would be closed forcibly by monitoring 
software. 
 
3.2.2 Enable and Configure Disk Alarm 
VF supports check the disk space in cycle, and disk alarm will raise when the disk space is less 
than or equal to the low limit, and the disk alarm will display as the system alarm in the real-time 
monitoring. 
Configure Steps 
1) Select [Start / All Programs/ VisualField System Tools/System Global Settings] in the OS 
system, and popup the dialog box shown as below to configure the disk alarm.
--- pag 21 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 18 
 
 
 
Figure 3-4 Disk Alarm Configure Example 
2) Click "Disk Alarm Config" to popup the dialog box shown as figure below.
--- pag 22 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 19 
 
 
 
Figure 3-5 "Disk Alarm Config" Dialog Box 
3) Configure the disk alarm by following table. 
Item 
Configure Instruction 
Disk 
It is used to specify the disk to be checked, and it is the letter from A to Z. 
Remaining 
Capacity Alarm 
It is used to specify the disk capacity limit. When the disk space is less than or 
equal to the value, the disk alarm will raise. It should be the integer greater than 1.
 
4) Click "OK" to save the current configuration. 
 
 
Caution: 
 
The maximum of disk alarms is twenty-six, and one disk supports one limit. 
 
The disk alarm only can configured in the domain server, trend server, and the 
configuration is only valid in the local. 
 
Effect in Real-time Monitoring 
After enable the disk alarm, VF will check the disk space in the cycle of 600 seconds. When the VF 
gather the disk alarm, a system alarm will raise and be recorded to the history diagnose. 
Click the disk alarm in process alarm list and click 
 in the popup interface to jump to the 
real-time diagnose page of the operation station that the disk is belonged to. It is important to note 
that the real-time diagnose page will not show the disk alarm, that is, the operation station with 
disk alarm will be in normal state in the real-time diagnose page.
--- pag 23 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 20 
3.3 Print Settings 
Select “Print” in system information dialog box, go to interface shown in Figure 3-6. 
 
Figure 3-6 “Print” setting interface 
 
Print Enable 
Select whether to enable Real-time Alarm Print and Report Print. 
 
Print Settings 
Set Real-time Alarm Print, Report Print, Trend Print and Other Print. Stylus printer should 
be selected for Real-time Alarm Print. 
3.4 Custom Button Settings 
Select “Custom button” in system information dialog box, go to interface as shown in Figure 3-7. 
Users can launch other program quickly by setting custom buttons.
--- pag 24 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 21 
 
Figure 3-7 “Custom button” setting interface 
Right-click on the interface of dialog box, the right-click menu pops up as follows. 
 
Figure 3-8 Right-click Menu 
3.4.1 Add Custom Button 
Select New Item in right-click menu, the interface of Custom Button Configuration pops up.
--- pag 25 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 22 
 
Figure 3-9 Dialog box of Custom button Configuration 
 Segment (This item must be filled in.) 
The only identifier of the custom button. Like calculator program could use “Calc”.. 
Chinese or English characters are allowed, but characters ‘[‘ and ’]’ are not. 
 Visible (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
Whether to display custom button on the monitoring list header. Up to 5 custom buttons 
could be displayed. 
 Start Program (This item must be filled in.) 
The program (.exe) is started up by the setting custom button, could be selected by 
button
. If the program locates in the path C:\WINDOWS\system32 (supposed that 
the system is installed in C disk), program name could be directly typed in to start up the 
program. Or else the full path of the program should be typed in, such as C:\Program 
Files\Adobe\Acrobat\Acrobat\Acrobat.exe. 
 Icon (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
The icon displayed on the custom button. An executable program (.exe), dynamic link 
library (.dll), icon file (.ico) could be specified. It is recommended that select or type the 
same content with the Start Program item in the edit box, so the software would
--- pag 26 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 23 
automatically obtain the program icon to display on the custom button. The custom 
button would display nothing if the input content of this item do not meet the requirement 
or be blank. 
 Command Line (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
The parameters need importing when start up the program. 
For example, if program C:\WINDOWS\system32\notepad.exe is selected in Start 
Program item, and input “1” in Command Line, then the text file with file name 1 would 
be opened when clicking the custom button. (It is supposed that the file exists, otherwise 
prompt message about whether to create the file would pop up.) 
 Description (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
The description displays in the status bar when the mouse moves over the custom 
button. 
 Authority (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
The authority to use the custom button, i.e. Observer, Operator-, Operator, Operator+, 
Engineer-, Engineer, Engineer+, Privilege-, Privilege, and Privilege+. The minimum 
authority is requested to be Observer in default. 
 Authority Grade 
The authority of Observer is 0 (the lowest grade), and the authority of Privilege+ is 9 (the 
highest grade). 
 Uniqueness (This item could be chosen to fill in.) 
Whether to start single instance control. Start single instance control in default. 
3.4.2 Modify and Delete Custom Button Configuration 
 
Modify the custom button 
Double-click the added custom button in dialog box as Figure 3-12, the Custom button 
Configuration dialog box pops up. Custom button configuration would be modified. 
 
Delete custom button 
Select the added custom button in dialog box shown in Figure 3-12, select Delete Selected in 
right-click menu shown in Figure 3-8 to delete the custom button. 
3.4.3 Move Up/Down 
Not more than 5 custom buttons could be displayed in toolbar of monitoring software at one time. 
In the case of more than 5 buttons have been set, the 5 buttons at top would be displayed 
according to the sequence shown in Figure 3-12.
--- pag 27 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 24 
Users can modify the sequence with Up and Down in right-click menu shown in Figure 3-8. 
Right-click a custom button information, and modify the sequence with “Up” and “Down” 
commands, 
3.4.4 Examples of Custom Buttons 
Example: Add 2 custom buttons, respectively open notepad (use custom notepad icon) and 
calculator program (use calculator program icon). 
 
Notepad uses custom notepad icon (.ico). Its minimum authority is Engineer and it starts 
single instance control. 
 
Calculator program uses calculator program icon. Its minimum authority is Operator and 
it.

Finish the adding of custom button 
Custom button configuration is shown in Figure 3-12. Click OK to complete the configuration.
--- pag 29 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 26 
 
Figure 3-12 Custom button configuration 
 
Attention: 
Click Cancel to abandon current custom button configuration. 
 
Display the custom button 
Custom buttons display in toolbar when monitoring software is rebooted, as shown in Figure 3-13 
 
Figure 3-13 Custom buttons 
The configuration information would display in prompt text area when the mouse moves over the 
custom button.
--- pag 30 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual 
 27

The custom buttons would not be displayed in the toolbar of monitoring list header after

3.5 Configure System Shortcut Key 
The shortcut keys Alt+Shift and Ctrl+Shift default in operation system conflict with the self-defined 
key of VF monitoring. Therefore, the shortcut keys Alt+Shift and Ctrl+Shift should be disabled after 
installing VF. 
Here takes Windows 7 as an example to introduce the operation method to disable system 
shortcut keys in other operation system. 
1. Right-click 
 in the right lower corner of operation system in task bar and select 
“Settings”, to pop up the “Text Services and Input Languages” window. 
2. Select “Advanced Key Settings” tab in the “Text Services and Input Languages”, as 
shown below.
--- pag 31 ---

Key Sequence” to pop up the “Change Key Sequence” dialog. 
4. Select “Not Assigned” in “Switch Input Language” and “Switch Keyboard Layout”, as 
shown below. 
 
Figure 3-15 Change Key Sequence (Windows 7) 
5. Click “OK” to return to “Text Services and Input Languages”. 
6. Click “OK” to save the settings for system shortcut keys.
--- pag 32 ---
VisualField Software Installation User Manual

3.6 Windows Security Configuration 
Windows Security Configuration support automatic settings for firewalls. When the VF runs for the 
first time, the firewall permissions and the firewall trust rules should be configured to make sure 
that the VF files will not be deleted or isolated by Windows Defender when the Windows Defender 
turning on. 
Select [Start / All Programs/ VisualField System Tools/ Windows Security Configuration Tool] in the 
OS system, and popup the dialog box shown as below to configure the VF white list directory. 
 
Figure 3-16 Example of Add VF White List Directory 
After VF installed, the OS will automatically recognize and configure the white list directory by the 
above configuration. The Windows security Configuration tool supports adding and deleting the 
white list as follows: 
Add

 
Click "Add Directory" to add the VF white list directory by requirement. 
 
Click "Add Directory" to delete the VF white list directory. 
 
Check the VF white list directory and click "Execute" to add the VF white list directory to 
OS. 
Delete 
Select "Delete" tab to show the interface as shown as below figure. The configured VF white list
--- pag 33 ---

directory in the OS has listed in the interface. 
Check the VF white list directory and click "Execute Deleting" to delete the configured VF white list 
directory.

VxBatch Monitoring Software 
Section 1 Overview 
The batch management software monitoring period mainly includes the following three parts: 
 
VxBatch client: contains all aspects of process production such as batch creation, batch 
process management, historical batch analysis, and supports operations such as batch 
state switching, equipment selection, interactive confirmation, or viewing alarm 
information. 
 
Overview control of equipment information: It can be built into the monitoring flow chart of 
the DCS system, and batch operation information can be monitored without switching 
pages, including operation status, interactive operation, alarm and other information. 
 
Batch report software: display batch production process data, and customize report 
styles for system status check and process analysis. 
This document mainly introduces the VxBatch client and equipment information overview control. 
For the introduction of batch report software, please refer to the VxBatchReport Software User 
Manual.

Through the VxBatch client (BatchClient), you can create batch, dispatch, and execute scheduling,

operation status without unnecessary delay.. 
3.1 Basic Settings

VisualField as an example, after configuring the custom button in the global option of the VF 
system, you can open the VxBatch client through the shortcut button at top of the monitoring 
software. The interface is shown in Figure 3-2. The login user is the authorized user in the 
configuration period. If there is a to-do event, the corresponding page name will flash in blue

Section 4 Batch Dispatch 
Batch dispatch controls are used to create, edit, generate batches, and dispatch operations. As 
shown in Figure 4-1, the parameters of the gray bottom cannot be changed automatically, and the 
parameters of the white bottom are changed. 
 
Figure 4-1 Batch dispatch control main interface 
4.1 Interface Introduction 
Batch dispatch control interface contains three parts, function buttons, batch list, batch master 
formula of the procedure list, respectively for the implementation of the function, batch parameter 
viewing and editing, the main Formula procedure view and edit. 
4.1.1 Function Button 
The series of function buttons in the upper left corner of the interface are described as follows: 
 
New: Create a new batch. 
 
Delete: delete the batch. 
 
Save: Save edit or create new content. 
 
Compile: Generate saved batches. 
 
Dispatch: The batch that was sent. 
 
Refresh: Manually refresh the batch information status. 
 
Reload: Reload the configuration. If the batch configuration is updated, just click this 
button to update the information to the monitoring period. 
4.1.2 Batch List 
Located below the function button, the parameters in the batch list are as follows:
--- pag 10 ---
VxBatch Monitoring Software User Manual 
6 
 
Batch Number: When creating a new batch, the system automatically sets the current 
time, which can be modified. 
 
Master Recipe: The master recipe selected when the batch was created cannot be 
changed after creation. 
 
Version: the version information of the master recipe and the system will automatically 
add the version information 
 
Remark: double click to add the remark information. 
 
Lock: Locking function is only used to inform other users that this batch is being used by 
locked users. Please operate cautiously instead of restricting the operation. Right-click to 
“lock” the unlocked and “unlock” the locked in the right-click menu. After lock is applied, 
the locked user name is displayed in this cell. 
 
Process Cell: The equipment selected by the main recipe is automatically generated if 
the main recipe has been specified in the configuration period, otherwise it is configured 
when the batch is newly created. 
 
Product: Double-click the form and fill it out directly. 
 
Recipe Power: when filling configuration, you cannot modify the authority types of the 
recipe. 
 
Planned Quantity: fill in the new batch and modify it. 
 
Status: The edit is not saved, saved, generated, and rejected. It is automatically 
generated according to the execution status and cannot be changed. 
 
Creator/Create Time: Record creator and creation time, automatic generation cannot be 
changed. 

