3.6.1 Event Definition
Event is the triggering condition described by some configuration information. It can generate a
group of relevant time points and spans. “Time Point Event" is the event triggered at a group of
relevant time points and "Span Event" in a group of relevant spans. “Time- Based Event" is the
event triggered according to time and "Expression Event" according to expression.
"Time-Based Event” includes: single event, daily event, weekly event and monthly event. All the
events can be either "Time Point Event" or "Span Event" except one time only event which can
only be "Time Point Event".
Statistic item "Instantaneous Value" and "Instantaneous Time" are suitable for "Time Point Event"
and others are suitable for "Span Event".

Section 6 Report Server
Report server includes real time proxy sever, real time statistical server and real time print server.
The report server has no main interface. The generated report server starts up with real time
supervision software. The report server will load the current project designated in the report editor
with the running project automatically in the start-up.
When the report server is running, system will load and run the statistical server and the print
server automatically. In the run period, the report server monitors the running status of the
statistical server and the print server every 1.5 s.
When exiting the supervision software, exit the report server automatically and exit the statistical
server and the printing server subsequently. In the period of waiting for exit, the report server will
wait for about 10 s to check whether the system exits the statistical server and the printing server
safely.

real time supervision: Select [Start/Program/SOLISCADA/System Tool/ System Global

doesn't prompt saving file. It is suggested that users don't open Excel report mode editor
and Excel worksheet simultaneously.

Ways to stop the configured report:

There are several operation teams in the configuration. If users want to make some
report invisible to some operation team, users only need to delete the configured
report item of the corresponding operation team in the configuration software.

If some report is no longer required by any operation team, users need to delete the
corresponding report page in the report editor and the report item of all operation
teams in the configuration.

When the printing queue is too long, the generated reports are not sent to the print
queue.

When the disk space is less than 500M, reports are not any longer configured.

If OFFICE 2010 is used in the system, and the follow setting should be done. Open Excel
2010, click menu [File/Excel Options], select [Trust Center/ Trust Center Settings] in
Excel Options, and select [Trusted Locations/Add New Location] in Trust Center, select
ECSData via "Browse", and select "Subfolders of this location are also trusted", and click
"OK" to finishing the settings.

User Setting Guide of Windows Domain
Section 1 Introduction
A Windows domain is a collection of computers that share public domain databases and security
policies. The Windows domain is managed by a domain server, which verifies user’s identification
and maintain domain’s security policy and master account database. Each domain and each
computer in the domain have a unique name.
The SOLISCADA system can divide the SOLISCADA control system into one or more sub-
projects. Users are allowed to use normal accounts or Windows domain accounts to log in
monitoring software. SOLISCADA effectively reduces load of system network by managing
each sub-project, therefore guarantee the real-time performance of the control network under the
large scale system.
1.1 Typical Network Structure
In the actual typical network, it can be configured as shown in the figure below. A data server and
multiple operation nodes and application servers are configured in the SOLISCADA project. The
Windows domain and the SOLISCADA project can be the same group of devices. One server is
deployed as a Windows domain server and SOLISCADA data server, the other server is deployed
as a Windows client and SOLISCADA application server, and the remaining devices are deployed
as Windows clients and SOLISCADA operation nodes.
--- pag 5 ---
User Setting Guide of Windows Domain
2
Figure 1-1 SOLISCADA project and network topology of Windows domain
1.2 Network Structure Illustration
In the network topology shown in the figure above, the top is the network of the SOLISCADA
system, and the bottom is the integrated network diagram of the SOLISCADA project and the
Windows domain.

In the top network, the data server of the SOLISCADA project provides data for one or
more operation nodes and application servers.

In the bottom network, integrate the SOLISCADA project with the Windows domain,
that is, the SOLISCADA data server also serves as the Windows domain server, the
SOLISCADA operation node, application server and the Windows domain client.

In each device shown in the figure above, the SOLISCADA data server (also a Windows
domain server) should be installed with the Windows Server version of the operating
system, and other devices can be installed with the Windows operating system as
requirement.
When there are multiple sub-projects on site, you can set up a Windows domain server for each
sub-project, or you can set up a Windows domain server for multiple sub-projects. It should be
noted that if multiple Windows domain servers are set up on the same network, the domain name
in each Windows domain server cannot be repetitive. Each Windows domain server can be
distinguished by scada1.com, scada2.com or subproj1.com and subproj2.com, by which the
domain users can be managed.

and log in with a local account (usually Administrator).


TPT (Time-series Pre-trained Transformer), a process industry time-series model independently developed by SUPCON, has dual capabilities of simulation and prediction. It can forecast process parameters like temperature, pressure, and flow rates, as well as future trends of equipment.
Capable of providing real-time supervision of equipment operation around the clock without environmental interference, TPT offers monitoring reports on process parameters, equipment health, production performance indicators, and dynamic risks. This reduces the labor intensity of manual operations and ensures sustainable economic operation. TPT (Time-series Pre-trained Transformer, a Large Model for Process Industry) Sales Technical Manual
Version: V1.0
SUPCON
07/20/2024
TPT Product Overview
Application Background
Industry Market Analysis
At present, industrial enterprises have begun to explore the path of intelligent transformation under the trend of intelligent manufacturing. Industrial intelligence based on industrial big data technology has huge business value and is attracting more and more attention from industrial enterprises, hoping that industrial big data technology can bring new production methods, business models and efficiency growth points for industrial enterprises. Accompanied by the commercialization of more industrial big data products, it is expected that the scale of China's industrial big data industry is expected to reach 49.76 billion yuan in 2025 (source: Prospect Industry Research Institute).
After ChatGPT led the trend of using generalized basic big models in 2017, big model experiments in various industries appeared one after another. Until now, the big model landing products in the industrial field are mostly big language models applied to natural language processing. There is a lack of generalized big models for data processing. Pilot projects that have been made public usually cover only a small number of scenarios, are highly dependent on customization, and lack generality for multiple scenarios. SUPCON, as the first manufacturer to anchor its big model to generic scenarios, has a great advantage in differentiation. However, at the same time, we may encounter customers' doubts about the results, and we need to change some customers' misconceptions about "universal big model = big language model = ChatGPT-like chatbot".
Customer Demand Analysis
Data is the core of industrial system operation and the critical asset of enterprises. How to collect the massive industrial data? How to combine with AI to realize intelligent manufacturing? How to achieve the goals of efficient data utilization, enterprise cost reduction & efficiency enhancement, and safe production? Enterprises have high expectations for how industrial big data applications can solve these problems. In recent years, supervisory warning and autonomous optimization products based on mechanism models + AI models have become quite mature, but the modeling process still requires rich professional background and in-depth understanding of specific mechanisms. This brings about a double increase in hardware and software costs and labor costs, leading to a lack of final profit and cost-effectiveness. In this case, customers need an industrial intelligence product with low labor & software & hardware costs to solve complex problems, which can quickly find and solve anomalies, and efficiently explore the potential of data.
Overview of TPT Product Solution
TPT (Time-series Pre-trained Transformer) is a large model developed independently by SUPCON, focusing on the analysis and prediction of time-series data in the process industry. Based on the capabilities of simulation, prediction and natural language interaction of TPT, SUPCON has created brand new products and applications that can be used in the process industry for plant operation, decision-making, optimization and other fields. From the functional level, TPT products are divided into Production Supervisor Toolbox (TPT Supervisor) and Operation Optimization Toolbox (TPT Optimizer). The standard version includes the functions of the Supervisor toolbox, while the premium version includes all the functions.
TPT Product Application Scenarios
The customer lacks the means to effectively explore the potential of device data and cannot effectively utilize data to empower production;
The customer wants to improve the ability of employees to operate the device and is willing to use AI to answer questions and solve problems;
The customer wants to further enhance the capability of the existing alarm/supervision system and explore the abnormalities that are difficult to be discovered by traditional automation software;
The customer has plans for unmanned factories / smart factories and wants to build a solid data foundation.
(Premium Version) The device often experiences fluctuations or instability, resulting in higher labor costs and inconsistent product quality;
(Premium Version) The customer wishes to further improve the control optimization capability of the device;
(Premium Version) The customer wants to cooperate and share data with SUPCON, and conduct research on the optimization of a certain process together.
Industry of Use and Main Competitors
At present, AI big model products in the industrial field are mostly at the starting phase, and are mostly focused on natural language processing (NLP), computer vision (CV), and other tracks where competing companies have been deeply cultivating for a long time.
Huawei: Huawei PanguLM has a strong track record in the mining and coal chemical industry. However, its strengths are focused on image and video recognition. Although it contains data prediction capabilities but did not publicize the relevant performance.
Aliyun: Aliyun AI Model contains data processing functions. However, the product itself focuses on the establishment of the platform, the subsequent modeling needs to be completed by the customer themselves or hired Aliyun experts.
Other products: These products are mainly language models, which are commonly known as "ChatGPT-like chat software". At present, most of the tenders are also focused on large language model-enabled private domain knowledge base query software. However, there are many competitors in this track. Cross-industry language models can also be somewhat competent for some industrial needs. Big models that fully satisfy deep industrial needs have not been reported.
Overall, AI big model products that focus on using cross-scenario data to achieve time series prediction do not have any obvious competitors, and enterprise users generally have not yet formed a fixed form of perception on industrial AI big model products. Through the release and use of TPT products, enterprise users can gradually form a product form perception with TPT as an example, thus improving user stickiness and occupying the market.
Value and Benefit Analysis
Extremely large data streams are generated in smart factories every moment. Traditional data processing and automated optimization software requires high levels of user expertise and long process times to complete specific tasks or optimizations. Moreover, the responsibilities of each software are decentralized, which can easily lead to increased operation and maintenance costs and security risks. SUPCON has built a number of software functions based on the process industry time sequence model TPT, including Knowledge QA, Real-time Report, Data Analysis, Operational Training, Autonomous Supervision and Independent Optimization, etc. It creates the experience of "one software, one model, cross-scene, multi-function", promotes the empowerment of big data and artificial intelligence technology for industrial enterprises, and provides strong support for the intelligent transformation of industrial enterprises.
The use of TPT can bring the following values:
TPT's data prediction function can identify and detect anomalies in advance and generate warnings. The warning function covers trend anomalies in key process parameters and production indicators, as well as health status anomalies in instruments, controllers, and key equipment.
Users only need to input one sentence to generate a whole-plant examination report, which summarizes the plant operation status and analyzes the abnormalities of process parameters, production indexes, and equipment health in detail.
The private domain knowledge base query, report query and data processing functions can enhance the user's information and knowledge acquisition efficiency, reducing the personnel's reliance on experience.
Premium Version Values：
TPT can quickly assist users to build "zero-threshold, cross-scenario, executable" optimization models and conduct real-time optimization based on the models, which is expected to ultimately improve revenue by 1% - 3%.
TPT integrates multi-industry experience, provides operational guidance, reduces reliance on employee production experience, and is expected to save 30% - 50% of labor costs.
TPT can build a dynamic simulation GUI interface to assess and evaluate the operation of employees and improve their operation ability.
TPT Product Features
TPT Functional Characteristics
TPT software is built around SUPCON TPT (Time-series Pre-trained Transformer) model, using a single model and a single software to integrate multiple applications for various scenarios. TPT's functions cover the entire decision-making chain of information processing, data analysis, and (advanced version) optimization proposal and implementation. TPT focuses on industrial knowledge, and is able to analyze the data at high speed while ensuring data security. TPT software has a friendly and flexible interaction mode and supports multi-modal input/output.
TPT Product Functionality Introduction
TPT contains a series of functions such as Knowledge QA, Real-time Report, Data Analysis, Operator Training, Autonomous Supervision, Autonomous Optimization. Each function can be accessed either through chat interaction or through a graphical interface with corresponding menus. The setup and management interface for each function is centralized in the "AI-Toolbox" and can be adjusted at any time by accounts with permissions.
Knowledge QA
TPT supports quickly query and provides private domain knowledge such as device manuals, operation guides and maintenance records, and users can efficiently obtain the information they need through natural language interaction, which significantly improves their work efficiency. TPT is equipped with powerful local data parsing and searching functions, which can support a variety of document formats while safeguarding the security and privacy of the information. TPT can also self-learn and update its knowledge base with the addition of new documents. TPT can also learn and update itself as new documents are added to the knowledge base, continuously improving query accuracy and response speed.
Knowledge Q&A Management: In AI-Toolbox → Production Supervisor Module → Knowledge Enhancement, you can maintain and update the private domain knowledge base.
Real-time Report
TPT can parse device data and generate reports, as well as visualizing the data, generate statistical charts and supports one-click download and export. TPT has a thorough understanding of ambiguous time in natural language, such as "today's morning shift". Users can get detailed report information and intuitive graphical presentations in natural language to help better understand and analyze data. TPT supports a wide range of report formats and chart types to ensure accurate information and real-time updates. This function can solve the pain point of suddenly needing reports urgently, which requires operators to retrieve and report to the leaders layer by layer, greatly improving work efficiency and decision-making ability.
Real-time Report Management: In AI-Toolbox → Supervisor Module → Operation Reports, you can upload report configurations and report configurations for which the customer has specific needs, which will help the big model's understanding of reporting needs.
Data Analysis
Users can upload any data file that needs to be analyzed. TPT can utilize the modeling capability to process, organize, analyze, sort, filter and graph the uploaded data set through dialogues, so that it can be transformed into the information required by the user and displayed. This function also supports further data analysis of reports generated from previous questions or query data.
Production/operations training
TPT can generate online production training Q&A questions for testing and evaluation purposes based on the generating capability of the big model in accordance with the documents uploaded by the enterprise, such as process technical regulations and job operation laws, etc. It can also construct dynamic simulation GUI interfaces for operation interaction and conduct assessment and evaluation of operation training based on the simulation capability of the time sequence big model.
Production Training Management: In AI-Toolbox → Operation Optimizer Module → Process Simulation and Training, you can upload the exam files generated by TPT and import the self-made questions to generate production training exams.
Operation Training Management: In AI-Toolbox → Operation Optimizer Module → Process Simulation and Training, you can select the devices and faults that can be simulated by TPT to generate the operation training exam.
Designate Candidate: After the exam is generated, you can designate other TPT software users as candidates in the same menu, and the candidate's TPT software will display the exam entrance.
Autonomous Supervision
TPT will evaluate the operational status from multiple dimensions such as controller, valve, equipment, instrumentation, process, etc., and the production efficiency from multiple dimensions such as energy consumption and various types of load rates. Combined with accurate time-series prediction, it can identify potential problems in advance and provide timely warnings.
Users can view the content of the warning, the reason for the warning, and the prediction results displayed using visual charts through an intuitive interface. At the same time, each alert detail page will call knowledge Q&A function, providing TPT big model's view on cause analysis, risk analysis and solutions, helping maintenance and operation personnel to take effective measures.
Autonomous Supervision Management: In AI-Toolbox → Production Supervisor Module → Analysis of Equipment Condition/Analysis of Process Parameters/Analysis of Production Factors, it is possible to switch on/off whether each assessment item (instrument, valve...) in the three sections is enabled or not, and also adjust the credibility of each item to intervene in the supervision process artificially.
Autonomous Optimization
TPT understands optimization commands from natural language inputs and provides identification of device states and suggestions for optimization plans. After the user's confirmation, TPT can automatically generate the optimization plan in the background and start building the corresponding optimization model.
After TPT proposes an automated optimization plan and runs it, the user can enter the corresponding interface to view the running optimization plan and corresponding optimization goals, the historical data involved in the plan, as well as track the changes in the optimization results. Users can also switch between executing and not executing an autonomous optimization plan with a single click.
Autonomous optimization management (operation/control optimization): If the TPT proposes an automatic optimization plan, the AI-Toolbox → Optimizer Module → Operation/Control Optimization allows you to view the optimization plans that are currently in progress, as well as the process parameters that are affected. It is possible to switch on/off or make adjustments (execution cycle adjustments, tolerance value adjustments, etc.) on a plan by plan basis.
AI-Toolbox
In addition to the management functions for each of the previous features, users with permissions will have access to the following functions within the AI-Toolbox:
SUPCON TPT model management: You can fine-tune the TPT model provided by SUPCON with new data and develop multiple fine-tuned versions of the TPT to be applied to each unit.
Information Generation Management: allows one-stop management of all plant information (nodes, rules, materials, units, bit numbers, data sources, external resource nodes...) and the results of this management are valid for all functions of the TPT software.
Typical Application Device
A large ionic membrane caustic soda plant
Project Introduction
The existing alarm and optimization device of a large ionic membrane caustic soda plant cannot meet the higher requirements of the company and plant managers for safety and intelligence, and it is difficult to explore the potential value of historical data. Therefore, the company hopes to adopt information technology, industrial big data and other technologies to build an intelligent warning and optimization system to improve the level of abnormality identification and operation efficiency of the device. SUPCON fused partner data and its own industry experience to provide this customer with chlor-alkali process specialization TPT big model and supporting software (Premium Version).
Supervision Requirements、
Ionic membrane performance in ionic membrane caustic soda plant is easy to decay and the root cause is difficult to locate, so it is difficult to capture the life cycle. Meanwhile, because the material is highly corrosive, flammable and explosive, the risk of equipment dripping and leaking is high, resulting in harsh operating conditions and high priority for troubleshooting.
TPT-driven prediction model realizes the long-cycle prediction of the total voltage and the life of ion membrane. At the same time, based on a large amount of unlabeled time series data, the TPT model was able to judge abnormal segments and complete the downstream unsupervised abnormality detection task.
Supervision Effects
Accurately guided the planned replacement of ionic membranes in electrolysis tanks.
Realized fault warning for 89 valves in the chemical chlor-alkali unit, determining 1 valve definite fault and 12 initial abnormal alarms.
Realized full-coverage process warning for 16 key variables in the electrolysis tank, and pushed risk warnings in a timely manner to effectively reduce potential safety hazards.
Optimization Requirements
It is difficult to quantitatively assess the optimal life cycle of ion membrane in ion membrane caustic soda plant. In addition, the process itself has a narrow range of control requirements and a long feedback lag time. Adjustment of the process basically relies on the operator to figure out the means, and the adjustment period is extremely long.
TPT-driven prediction model achieves a full range of automatic optimization. TPT can establish an optimization plan according to the process characteristics of ionic membrane caustic soda plant, combined with the ionic membrane life prediction data returned by the prediction model. The optimization plan can calculate the comprehensive cost from the purchasing cost of membrane replacement, installation cost, loss of maintenance and parking, additional electricity cost for maintenance, increase or decrease of production revenue and other dimensions, and determine the optimal operating cycle of ion membrane.
Optimization Effects
Accurate guidance on ionic membrane replacement increased production and reduced electricity consumption per ton of alkali. Final estimated economic savings were 2 million CNY.
Comprehensive energy consumption of caustic soda production reduced by ≥ 0.5%.
Qualified rate of 32% lye was 100%, and the fluctuation of concentration stability control was less than 0.1.
Sales Norms
Sales Instructions
TPT Model (Standard Version) includes five major functions: Knowledge QA, Real-time Report, Data Analysis, Operational Training, and Autonomous Supervision. It can fulfill the basic functions of autonomous supervision and big model empowerment to improve workforce effectiveness at a very competitive price. It also can be converted to Premium Version in the future when clients require, without the need to re-import and fine-tune the big model. It will be the main product until the autonomous optimization function is completed, and then it will be a complementary product for the advanced version.
TPT model (Premium Version) has all the functions of the Standard Version. At the same time, it can complete the autonomous optimization and operation training empowered by TPT process simulation ability. It can improve the production efficiency and realize the optimized operation in a closed loop. It will be the subsequent main product with brand influence.

--- slide 30 ---
Typical Case2: Zinc Smelting Purification Process
The purification process is a key link in hydrometallurgical zinc smelting, and the quality of purified solution directly affects the smooth progress of zinc electrolysis. Before electrowinning, the zinc sulfate solution undergoes four-stage purification to remove impurities such as Cu, Cd, Ni, and Co, meeting the impurity content requirements of the electrolysis process. To ensure the quality of the purified solution, antimony salt and zinc powder are generally added in excess, leading to high consumption of these materials.
--- slide 31 ---
Typical Case3: Ball Milling & Classification Process
Ball milling is a complex multi-parameter, multi-variable process with strong parameter correlations, non-linearity, uncertainty, and time-variability. Conventional PID control fails to achieve overall process optimization. Therefore, an optimization module based on mill operation mechanisms should be established to realize optimal material level control and stable regulation of water/ore feed rates. By online detecting slurry output, concentration, and particle size, the system analyzes mill filling status and ore property changes, predicts operational trends, and adopts self-optimizing load control for optimal ore feeding. It also incorporates idle impact protection to ensure the mill operates in the "high-efficiency zone," maximizing output and economic efficiency while achieving collaborative optimization with upstream/downstream processes and equipment.
--- slide 32 ---
Typical Case4: Flotation Process Automatic Dosing and Optimization Control
Addressing the need for intelligent system control of each production link (crushing, grinding-classification, separation, thickening) in non-ferrous metal mineral processing and the requirement for collaboration between these process links, a full-process production optimization decision model and a decision support software system will be constructed. Based on objectives such as concentrate product specifications and grades, production output, and quality, while considering factors including the production capacity of key mineral processing equipment, raw ore resource constraints and quality fluctuations, power consumption, and reagent and material consumption, the technical indicators of each mineral processing link will be optimized. Additionally, combined with changes in the operating conditions of the crushing-grinding-separation-thickening production links, the allocation of resources such as raw ore and equipment will be dynamically adjusted for optimization.
--- slide 33 ---
Typical Case5: Mineral Hot Electric Furnaces (Ferronickel, Industrial Silicon)
Current furnace control focuses on basic equipment requirements rather than full-process energy-saving optimization. Silo batching and feeding rely on manual operation, leading to high labor intensity, poor batching accuracy, and uneven mixing—negatively impacting in-furnace reactions and ferrosilicon product stability. The three-phase electrodes in furnaces have strong coupling effects; their lifting is manually adjusted by experience, resulting in inconsistent operation, unbalanced electrode work, and compromised product quality, output, and energy consumption.
Control Objectives: 
Stabilize in-furnace pressure to prevent fire/long-term negative pressure, ensuring safe and eco-friendly operation. Improve automation for continuous unit operation, reduce labor intensity, and achieve staff reduction and efficiency gains. Overcome variable coupling to realize stable control and edge optimization of process indicators, enhancing operation stability, product quality/output, and reducing consumption.

Impregnation Zone：cooking liquor penetrates the wood chips.
Heating Zone：the chips and cooking liquor is heated up between 140 and 175 °C.
Cooking Zone： most of the delignification reaction takes place, where the intensity of the reaction is dependent on the chemical concentration, cooking temperature and cooking time.；
Extraction Zone：the spent or black liquor is separated and extracted by using the extraction screens.；
counter current washing zone：the reaction is quenched by removing the remaining spent liquor and cooling down the pulp to reduce damage to the cellulose fibers，
Difficulties for digester Control：
Delignification process is highly nonlinear；
chips stay in digester for a long time, and the process output lags seriously；
Randomness of incoming wood chip’s lignin content .

Cooking to produce pulp with a stable specified quality of Kappa number (K)（influenced by raw wood chip quality, yield, liquor,temperature and cooking time）；
maintaining adequate chip and liquor level in the digester；（balanced material input and output，stable inner liquor and chip ratio ，cold blow/discharge of pulp speed（yield），wood chip feeding speed, chemical and liquor amound and adding speed in each zone.）
control the maximum cooking temperature；
Continuous Pulp Digester APC and big data optimization solution
--- slide 20 ---
Cooking Feature
Kappa number is the key quality indicator ；it's indicates the amount of residual lignin in the produced pulp；
Kappa number is directly linked with the incoming wood chip’s lignin content and the intensity of the delignification reactions inside the digester. 
The intensity of the reactions inside the digester can be controlled by manipulating the cooking temperature and cooking liquor concentration.
The residence time (output delay) is defined by the production rate. 
The incoming wood chip’s lignin content is subject to natural variation and a major source of unmeasured disturbances to the process.
The Kappa number of the produced pulp is measured physically at the digester blow line (output), and the current Kappa value corresponds to the process conditions and inputs that existed 5 - 8 hours earlier (residence time).（Large time delay process）；
A robust process model identification of the digester is required for a successful MPC and Optimization control.

--- slide 2 ---
Mobile Quality Inspection
2
A lightweight laboratory inspection digital management system specifically designed for small and medium-sized enterprises based on the Q-Lab quality data monitoring platform.
Mobile Quality Inspection is an inspection management system that utilizes mobile communication technology and mobile applications. It covers the whole process of inspection management, allowing for sample inspection registration, sampling, item inspection, result review, sample audit, report management, and other functions. The inspection process is designed to be convenient, easy to operate, and compliant with laws and regulations.
Pain Point 1
Low Inspection Efficiency
The level of informatization is low, inspection personnel are insufficient, the approval process cycles are long, and the workload of data statistics is heavy.
Poor Departmental Coordination
Low efficiency, untimely reports, and transmission errors lead to production risks.
Pain Point 3
Lack of Transparency in Information
Tracking sample inspection progress is difficult, and samples are omitted to be inspected.
Pain Point 4
Reports Requiring Management by Special-assigned Personnel
Reports are often managed by special-assigned personnel, including sorting, printing, and distribution, resulting in low work efficiency.
Pain Point 2
Pain Point 5
Data Security Issues
Lack of automated information management systems, prone to data loss or errors.

History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
1
TrdHisBrowser
Section 1 Overview
TrdHisBrowser, which also can be called history trend offline viewer, is one of the accessorial
functions in the SOLISCADA system software and users can view the history trend off-line via it.
The function of history trend off-line view can provide various history trend view modes to users
when the supervision software is not running, so that it is convenient to analyze the history data.
--- pag 6 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
2
Section 2 Interface Introduction
Select the [Start / SOLISCADA / SystemTools / History Trend Offline Viewer] in the Start menu
or click the TrdHisBrowser.exe
(C:\SOLISCADA\TrdHisBrowser.exe) in the installation directory,
and then open the view software and enter into the history trend off-line view interface as shown in
the Figure 2- 1.
The view window can be divided into title bar, menu bar, system tools bar, trend tools bar, trend
page, trend window, tag information page and status bar, etc.
Figure 2- 1 Trend History Data View Interface
Right click the blank place at right of menu bar, users can set the display or hide the “Standard”,
and “Trend tools bar” in the pop-up right-key menu.
2.1 Menu Bar
File, View, Operation menu options are displayed in the menu bar and the letter in the bracket at
the right of each menu option expresses the shortcut key.
2.1.1 File
File menu includes the options of Open, Save, Print, Print Preview, Print Setting, exit and Recent
Files.
Open
It is used to select the project of history trend to be viewed and set the project directory. When
--- pag 7 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
3
select the [File/Open] option, or click the button
, the “Configuration Selection” setting dialog
will be popped-up. When click the
button, the “Open” dialog used to select project file will
be popped-up, and then choose “ECSRun/Project name/Project.scp”. After clicking the “Open”,
selected path is displayed in the input frame under the “Configuration Selection”, as show in the
Figure 2- 2 Click the “OK” after selecting a subproject.
Figure 2- 2 Effect of project path setting
Save
It is used to save free configuration file. Select the option [File/Save], or click the button
on the
“System tool bar” and save the information of “Free configuration”. Furthermore, “Free
configuration” will be saved when close the software normally either.
Print
Select the menu option [File/Print], or click the button
, and the print setting window will pop-up
as show the Figure 2- 3. Time setting, curve setting and tag setting can be operated respectively in
this window.
--- pag 8 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
4
Figure 2- 3 Print Setting Window

Time Settings
Time setting includes “Current Page Time” and “Time Modification”. No need to set
others if select “Current page time”, and the print content is trend diagram current page
in the current coordinate time of each tag. It needs to set the “Beginning Time”, “Total
Span”, “Page Span” and whether “Unified” respectively if select the option “Time
Adjusting”, as shown the Figure 2- 4.
--- pag 9 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
5
Figure 2- 4 Time Adjusting Setting (Select unify start time)
The detail operations as followings:

Beginning Time: Click the increase/decrease button or input the time by keyboard
can set the starting time.

Total Span: Click the list button of “day(s)”, “hour(s)”, “min(s)” to selecting. Range of
Day: 0~3

Page Span: Click the list button of “day(s)”, “hour(s)”, “min(s)” to selecting. Range
of Day: 0~3

Unified: If select “Unify Start Time”, “Tag” can not be operated and only one time
coordinate will be displayed in history trend diagram. If don’t select this option,
“Start Time” of each tag can be set in the option “Tag”, as shown in the Figure 2- 5.
Detail operation: Click the list button beside the “Tag” and select a tag (only set the
configured tag in the current off-line trend page), and then modify the starting time;
After that, click the list button beside the “Tag” again to select another tag, and
modify the starting time, repeat the above operations, and click the “OK” to finish the
starting time setting. If the starting time setting of each tag is different, each tag will
have a corresponding axis as show the Figure 2- 6.

Total Page: Display the number of current pages printed. Software will calculate it
automatically according to the setting, no need to set by users.
--- pag 10 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
6
Figure 2- 5 Time Adjusting Setting (Not select unify start time)
Figure 2- 6 Multi-Time Coordinates

Curve Settings
Curve setting are used to set the line shape, width and color of trend curve.
--- pag 11 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
7

Line type and width: Click corresponding list button to select suitable line shape
and width.

Color: Click Color frame to open the color plate and select suitable color. Besides.
User can enter the customized color setting window via clicking the button
at
the right-bottom of color plate to set, add and use customized color, as shown in the
Figure 2- 7.
Figure 2- 7 Curve Setting
Tip:
100 curves in the Curve Setting window are corresponding to the 100 tags from up to down
in the trend configuration page respectively. Users can set different line shape, width and
color to distinguish different trend curves in the same trend window.

Tag Settings
--- pag 12 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
8
Tag Settings are used to select the trend curve to be printed and set the maximum and
minimum of its coordinate, whose expression has two types: value and percentage.

Maximum and Minimum of Coordinate: Input value into the corresponding
position of each tag directly or input value after selecting “%”.

“Select” Tag Name: print the trend curve of this tag

“Not select” Tag Name: no need to print the trend curve of this tag
Print Preview
Select [File/Print Preview] option on the menu bar, and print preview setting window will pop up, as
show the Figure 2- 8. Set print firstly and the method of print setting can be found in the
introduction of menu command “Print”.
Figure 2- 8 Print Preview Setting
After setting print, click “OK” and the print preview window will pop-up shown as in Figure 2- 9. The
specifications of button functions of the toolbar in this window are shown as followings:

Click
button (its function is same as the
on the system toolbar) and pop-up
the print setting panel.

Click
button to page down.

Click
button to page up.

Click
button to display one or two pages in the same window.

Click
button to zoom in.

Click
button to zoom out.

Click
button to close print preview.
--- pag 13 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
9
Figure 2- 9 Print Preview Window
Print Setting
Set properties of printer and paper
Exit
Exit TrdHisBrowser
2.1.2 View Menu
View menu can choose whether “Standard” or “Trend Tool Bar” will be displayed in the history
trend off-line browse window.
2.1.3 Operation Menu
Operation menu includes window setting, time setting, coordinates restore, data point, page
turning and zoom in/out. Details can be found in the introduction of “Trend Toolbar”.
2.2 System Toolbar
System toolbar lists part of menu functions in “File” as icon shortcut.

: Open File. The same as [File/Open]
--- pag 14 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
10

: Save free configuration. The same as [File/Save]

: Print trend. The same as [File/Print]
2.3 Trend Toolbar
Trend toolbar lists all the submenu functions in “Operation” as icon shortcut.

: Previous Screen

: Previous Half Screen

: Next Half Screen

: Next Screen

: Zoom out. Enlarge the time span of X axis (time axis) in the visible trend display
window.

: Zoom in. Reduce the time span of X axis (time axis) in the visible trend display
window.

: Zoom Benchmark: Select the benchmark line of curve zoom. (it can be
Starting time, cursor time, finish time)

: Display Settings. It can set “coordinates limit”, “coordinates setting”, “curve section”
and “display setting”.

: Time Settings. Set starting time, time span and data interval of trend curve displayed
in the trend display window.

Data List. Tag data list, which lists all the tags data displayed on the window.

Reset Coordinate. Reset the maximum and minimum of all the tags to the setting
same as configuration

: Export Data: Export the history data of tag as the format .CSV for easy to view the
history value of one tag at one time.
2.3.1 Page Turning
Click the icons on the “Trend Toolbar” to achieve the trend page turning operation, as show the
Figure 2- 10.
Figure 2- 10 Page Turning Buttons
2.3.2 Curve Zoom
Select the buttons
on the “Trend Toolbar” can zoom the trend curve in the visible time
--- pag 15 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
11
range of X axis. Select button “Zoom out”
to enlarge the time span of X axis (time axis) in the
visible trend display window. Select button “Zoom in”
to reduce the time span of X axis (time
axis) in the visible trend display window.
2.3.3 Curve Zoom Benchmark Line Selection
When set “Curve Zoom”, users can select benchmark line in
on the Toolbar.
Start
When select “Start” as zoom benchmark line, when click
, trend window will set “start time” as
benchmark and double the whole time span of time axis. Suppose that original starting time is
2006-1-5 9:00:00 and the whole time axis span is 10 minutes. After clicking this button, the starting
time will not change, but the time span will be 20 minutes. When click the icon one time, the time
span will be doubled. The maximum span is 3 days. The same as zoom in, when click
, trend
window will set the starting time as benchmark and reduce the time span to half. The minimum
time span is 2 minutes.
Cursor
When select “cursor” as benchmark for zoom, trend window will be zoomed based on “Cursor
time”. Selecting one time and clicking icon
, “Cursor time” will be the middle line of trend window,
and based on it, double the time span. Figure 2- 11 and Figure 2- 12 corresponding picture before
and after clicking the icon
. Similarly, clicking icon
, the time span will be reduced as half of
original one. Therefore, zoom by using “Cursor” as benchmark line is convenient for viewing the
trend around cursor time.
Figure 2- 11 Before clicking zoom in button
--- pag 16 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
12
Figure 2- 12 After clicking zoom in button
Cursor also used to locate time. Drag cursor by mouse left key, or scroll up or down the mouse
wheel, cursor moves left or right. Time of the location displayed in the bottom of cursor (near the
time axis), user can view the trend data in some time easily.
Stop
When select “Stop” as the benchmark for zoom, the principle is the same as “Start”, but the effect
is converse, meaning that the stop time will not be changed and starting time will move forward or
backward which makes the span of whole time axis zoom in or zoom out. The maximum of time
span is 3days and minimum is 2 minutes.
2.3.4 Interface Setting
Clicking icon
, “Display Settings” will pop up and users can operate the “Coordinate Limit”,
“Coordinate Settings”, “Curve Area” and “Display Settings”.
Coordinate Limit
It is used to set the maximum and minimum of Y axis of each tag current trend page. Coordinate
limit can be displayed by “value” or “percentage”, as show the Figure 2- 13. Y axis maximum and
minimum in the trend window will be the value which had been modified in the interface setting.
The setting effect here is the same as the setting effect of maximum and minimum in the tag
information setting window.
--- pag 17 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
13
Figure 2- 13 coordinate limit setting window
Configure Coordinate
It is used to set “data precision, display location, display interval, background color, data color and
scale color” of the value coordinate (Y axis) and “time format, display location, display interval,
time color, scale color and background color” of the time coordinate (X axis).

Data Coordinate
It is used to set “Accuracy”, “Position”, “Interval”, “BK Color”, “Color” and “Scale color” of
the Data coordinate.

Accuracy: It refers decimal digits of the value displayed at each scale. The data can
only be set any one integer between 0~5 else a dialog “Please input an integer
between 0 and 5” will pop-up.

Position: It refers value are displayed to “inside” or “outside” of the trend window;

Interval: It refers how many scales displaying a value. The value to be set must be
positive integer, or a dialog “Please input a positive integer” will pop-up.

BK Color: It depends on the display position. When the position is “outside”, it
means the background color of Y axis; when the position is “inside”, background
color can not be seen, because the background color of Y axis is the same as the
background color of trend window.

Color: It refers the color of the data on the Y axis.

Scale Color: It refers the color of scales.
--- pag 18 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
14
If the value coordinate as show in the Figure 2- 14, and the effect after setting is shown
as Figure 2- 15 (a). Figure 2- 15(b) is the effect which the display position is set as
“inside”.
Figure 2- 14 value coordinate setting
Figure 2- 15 value coordinate setting effect

Time Coordinate
It is used to set “Time format”, “Position”, “Interval”, “Time Color”, “Scale Color” and “BK
Color” of the time coordinate
--- pag 19 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
15

Time Format: It can be displayed by two modes. (HH:MM:SS and yy:mm:dd
HH:MM:SS)

Define of other items are the same as the relative define in the value coordinate
setting. Details can be found in the “Data Coordinates”.
Curve Area
In “Curve Area”, users can set “Curve Graph” “Grids Line” and “Line Information (the font color of
the tags in tag section)””.

Curve Graph (Trend Graph)
Users can set “Background”, bar width and bar color of “Slide”. The slide width only can
be an integer between 1 to 3, else a dialog” Please input an integer between 1 and 3.”
will popup. Figure 2- 16 is the setting of curve diagram and the effect is shown as Figure
2- 17.
Figure 2- 16 curve diagram setting
--- pag 20 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
16
Figure 2- 17 curve diagram setting effect

Grid Line
Users can set “color, line shape, X axis/Y axis segments” of grids, where the sectoring of
X/Y axis should be an integer between 1 and 10, or a dialog “Please input an integer
between 1 and 10”.The effect of Figure 2- 18 is as Figure 2- 19.
Figure 2- 18 grids setting
--- pag 21 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
17
Figure 2- 19 Grid setting effect diagram

Line Information
It is used to set the font color of the tags in tag information bar. Except the color of the
selected tag will be different, rest of them will be the color that be set. The effect of
Figure 2- 20 is as Figure 2- 21.
Figure 2-20 font color setting
Figure 2- 21 font color setting effect diagram
--- pag 22 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
18
Display Setting
Display setting includes the setting of “display information” and “tag information”.

Display information
It is used to set whether display the value axis (Y axis), time axis (X axis), grids, slide bar,
and tag information bar. Set the display information by “Selected” or “Not selected”.

Tag Information
It is used to set the number of tags displayed in each row. Click the list button besides
the information frame, users can select the number, the range of which is the integers
between 1 and 4. The effect of setting as Figure 2- 22 is as Figure 2- 23.
Figure 2- 22 Display Setting
--- pag 23 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
19
Figure 2- 23 Display setting effect diagram
2.3.5 Time Setting
Clicking the icon
on the “Trend Toolbar”, the time settings interface shown as the figure below
will pop-up. Users can set “Start Time”, “Time Span”, “Data Interval” and whether “Unify Start
Time” respectively.
Figure 2- 24 Time Settings

“Beginning Time”, refers the beginning time of trend curve for each tag in the current
trend page displayed in the trend window.

“Time Span”, refers span of X axis of trend curve for each tag in the current trend page
displayed in the trend window.

“Data Interval”, refers the time interval between two adjoin data points. Programs will
--- pag 24 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
20
select one suitable value as the parameter automatically, and users don’t need to set it
generally. However, if users want to obtain different trend curves at the same period time,
they need to set it, E.g., time segment is 2000s, when the parameter is 2s, 1000 points
can be got; when the parameter is 4s, only 500 points can be got. The setting of this
parameter needs to make the data amount is a number between 120 and 1200, allowed
by the window. When setting it, select corresponding positions (Hour, Min or Sec), and
click the increase/decrease button besides the “Data interval”.

“Unify Beginning Time”, refers the starting time of X axis for each tag in current trend
page is the same one, time span of X axis is same and data interval is same as well.
Details for “Time setting” please see the “Time setting” in “2.1.1File”.
2.3.6 Data Point
Click the button
on the “Trend Toolbar”, “Tag Data List” shown as Figure 2- 25 will pop-up. Tag
data displayed on the window is listed in the list. If one point data is empty, it refers there is no data
at that point.
Figure 2- 25 Tag Data List
Tip:
Time interval of two adjoin data points of one tag depends on “Time Settings -> Data
Interval”, details can be seen in relative specification “Trend Toolbar->Time Settings->Data
Interval”.
--- pag 25 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
21
2.3.7 Coordinates Restore
Click the button
on the “Trend Toolbar”, maximum and minimum of all the tags will restore to the
setting same as configuration.
2.3.8 Data Export
Click the button
on the “Trend Toolbar”, “Data Export Settings” will pop up, as shown in the
Figure 2- 26.
Figure 2- 26 Data Export Setting Window

Add: Click “Add” button, select the tag to be export history data in the pop-up trend tag
selector.

Delete: Select one tag and click “Delete” button.

Clear: Click “Clear” button to delete all tags.

Time: Beginning time, time span and data interval setting exported from history data of
each tag.
Part of data exported is shown as the diagram below.
Figure 2- 27 the format of data after being exported
--- pag 26 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
22
2.4 Trend Page
Trend page can be divided into trend configuration page and free configuration page.
2.4.1 Trend Configuration
Click icon
to enter trend configuration page. After opening specified file,
“Trend configuration page” will show its trend configuration, and then click the node
to expend
trend configuration tree. Click one “Trend page”, all tags of trend curves in this page will be
displayed in the trend window; the information of tags including in this trend page will be displayed
in tag information page. Meanwhile, part of trend window information will be displayed in the status
bar: whether unify the Starting time, (X axis) time span and current cursor time.
2.4.2 User Defined Configuration
Click icon
to enter “User Defined Configuration” page. User defined
configuration page can put tags in different trend pages into one trend window to be displayed, so
that it is convenient to analyze. Right click” Trend window configuration”, users can “Add”, “Modify”
or “Delete” trend configuration of free page.
Add free page trend configuration
Operation Steps:
1.
Right click “Trend window configuration” and click “add”, “Trend page setting” window will
pop-up, as shown in the Figure 2- 28.
Figure 2- 28 free page trend configuration
2.
Fill in “Page name” in the trend page setting window (“Page name” can be empty. In order to
distinguish easily, recommend to fill in the “Page name”).
--- pag 27 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
23
3.
Input “tag name” into edit box besides “Tag name” directly, or click the button
, select the
tag in the pop-up “Tag selector”.
Tips:

Select one tag in the tag selector and press “Shift” key, and then select another tag,
which means it can select several continuous tags.

Select any one tag and press the “Ctrl” key, which can select several discontinuous
tags.
4.
Select the color of trend curve for the tag. Color settings please see the relative introduction in
2.1.1 “Curve Setting”.
5.
Click “Coordinate” button, “Value coordinate maximum and minimum setting” will pop-up. Set
the maximum and minimum of the coordinate in this window, and the display mode is
percentage, as shown in the Figure 2- 29.
Figure 2-29 coordinate limit setting in the free configuration trend page
6.
Click the “OK” button to finish adding free trend configuration page.
7.
After adding, free configuration trend page window is as Figure 2- 30.
Figure 2-30 free configuration trend page
Modify trend configuration of user defined page
Right click one configuration page to be modified in free configuration, and then click “Modify” and
--- pag 28 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
24
modify in the pop-up panel of “Trend page setting”.
Delete trend configuration of free page
Right click one configuration page to be deleted in free configuration, and then click “Delete” to
delete it.
Save trend configuration of free page
Click the button
on the “System toolbar” to save the modify information in “Free configuration”.
2.5 Tag Information Page
Select one trend page and corresponding configuration information will be displayed in the tag
information page. Configuration information content should be consistent with the tag information
in the tag list (or domain variable configuration).
2.6 Trend Window
Trend window can be divided into X axis (time coordinate), Y axis (value coordinate), trend display
window, zoom slide button, up/down slide button and tag information bar.
Figure 2- 31 Trend Window

X axis (time coordinate): After dividing equally the time span, a horizontal axis with
equal dividing scale will be generated.

Y axis (value coordinate): After dividing equally the range of maximum and minimum of
a tag, a vertical axis with equal dividing scale will be generated.

Trend display window: Display all the trend curves of selected tags.
--- pag 29 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
25

Zoom slide button: Slide upwards the button can zoom in the trend display window,
while slide downwards will zoom out the window. Figure 2- 32 shows the comparison of
one trend window with normal, zoom in and zoom out status.
Figure 2- 32 trend diagram zoom in and zoom out effect

Up/down slide button: as shown in Figure 2- 33, slide upwards will move up the trend
display window, while slide downwards will move down the window.
Figure 2- 33 trend window move up/down
--- pag 30 ---
History Trend Offline Viewer User Manual
26

Tag information bar: Display all the tag names and current value of the data point
where the trend curve cursor is in current trend window.
Figure 2- 34 Tag information bar
In the tag information bar, user can carry out following operations:

Select the tags displayed in the trend window: Click the selection box in front of
each tag, and operate “Selected” or “Not selected”, namely display or not display
the trend curve of the tag.

Set the tag to be displayed on the Y axis and X axis: Click the tag name in the tag
information bar, and color of the selected one will be blue, as the first tag in Figure
2- 34, meanwhile, Y axis displays the maximum and minimum range of this tag and
X axis shows the display time.

View the information and set some information: Double click the tag name in “Tag
information bar”, and the “Tag information setting” window will pop-up, as shown in
the Figure 2- 35. Users can modify the setting of “Coordinate maximum and
minimum” and “Tag color”.

A customer not only wanted to explore anomalies in their chlor-alkali plant that were difficult to detect with traditional automation, but also wanted to further improve the control optimization capability of their chlor-alkali plant and maximize the potential of the plant data through artificial intelligence with both supervision and optimization functions.
Contexts
Chlor-alkali Industry (Ion Membrane) Case
--- slide 53 ---
Customer's Pain Points
As the key material of the electrolyzer, ion exchange membrane is expensive and its performance is easy to decay. The aggregation, blistering, and shrinkage of calcium and magnesium ions occurring in the reaction has a long cycle and the cause is difficult to capture.
The material is highly corrosive, flammable and explosive, and the risk of equipment running, bubbling, dripping and leaking is large. Improper operation may cause safety accidents.
The concentration of lye in the electrolyzer is easily affected by the load and components, resulting in fluctuations, and the temperature of the electrolyzer is strongly coupled with a large hysteresis, which is not easy to control smoothly.
The electrolysis process of electrolyzer consumes a large amount of electric energy, and the current efficiency varies greatly among different operation cycles and operation parameters, resulting in low operation efficiency.
